body: Human rights organisations express concern over shrinking democracy in Bangladesh Global human rights organisations have expressed concern that the targeting of politicians, activists, major media outlets and cultural institutions in Bangladesh, amid heightened political tensions ahead of the 2026 national election, signals a troubling erosion of the rule of law and a shrinking space for free expression, civic discourse and democratic participation...

title: Ferry services on Chandpur-Shariatpur route resume after nine hours
body: Ferry services between Chandpur and Shariatpur resumed on Sunday morning after nearly nine and half-an-hours of suspension due to dense fog. Faisal Alam Chowdhury, manager of Harina ferry terminal, said that operations were halted from 11:00pm on Saturday until 8:30am on Sunday to prevent accidents and ensure passenger safety, leaving over a hundred vehicles, including trucks and pickups, stranded on both sides of the ferry terminals. The ferry operations returned to normal around 9:00am after the dense fog removed from the River Meghna. Meanwhile, several passenger launches operating on Dhaka-Chandpur route, including MV Rof Rof, Jhom Jhom, Bogdadia, and Meghna Rani, arrived at Chandpur ghat with delays of five to six hours, ferry owners and supervisors said.

title: Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury takes oath as new chief justice of Bangladesh
body: Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury on Sunday took oath as the 26th Chief Justice of Bangladesh. President Mohammed Shahabuddin administered the oath taking ceremony at Bangabhaban at about 10:30am on Sunday. Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, among others, attended the oath-taking ceremony which was broadcast live by Bangladesh Television and Bangladesh Betar. Earlier, on December 23, president Shahabuddin appointed him as the new chief justice. On Saturday, Chief Justice Syed Refaat Ahmed retired from his post. Born on May 18 in 1961, Justice Zubayer is the son of the late AFM Abdur Rahman Chowdhury, who also served as a judge of the Supreme Court. Obtaining LLB (Honours) and LLM degrees from the University of Dhaka, he did a master’s degree from the United Kingdom on international law. He started his career as a lawyer in the district judges’ court in 1985 and at the High Court in 1987. On August 27, 2003, he was appointed as an additional judge of the HC Division, with his position made permanent two years later. President Shahabuddin appointed him as a justice of the Appellate Division on August 12, 2024, and he took oath the following day, on August 13.

title: Tarique thanks nation, urges democratic coexistence
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Saturday night expressed gratitude to the people of Bangladesh for the reception he received upon returning home on Thursday after 17 years, while calling for unity, democratic coexistence and a politics free from vengeance. In a Facebook post published at 10:00pm on his verified page, Tarique described his return last Thursday as an emotional milestone. Tarique returned to the country on Thursday after ending 17 years of forced exile in the United Kingdom, receiving a roaring welcome from more than a million people. ‘Last Thursday was a day I will carry in my heart forever, the day I returned to the soil of my homeland after 17 long years,’ he wrote, recalling the crowds along the streets of Dhaka and what he described as the prayers of millions. Thanking supporters who stood by him and his family over the years, Tarique said, ‘Your courage continues to give me strength,’ adding that words could not fully express the respect and love he felt for the homecoming he received. He extended his appreciation to citizens from across society, including members of civil society, young people, professionals, farmers and workers, saying they had reaffirmed that ‘the true power of Bangladesh always lies in its people when united’. Tarique also thanked the media for covering his return ‘with professionalism and care’ and acknowledged those responsible for ensuring security and maintaining calm during the event. ‘Your service matters,’ he said. In the post, the BNP leader recognised leaders of other political parties and movements who welcomed his return, noting their emphasis on democracy and multiparty coexistence. Tarique in his post, said that he was encouraged by calls for a peaceful political culture and for moving beyond confrontational politics. ‘I am grateful for the warm welcomes and for the hope expressed for a democratic, peaceful political culture, as well as the call to move beyond politics driven by vengeance,’ he wrote, adding that he accepted such messages ‘with humility and respect’. Referring to his speech delivered on the day of his return, Tarique said he had outlined ‘a plan, not just a dream’ for the country’s future – one centred on peace, dignity and inclusion. He described a vision of Bangladesh where ‘every community feels secure and valued, and where every child can grow with hope’. ‘This is a plan for all Bangladeshis,’ he wrote, calling for ‘a united, inclusive Bangladesh’ that ‘moves forward together’. Tarique had previously been sentenced in several cases, including to a life term of imprisonment, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail on September 3, 2008, after which he travelled to London on September 11 for medical treatment and remained there. Following the end of the Awami League’s 16-year rule on August 5, 2024, amid a mass uprising, the High Court acquitted Tarique of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, clearing the legal hurdles to his return.

title: Tarique to contest 13th parliamentary elections from Bogura-6, Dhaka-17
body: Bangladesh National Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman will contest the 13th parliamentary election billed for February 12 next year from two constituencies — Bogura-6 and Dhaka-17. BNP Standing Committee member Salahuddin Ahmed confirmed the decision while speaking to UNB on Saturday night. ‘Our party’s acting chairman Tarique Rahman will contest the election from two seats. One is Bogura-6 and the other is Dhaka-17. This is a party decision,’ he said. Salahuddin said BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia will contest the election from three constituencies —Bogura-7, Feni-1 and Dinajpur-3, while Tarique Rahman will contest from Bogura-6 and Dhaka-17. When asked about campaign activities suggesting that Bangladesh Jatiya Party chairman Andaleeve Rahman Partho, a BNP ally, will contest from the Dhaka-17 seat, Salahuddin said Partho is not contesting the polls from Dhaka-17. ‘He will contest the election from his home constituency, Bhola-1, using his party’s own election symbol,’ the BNP leader said.

title: Khaleda Zia in critical condition: Zahid
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party chairperson and former prime minister Khaleda Zia is in an extremely critical condition and is going through a crisis period, according to her medical board member AZM Zahid Hossain. Zahid, who is also a BNP standing committee member, briefed reporters outside Evercare Hospital in Dhaka shortly after 12:30am on Sunday. Responding to questions about Khaleda Zia’s latest health condition, he said ‘Naturally, it cannot be said that her condition has improved. Her condition is very critical and she is passing through a crisis moment.’ Khaleda Zia was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23, after which her physical condition deteriorated significantly. Due to the continuous decline in her health, she was first shifted from a cabin to the Critical Care Unit and later transferred to the Intensive Care Unit. Zahid said that both local and foreign doctors remained involved in her treatment, with her daughter-in-law, Zubaida Rahman, also part of the medical team. Meanwhile, BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman visited the hospital late on Saturday night to see his mother after completing a series of political programmes earlier on the day. The 79-year-old politician has long been suffering from multiple health conditions, including arthritis, diabetes, kidney complications, and eye problems.

title: Government extends income tax return deadline till Jan 31
body: The government has extended the deadline for submitting income tax returns for individual taxpayers for the second time for the 2025–26 tax year. According to an order issued by the National Board of Revenue, the return submission deadline has been extended from December 31, 2025, to January 31, 2026. It says the decision was taken in public interest under the powers conferred by Section 334 of the Income Tax Act, 2023, with prior approval from the government. Earlier, the NBR had extended the original deadline once from November 30 to December 31, citing various difficulties faced by taxpayers. The latest extension aims to provide additional time to facilitate wider compliance and ease pressure on taxpayers. The NBR has urged eligible taxpayers to avail themselves of the extended time and submit their returns within the revised deadline to avoid any inconvenience.

title: DAP amendment to increase hazard risks for Dhaka: urban planners
body: Repeated amendments to the Detailed Area Plan for Dhaka, allegedly driven by vested quarters, would intensify civic crises and hazard risks for the city already struggling to ensure minimum liveable condition for its dwellers, urban planners said on Saturday. They expressed their concerns at a press conference organised by the Bangladesh Institute of Planners at its office in the capital. Speakers warned that the consequences would be severe as a recent United Nations projection indicates that Dhaka may become the world’s most populous city by 2050 from present 2nd populous city with almost 37 million. Organisation president Professor Adil Mohammad Khan read out a written statement, saying that while the government might amend the Detailed Area Plan, in short DAP, in public interest, they observed that two amendments within three years were made primarily to accommodate vested business interests. ‘The government did not consider our concerns over decisions that will further increase population density in a city already overwhelmed with population,’ he said. Urban planners said that the latest amendment would significantly increase population density without a corresponding increase in essential urban amenities, such as open spaces, water bodies, transport infrastructure, healthcare and educational facilities. They also observed that the revised DAP allowed high-rise construction in areas including flood flow zones and farmlands that are highly vulnerable in the event of earthquakes, particularly as Dhaka was located in an earthquake-prone region. According to the planners, the amended DAP proposes increasing population density to as high as 280 people per acre, compared with the current density of about 220 people per acre. In some zones, density limits have reportedly been raised to 250 from 200 or to 280 from 180 people per acre. Bangladesh Institute of Planners fellow AKM Riaz Uddin said that planners might be blamed in the future for the consequences of unplanned growth, but the public should understand how their warnings and opinions were ignored in the decision-making process. Political leaders are mounting more and more pressure on Dhaka because they failed to build alternative cities, decentralise employment opportunities, and promote balanced regional development, he said, warning that ordinary people would ultimately bear the cost of such policies. The organisation’s senior fellow Salma A Shafi and vice-president Shahrier Amin, among others, also spoke at the press conference. The government finalised a new DAP for Dhaka for 2022–35 after the expiry of its previous version in 2015. Since 2022, the government amended the DAP twice, one in 2023, another in 2025. Real Estate and Housing Association of Bangladesh and Institute of Architects Bangladesh continue calling for amending the DAP further increasing its floor area ratio, FAR in short.

title: A hope for Bawm community
body: A new tourist centre, Ala Mi Tlang Eco Resort, is being constructed at an altitude of about 2,100 feet above sea level at the foot of Keokradong, one of the country’s highest mountain peaks, in Susuang Para of Bandarban. Ala Mi Tlang, which means song of the distant mountains, is being developed with financial assistance from the Bangladesh Army to help improve the livelihoods of the economically backward Bawm community. The scenic Susuang Para, located around 90 kilometres from Bandarban district town, is known for its vast natural beauty. A Bangladesh Army camp is situated adjacent to the resort site. The foundation stone of the eco resort was laid on Saturday noon by Brigadier General SM Rakib Ibn Rezwan, commander of the 69 Infantry Brigade and Bandarban Army region commander. Brig Gen Rezwan said, ‘The resort is being constructed at a cost of Tk 30 lakh with funding from the 24th Infantry Division and planning support from soldiers of the Magisterial Tiger unit.’ He said that from November 18, 2024, members of the displaced Bawm community began returning to their ancestral homes following improvements in the security situation involving the security forces and the Kuki National Army. So far, 503 members of 202 returning Bawm families have been provided with housing construction materials and humanitarian assistance. An allocation of Tk 20 lakh has already been made by the 24th Infantry Division for the rehabilitation of the returning families, he added. At present, tourists are not permitted to travel to Susuang Para. However, once construction is completed, the resort will be opened to visitors. The eco resort will be managed by the Bawm community, and the income generated will be used for education, healthcare and humanitarian activities for the Bawm group. Senior military officials and local dignitaries attended the foundation stone laying ceremony, including Lal Jarlam Bawm, president of the Bawm Social Council, as well as the captain of the Magisterial Tigers unit and the Ruma Army zone commander.

title: Skills, competence key to employment: Supradip Chakma
body: Chittagong Hill Tracts affairs adviser Supradip Chakma on Saturday said that the youth were the country’s greatest asset, stressing that skills and competence were the main keys to employment. ‘The government is continuing all-out support to create employment opportunities for the country’s four crore youths,’ he said while speaking as chief guest at the UCEP Gazipur Region Job Fair-2025 on the regional office premises at Salna in Gazipur. Mentioning that Bangladesh has a population of 18 crore, the adviser said, If the four crore youths can be developed into a skilled workforce, a fundamental transformation of the country’s socio-economic condition would be possible.’ He noted that chief adviser Muhammad Yunus had always given priority to youths. Praising UCEP Bangladesh, Supradip Chakma said that the organisation had been playing a commendable role by equipping unemployed youths with technical skills through vocational training. He urged the concerned authorities to ensure employment opportunities for these trained youths in both local and foreign institutions. Highlighting the importance of job-oriented education, the adviser said that such education not only enhanced skills but also helped build entrepreneurs. ‘There is a huge global demand for skilled human resources,’ he said, adding that women were now becoming economically self-reliant by engaging in various online businesses and through group-based training. This positive change will play a leading role in the country’s development, he added. The adviser also visited different stalls of the fair and interacted with jobseekers. Chaired by UCEP Bangladesh executive director Md Abdul Karim, the programme was also attended, among others, by Gazipur deputy commissioner Mohammad Alam Hossain; additional police commissioner, north, crime, of Gazipur Metropolitan Police Md Rabiul Islam; and GoodWeave managing director Md Shahinur Rahman, among others.

title: Ansar, VDP launches countrywide medical campaign
body: The Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party on Saturday launched a special nationwide free medical campaign for its members and family members as part of the force’s ongoing humanitarian and welfare-oriented activities. Under the programme, three-day-long free medical camps will be organised in phases from Saturday until January 13, in four districts - Bogura, Jamalpur, Bhola and Lalmonirhat, said a press release. Through these camps, Ansar and VDP members and their families will be able to receive medical services completely free of cost, it said, adding that the first phase of the programme was inaugurated on the premises of Gabtali Government College in Bogura. The formal inauguration of the Bogura camp was conducted by Bogura district commandant of Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party Md Saddam Hossain. Ansar and VDP members have been performing their duties with dedication, professionalism and self-sacrifice in maintaining law and order and taking part in various development activities across the country. Ensuring healthcare and wellbeing of these members and their families is regarded as a moral and social responsibility of the force. The free medical campaign has been organised as a practical reflection of this commitment, said the release. Under the medical service programme, a range of essential healthcare services are being provided, including eye and dental treatment. Eye specialists are conducting necessary examinations, while arrangements have also been made for free cataract surgeries in appropriate cases. Dental specialists are offering modern dental treatment along with necessary medical advice. Besides, general health check-ups for patients suffering from common ailments are being carried out, along with medical consultations and free distribution of essential medicines. Organised under the overall guidance of the director general of Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party, participants of the medical campaign expressed satisfaction and gratitude after receiving the healthcare services. The free medical campaign is not merely a healthcare initiative but also a strong expression of the force’s humanitarian responsibility, accountable leadership and social commitment towards the welfare of its members and their families, said the release. Through this programme, mutual trust and morale within the force are expected to increase, while the positive image of Ansar and VDP in society will be further strengthened. Experienced physicians, along with officials and employees of Ansar and VDP from different levels, were present at the inauguration ceremony.

title: Expatriates accorded reception in Sylhet
body: Sylhet district administration on Saturday accorded reception to more than one hundred expatriates for their contribution to Bangladesh’s economy. Posts and telecommunications ministry secretary Abdul Naser Khan addressed the programme as the chief guest at Kabi Kazi Nazrul Auditorium at Rikabibazar in the city at noon. He said in the programme that Bangladesh is in an economically stable position because of the expatriates. ‘They have contributed to every aspect of this country. The government will provide different benefits to the expatriates, including tax-free investment,’ the post and telecommunications secretary said. Emphasising the need to eliminate all sufferings, including land, documents and security related issues of the expatriates, he also said that a zone for Non-Resident Bangladeshis can be established in Sylhet for their safe investment. Sylhet divisional commissioner Khan Md Reza-Un Nabi, deputy commissioner Md Sarwoer Alam, and district police superintendent Kazi Akhtarul Alam, among others, were present at the award ceremony. According to the district administration, 103 expatriates from Sylhet residing in 12 countries of the world were selected from different categories to accord reception for their special contribution. The categories include successful professionals, businessmen, community leaders, women entrepreneurs, successful sports personalities and importers of Bangladeshi products in the relevant countries.

title: Teenager dies in Chandpur market fire, 5 shops gutted
body: A 15-year-old boy died in a fire that broke out at Sahar Bazar under Faridganj in Chandpur on Saturday morning. The fire also gutted five business establishments. The deceased was Sabbir Hossain, a resident of Shaldah village. He was employed at Joynal’s grocery shop, where the fire was believed to have originated. According to the Fire Service and Civil Defence, the blaze broke out around 10:00am, reportedly due to an electrical short circuit at Joynal’s grocery shop. The fire quickly spread to adjacent establishments in the market. Faridganj Fire Service Station in-charge Kamrul Hasan said that a fire service unit, with assistance from local residents, went to the scene and managed to bring the fire under control. ‘Sabbir Hossain’s body was recovered from the site and handed over to police for necessary legal proceedings,’ he said, adding that an investigation was underway to assess the extent of the damage and confirm the cause of the fire.

title: Navy arrests 11 with huge cement, diesel while smuggling to Myanmar
body: The Inter Services Public Relations in a press release on Saturday said that the Bangladesh Navy had arrested 11 ‘smugglers’, including an engine-powered boat with huge cement and diesel being smuggled to Myanmar from the Kutubdia outer anchorage area in the Bay of Bengal. Acting on a tip-off, the Navy members seized the boat on Friday and recovered 1,000 litres of diesel and 650 bags of Bangladeshi diamond cement, Shah Cement, from their possession, said the press release. Those seized items were smuggled to Myanmar illegally by evading custom duties through sea routes by the engine-powered boats, it said. Based on secret information in St Martins and the adjacent areas, the Bangladesh Navy ship Shahid Mohibullah earlier kept watch on a suspicious fishing boat identified as FB Ankita Anbesha about 42 miles away from the Kutubdia lighthouse. Later, the seized goods and the arrested were handed over to Patenga model police station for legal action, the ISPR added.

title: Trial of attackers on Prothom Alo, Daily Star demanded
body: Journalists and photojournalists from different news media houses on Saturday protested at the recent arson attack on and vandalism and looting of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, demanding speedy trial of the perpetrators. Their demands came at two human chains organised by the Crime Reporters Association of Bangladesh and Bangladesh Photojournalists Association in the capital. Holding banners during the demonstration, members of the CRAB in front of its office termed the attacks as a direct assault on freedom of expression, threat to press freedom and democracy alike. Speaking at the programme, Dhaka Reporters Unity president Abu Saleh Akond alleged that sections of the police and administration failed to act despite having prior information about the attacks. They also stated that the attacks could be prevented through timely intervention. They demanded an immediate and impartial investigation, identification of the attackers and exemplary punishment of the perpetrators. In another human chain in front of the National Press Club, Kader Gani Chowdhury, secretary general of a faction of the Bangladesh Federal Union of Journalists, urged the interim government to take immediate action, expressing concern that an absence of justice would embolden the perpetrators. The protesters also condemned the harassment of veteran journalist and writer Nurul Kabir, editor of New Age and president of the Editors’ Council. Prothom Alo assistant editor Lazzat Enab Mahshi, The Daily Star chief photographer Anisur Rahman, Bangladesh Photojournalists Association publicity secretary and New Age photojournalist Md Saurav were among others present at the protests. On the night of December 18, hundreds of attackers vandalised and looted the offices of the Prothom Alo in the capital’s Karwanbazar and The Daily Star across the road on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and then set fire to both the buildings. Nurul Kabir was harassed when he rushed to the rescue of the journalists trapped in the fire-engulfed The Daily Star building. The two media houses filed two cases with the Tejgaon police. So far, 32 suspects over the attacks were arrested.

title: Mamun Habib gets award from Thailand
body: Professor Md Mamun Habib, head of the Department of Management at Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB), has received ‘Excellence Researcher Award’ conferred by Shinawatra University of Thailand. The award was handed over at the International Higher Education Excellence Award 2025, ceremony on December 22 in recognition to his research impact and international academic collaboration, said a press release. Professor Habib thanked SIU and Chanyanan Somthawinpongsai, director of the International Reputation Centre, for the nomination. In a statement, he said the recognition reflects IUB’s focus on quality education and research, adding that the School of Business and Entrepreneurship (SBE) continues to work on research and academic leadership. Earlier this month, Professor Habib received the ‘Supply Chain Management Award’ at the 8th IEOM Bangladesh International Conference on Industrial Engineering and Operations Management held at World University of Bangladesh.

title: Youth beaten after being tied to electric pole admitted to NITOR
body: The youth, who was beaten and hacked after being tied to an electric pole at Shibganj upazila in Chapainawabganj, has been admitted to the National Institute of Traumatology and Orthopaedic Rehabilitation in Dhaka as his condition deteriorated. Sufia Begum, mother of the injured Abu Sufian Siju, 25, told New Age that doctors at Rajshahi Medical College Hospital referred his son to NITOR where they admitted him. She said that doctors informed them that her son’s condition was critical as a blood vessel in his left hand had become blocked. Sufia Begum alleged that local activists of Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami beat and hacked his son, who was a Bangladesh Nationalist Party activist, without any reason. Shibganj upazila Jamaat ameer Shadiqul Islam, however, denied the allegation. He claimed that Siju was a known criminal in the area and was involved in extortion and robbery. Shadiqul alleged that Siju had lured two local youths to a bridge over the Pagla River and later tried to forcibly take them away. When the youths managed to escape and sought help at a nearby market, locals intervened and beat the man, he added. The Jamaat leader claimed that the incident later took place at night and that the responsibility was subsequently pinned on Jamaat supporters without evidence. Shibganj police station officer-in-charge Humayun Kabir told New Age that after the victim’s father filed an attempted murder case, they had arrested two named accused. About the Siju’s family’s allegation, the official said that they did not find any political involvement in the incident. ‘Once the investigation is completed, we will let you know what happened,’ he added.

title: BSF halts fence construction at Jaipurhat border after BGB intervention
body: The Indian Border Security Force attempted to construct a barbed wire fence at the Ghonapara border under Panchbibi in Jaipurhat on Saturday morning, violating international border regulations, but was forced to stop after intervention by the Border Guard Bangladesh. Early Saturday morning, under dense fog, BSF personnel began the construction near the zero line at East Unchana Ghonapara, under the Koya BOP, around sub-pillars 47, 48, and 49 of border pillar 281. Local residents informed the Koya camp of the Jaipurhat-20 BGB battalion, prompting BGB personnel to arrive at the site and halt the construction. Subsequently, a flag meeting was held between the BGB and the BSF officials. During the meeting, the BSF assured that no further construction would take place and agreed to remove any erected barbed wire. BGB also formally lodged a protest regarding the incident. Confirming the incident, assistant director of Jaipurhat-20 BGB Mohammad Imran Hossain said, ‘A flag meeting was held today with BSF at the company commander level. BGB always maintains a firm stance against border violations and will take all necessary measures to protect the country’s sovereignty.’

title: BSF pushes 14 more into Bangladesh
body: THE Indian Border Security Force reportedly forced 14 members of an Indian family into Bangladesh through Chuadanga border on Friday night. The individuals are Gulshan Bibi, 90, Sheikh Jabbar, 70, Alkum Bibi, 65, Sheikh Ukil, 40, Sabera Bibi, 35, Shakila Khatun, 11, Sheikh Hakim, 45, Shamsheri Bibi, 40, Sheikh Raja, 30, Mehrun Bibi, 25; Nasrin Parvin, 12, Sheikh Tawhid, 11, Sheikh Rahid, 2, and Sheikh Bunty, 28. The group is now under the custody of the Border Guard Bangladesh. According to local people and the victims, the family was pushed through the Nimtala border gate under the cover of dense fog. The individuals, permanent residents of Jagatsinghpur area of the Indian state of Odisha, claimed they were expelled due to their religious identity. They also alleged that their Aadhaar cards and ration cards were confiscated by Indian authorities before being sent into the country. After entering, the family wandered near the border before reaching Darshana bus stand, where locals provided temporary shelter, food, and warm clothing. The incident drew attention after spreading on social media, prompting intervention by authorities. Darshana police and Chuadanga BGB-6 Battalion took the group into custody to verify their identities and citizenship. None were found to have passports, Aadhaar cards, or other valid identification. BGB is coordinating with BSF and relevant authorities to confirm the details. Lieutenant Colonel M Nazmul Hasan, commanding officer of Chuadanga BGB, confirmed the matter, saying that the families were provided food, warm clothing, and basic medical care. Legal action would follow after identity verification and consultation with higher authorities, he added. Earlier on December 14, India’s BSF pushed 15 more people, including two children and nine women, into Bangladesh through the Bibishan border point at Gomastapur upazila in Chapainawabganj district. With the latest push-ins, the number of people, including Rohingyas and Indian nationals, pushed into Bangladesh by India since May 7, has increased to 2,431.

title: Shahbagh blockade continues for justice for Osman Hadi
body: Leaders and activists of Inquilab Mancha, along with general students and public, blocked Shahbagh for second consecutive day on Saturday, demanding justice for Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, who died on December 18 after a shooting attack days earlier. The platform staged a sit-in since Friday afternoon into Saturday onward, announcing that the protest would continue until justice was ensured in Hadi’s killing. Protesters, however, temporarily withdrew the blockade for the Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairperson Tarique Rahman’s visit to Hadi’s grave in the first half of Saturday morning when they moved to in front of nearby Aziz Super Market, New Age Dhaka University correspondent reported. After Tarique Rahman had visited Hadi’s grave left with his motorcade, the platform returned to Shahbagh crossing at around 12:30pm. At the time of filing this report at around 9:00pm, protesters remained on the one of the Shahbagh intersection, causing traffic congestion and severe suffering for commuters. Public suffering was intense on the day as the admission test for Dhaka University Science Unit was held with several hundred aspirants with their guardians converged from all over the city to the area. To manage the choking traffic, vehicles coming from the Farmgate side were diverted through the road in front of BIRDEM Hospital towards Matsya Bhaban. Small vehicles coming from the Matsya Bhaban side were allowed to move towards Dhaka University only via the road in front of the Shahabagh flower market. Inqilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Zaber claimed that they allowed ambulances to pass. From the protest in the Saturday evening, he said that they had requested interim government advisers the previous day to come and talk to them, but their request was ignored. The protesters on the day said that they would not leave the streets until justice was ensured for Hadi. Meanwhile, protesters staged a sit-in in Kushtia, demanding the immediate arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible for Hadi’s killing, New Age correspondent in Kushtia reported. Following the blockade, all vehicular movement was halted on the Kushtia-Jhenaidah and Kushtia-Ishwardi highways for about two hours starting from about 2:30pm. In Chattogram city, Inquilab Mancha staged a sit-in on one side of the New Market crossing, demanding justice for Hadi, New Age correspondent in the district reported. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head from close quarters in the capital while conducting his electioneering as an independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency. After treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and Evercare Hospital in the city, he was flown to Singapore for advanced treatment. There he succumbed to injuries on the night of December 18. Law enforcers have so far arrested at least 11 people for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi, but the main suspects are yet to be arrested and are believed to have fled to India.

title: No media reform resented
body: Senior journalists of the country expressed frustration over what they called the interim government’s inertia over media reform, which was crucial to the country’s democratic transition. However, information ministry adviser Syeda Rizwana Hasan hoped that she would finish some media-related policy reforms by early January ahead of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections, scheduled for February 12, 2026. They were speaking at the 6th Broadcast Conference on Saturday, organised by the Broadcast Journalist Center, Bangladesh, at the International Mother Language Institute auditorium in Dhaka. At the event, BJC leaders and distinguished guests unveiled a code of ethics for the broadcast journalists. According to the organisers, drafting the code took three years. Speaking at a special session on policy discussion, senior journalist and BJC adviser Khairul Anwar Mukul said that the current government had appointed three information advisers, two of whom were top leaders of the July uprising. ‘Frustratingly, no reform was carried out in the media sector,’ he resented. Mukul, while questioning the government failure to prevent the 18th December arson attacks on the offices of Bangla daily Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, also expressed grave concern over the security of journalists. Consulting editor of The Daily Star, Kamal Ahmed, former chief of the Media Reform Commission, recollected that a short list of immediately implementable reform proposals was shared with the chief adviser on March 23, but no progress had happened yet. Citing one proposal for the autonomy of the state-run broadcasting and news channels, Kamal said that the bureaucratic review of the proposals came up with a comment that nothing could be implemented right now. New Age editor and Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir said that the media authorities who misreported July events in the past year should apologise to the viewers and readers to regain their trust. ‘As many of us demand apologies from the Jamaat-e-Islami for their misdeeds during the country’s liberation war, we should also demand apologies from the media authorities for their misdeeds committed during the July uprising,’ Kabir said. He also noted that print media journalists were still paid according to the 2013 Wage Board Award while the advertisement rate card of the news outlets had also not been revised since 2013. Citing that a draft broadcasting policy has already been prepared, Kabir opined that the present government could address these issues within a very short time. ‘The interim government’s failure to implement any reform in the media sector may mean its lack of political will,’ he said, urging the information adviser not to remain on the wrong side of the history. Information adviser Rizwana said that she would expedite the drafting and the approval of the Broadcast Policy Ordinance and the Press Council Ordinance. She also stated that her ministry would investigate the issues of upgrade of the wage board and the advertisement rate card. Talking about the arson attacks on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star vis-a-vis the government responsibility, she said, ‘The attackers were our common enemies. We could have probably been proactive to minimise the intensity of the attacks.’ Praising the BJC code of ethics, Rizwana urged the journalists to engage in constructive journalism instead of overlooking governance failure, as happened during the ousted Awami League regime. Supreme Court lawyer Sara Hossain, BJC chair Rezwanul Haque, member secretary Ilias Hossain, trustee Fahim Ahmed, senior journalist Shahnaz Sharmeen, and BBC Media Action country manager Mohammad Al Mamun also spoke at the event.

title: Thakurgaon shrine attacked
body: A shrine was vandalised allegedly by some unidentified miscreants in Thakurgaon town early Saturday, prompting tensions among the local residents and devotees. The incident occurred after midnight as the miscreants vandalised Hazrat Baba Shah Satyapir Mazar and several adjacent graves, according to the devotees and police officials. Officials from the district police administration and the Thakurgaon Sadar upazila administration later visited the scene. Thakurgaon additional superintendent of police for administration and finance, Khodadad Hossain, said that the site had already been inspected and the matter was being investigated with due seriousness. ‘We are trying to identify the attackers. Following the investigation, those involved will be brought under the law and necessary punitive measures will be taken promptly,’ he added. Different political parties have expressed suspicion of the involvement of extremist elements. The damage was discovered on Saturday morning when local residents and devotees visited the site. As news spread, large numbers of followers gathered at the shrine. The followers condemned the vandalism and called for those responsible to be identified and brought to justice.

title: Doc forgery intensifies visa difficulties
body: Outbound travellers and aspiring migrant workers from Bangladesh are facing growing difficulties in securing visas to popular destinations across the world over the past year amid allegations of using forged documents in many cases. Authorities and manpower industry insiders largely blamed the widespread use of forged documents in visa applications along with political instability in the country and the tendency of undocumented stays abroad for the situation. Tour operators, recruiting agencies and visa consultants said that the situation had worsened noticeably since 2024, affecting migrant workers, students, medical travellers, businesspeople and tourists alike. Several destination countries have unofficially tightened visa scrutiny for Bangladeshi applicants, while others have reduced approvals amid concerns over document fraud and visa overstays. Criminal practices such as submitting forged educational certificates, falsified employment letters and fake bank statements have emerged as a major factor behind visa complications, insiders said. Addressing an event in observance of International Labour Migration Day on December 18, Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus warned that the extensive use of fake documents was effectively closing doors for Bangladeshi workers seeking overseas employment. Highlighting the importance of safer, fairer and skills-based migration, Yunus said that forged paperwork had become a critical barrier, despite strong labour demand for Bangladeshis in many destination countries. ‘Bangladesh has become quite famous globally for the submission of fake documents,’ he said, noting that receiving countries continued to raise similar complaints regardless of destination. He cited concerns raised by the United Arab Emirates as an example of how the issue has intensified. According to tour operators, outbound travellers are increasingly facing visa refusals or prolonged processing delays. Some countries have introduced informal restrictions, while others are issuing fewer visas following allegations of widespread overstays by Bangladeshi nationals. Industry sources said that visa complications were particularly acute in Europe and the Middle East, though problems had also been reported in parts of Asia. The tightening has caused sufferings for thousands of travellers seeking medical treatment, business opportunities, or family visits, while it is also shrinking overseas job prospects for Bangladeshi workers. Md Rabiul Islam, managing partner of Suti Tour Operator, said that clients with similar or even stronger profiles were now being rejected for destinations such as the UAE, Thailand and Malaysia, despite receiving visas to the same countries in previous years. ‘More than 30 per cent of visa applications are being rejected at this time,’ he said, adding that embassies rarely explained the reasons, as providing justification was not mandatory. Countries in Asia with high rejection rates for Bangladeshi applicants include Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Turkey and the UAE, tour operators said. European countries such as Italy, Germany, Finland, Cyprus and the United Kingdom, among others, have increased visa refusals for Bangladeshi applicants. Several destination countries have publicly warned Bangladeshi applicants against submitting forged documents. Italy and the UK have both issued statements in recent months, cautioning applicants about document fraud. In May, when thousands of Bangladeshi visa aspirants demonstrated in the capital Dhaka, demanding faster Italian visa processing, the Italian embassy said that it was detecting increasing numbers of fake Bangladeshi and Italian civil status documents. In November, the UK launched a social media campaign titled ‘Don’t risk a 10-year ban!’, warning that applicants submitting fraudulent documents could face a decade-long prohibition from entering the country. The United States embassy in Dhaka has also announced tougher measures, warning that providing false information or forged documents could result in a permanent travel ban to the US. ‘The US Department of State remains committed to upholding the highest standards of national security in its visa adjudication process,’ the embassy said in a brief message on its verified Facebook page, adding that no visas would be issued until all security concerns were resolved. In September, the Royal Thai Embassy in Dhaka also warned against falsified documentation. It advised Bangladeshi applicants to apply independently, make direct hotel bookings and arrange hospital appointments directly with medical institutions when required. The tightening visa regime has taken a toll on recruiting agencies and tour operators, many of whom invest significant resources before a worker or traveller applies for a visa. Ali Haider Chowdhury, former general secretary of the Bangladesh Association of International Recruiting Agencies, said that agencies were facing mounting losses due to visa rejections. ‘When a migration process starts, agencies invest money in preparing workers. If a visa is rejected, the agency has no way to recover those costs,’ he said, describing the situation as financially unsustainable for many recruiters. Migrant rights activists said that visa restrictions ultimately hurt workers the most, pushing some to seek irregular migration routes, which increased risks of exploitation, trafficking and abuse. Officials at the Bureau of Manpower Employment and Training said that visa approval remained a sovereign decision of destination countries. Director general Saleh Ahmed Mujaffor said that the bureau had no role in visa adjudication, but continued to urge all applicants to submit authentic documents. ‘We consistently advise everyone to provide valid and genuine documents for all overseas travel and employment purposes,’ he said. Migration experts said that addressing the crisis would require stronger regulation of intermediaries, tougher action against document forgery networks, better financial literacy among migrants and expanded skills training aligned with destination country demands. Without systemic reform and effective monitoring, they warned, Bangladesh risks further erosion of trust in global migration systems — making legal mobility increasingly difficult for genuine travellers and workers alike. Special envoy for international affairs to the chief adviser Lutfey Siddiqi at a seminar titled ‘Japanese Labour Market: Opportunities and Challenges’, organised by the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment in July also blamed forged documents for visa difficulties. At the event, Zia Hasan, policy adviser to the ministry, mentioned that the Japanese embassy had previously issued visas directly for Bangladeshi applicants, but halted the practice after a case of fake document submission was detected.

title: Division deepens in NCP
body: National Citizen Party senior joint member secretary Tasnim Jara resigned from the party on Saturday evening, bringing to the fore sharp and entrenched internal divisions over the party leadership’s push to forge an election-centric alliance with the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. Jara could not be reached by phone for comments. She, however, clarified her decision in a post on her verified Facebook account. Her party colleagues, including several joint conveners, confirmed the matter to New Age. ‘I was born and raised in Khilgaon. My dream has been to serve the people of my area and my country by going to Parliament from the platform of a political party,’ Jara, a physician by profession, wrote. ‘However, due to the current political realities, I have decided not to contest the election as a candidate of any specific party or alliance.’ She said. ‘I had promised you and the people of the country that I would fight for you and for creating a new political culture,’ she continued. ‘No matter the circumstances, I am determined to keep that promise. Therefore, I will be contesting as an independent candidate from Dhaka-9 in this election.’ Tasnim Jara had previously been nominated by the NCP to contest for the Dhaka-9 Jatiya Sangsad constituency in the next general elections slated to be held on February 12, 2026. Earlier, in the day, 32 NCP leaders submitted a memorandum to party convener Nahid Islam protesting against the NCP top leadership’s move to forge an election-centric alliance with the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. Nahid and party member secretary Akhtar Hossen did not respond to New Age phone calls made for comments. The memorandum said, ‘The basis of our objection lies in our party’s declared ideology, our historical responsibility in relation to the July uprising, and questions of democratic ethics.’ The document further alleges that the Jamaat and its student wing Islami Chhatra Shibir have engaged in divisive political activities, espionage, and sabotage within other parties. The Jamaat and Shibir attempted, it also alleged, to shift blame for various misdeeds to the NCP, rigged student union elections, and spread false narratives about student power since the July uprising. The signatories said that the Jamaat’s political history, particularly its role during the 1971 War of Independence and its stance on the genocide and other wartime crimes, was fundamentally incompatible with Bangladesh’s democratic values and the NCP’s core principles. ‘An alliance with the Jamaat would create confusion and disappointment among many of our activists and supporters, especially among the younger generation and ordinary citizens who support new politics,’ the memorandum said.

title: Dense fog disrupts communications
body: Road and air communications were disrupted on Saturday due to dense fog as eight Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport-bound flights were diverted and a bus-truck collision on the Dhaka-Mawa expressway left at least 10 people injured. Ferry services on the Aricha-Kazirhat route and the Paturia–Daulatdia route resumed after nearly 15 hours due to dense fog. HSIA officials said that one flight was diverted to the Bangkok airport, four to the Kolkata airport and three to the Shah Amanat International Airport in Chattogram. They said that the operations of the flights would resume once the weather became normal. They also said that airlines concerned arranged hotels and necessary foods for the passengers of the diverted flights. According to HSIA flight operations, Kuwait Airways flight KU283 was scheduled to reach the HSIA at about 1:00pm on December 26 and it was yet to be arrived. The flight was diverted to the Bangkok airport. HSIA officials, however, could not provide details of the flights diverted to Kolkata of West Bengal and Chattogram. Quoting Chattogram airport officials, New Age correspondent in Chattogram reported that a US Bangla Airlines’ Riyadh-Dhaka flight was diverted to the Chattogram airport and landed there at about 4:28am on Saturday. The flight departed for the HSIA from Chattogram at about 9:30am on the day. The officials also said that a Biman Bangladesh Airlines’ Dammam-Dhaka flight was diverted to the Chattogram airport and the flight landed at the airport at about 3:24am and left the airport at about 10:15am. New Age correspondent in Munshiganj reported that at least 10 people were injured as a passenger carrying bus hit a goods-laden truck from behind after losing control in the Chhanbari Bus Stand area on the Dhaka-Mawa expressway at about 1:00am on Saturday amid dense fog. Fire Service and Civil Defence Sreenagar station officer Dewan Azad said that 10 people were injured and two of them, including the bus driver, were now in critical condition. ‘We went to the spot immediately after hearing the news. We have recovered injured bus passengers from the spot and taken them to the Sreenagar Upazila Health Complex.’ Ferry services on the Paturia–Daulatdia and Aricha–Kazirhat river routes resumed on Saturday morning after remaining suspended for nearly 15 hours due to dense fog, the United News of Bangladesh reported. According to the Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation authorities, ferry movement on the Paturia–Daulatdia route was suspended at 7:15pm on Friday to avoid accidents amid poor visibility. Ferry operations resumed at about 10:00am on Saturday as visibility improved. Ferry services on the Aricha–Kazirhat route were also halted from 8:00pm on Friday as fog density increased, leaving more than 200 vehicles waiting at the Aricha and Kazirhat terminals. Due to the suspension on both routes, hundreds of vehicles including buses, private cars, microbuses and goods-laden trucks were stranded at four ferry terminals. As the night progressed, the number of waiting vehicles continued to rise, with more vehicles arriving at the terminals on Saturday morning. At Paturia Ghat, the queue of stranded vehicles stretched three to four kilometres from the terminal onto the highway. At least six people were killed and several others injured in two separate incidents of vessel collisions in the Meghna River in Chandpur and in the Buriganga River in Narayanganj in dense fog early Friday.

title: Applicants struggle to attend DU intake amid tailbacks
body: Many applicants for admissions to University of Dhaka struggled to reach examination centres on Saturday due to severe traffic congestion in the capital, caused by political and cultural programmes on major city roads. Witnesses said traffic congestions intensified following the movement of Tarique Rahman, acting chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, who visited the Dhaka University campus at about 11:20am to offer prayers at the grave of Sharif Osman Hadi, the slain convener of Inqilab Mancha, amid tight security. At about 11:52am, Tarique Rahman’s motorcade left the DU area via Shahbagh for the Election Commission office at Agargaon. Traffic for both vehicles and pedestrians was halted on both sides of the road from Shahbagh towards the DU campus during this time. Many applicants were seen running leaving their transports to reach the exam centres on the campus for the blockade at Shahbagh intersection. At Shahbagh, activists of Inqilab Mancha continued their blockade for the second consecutive day demanding justice for Hadi, further worsening the traffic situation. The congestion was compounded as three universities – University of Dhaka, Jagannath University, and the Military Institute of Science and Technology – held admission tests on the same day, the weekly holiday, at different times and locations. Applicants and their guardians said that as authorities fixed major admission test dates on the same day in the capital, thousands of students were forced to travel across the city amid insufficient public transport and widespread road congestion. The admission test for first-year undergraduate programmes under the Science Unit of Dhaka University for the 2025–26 academic year was held from 3:30pm to 5:00pm. According to a press release issued by the university’s public relations office, a total of 114,114 candidates applied for the test against 1,891 seats. Although the test began on time, many candidates were seen entering examination centres after the scheduled start, some arrived 10 to 15 minutes late. Considering the overall traffic situation, all latecomers were allowed to sit for the examination, Science Faculty dean Professor Abdus Salam told New Age. He said information on absentee numbers was not yet available, adding that overall attendance appeared similar to previous years despite the delays. Meanwhile, the admission test for the ‘C’ Unit, Faculty of Business Studies, of Jagannath University for the 2025–26 academic session was held from 11:00am to 12:00pm on Saturday. According to the university sources, 20,537 candidates applied for 520 seats in the ‘C’ Unit, resulting in nearly 40 applicants competing for each seat. Dean of the Faculty of Business Studies professor Dr Muhammad Manzoor Morshed Bhuiyan said the test was conducted at three centres in Dhaka, with no centres arranged outside the capital. The Military Institute of Science and Technology held its A unit admission test for engineering students from 10:00am to 1:00pm at multiple centres, mostly in the capital’s Mirpur area, guardians said.

title: Attorney General Asaduzzaman resigns to contest Bangladesh national polls
body: Attorney General Md Asaduzzaman resigned on Saturday to contest the upcoming 13th national election as a Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) candidate. He submitted his resignation to the president through the Attorney General’s Office. Earlier in the day was received a farewell hosted a farewell at the Supreme Court Judges’ Complex. Administrative officer Md Nasir Uddin confirmed the resignation and said it would be sent to the law ministry to this effect on Sunday. On December 18, Asaduzzaman was nominated by the BNP to contest from the Jhenaidah-1 (Shailkupa) constituency. He was appointed the 17th attorney general on August 8. He is also a BNP human affairs secretary. The post fell vacant after AM Amin Uddin resigned on August 7, 2024, citing personal difficulties, two days after former prime minister Sheikh Hasina stepped down and left the country amid the student movement over job quota reform. This was the first appointment of an attorney general made by the president after the departure of the prime minister and her cabinet. Asaduzzaman previously worked at the law firm Syed Istiaq Ahmed and Associates. In his resignation letter, he said he had been appointed attorney general on August 8, 2024, and that he was now unable to continue his duties for personal reasons.

title: Tasnim Jara quits NCP, decides to contest JS polls independently
body: National Citizen Party (NCP) senior joint member secretary, Tasnim Jara, resigned from her position on Saturday evening and announced that she would contest the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections as an independent candidate from the Dhaka-9 constituency. Jara, a physician by profession, could not be reached for immediate comment, but she clarified her decision in a post on her verified Facebook account. ‘I was born and raised in Khilgaon. My dream was to serve the people of my area and my country by going to Parliament from the platform of a political party,’ she wrote. ‘However, due to the current political realities, I have decided not to contest the election as a candidate of any specific party or alliance.’ She said. ‘I had promised you and the people of the country that I would fight for you and for creating a new political culture,’ she continued. ‘No matter the circumstances, I am determined to keep that promise. Therefore, I will be contesting as an independent candidate from Dhaka-9 in this election.’ Although she could not be reached directly, several of Jara's colleagues, including multiple joint conveners, confirmed her resignation and decision to New Age. Tasnim Jara had previously been nominated by the NCP to contest the Dhaka-9 constituency for the next general election scheduled to be held in February. Earlier on Saturday, 32 NCP leaders submitted a memorandum to party convener Nahid Islam, protesting at the party’s decision to forge a reform-centric alliance with Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami. Neither Nahid Islam, the NCP convener, nor Akhtar Hossen, the party’s member secretary, responded to New Age’s calls for comment. The memorandum expressed concerns over the NCP's alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami, stating that it conflicted with the party’s declared ideology, its historical stance regarding the July uprising, and its democratic ethics. The signatories also highlighted Jamaat’s controversial political history, particularly its role during Bangladesh's 1971 War of Independence, and its stance on genocide and other wartime crimes, which they argued was incompatible with Bangladesh's democratic values and the NCP's core principles. ‘An alliance with Jamaat would create confusion and disappointment among many of our activists and supporters, especially among the younger generation and ordinary citizens who support new politics,’ the memorandum concluded.

title: UDJFB gets new body
body: The Urban Development Journalist Forum, Bangladesh on Friday got a 14-member new executive body for the next two-year term 2026–27. The Daily Jugantor special correspondent Motin Abdullah was reelected as the president and the Daily Bangladesh Pratidin staff reporter Hasan Emon was elected as the general secretary of the organisation. The election of the committee took place followed by the biennial general meeting of the forum held at a restaurant in Banglamotor of Dhaka. Election commission headed by Amitosh Pal announced the names of the elected committee members. Other election commissioners were — Khalid Saifullah, senior reporter of the Daily Naya Diganta, and Mizanur Rahman, senior reporter of the Daily Observer. Other key office-bearers of the committee include Faisal Khan of the Desh Rupantor as vice-president, Easin Rana of ATN Bangla as joint general secretary, Rashidul Hasan of the Daily Sun as finance secretary, Zahidul Islam of The Business Standard as organising secretary, Md Billal Hossain (Sagar) of RTV as publicity and publication secretary, Latiful Islam of the Samakal as office secretary, Rahat Hossain of the Protidiner Bangladesh as training and research secretary, and Delawar Hossain Dolon of Channel 24 as hospitality and welfare secretary. Executive members include Mahmuda Dolly of the Amar Desh, Moinul Islam (Rajib) of Jamuna TV, Niaz Morshed of Desh TV, and Abdul Kaiyum of the Naya Diganta.

title: India seeks closer relationship with Bangladesh, stresses free, fair, inclusive polls
body: Highlighting the importance of stability and inclusive elections in Bangladesh, India has said it wants close and friendly relations with the people of Bangladesh, which is rooted in the liberation struggle and strengthened through various development and people-to-people initiatives. ‘We are in favour of peace and stability in Bangladesh and have consistently called for free, fair, inclusive and credible elections conducted in a peaceful atmosphere,’ Randhir Jaiswal, official spokesperson at the Ministry of External Affairs told reporters in New Delhi. Responding to a question during a weekly briefing on Friday, Jaiswal said they supported free, fair and inclusive elections in Bangladesh, and the return of BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman from London should be seen in that context. In response to another question, the MEA spokesperson said that their point on Bangladesh had been very clear and consistent all throughout. ‘India stands for strengthening our ties with the people of Bangladesh. We favor peace and stability in Bangladesh and also our point of view on elections, you are aware. We stand for free, fair, inclusive and participatory elections in Bangladesh, which is to be held in a peaceful atmosphere. So that is where we are. We stand for fair, free and inclusive and participatory elections in Bangladesh,’ he said. Regarding anti-India remarks, Jaiswal said that they had issued more than a couple of statements over the last few days and they have rejected the false narrative that has been projected in Bangladesh. ‘You would understand that the law and order or security situation or the developments that are happening in Bangladesh is the responsibility of the Government of Bangladesh. And to portray a narrative where things go in some other direction is completely false and we reject that,’ said the MEA Spokesperson. He said they are all aware of the recent developments in Bangladesh and have been closely following them. ‘And as far as the law and order situation is concerned, I have been apprising you from time to time as to what our position has been or should be and is today.’ Jaiswal said the ‘unremitting hostility’ against minorities in Bangladesh, including Hindus, Christians and Buddhists at the ‘hands of extremists’ is a matter of grave concern. ‘We condemn the recent gruesome killing of a Hindu youth in Mymensingh, and expect that the perpetrators of the crime would be brought to justice,’ he said. Earlier, Bangladesh rejected the attempt of the Indian authorities to depict an ‘isolated attack’ on a Bangladeshi citizen, who happens to belong to the Hindu community, as attacks on minorities. ‘The government of Bangladesh has promptly apprehended the suspects in this incident,’ said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in a statement. The inter-communal situation in Bangladesh is better than in many other parts in South Asia, said the MoFA. Over 2,900 incidents of violence against minorities, including cases of killings, arson, land grab have been documented by independent sources during the tenure of the interim government, said the MEA spokesperson. These incidents cannot be brushed aside as mere media exaggerations or dismissed as political violence, he said. On Myanmar, he said they stand for democratic transition in the country. ‘Elections are to be held. We support free, fair and inclusive development elections in which everybody participates. And India stands for peace and stability and return of normalcy in the country.’

title: Gono Odhikar’s Rashed joins BNP to contest national election
body: Gono Odhikar Parishad general secretary Rashed Khan on Saturday joined the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, leaving his party to contest the forthcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections with the BNP’s electoral symbol ‘Sheaf of Paddy’. Rashed joined the BNP at the party chairperson’s Gulshan office in the capital Dhaka by presenting a bouquet to BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. The JS elections and a referendum on reforms are scheduled to be held on February 12 next year. Under a seat-sharing arrangement among the allies of the simultaneous movement, the BNP has given the Jhenaidah-4 constituency to Rashed and the Patuakhali-3 constituency to Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque Nur. As per the Election Commission’s newly introduced rules, alliance candidates must contest the national election using their own party symbols. As a result, Rashed was initially supposed to contest with his party symbol ‘Truck’. After rumours spread on Friday evening that Rashed was joining the BNP, Nurul Haque clarified the party’s position in this regard in a Facebook post. He said, ‘As an electoral strategy decided by the party, Rashed Khan will contest from Jhenaidah-4 using the BNP’s symbol Sheaf of Paddy, and I will contest from Patuakhali-3 using my party symbol Truck.’ Under election rules, a candidate must resign from his party and secure nomination from another party to contest using its symbol. Following this provision, Rashed resigned from Gono Odhikar Parishad and joined the BNP. Welcoming him, Mirza Fakhrul said Rashed’s joining would strengthen the party. ‘Rashed has joined the BNP today (Saturday). I congratulate him. The BNP has decided to nominate him from Jhenaidah-4 with the Sheaf of Paddy symbol,’ he said, urging party leaders and activists to work together for Rashed’s victory. Rashed said that the BNP was fighting to establish the rights of the people. ‘Shaheed president Ziaur Rahman is my political ideal and that the party is now being led by Tarique Rahman,’ he said referring to the founder of the BNP and his son. Earlier, Liberal Democratic Party secretary general Redwan Ahmed joined the BNP and has been nominated for the Cumilla-7 constituency for contesting the national polls. Bangladesh Liberal Democratic Party chairman Shahadat Hossain Selim and Jatiya Dal chairman Syed Ehsanul Huda also joined the BNP to contest the polls. Selim will contest from Lakshmipur-1 and Ehsanul Huda from Kishoreganj-5 with the Sheaf of Paddy symbol.

title: Blast damages Keraniganj madrassah
body: The police in a drive on Saturday recovered bomb-making materials, crude bomb and liquid flammable chemicals at a location at South Keraniganj in Dhaka, a day after a bomb blast at a madrassah left four people, including a woman and two children, injured. The police filed a case under the Explosive Substances Act on Saturday and arrested three people in this connection, said South Keraniganj police station officer-in-charge Saiful Alam. The arrestees are Achhia,28, Yasmin Akter, 30, and Asmani Khatun, 34. The police official said that they had arrested Achhia first and then Achhia’s elder brother’s wife Yasmin from Bagherhat and Asmani from Basabo area in the Dhaka city. ‘The explosion occurred on Friday morning at Ummal Quran International Madrasa at Hasnabad. We have received information about the blast at about 10:00am on Friday,’ he said. He said that a team of South Keraniganj police went to the spot and found parts of two rooms and walls damaged due to the explosion. ‘We have admitted the injured woman and children to the Dhaka Medical College Hospital after recovering them,’ said the South Keraniganj police station OC. Crime Scene Unit of the Criminal Investigation Department, Anti-Terrorism Unit and others visited the spot, the OC added. According to the police, Al Amin, 32, from Bagerhat, now a fugitive, have been running this madrassah after renting two rooms since 2022 with 25-30 students. The police also said that Al-Amin was arrested in 2017 and 2020 and he was a fugitive accused in seven cases, including in Dhaka and surrounding areas. Arrested accused Asmani is also facing several cases. The United News of Bangladesh reports: Humayun Kabir, a resident of a nearby building, said that bricks fell on his head during the explosion, causing him to lose consciousness. He was later taken to a hospital by locals. Parveen Begum, the building owner, said that the madrassah was previously run by Mufti Harun, who handed over its management to Al Amin and his wife three years ago. ‘I used to keep in touch regularly, but had no idea what was happening in the guise of a madrassah,’ she said.

title: Dhaka’s air ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’ with AQI score of 120
body: Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked 21st on the list of cities with the worst air quality with an AQI score of 120 at about 09:00am on Saturday. On Saturday, Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’ referring to a health threat, according to the AQI index. Pakistan’s Lahore, India’s Delhi and Kolkata and Kuwait’s Kuwait City occupied the first four spots on the list, with AQI scores of 448, 410, 221 and 176, respectively. An AQI score between 50 and 100 is considered ‘moderate’ with acceptable air quality usually sensitive individuals should consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion, between 101 and 150, air quality is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, between 150 and 200 is ‘unhealthy’, between 201 and 300 is said to be ‘very unhealthy’, while a reading of 301 and above is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks to residents. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon. As per the World Health Organisation, air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, mainly due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: Tarique completes voter registration
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairTarique Rahman and his daughter Zaima Rahman completed their voter registration on Saturday, with the Election Commission set to make a final decision on their inclusion in the voter list today. Tarique arrived at the Election Commission office at Agargaon, Dhaka, at around 1:00pm and completed his registration as a resident of Dhaka North City Corporation Ward 19, which falls under the Dhaka-17 Jatiya Sangsad constituency. The procedure included the submission of biometric information, such as fingerprints and iris scans. He had earlier applied for the registration through the EC’s online system. Election Commission officials said that Tarique was expected to receive his National Identity Card within five to 24 hours after the completion of the biometric process. Election Commission senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed told reporters that both Tarique Rahman and Zaima Rahman had submitted Form 2, along with their photographs and biometric data, as part of the registration process. The information would undergo internal verification, including the matching of the fingerprints, signatures, and facial identity, before the issuance of an NID number, he said. The EC had earlier reiterated that only individuals who turned 18 and completed voter registration by October 31 were eligible for the inclusion in the voter list for the February 12, 2026 national elections. But the EC secretary on Saturday said that the Election Commission was empowered to enrol any eligible adult as voter under Section 15 of the Voter List Act 2009. While the initial registration formalities have been completed, he said, the final inclusion in the voter list is subject to approval by the commission, which may be granted either through a formal meeting or via an official file-based process. The applications are scheduled to be placed before the commission on Sunday, the EC secretary further said. The voter list inclusion, he also said, is a continuing process linked to preparations for the national election scheduled for 12 February. NID director general ASM Humayun Kabir told reporters that once biometric data collection was completed, the system automatically cross-checked the information with the central server to ensure that there was no duplication. ‘If there is no duplication, an NID number is generated within 5 to 24 hours. This process is fully automated and not controlled manually,’ he also said. Humayun said that Tarique would be able to collect his NID or smart card directly from the authorities, while a confirmation SMS would also be sent to his mobile phone, enabling him to access the information digitally. Tarique Rahman returned to Bangladesh on December 25, ending 17 years of exile in the United Kingdom. The BNP has already announced party candidates in most parliamentary constituencies and accordingly Tarique Rahman would contest as a paddy sheaf candidate for his ancestral seat of Bogura-6. Local leaders have already collected nomination papers on his behalf. Tarique Rahman had previously been sentenced in several cases, including to a life-term imprisonment, and faced numerous other charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail on September 3, 2008, after which he had travelled to London on September 11 for medical treatment and had remained there. Following the end of the Awami League’s 16-year rule on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising, the High Court acquitted Tarique of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, clearing the legal hurdles to his return.

title: Three of same family killed in Faridpur road accident
body: Three members of a family, including a patient, were killed and two others wereinjured when a truck hit an ambulance on Bhanga-Khulna highway at Mansurabad in Bhanga upazila of Faridpur district on Saturday. The deceased were identified as patient Mizanur Rahman, 40, son of Babor Ali of Jashore district, his wife Rukaiya Akter Nila, 32, and Rukaiya’s brother Sakibur Rahman Nishan, 27, son of Rahmatullah. The accident took place at about 7:30am when the Khulna-bound truck crashed into the Dhaka-bound ambulance from Jashore, leaving the three dead on the spot and two others injured, said Helal Uddin, officer-in-charge of Bhanga Highway Police. The injured were taken to Bhanga Upazila Health Complex from where doctors referred two of them to Faridpur Medical College and Hospital for better treatment. Mizanur had suffered a stroke a few days ago and met the accident while going to Dhaka for treatment.

title: Ferry services resume on different routes after 15 hours
body: Ferry services on Paturia–Daulatdia and Aricha–Kazirhat river routes resumed on Saturday morning after remaining suspended for nearly 15 hours due to dense fog. According to Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Corporation authorities, ferry movement on the Paturia–Daulatdia route was suspended at about 7:15pm on Friday to avoid accidents caused by poor visibility. Ferry operations resumed at about 10:00am on Saturday as visibility improved. During the suspension, three ferries — Shah Makhdum, Barkat and Enayetpuri — remained stranded mid-river with passengers and vehicles on board, causing severe hardship to commuters and transport workers. Ferry services on the Aricha–Kazirhat route were also halted from 8:00pm on Friday as fog density increased, leaving more than 200 vehicles waiting at the Aricha and Kazirhat terminals. Due to the suspension on both routes, hundreds of vehicles including buses, night coaches, private cars, microbuses and goods-laden trucks were stranded at four ferry terminals. As the night progressed, the number of waiting vehicles continued to rise, with more vehicles arriving at the terminals on Saturday morning. At Paturia Ghat, the queue of stranded vehicles stretched three to four kilometres from the terminal onto the highway. Aricha Sector BIWTC deputy general manager Abdus Salam said that the long suspension led to a significant backlog of vehicles at the terminals. ‘Considering passenger inconvenience, buses, private cars and microbuses are being given priority in ferry crossings and the goods-laden trucks will be ferried gradually,’ he said.

title: Dense fog disrupts flight operations at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport
body: Several international flights could not land at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Saturday morning due to dense fog, airport sources said. The flights were diverted to Chattogram, Kolkata and Bangkok as visibility dropped sharply over the capital, Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh officials said. They said flight operations will resume as normal once weather condition improves. Airlines concerned were providing meals and hotel facilities to passengers of delayed flights as required, it added. Severe cold weather has gripped Dhaka and other parts of the country, disrupting normal life. Dense fog and cold winds have added to the hardship especially during the morning hours. The Met office forecast dry weather with partly cloudy sky across the country. It also said moderate to dense fog may occur in different areas from midnight to morning and in some places, may continue until noon.

title: Tarique offers prayers at graves of Osman Hadi, Kazi Nazrul
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Saturday visited the graves of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi and National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam on the Dhaka University campus and offered prayers at their graves. Tarique also visited the graves of his younger brother Arafat Rahman Koko, his father-in-law Mahbub Ali and the army officers who were killed in the Pilkhana massacre in 2009 and offered prayers there. Earlier, on December 25, Tarique returned to the country after ending 17 years of forced exile in the United Kingdom, receiving a roaring welcome from more than a million people. On Saturday, Tarique along with party senior leaders, including secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, and Dhaka university vice-chancellor professor Niaz Ahmed Khan offered prayers at the grave of Sharif Osman Hadi at about 11:30am, near the Dhaka University Central Mosque. Osman Hadi was shot in the head on December 12 in Paltan area in the capital Dhaka. He was airlifted to Singapore for advanced treatment, where he died on the night of December 18. After visiting Hadi’s grave, Tarique also prayed at the grave of National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, located in the same area. Tarique left his Gulshan Avenue residence and arrived at the Dhaka University campus at about 11:15am under tight security. Ahead of Tarique’s arrival, leaders and activists of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, the student wing of the BNP, lined both sides of the road in front of the DU’s Faculty of Fine Arts, chanting slogans to welcome Tarique.
