title: Delhi summons Bangladesh envoy
body: India on Tuesday summoned Bangladesh high commissioner Riaz Hamidullah amid growing tensions between Dhaka and Delhi. This development came hours after the Bangladesh foreign affairs ministry summoned his Indian counterpart, Pranay Verma, to express Dhaka’s ‘grave concern’ over a series of incidents in India targeting Bangladeshi diplomatic missions. This is the second time the envoys to India and Bangladesh were summoned amid tense ties between the two countries following violent anti-India protests in several parts of Bangladesh. Meanwhile, India deployed 15,000 security forces in front of the Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi.

title: ​NCP supports restoring political rights of ordinary AL supporters, says Nahid
body: The National Citizen Party convener, Nahid Islam, on Tuesday said his party supports restoring the civic and political rights of ordinary supporters of Awami League. ‘Those who support a fascist party may have committed a moral crime, but if they were not involved in mass killings during the July Uprising. NCP wants their civic and political rights to be restored,’ Nahid said while speaking at the ‘Star Election Dialogue: Your Party, Voters’ Questions’ at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital. He said BNP and Jamaat are competing to secure Awami League votes, with members of the ousted party openly joining them, but there has been no solution on the Awami League issue yet. ‘If the Awami League problem is not resolved, it will continue to resurface. In that case, a “Truth and Reconciliation Commission” should be formed, and the political and civic rights of Awami League supporters should be restored on the condition that they seek forgiveness,’ Nahid said. Calling for the dissolution of the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB), Nahid said, ‘RAB must be dissolved. We have been demanding its dissolution from the very beginning. Alongside abolishing RAB, institutions like the DGFI must also be brought under accountability.’ On the upcoming election, he said, many are viewing it solely as a national election, but the referendum must also be kept in mind, stressing that the July Uprising must not be compromised under any circumstances. Referring to the implementation of the July Charter, Nahid said, ‘We were forced to make compromises in many parts of the charter. Many things had to be accepted in light of reality. But the commitment to uphold the charter that has been formulated cannot be violated.’

title: TARIQUE RETURN: Railway to run special trains, HSIA prohibits visitor entry from evening
body: Bangladesh Railway is scheduled to start running special trains from today to carry Bangladesh Nationalist Party leaders and activists on the occasion of the party’s leader Tarique Rahman’s homecoming tomorrow. Also, Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport authorities prohibited all visitors except designated passengers from entering its area for 24 hours starting from 6:00pm today citing special operational and security reasons. Biman Bangladesh Airlines authorities in a press also also requested the airport-bound passengers to start from their homes with enough time in hand tomorrow. Dhaka Metropolitan Police is also preparing a traffic management schedule for the city roads tomorrow, anticipating extreme pressure on the city roads tomorrow. The moves come as BNP acting chairperson Tarique Rahman is scheduled to return to Dhaka tomorrow after over 17 years of stay in the United Kingdom. The railway already has cancelled the scheduled journeys of three regular trains—Rajbari Commuter on Rajbari-Poradah, Dhalar Char Express on Pabna-Rajshahi and Rohonpur Commuter on Rohonpur-Rajshahi routes—tomorrow as it would use 10 special trains to carry the party leaders and activists between today and tomorrow. The special trains will run on Cox’s Bazar-Dhaka-Cox’s Bazar, Jamalpur-Mymensingh-Dhaka- Jamalpur, Tangail-Dhaka-Tangail, Bhairab Bazar-Narsingdi-Dhaka-Narsingdi-Bhairab Bazar, Joydebpur-DhakaCantonment-Joydebpur (Gazipur), Panchagarh-Dhaka-Panchagarh, Khulna-Dhaka-Khulna, Chatmohor- Dhaka Cantonment-Chatmohor, Rajshahi-Dhaka-Rajshahi, and Jashore-Dhaka-Jashore. Today special trains will start from Chattogram, Panchagarh, Chatmohor and Rajshahi to the capital, according to the railway officials. A press release, issued on Tuesday and signed by the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport executive director Group Captain SM Ragib Samad, read that entry of all visitors would be prohibited between 6:00am Wednesday and 6:00pm Thursday. The Biman press release, citing different media reports, said that since there was a possibility of a large gathering in the airport area, the roads from the airport to Gulshan and Purbachal Expressway (300 feet road) on December 25, airport-bound passengers were requested to leave their homes with enough time in hand. Meanwhile DMP senior system analyst (traffic) Md Nurus Samad said on Tuesday that their Uttara traffic division was preparing a road plan for tomorrow. Diversion would be given on different roads in Uttara, airport and adjacent areas, he added.

title: Protests at RMG worker lynching continue
body: Protests continued in the capital Dhaka on Tuesday, demanding justice for the brutal killing of readymade garment worker Dipu Chandra Das at Bhaluka in Mymensingh. The interim government’s education adviser and an 18-member delegation of human rights activists separately visited the victim’s family to express condolences and assure support on the day. Different organisations held protest programmes in the capital, condemning the killing and urging the interim government to ensure public safety and bring the perpetrators to justice. The Minority Oikya Morcha, led by leaders of the Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council, staged a rally in front of the National Press Club in the capital. Speakers at the rally called on the interim government to take immediate steps to ensure the safety and security of people across the country. BHBCUC president Nirmal Rozario, who chaired the rally, strongly condemned the killing of Dipu Chandra Das and demanded the arrest and exemplary punishment of those responsible. The rally was followed by a protest procession that paraded several city roads. Meanwhile, leaders of several garment worker rights bodies at a press conference at the Communist Party of Bangladesh central office in the capital also demanded swift arrest and punishment of the killers. Garment labour leader and Garments Sramik Oikya Forum president Mushrefa Mishu called on the interim government to take immediate action, warning that tougher movements would be launched if the killers were not brought to justice promptly. Garment worker leaders Montu Ghosh, Harun Ur Rashid, Joly Talukder and Shabnam Hafiz, among others, were present at the press conference. At the same time, the Chief Adviser’s Office expressed profound sorrow over the killing and extended condolences to Dipu’s family. On behalf of the government, education adviser Professor CR Abrar visited the bereaved family in Mymensingh to convey sympathy and assure state support. During the visit, Abrar talked to Dipu’s father, Rabilal Das, and other family members. He said the killing was a heinous criminal act with no justification and no place in Bangladeshi society. Allegations, rumours or differences of belief can never excuse violence, and no one has the right to take law in their own hands, he said. Reaffirming the interim government’s commitment to the rule of law, Abrar assured the family that all allegations would be investigated and justice ensured through due process. Abrar also confirmed that financial and welfare assistance would be provided to the family and that the relevant authorities would remain in close contact with them in the coming days. Separately, an 18-member delegation of human rights activists visited Dipu’s home at Mokamiyakanda village at Tarakanda upazila to express condolences and demand justice from the state and the government, New Age correspondent in the district reported. Members of the delegation talked to Dipu’s wife, Meghna Rani, and inquired about the family’s overall condition, including their financial situation. Speaking to journalists, human rights activist and photographer Md Shahidul Alam said that the delegation was outraged and deeply saddened. He said that Dipu was killed on the basis of an unverified allegation and that his body was subsequently burned and dishonoured, calling the incident extremely painful. He said that the delegation sought not only justice in this case but also effective measures to prevent such incidents from recurring, so that a truly discrimination-free Bangladesh could be ensured. He added that the state bore responsibility for the maintenance of Dipu’s family and children, while the delegation would stand by the family in any need. The delegation also included Nagorik Uddyog chief executive Zakir Hossain, Nari Mukti Kendra president Seema Dutta, writer and former constitution reform commission member Firoz Ahmed, human rights activist Dipayan Khisa, and writer and anthropologist Rehnuma Ahmed, among others. Representatives of the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust and the Human Rights Cultural Foundation were also present. Earlier, on the night of December 18, Dipu Chandra Das who had been working at Pioneer Knitwears BD Limited was beaten to death by a mob following allegations of religious desecration. His body was later hung from a tree and set on fire. On December 19, victim’s younger brother Apu Das filed a case with the Bhaluka police station against 150 unnamed people. The police and the Rapid Action Battalion have so far arrested 12 accused, and a court has granted three days’ remand for each.

title: UN special rapporteur calls for justice against mob attacks
body: United Nations Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression Irene Khan on Tuesday said that the violent mob attacks on media outlets and cultural institutions in Bangladesh were deeply alarming and must be promptly and effectively investigated, with perpetrators brought to justice without delay. In a statement to the media, she condemned the attacks on the night of December 18, when hundreds of people vandalised media houses at Karwan Bazar in Dhaka and targeted cultural institutions following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi and one of the organisers of the July uprising. Hadi was shot in the head in Dhaka on December 12 and later died while undergoing treatment at a hospital in Singapore. ‘I strongly condemn the targeted killing of an inspiring leader as well as the orchestrated mob violence against independent journalists and artists which followed the announcement of his death,’ Irene Khan said. She specifically denounced the attacks on The Daily Star and Prothom Alo as well as the assault on Chhayanaut and the harassment of Nurul Kabir, president of the Editors’ Council and editor of New Age. ‘The weaponisation of public anger against journalists and artists is dangerous at any time, and especially now as the country prepares for elections,’ Irene Khan warned. She said that such violence could have a chilling effect on media freedom, minority voices, and dissenting opinions, with serious consequences for democracy. According to the UN rapporteur, the mob violence did not occur in isolation but reflected a broader failure of the interim government to address impunity and protect media and artistic freedom. Over the past year, freedom of expression — particularly media freedom — has come under intense pressure from both state and non-state actors, online and offline. Since August 5, 2024, she said, hundreds of journalists have reportedly been arrested on politically motivated and dubious charges, including murder and terrorism, with many subjected to prolonged arbitrary detention. Several journalists have also been killed, the most recent case occurring last week, she observed. She said that repeated attacks, threats, and smear campaigns against journalists, artists, cultural organisations and women’s groups — when left unaddressed by authorities and social media platforms — inevitably translate into violence. The Bangladeshi British lawyer and human rights activist urged the government to investigate both the killing of Hadi and the attacks on media outlets promptly, impartially and transparently, ensuring full due process. ‘If the interim government is to deliver safe and fair elections, it must uphold freedom of expression and peaceful assembly and ensure that journalists, civil society actors, political candidates, women, and minorities can exercise their rights without fear of reprisals,’ Irene Khan commented.

title: Five killed in clash over possession of char land
body: At least five people were killed and 10 others were injured on Tuesday as two groups of people exchanged fire during a clash over the possession of the land of Janglar char, a newly emerged char under Hatiya upazila in Noakhali district. The police said that they, until 8:00pm on Tuesday, could identify three of the deceased. They are Alauddin, Samsuddin, and his son Mobarak. The identities of two other deceased could not be known until the time, they said. They said that the incident occurred at about 10:00am in the char along the border of Wards 7 and 8 of Sukchar union. Local people said that several hundred landless families currently live on Janglar Char, as nearly half of it is owned by the government, while the rest is controlled by a private group. For years, an armed group allegedly led by Farid Member, also known as Farid Commander of Hironni union, and former chairman Md Mushfiq, had been controlling the char and its newly formed land. The group reportedly sold lands on the char to landless people in exchange of Tk 20,000 to Tk 30,000 per acre, they said. On Tuesday morning, an armed group of 30 to 40 people, led by Alauddin, Kamal, and Nizam Member, attempted to take possession of the char. Sensing the move, supporters of Farid and Mushfiq, armed with firearms, attacked their rivals, leaving four dead on the spot and several others injured, they said. They said that Samsuddin, his son Mobarak, and two others from Farid and Mushfiq’s group were found dead at the scene. Of the injured, Alauddin was rushed to Noakhali General Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Local people said that tension had been prevailing in the area following the incident. Hatiya police station officer-in-charge Md Saiful Alam said that members of the police, the Coast Guard and the Navy were deployed in the area to prevent any further untoward incident. He said that the police were trying to identify the other victims. No case was filed, and none was arrested so far in this connection until 8:00pm on Tuesday, he said.

title: Training for temple-based edn managers begins in city
body: The religious affairs ministry has organised a five-day training programme titled ‘Special Training for Project Managers/Executives’ that began at the National Academy for Planning and Development on Saturday. The Hindu Religious Welfare Trust is conducting the programme under the ‘Temple-Based Child and Mass Education Programme (6th phase)’ project. Officials from the Ministry of Religious Affairs, Planning Commission, Implementation Monitoring and Evaluation Division (IMED), Finance Division, the Hindu Religious Welfare Trust and relevant project offices are taking part in the training. Senior secretary Siddiq Zubayer, director general of the National Academy for Planning and Development, inaugurated the programme as chief guest. The event was presided over by joint secretary Sayma Afroz, additional director general of the National Academy for Planning and Development.

title: Govt offers rewards for submitting photos of waste burning
body: The government on Tuesday announced rewards for submitting photos of waste burning, a source of air pollution, as an initiative to protect the environment. The photos will help the government collect precise information on locations of waste burning. As part of its efforts to check air pollution, the government has made a decision to take firm action against waste burning. A press release issued by the environment, forest and climate change ministry on the day said that the government was requesting all citizens of Bangladesh to submit photographs of waste burning incidents. ‘If such incidents are observed, relevant photographs may be sent to [email protected]. Each submission must include the name of the photographer or sender, mobile phone number, the exact location and address, and the time of the incident,’ it said. The release also said that each month the best 10 photographs would be selected from the submissions after verification, and appropriate rewards would be awarded to the selected contributors. The government expects that active public participation in this initiative will play a significant role in controlling air pollution, the release also said. According to the ministry, air pollution has emerged as a serious threat to public health in Bangladesh. Emissions from vehicles, brick kilns, industrial facilities and the burning of waste are steadily deteriorating air quality across the country. As a result, health risks, including respiratory illness, are increasing, posing particular danger to children, the elderly, and people with existing health conditions. To address this challenge, the press release said, the government has undertaken strong measures to identify and control the sources of air pollution.

title: Biman requests airport-bound passengers to leave houses with enough time on Thursday
body: Biman Bangladesh Airlines authorities on Tuesday recommended the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport-bound passengers should leave their houses for airport with enough time on Thursday. A press release issued by the Biman on Tuesday read that according to different media reports, on December 25, there is a possibility of a large gathering in the airport area, the roads from the airport to Gulshan, and the Purbachal Expressway (300 feet road). As a result, huge traffic gridlock might take place in the areas, it continued. Following this, Biman requests all airport-bound passengers to leave their houses with enough time. BNP acting chairperson Tarique Rahman is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka on December 25 after over 17 years of stay in the United Kingdom.

title: Bangladesh-India ties under further strain
body: Several hundreds of Hindu protesters on Tuesday demonstrated before the Bangladesh missions in New Delhi, Kolkata, and Agartala along with other places in India hours after the Bangladesh foreign ministry in the morning summoned the Indian high commissioner amid escalating tension in bilateral relations over a series of recent incidents. Holding saffron flags and shouting slogans against the lynching of a Hindu youth in Bangladesh, hundreds of supporters of the Vishva Hindu Parishad and the Bajrang Dal broke barricades and clashed with police near the fortified Bangladesh high commission in Delhi on Tuesday, Indian newspaper The Hindu reported in the afternoon. Protesters forced several barricades down as police struggled to contain the surge protesting at the lynching of a Hindu man in Bangladesh, according to the reports available online. The protesters raised slogans and held banners against the Bangladesh government. ‘Hindu rakt ki ek ek boond ka hisaab chahiye (You must be held accountable for each drop of blood of a Hindu),’ a placard read as reported by the local media. Meanwhile, foreign secretary Asad Alam Siam conveyed Bangladesh’s grave concern to India summoning the Indian envoy, Pranay Verma, at the ministry at around 10:00am over incidents outside the Bangladesh high commission and diplomatic residences in New Delhi on December 20. Concerns were also expressed over the acts of vandalism at the Bangladesh Visa Centre in Siliguri on 22 December, the ministry officials confirmed. Amid growing tensions between Dhaka and Delhi, India on Tuesday, too, summoned Bangladesh high commissioner Riaz Hamidullah, which the United News of Bangladesh reported in the evening. This is the second time the envoys to India and Bangladesh were summoned amid the tensions between the two countries following a series of incidents in the two neighbouring countries. ‘The foreign affairs ministry summoned the Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma today to convey the Bangladesh government’s grave concern to the Government of India over the regrettable incidents outside the perimeter of the Bangladesh High Commission and residence in New Delhi on December 20 and the acts of vandalism at the Bangladesh Visa Centre in Siliguri on December 22 by different extremist elements,’ said foreign ministry spokesperson and public diplomacy wing director general SM Mahbubul Alam at a media briefing at the ministry, reading out a written statement. He said that the visa services at Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi, Assistant high commission in Agartala and the visa centre in Siliguri of West Bengal remained suspended over security concerns. ‘Visa services would resume soon after the situation becomes normal,’ the official added, responding to a question. The foreign ministry statement said that Bangladesh condemned such acts of premeditated violence or intimidation against diplomatic establishments, which not only endangered the safety of diplomatic personnel but also undermined the principles of mutual respect and values of peace and tolerance. The government of Bangladesh called upon the government of India to conduct a thorough investigation into the incidents, to take all necessary measures to prevent the recurrence of such acts and to ensure safety and security of Bangladesh’s diplomatic missions and related facilities in India. Bangladesh expects India to immediately take appropriate steps in accordance with its international and diplomatic obligations to safeguard the dignity and security of diplomatic personnel and establishments, according to the statement. A sea of banners and placards bobbed in the air, reading denunciatory messages against the Bangladesh government, The Hindu reported from New Delhi. The area had been secured with three layers of barricading and more force from the police and paramilitary forces, the report mentioned. On December 18, Dipu Chandra Das, a 25-year-old garment factory worker, was lynched by a mob and his body was set afire over alleged blasphemy in Mymensingh. Protesters in Dhaka and some other divisions also held anti-India protests near Indian missions recently following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, a critic of the ‘Indian hegemony’, from bullet injuries. Massive protests were also held in Jammu and Kashmir to protest the violence against Hindus in Bangladesh, NDTV reported. Hundreds of protesters tried to march to the Bangladesh deputy high commission office in Kolkata, shouting slogans against alleged violence on minority Hindus in the neighbouring country. The protest march titled ‘Hindu Hunkar Padayatra’ was organised under the banner of ‘Bangiya Hindu Jagaran’. The march started from Sealdah and was proceeding towards the Bangladesh deputy high commission office when it was stopped by the police in the Beckbagan area of Kolkata. A huge police force was deployed near the Bangladesh deputy high commission office. The protesters raised slogans ‘Hindu Hindu Bhai Bhai’, ‘safety for Hindus in Bangladesh’ and over the lynching of the Hindu youth in Bangladesh. The Bangladesh assistant high commission in Tripura capital Agartala has suspended all visa and consular services since Tuesday for an indefinite period due to ‘unavoidable circumstances’. A series of incidents in the recent time dampened the bilateral relations between the two nations already strained since the interim government of Professor Muhammad Yunus took over following the July uprising that forced the fall of Sheikh Hasina on August 5, 2024. Hasina fled to India on the day and has been staying there since. The Indian Visa Application Centre in Bangladesh capital Dhaka was closed for hours from 2:00pm on December 17 amid a march towards the Indian high commission, which the police intercepted on its way to the high commission. The Indian assistant high commission in Chattogram has also suspended its visa services for an indefinite period since Sunday, citing security concerns. Around 20–25 activists held demonstrations near the Bangladesh mission in Delhi on December 20, chanting anti-Bangladesh slogans. Bangladesh foreign adviser Md Touhid Hossain on Sunday said that ‘normal security’ was not maintained at the Bangladesh mission in India while the high commissioner, who was staying there with his family, felt threatened. Rejecting India’s press statement on Saturday’s demonstration before the Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi, he said that Bangladesh would rely on the host country for the security and expected that the incident in Delhi would not be repeated in the future. About the lynching of the youth in Mymensingh, the Bangladesh foreign adviser said that the murder of an individual was not an issue of minority and it might happen anywhere. The victim was a Bangladeshi citizen and the important thing was that prompt actions were under way in the case, he mentioned. The government of Bangladesh has promptly apprehended the suspects in this incident, the foreign ministry release said. In early December, 2024, a group of Indian protesters launched an attack on the Bangladesh mission in Tripura capital Agartala forcing authorities to shut it temporarily.

title: ICT charges Hasina, 11 army officers, 5 others
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Tuesday framed crimes against humanity charges against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan, her former defence adviser retired major general Tarique Siddique, 11 army officers and three senior police officers. The three-judge tribunal chaired by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder framed charges against the 17 accused who bore superior command responsibility for enforced disappearances carried out through abduction, detention and torture at the Task Force for Interrogation cell at the Rapid Action Battalion headquarters in Dhaka during the ousted Awami League regime between January 2009 and August 2024. Asked by the tribunal whether they were guilty or not, all 10 detained army officers pleaded ‘not guilty’. Seven other accused, including Hasina, Asaduzzaman, Tarique, a retired army officer and three former senior police officers, are still in hiding and will be tried in absentia. The tribunal fixed January 21 for the commencement of their trial through opening statements by the prosecution and recording prosecution witnesses’ depositions. The tribunal on the day cautioned chief prosecutor Tajul Islam for repeatedly interrupting the proceedings, saying the tribunal was not obliged to hear him at that stage. The judges said that they expected restrained and professional conduct from Tajul. The detained army officers are Colonel KM Azad, Colonel Abdullah Al Momen, Brigadier General Md Mahbub Alam, Lieutenant Colonel Anwar Latif Khan, Brigadier General Md Jahangir Alam, Lieutenant Colonel Sarwar Bin Kashem, Lieutenant Colonel Saiful Islam Suman, Brigadier General Tofayel Mostafa Sarwar, Brigadier General Kamrul Hassan and Lieutenant Colonel Moshiur Rahman Jewel. Lawyer ABM Hamidul Mishnah appeared for three detained army officers, namely Tofayel, Kamrul and Moshiur, while lawyer Tabarak Hossain appeared for seven other detained army officers. Besides Hasina, Asaduzzaman and Tarique, the other absconding accused are retired lieutenant colonel Muhammad Khairul Islam, a former RAB intelligence chief now believed to be living in the United Kingdom, and three former police officers - Benazir Ahmed, a former inspector general of police, Khurshid Hossain and barrister Harun-or-Rashid, all former RAB director generals during the Awami League regime. On December 3, the tribunal began hearing the case against the 17 accused for the enforced disappearance of 11 victims at RAB-1 secret detention cell, popularly known as TFI cell. The 11 victims include Supreme Court lawyer and executed war crimes convict Mir Quasem Ali’s son Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem Arman, Tajul Islam Suman, physician Ashik Ul Akbar, Mahmudul Hasan, Nur-e-Alam, Md Shariatullah, Md Rajibul Islam, Saiful Islam, Rizwanul Mahmud Anik, Md Foyez and Masrur Anwar Chowdhury, according to the charges. According to the charges regarding the detention and torture in TFI cell, 14 of the accused, acting under the authority of the then prime minister, her security adviser and the home minister, ordered the abduction, detention and torture of 11 Awami League dissidents through their subordinate officers. Defence lawyer Tabarak Hossain told the tribunal that he had planned to file a review petition against the charge-framing order. The tribunal heard sharp exchanges on a defence request for additional time to prepare for trial. Tabarak sought three months, citing the volume of documents and 29 prosecution witnesses but the tribunal noted that the defence had already received the papers on November 25 and that the law allows only 21 days for preparation. Chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam opposed the request, arguing that the defence was attempting to delay proceedings in a case that must be tried speedily under a special law. Tribunal member Justice Md Shofiul Alam Mahmood intervened repeatedly, asking both sides to maintain courtroom decorum and clarifying that the defence must be heard before the prosecution. The tribunal told defence counsel that the defence had already received one month since November 25 for preparations, and that the additional four weeks granted would make it nearly two months in total. The tribunal noted that the law allows only 21 days for preparation. Tabarak argued that ensuring a fair trial required giving the defence adequate time. Tajul Islam strongly opposed the request, saying that the tribunal could not grant time without hearing the prosecution. During the exchange, tribunal member Justice Shofiul Alam Mahmood asked Tajul to maintain decorum, saying that he was speaking with excessive passion. Tajul argued that the defence intended to file a review petition and that the tribunal should not remain idle while waiting for such a filing. He requested the tribunal to sign the charge-framing order immediately so that the defence could file the review the following day. The judge responded that the tribunal had not yet formed any opinion on granting time and questioned why the prosecutor repeatedly interrupted the defence during submissions. The judge said that the defence must be heard first. Tajul insisted that time could not be granted without hearing him and urged the tribunal to consider the suffering of victims of enforced disappearance. He said that the case was being tried under a special law and must proceed speedily, alleging that the defence was trying to delay the trial. When Tajul referred to past practices of the tribunal, the chairman said that those issues were grievances of the past and would not be repeated. He added that the tribunal would not adopt a rigid approach. The tribunal chairman also said that no adjournments would be allowed after beginning the trial. Tajul further told the tribunal that prosecution witnesses had received death threats and added that justice should not be delayed. Responding to defence claims that the tribunal was trying the army as an institution, Tajul said the case concerned individual officers for alleged crimes committed while serving at DGFI and the RAB. During Tajul’s submission, Tabarak stood up, prompting Tajul to ask him to sit down. Tabarak later complained to the tribunal, urging it to maintain courtroom decorum and stating that the prosecution should not speak to him in a rude manner. Tajul also criticised Hasan Imam, a tribunal-appointed state defence lawyer for the fugitive accused, when he sought additional time. Tajul said that as a state-appointed lawyer, Imam should assist the tribunal rather than seek delays. At the end of the hearing, the tribunal chairman urged both the defence and the prosecution to refrain from such conduct in the future and to maintain discipline in court. On December 18, the same tribunal framed charges against Hasina, Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and 11 other serving and retired army officials for their alleged involvement in committing crimes against humanity, including abduction, detention and torture of 26 people with dissenting views against the Awami League.

title: BNP cedes 4 seats to Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam
body: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party allotted four Jatiya Sangsad constituencies to the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh as part of an electoral understanding ahead of the 13th JS elections. As a result of the agreement, BNP electoral symbol ‘sheaf of paddy’ will not be used in these constituencies. Instead, voters were urged to cast their votes for the candidates contesting with the ‘date palm tree’ symbol. BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir made the announcement at a press conference on Tuesday at the party chair’s political office at Gulshan in the capital. He confirmed that the BNP would not field any candidate in the constituencies ceded to the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh. The seats ceded under the arrangement are Nilphamari-1, Narayanganj-4, Sylhet-5, and Brahmanbaria-2. According to the announcement, Jamiat president Ubaidullah Farooq will contest for Sylhet-5, while the party’s secretary general Manjurul Islam Afendi will vie for Nilphamari-1. Vice-president Junayed Al Habib was nominated for Brahmanbaria-2, while joint secretary general Monir Hossain Kasemi will contest for Narayanganj-4. Mirza Fakhrul reiterated that in all constituencies where the Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam Bangladesh candidates would contest under this agreement, the BNP would refrain from nominating its own candidates. Earlier, the BNP announced its candidates for 272 out of the 300 JS seats across the country in two phases. The party has been continuing negotiations with its movement partners over seat sharing and Fakhrul said that the details of the seat-sharing arrangements with other parties would be announced shortly.

title: VOTER SAFETY, COMMUNAL HARMONY: CEC orders strict steps
body: Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin instructed the field-level administrations to accord the highest priority to maintaining communal harmony in order to ensure a peaceful and inclusive election environment. The CEC was speaking at a meeting with divisional commissioners, metropolitan police commissioners, deputy commissioners and superintendents of police at the Election Commission headquarters in the capital on Tuesday. The CEC said that special emphasis must be placed on reassuring the minority communities — who often felt vulnerable during election periods — so that their safety and dignity would remain fully protected. Referring to a recent incident involving the burning of the body of a Hindu youth, the CEC warned that similar incidents of incitement could recur if not addressed promptly. Such incidents, he stressed, call for immediate remedial action by the authorities to prevent escalation and uphold communal harmony. Field-level administration officials identified major challenges to the law and order and election preparedness ahead of the polls, including the frequent granting of bail to criminals, which undermines law enforcement and weakens deterrence, potentially disrupting election security. Senior police officials stressed an urgent need to recover illegal arms, noting that at least 455 police pistols and other weapons were lost during the July movement, posing serious security risks due to the ease of their concealment and transportation. Efforts to recover the weapons were constrained by insufficient intelligence and limited community cooperation, they said. District superintendents of police also alleged that some political leaders publicly speak out against criminals at daytime meetings, while privately exerting pressure on the police at night to secure the release of such arrested offenders. Field-level administration officials also identified rapid spread of misinformation, particularly AI-generated content and disinformation on social media as another major challenge. As a solution, they proposed the formation of division-wise cyber patrol teams, clearer legal decisions on AI-driven propaganda, and closer coordination with the Bangladesh Telecom Regulatory Commission. They also warned of the risk of voter suppression through the misuse of money, leading to calls for tighter oversight, and ceilings on digital money transfers. Further recommendations included strengthening border security with support from the home ministry, ensuring uninterrupted power supply, improving coordination through joint district-level command centres, deploying Ansar forces at upazila polling centres during the night and conducting joint security rehearsals. Inspector general of police Baharul Alam stressed the need for continued backing from the Election Commission to take firm actions against road blockades, highway obstructions, and small-scale disruptive activities that create instability. He warned that unless the law and order was fully established everywhere, it would be difficult for the police to provide effective support to the commission. Deputy commissioner of Chattogram Mohammad Zahidul Islam Mian highlighted major challenges ahead of the upcoming elections, focusing on the district’s geographical and logistical complexities. He described Chattogram as a unique district with hills, a 45 km border with India, and coastal areas, making access difficult, particularly to remote locations like Urirchar Union in Sandwip upazila, where reaching two polling centres with 7,095 voters takes two hours by trawler. The DC raised urgent security concerns, including the need for rapid recovery of illegal arms and a shortage of officers to adequately cover the large area. He also warned about the fast spread of issues through the internet and expressed concern over groups potentially using funds to influence or suppress voter turnout. To tackle these challenges, he recommended immediate arms recovery, arranging a helicopter for Urirchar on the polling day, and stricter monitoring of financial activities, including temporarily limiting electronic money transfers at least seven days before the polls. The divisional commissioner of Mymensingh Farah Shammi urged the home ministry to strengthen border security through increased cooperation, calling for a meeting with the judiciary to review the issue of granting bail to criminals. The commissioner also requested the Power Division to ensure an uninterrupted electricity supply, noting its importance for the campaign activities and overall election preparedness. The Khulna divisional commissioner warned of a triangular threat to the elections, including illegal weapons, misinformation spread via AI technology and other digital media, and continuously active negative forces. Rajshahi metropolitan police commissioner Md Zillur Rahman raised concerns over AI-generated videos and images circulating on social media, proposing a division-wise cyber patrolling team to address such content swiftly. The police official also highlighted the risks of digital money misuse to manipulate voter turnout. Rather than enforcing a complete shutdown on the platforms, he suggested imposing ceilings on the transactions through platforms like bKash and Upay to prevent financial influence without harming the economy. During the meeting, the administration and the police were instructed to ensure that minority voters could travel to and from polling centres without fear, cast their votes freely, and return home safely. The chief election commissioner also reminded election officials that the returning officers held critical responsibilities and must carefully study all election circulars and the code of conduct. All officials were instructed to act impartially and professionally, without showing bias towards any candidate or party. The CEC said that complaints involving threats to the lives of candidates or harassment of their supporters must be handled with the utmost seriousness.

title: 11 more held for attacks on media
body: The police have arrested 11 more people in connection with the December 18 vandalism, looting and arson on the offices of two newspapers, the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star. With the latest arrests on Monday, the number of arrestees in connection with the attacks has risen to 28. The police had earlier arrested 17 people in connection with the attacks following the death of the Inquilab Mancha convener and a July uprising organiser, Sharif Osman Hadi, at a hospital in Singapore. A Dhaka Metropolitan Police press release issued on Tuesday said that the metropolitan police’s Detective Branch arrested nine people from different parts of the capital on Monday and two other people were arrested by Tejgaon police on the day. The arrestees are Abdur Rahman, 30, Md Jannatul Naim, 21, Md Faisal, 24, Kari Muaz Bin Abdul Rahman, 33, Jubaer Hossain, 21, Md Almas Ali, 29, Zulfiqur Ali Sourav, 22, Niaz Mahmud, 28, Mohammad Mainul Islam, 22, Md Hashem, 26 and Arafat Yasmin, 29. Asked about the political identities of the arrestees, DMP spokesperson Muhammad Talebur Rahman said that they were interrogating the arrestees and investigating to find out their political links. On Monday, the authorities of the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star filed separate cases with the Tejgaon police station over the December 18 vandalism and arson on their offices. The Prothom Alo filed a case against 400-500 unnamed people and The Daily Star filed another case against 350-400 unnamed people in connection with the vandalism, looting and arson on their offices. The authorities of the Prothom Alo said that they had incurred a loss of Tk 32 crore and The Daily Star authorities said they had suffered a loss of Tk 40 crore, according to separate case documents. United Nations Special Rapporteur on freedom of expression Irene Khan on Tuesday said that the violent mob attacks on media outlets and cultural institutions in Bangladesh were deeply alarming and must be promptly and effectively investigated, with perpetrators brought to justice without delay. In a statement to the media, she condemned the attacks on the night of December 18, when hundreds of people vandalised media houses at Karwanbazar in Dhaka and targeted cultural institutions following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. On Tuesday, French ambassador Jean-Marc Séré-Charlet and the German Embassy’s Chargé d’Affaires Anja Kersten visited Prothom Alo and The Daily Star offices following the recent incident, expressing their solidarity with the journalists and the steadfast support of France and Germany for press freedom, according to a Facebook post of the German Embassy in Dhaka. On the night of December 18, hundreds of attackers vandalised and looted the offices of the Prothom Alo in the capital’s Karwanbazar area and The Daily Star on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and then set fire to the offices. Veteran journalist and writer Nurul Kabir, the editor of New Age and the president of the Editors’ Council, was harassed when he went in front of The Daily Star office early December 19 to rescue the journalists and staff trapped in the office during the fire. Chhayanaut–Sanskriti Bhaban in the Dhanmondi area was attacked early Friday and the central office of cultural organisation Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi on Topkhana Road in Dhaka was torched Friday evening.

title: Class VII students to get 70pc, Class VIII students to get 60pc books on Jan 1: NCTB
body: Officials of the National Curriculum and Textbook Board on Sunday said that Class VII students would get 70 per cent and Class VIII students would get 60 free textbooks for 2026 academic year on January 1. The board officials also said that on January 1 the students of Class VI and IX would get about 100 per cent books. The primary level students however would get all books on the first day of 2026, they also said at an event titled ‘Uploading of online version of textbooks for the 2026 academic year to the website’. Education adviser Professor Chowdhury Rafiqul Abrar and primary and mass education adviser professor Bidhan Ranjan Roy Podder attended the event at NCTB Bhaban in the capital. 'We cannot give all textbooks to the students on January 1,’ NCTB chairman Md Mahbubul Hoque Patwary told New Age on December 24, adding, ‘We hope that we will be able to distribute all books by January.’ Due to re-tender issue for a portion of books, they had to give the printers time till January 22 next year, he mentioned.

title: Ten houses burnt in Gazipur fire
body: At least ten houses were gutted in a fire that broke out at village Abdar in Sreepur upazila of Gazipur district on Tuesday. Md Nurul Karim, inspector of Sreepur Fire Service and Civil Defence, said the fire broke out at a tin-shed house in the morning and engulfed the adjoining houses. On information, two firefighting units rushed to the spot and extinguished the fire after an hour of frantic effort. However, no casualty was reported in the fire and the cause of the fire will be known after an investigation.

title: Bangladesh foreign ministry summons Indian high commissioner
body: Bangladesh on Tuesday expressed grave concern to the government of India over incidents involving extremist elements, including disturbances outside the Bangladesh High Commission and the official residence in New Delhi on December 20, as well as vandalism at the Bangladesh Visa Centre in Siliguri on December 22. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma and expressed deep concern over violent protests staged outside the premises of the different diplomatic missions of Bangladesh in India. Bangladesh condemned such acts of premeditated violence or intimidation against diplomatic establishments, which not only endanger the safety of diplomatic personnel but also undermine the principles of mutual respect and values of peace and tolerance. The government of Bangladesh called upon the government of India to conduct a thorough investigation into the incidents, to take all necessary measures to prevent the recurrence of such acts and to ensure safety and security of Bangladesh’s diplomatic missions and related facilities in India. The government of Bangladesh expects the government of India to immediately take appropriate steps in accordance with its international and diplomatic obligations to safeguard the dignity and security of diplomatic personnel and establishments, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

title: Human rights organisations express concern over shrinking democracy in Bangladesh
body: Global human rights organisations have expressed concern that the targeting of politicians, activists, major media outlets and cultural institutions in Bangladesh, amid heightened political tensions ahead of the 2026 national election, signals a troubling erosion of the rule of law and a shrinking space for free expression, civic discourse and democratic participation. ‘We stand in solidarity with Bangladesh’s journalists, media workers, artists, and diverse communities,’ said the organisations in a joint statement shared by the Human Rights Watch on Monday. The organisations reiterated their commitment to defending freedom of expression, accountability, and the rights of communities to participate safely and freely in civic and cultural life—both offline and online. The signatories to the statement are Access Now, Article 19, Committee to Protect Journalists, Human Rights Watch, International Truth and Justice Project, Journalists for Democracy in Sri Lanka and Tech Global Institute. They strongly condemned the violent attacks on December 18, 2025 on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, two of South Asia’s oldest and most reputed media institutions, and the vandalism of Chhayanaut, one of Bangladesh’s most respected cultural and educational institutions. These apparently coordinated acts of violence represent a grave escalation in attacks against independent media, journalists, activists, and cultural spaces in Bangladesh, said the rights bodies. ‘We are also deeply alarmed at the credible reports of public beating to death and burning of Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh’s Bhaluka Upazila on the same night, following allegations that he made ‘derogatory remarks’ on religion,’ the statement reads. These incidents followed the death of Sharif Osman Hadi, a political activist and leading figure of Bangladesh’s 2024 July Uprising, who was shot in broad daylight in the country’s capital on December 12 and died on December 18, 2025. ‘We are particularly alarmed by verified reports indicating that journalists and staff were trapped inside the burning premises of the two news outlets, facing imminent risks to their lives,’ the joint statement says. Any failure to respond promptly and effectively in such circumstances engages the state’s fundamental duty to protect life, the organisations said. Besides, they said, the forced temporary suspension of both print and online editions of the newspapers marks an unprecedented disruption to Bangladesh’s media landscape and underscores the severity of the threat faced by independent journalism, while the harassment and physical intimidation of journalists present at the scene reflects the growing boldness of those who seek to undermine media freedom in the absence of effective state protection. The attack on Chhayanaut also signals a broader pattern of hostility toward cultural institutions and practitioners, revealing an increasingly unsafe environment for artistic expression and diversity of opinion. ‘These developments point to a dangerous convergence of online and offline violence, coupled with long-standing patterns of coordinated harassment and state-sanctioned surveillance that have fostered a culture of impunity,’ said the rights bodies. There has been a documented pattern of attacks on freedom of thought and expression through abuse of the legal system, and intimidation and attacks of bauls, journalists, media workers, and artists throughout this year, the statement said. A number of these attacks appear to have been fueled by hate speech and explicit calls to violence online apparently posted by some prominent personalities with large followings on social media platforms, and further amplified by their followers and affiliated networks, it mentioned. The continued circulation of such hate content highlights the technology sector’s failure to meet their human rights responsibilities, and their chronic underinvestment in user safety in the Global Majority, they said. These incidents further illustrate a failure of the state to respond promptly and effectively to online hate and incitement, despite well-documented and recurring patterns of hate speech and violent mobilisation. While the interim government has promoted extensive cyber law reforms — proposals that have drawn criticism from civil society groups for lacking substance, practicality, and adequate consultation—the persistent spread of incitement to violence online exposes a profound enforcement failure and raises serious concerns about the efficacy of this government’s commitments to online safety. Bangladesh has binding obligations under international human rights law, including the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, as well as constitutional guarantees that protect freedom of expression, media freedom, cultural life, political and civic participation, and personal security. These obligations require the state to do everything they reasonably can to prevent, protect against, investigate, hold accountable those responsible, and remedy violations committed by both state and non-state actors. These failures must be understood in the context of the recent developments in Bangladesh. The organisations called on the interim government of Bangladesh to ensure immediate and effective protection for journalists, media workers, media houses, cultural and intellectual institutions, and their practitioners across the country, including through the deployment of adequate security measures where credible threats exist. They also asked the government to conduct swift, independent, and transparent investigations into the attacks on Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, and Chhayanaut, as well as other journalists, media workers, and artists, and ensure that all perpetrators, planners, and instigators are held accountable through due process of law and victims or next-of-kin have access to effective remedies. They also asked the government to engage technology companies and social media platforms to implement proactive, proportionate and timely interventions against hate speech and incitement to violence, and which are responsive to emerging crises, and work with civil society and human rights groups to put in place safeguards that protect user safety and free expression during the election. They also asked the government to publicly and unequivocally condemn all acts of violence, intimidation, and harassment against journalists, media outlets, and cultural and intellectual institutions, and reaffirm the state’s commitment to protecting freedom of expression and cultural life. The organisations asked the government to guarantee a safe and enabling environment for journalism, cultural expression, and civic participation—both offline and online—particularly in the lead-up to the 2026 national election. They asked the government to align national laws, policies, and practices with Bangladesh’s constitutional guarantees and its international human rights obligations, including under the ICCPR, to safeguard freedom of expression, media freedom, and personal security.

title: Fire at Babubazar multi-storey building brought under control
body: The fire that broke out at the multi-storey building near Babubazar Bridge in the capital has been brought under control. The fire broke out at the 5th floor of the 14-storey building around 6:40am on Tuesday, said duty officer of Fire Service and Civil Defence, Shahjahan Hossain. On information, nine firefighting units rushed to the spot and extinguished the fire at about 8:10am. However, what caused the fire could not be known immediately.

title: Dhaka becomes 3rd most polluted city with AQI score of 252
body: Dhaka ranked third on the list of cities worldwide with the worst air quality, with an AQI score of 252 at about 9:00am on Tuesday morning. Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘very unhealthy’, according to the air quality index. Egypt’s Cairo, India’s Delhi and India’s Kolkata occupied the first, second and fourth spots in the list, with AQI scores of 374, 290 and 210, respectively. An AQI between 151 and 200 is considered ‘unhealthy’ while 201-300 is ‘very unhealthy’ and 301-400 is considered ‘hazardous’, posing severe health risks to residents. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon.

title: Bangladeshi youth injured in BSF firing
body: A Bangladeshi youth was injured in the firing by Indian Border Security Force along the Daikhawa border in Hatibandha upazila of Lalmonirhat district on Monday morning. Roni Mia, 22, son of Harun or Rashid of Daikhawa Gotamari village in Hatibandha, sustained bullet injury near Pillar 902 on the border at about 6:00am, according to Border Guard Bangladesh and local people. BGB officials said that when four to five Bangladeshis entered about 150 yards in the no man’s land allegedly for cattle smuggling, Indian BSF opened fire leaving Roni Mia injured. Local people said that Roni Mia was taking treating at a private clinic in Rangpur. BGB-15 Battalion commanding officer Lieutenant Colonel Mehedi Hasan said that the BGB was investigating the incident. Hatibandha police station officer-in-charge Shaheen Mohammad Amanullah said that a Bangladeshi youth was shot by BSF on Hatibandha border and they heard that he was receiving treatment secretly.

title: Ahasanul Huda dissolves his party, joins BNP
body: Bangladesh Jatiya Dal chairman Syed Ahasanul Huda on Monday dissolved his party and joined the Bangladesh Nationalist Party with his party leaders and activists. The joining ceremony took place at the office of the BNP chairperson in the capital’s Gulshan area, where Ahasanul presented a bouquet of flowers to BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. He is set to contest the upcoming parliamentary election for the Kishoreganj-5 constituency with BNP’s electoral symbol, the sheaf of paddy. Congratulating the newcomers, Fakhrul said that Ahasanul Huda and his team had joined the BNP, placing their trust in the leadership of acting chairman Tarique Rahman, upholding the 19-point programme of the party founder, Ziaur Rahman, and showing confidence in chairperson Begum Khaleda Zia. Fakhrul hoped that the induction would further strengthen BNP. BNP is a party that believes in nationalist ideals, he said and added that they had joined the BNP to support the path of democracy at the critical juncture for the country. BNP standing committee member Nazrul Islam Khan also attended the joining ceremony. Ahasanul Huda was the coordinator of the 12-Party Alliance, which was a simultaneous movement partner of the BNP. On December 9, Bangladesh Liberal Democratic Party chairman Shahadat Hossain Selim joined the BNP after dissolving his own party. Following his joining, BNP announced him as the party’s candidate for the Laxmipur-1 constituency. Before joining BNP, Selim served as the spokesperson for the 12-Party Alliance.

title: ACC prosecutes ex-NBL MDs, 29 others
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission on Monday filed a case against 31 people, including former National Bank managing directors MA Wadud and Chowdhury Mustak Ahmed, on charges of embezzling Tk 647 crore. The commission also filed two separate cases against 57 people, including former minister and president of the governing body of Willes Little Flower School and College Rashed Khan Menon, over alleged irregularities in teacher recruitment and promotions at the educational institution. ACC deputy director Afroza Haque Khan filed a case with its integrated district office in Dhaka-1 on Monday against 31 people on charges of embezzling Tk 647 crore from National Bank, said ACC director general Akhtar Hossain. According to the case, Manha Precast Technology Ltd, an organisation on paper, took Tk 403 crore from National Bank by using fake documents with the help of members of the board of directors of the bank. NBL members of the board of directors awarded the loan to Manha Precast, abusing their power and violating the related rules. Manha Precast Technology director Mansur Ali and its CEO Syed Mahtab Uddin Mahmud in collusion with the others accused took the loan which is now stand at Tk 647 crore. After the loan money was deposited in the account of Manha Precast Technology, the accused allegedly embezzled the money and laundered it. The accused are former NBL directors Monwara Sikder, Parveen Haque Sikder, Khalilur Rahman, Moazzem Hossain, Ron Haque Sikder, Anwar Hossain, Mabrur Hossain, Zakaria Taher, Badiul Alam, former NBL officials Shamim Ara Haque, Amirul Islam, Chandan Kumar Das, Munshi Sarwar Jahan, Kamrul Islam Chowdhury, Dilip Kumar Das, Jahanara Aktar, Md Enayetullah, Mustafizur Rahman Bhuyain, Ekramul Haque, Hasina Sultana, Saidur Rahman, ATM Emdadul Haque, Syed Rois Uddin, ASM Bulbul, Habibur Rahman, Abu Rashed Noab, and former lawmaker Aslamul Haque’s wife Maksuda Haque. The ACC filed two separate cases against former chairman of the governing body of Wills Little Flower School and College, Rashed Khan Menon, also the president of the Workers Party of Bangladesh, on allegations of irregularities in teacher recruitment and promotions at the institution. ACC director general (prevention) Md Akhtar Hossain said that the commission approved two separate cases over these allegations against Menon, a former minister of the Awami League government and former lawmaker for the Dhaka-8 constituency. In one of the two cases, Menon and 13 teachers, along with a total of 20 people, have been made accused while in the other case, 37 people, including Menon, have been named as accused. Following the political changeover after the fall of the AL regime on August 5, 2024, in a student-led mass uprising, police arrested Menon on August 22, 2024. Since then, the politician has remained in prison in a number of cases. In the first case, it has been alleged that through ‘irregularities and fraud, a recruitment examination was arranged in a ‘deliberate and pre-planned manner’ to appoint only 13 pre-selected candidates as teachers at Wills Little Flower School and College. It further stated that despite having no authority under the rules to conduct such recruitment, a special governing committee carried out the process. No director general or his representative, nor any subject-based teacher, was included on the recruitment board. Candidates were appointed without the NTRCA (Non-Government Teachers Registration and Certification Authority) certificates mentioned in the recruitment circular. Apart from Menon, former principal of the school and former member-secretary of the governing body, retired Lt Col Alamgir Hossain, former governing body members Mahbubur Rahman, Md Abul Hossain, Mir Mosharraf Hossain and Jahirul Islam Khan have been accused in the case. Teachers Shyamoli Hossain, Mahmudah Sultana, Ayesha Siddiqua, Nasrin Afroze, Mohammad Abdul Qaiyum, Tuhin Biswas, Md Bazlur Rahman, Md Rasel, Md Harun-or-Rashid Khan, Md Mosharraf Hossain, Utpal Biswas, AKM Masud Rana and Md Ariful Islam are also accused in the first case. In the second case, the ACC alleged that despite appointment letters clearly stating that the service rules of MPO-enlisted non-government schools would apply, 31 teachers were promoted to the post of lecturer in violation of those rules. Rashed Khan Menon, former principal retired Lt Col Alamgir Hossain, former governing body members Mahbubur Rahman, Md Abul Hossain, Mir Mosharraf Hossain, Jahirul Islam and Shyamoli Hossain Khan have been accused in the case. Apart from them, lecturers Mahbub Alam Bachchu, Md Golam Mostafa, Nilufar Yasmin, Shah Md Jewel Reza, Md Azgar Ali, Gazi Abul Bashar, Mohammad Saiful Islam, Ainun Nahar, Momtaz Begum, John Flerian Gomez, Nasima Begum, Himani Sen, Kamrun Nahar, Md Abdul Aziz, Moniruzzaman, Taksina Akhtar Banu, Sabina Naznin, Md Daud Iqbal, Shaheen Begum, Md Sazzad Hossain, Sukanta Chandra Saha, Tahmina Yasmin, Ismat Ara Faruk, Marufa Sultana, Farhana Rahman, Habiba Akhtar Khanam, Azimun Nahar, Syeda Fahima Begum, HM Gias Uddin and Rowshan Ara Tanjim are also accused in the second case.

title: ICT prosecution seeks to frame charges against Salman, Anisul
body: The prosecution of the International Crimes Tribunal on Monday prayed for framing crimes against humanity charges against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s industries affairs adviser Salman F Rahman and former law minister Anisul Huq for their alleged provocation and facilitation of atrocities during the July mass uprising. Chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam placed five counts of charges against the duo before the two-member tribunal chaired by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder. The tribunal fixed January 4 for hearing discharge petitions filed by Salman and Anisul. Their defence lawyer, Munsurul Haque Chowdhury, sought two more weeks to prepare his submissions. The charges also include allegations of provocation, abetment and facilitation of the killing of 16 people and injuries to many others. According to the prosecution, the violence was carried out by Awami League cadres using lethal weapons at Mirpur-2, Mirpur-10, Jhut Palli in Mirpur-13 and Mirpur-14 on August 5, 2024, to prevent the protesters’ ‘March to Dhaka’ programme. In support of the charges, the prosecution played an audio recording of a telephone conversation between Salman and Anisul on July 19, 2024, which the prosecution said showed provocation for the declaration of curfew and facilitation of the July atrocities. Salman and Anisul were present in the dock during the hearing. According to the prosecution, Anisul advised Salman to suppress the student-led movement and supported the imposition of curfew. The prosecution submitted formal charges against the two on December 4. Salman and Anisul were arrested on August 13, 2024, and are facing multiple cases related to the July uprising. According to the charge sheet, Salman and Anisul held a phone conversation at about 9:24pm on July 19, 2024, during which they discussed strategies to stop the movement and agreed in principle on imposing a curfew. Later that night, a meeting of the Awami League-led alliance was held at Ganabhaban in presence of Sheikh Hasina, also the leader of the alliance, and home minister Asaduzzaman Khan, where the decision was taken to deploy the army and impose a curfew, the prosecution said. Salman and Anisul were key members of the ‘Gang of Four which was formed to prevent the 2024 July movement. Two others were the then home minister Asaduzzaman Khan and Awami League general secretary Obaidul Quader. The prosecution further alleged that Salman, while serving as the prime minister’s adviser, abused his authority to interfere in political, economic as well as civil and military administrative affairs and aided Sheikh Hasina in committing crimes during the Awami League government’s tenure from 2009 to 2024. It also alleged that Salman played a role in the detention, killing or release of political opponents from ‘secret detention facilities’ operated by the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence and the Rapid Action Battalion-1 headquarters. According to the prosecution, on July 22, 2024, Salman met deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina at Ganabhaban along with a group of businessmen, where they expressed support for the crackdown on protesters, including killings, torture and repression. The prosecution alleged that through the meeting Salman provoked, instigated and aided the violence against protesters during the July uprising. It further said that Salman maintained communication with Hasina until her departure from the country on August 5, 2024, citing a phone conversation between Salman and Sheikh Rehena, Hasina’s younger sister. Regarding Anisul Huq’s individual role, the prosecution alleged that, as the then law minister and a member of the ‘gang of four’, he advised and instigated efforts to suppress the movement. The prosecution alleged that 286 cases were filed against about 450,000 protesting students and members of the public during the movement, leading to indiscriminate arrests and torture to stop the protests.

title: TARIQUE RETURN: Railway cancels 3 regular trains as BNP hires special trains
body: The Bangladesh Railway on Monday has cancelled the scheduled journeys of three trains on December 25 as it would use the trains to carry Bangladesh Nationalist Party leaders and activists on the occasion of the party’s leader Tarique Rahman’s homecoming. BNP acting chairperson Tarique Rahman is scheduled to arrive in Dhaka on December 25 after over 17 years of stay in the United Kingdom. The railways ministry, in a press release issued on Monday, apologised to the passengers who were scheduled to board the three trains: Rajbari Commuter on Rajbari-Poradah, Dhalar Char Express on Pabna-Rajshahi and Rohonpur Commuter on Rohonpur-Rajshahi routes. The press release also read that along with 10 special trains assigned for carrying BNP leaders and activists to the capital on December 25, additional coaches would also be added to regular trains. The special trains will run on Cox’s Bazar-Dhaka-Cox’s Bazar, Jamalpur-Mymensingh-Dhaka- Jamalpur, Tangail-Dhaka-Tangail, Bhairab Bazar-Narsingdi-Dhaka-Narsingdi-Bhairab Bazar, Joydebpur-DhakaCantonment-Joydebpur (Gazipur), Panchagarh-Dhaka-Panchagarh, Khulna-Dhaka-Khulna, Chatmohor- Dhaka Cantonment-Chatmohor, Rajshahi-Dhaka-Rajshahi, and Jashore-Dhaka-Jashore. In the release the ministry also mentioned that by arranging the special trains Bangladesh Railway would earn an estimated Tk 36 lakh. Instructions have been given for the leaders and activists to comply with the Election Code of Conduct-2025 while they are on board the special trains and additional coaches, the release added. Earlier on December 18, the BNP requested the railways ministry to arrange special trains or additional carriages on the key routes on the night of December 24, ahead of Tarique’s arrival. In a letter to the ministry secretary, the BNP highlighted the expected arrival of large numbers of students and supporters from across the country to welcome Tarique in Dhaka. Earlier this year, the government provided eight special trains to carry people from different districts to Dhaka city on August 5 to join the July Declaration announcement ceremony, had passengers fewer than the usual trains. Before that, Chattogram Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal rented a special train to take part in a student rally at Central Shaheed Minar in Dhaka on August 3, and the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami rented four special trains to transport leaders and supporters to Dhaka for its July 18 rally at Suhrawardy Udyan in the capital.

title: Travel ban imposed on BNP MP nominee Jalal, family
body: A Dhaka Senior Special Judge’s Court on Monday issued an international travel ban on Md Jalal Uddin, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party nominated lawmaker candidate for Chandpur-2 constituency in the next general election, over allegations of acquiring illegal wealth and laundering money abroad. Judge Abdullah Al Mamun of the court issued the travel ban on Jalal and his family members, responding to a petition filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission. The other family members are Jalal’s wife Shahanaz Sharmin, and their children Sayeed Md Rijvee, Sayeed Mohammed Alvee, and Ayesha Tasnima Tanvee. ACC assistant director SM Mamunur Rashid, in his petition, said that an inquiry was underway into allegations that the individuals earned money through unlawful means. There is an attempt to legitimize it by transferring the funds into bank accounts in their own names and in the names of related persons, as well as laundering the money abroad, said the petition. The petition also stated that there was a risk that the accused might leave the country, which could prolong or obstruct the ongoing inquiry. Therefore, in the public interest, it was necessary to impose a ban on their foreign travel. ACC director general Akhtar Hossain at a press briefing on Monday said that Jalal Uddin was the key suspect as an inquiry was ongoing against him for offences under the Money Laundering Prevention Act. He said that four other family members of Jalal were also under inquiry for the same charges.

title: FY27 budget at Tk 8.5 lakh crore likely
body: The size of the national budget for the 2026-27 financial year is likely to be about Tk 8.50 lakh crore with 6 per cent growth in the gross domestic product. The size of the revised budget for the current financial year (FY 2025-26) is likely to be Tk 7.88 lakh crore from the original Tk 7.90 lakh crore, said finance ministry officials after a meeting on the country’s overall economic progress and budget expenditure on Monday. The meeting was presided over by chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus at the state guest house Jamuna in the capital Dhaka. In the revised FY26 budget, the non-development expenditure will increase by about Tk 28,000 crore and the development expenditure will decrease by about Tk 30,000 crore. On the FY27 budget outline, finance ministry officials said that it was necessary to draw it before the February 12 national election for elementary exercises by the Finance Division. Waiting for the new government poses challenges for the Finance Division to complete preparatory works timely, said the officials. The officials also said that the new government would get about three and a half months before the announcement of the FY27 budget in the first week of June. The meeting was attended, among others, by finance adviser Salehuddin Ahmed, planning adviser Wahiduddin Mahmud and Bangladesh Bank governor Ahsan H Mansur. Focusing on the overall economy, the meeting expressed satisfaction that equilibrium was restored among the key indicators, according to a press release issued by the press wing of the chief adviser. The meeting discussed a range of key economic issues, including inflation, wage growth, agricultural production, financial and external sectors, current account, remittance, imports and letters of credit. The meeting was informed that as the 12-month average, the overall inflation in the country fell below 9 per cent for the first time in November 2025 after June 2023. It is expected that inflation will fall below 7 per cent by June 2026, according to the press release. The meeting was also informed that due to appropriate incentives and management in the agricultural sector, boro production was good in the past financial year, it said adding that as no major natural disasters had occurred so far, a good harvest of aman was also expected this year. As of December 18, 2025, the gross foreign exchange reserve stood at $32.57 billion compared with about $25 billion in August 2024. With exchange rate stability, increased remittance inflows and a significant rise in interest rates recently in the financial sector, the foreign exchange reserve is expected to increase further in the coming days, said the press release.

title: Law, order to improve as polls day nears: CEC
body: Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin on Monday said that the country’s law and order would steadily improve as the Jatiya Sangsad elections day would approach. He expressed the confidence that public fear surrounding the polls would go away. Speaking to reporters after inspecting the Mail Processing Centre for postal balloting at Tejgaon in the capital, the CEC said that there was a suitable environment for holding the elections and the EC had not lost its confidence. ‘The closer the voting day comes, the better the law and order will be. Fear will gradually go away and the elections will be held in a festive manner,’ he said. Responding to a question, the CEC said that the shooting incident involving Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi had created some public anxiety, but stressed that the overall electoral environment remained intact. He reiterated that both candidates and voters would feel more confident as the polling day would near. A day after the national elections schedule was announced, prospective independent Dhaka-8 candidate for the JS polls Hadi was shot in the capital on December 12 and later died on Thursday despite being flown to Singapore for advanced treatment. Ahead of the 13th JS elections, Nasir Uddin said that the commission had met with law enforcement agencies and assured the nation that all stakeholders were working together to ensure smooth and orderly polls. Referring to the large-scale introduction of postal voting for the first time in the country’s history, the CEC said that the commission was satisfied with the progress despite some initial registration challenges. Some 5.75 lakh people, he disclosed, have already registered for postal voting, hoping that the number would rise significantly in the next few days. Meanwhile, following a meeting with the CEC, BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday too hoped that the law and order would improve in the days ahead. Speaking to reporters after the meeting, he said that maintaining the law and order was mainly a government responsibility, while the EC has the power during the election period to appoint and transfer officials and oversee certain administrative matters. He said that the BNP had called for a smooth and credible election, adding that the public expected to vote freely and independently in a festive atmosphere.

title: Biman changes terminal at Guangzhou
body: Biman Bangladesh Airlines Limited has changed its operating terminal at Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport in China. All Biman flights operating on the Dhaka–Guangzhou–Dhaka route will be handled from Terminal 3 instead of the existing Terminal 1. The national flag carrier said in a press release that the terminal change is being implemented in accordance with directives from the Guangzhou Airport Authority and is aimed at ensuring improved passenger convenience and enhanced service standards. The passengers have been asked to check their tickets and boarding passes before arrive at the airport keeping sufficient time to reach Terminal 3, the press release added.

title: BATTERY-RUN THREE-WHEELERS: Regulations, safe design urgent, say experts
body: Battery-run three-wheelers should immediately be brought under regulations, said government officials and experts at a discussion on Monday. They also stressed a uniform structural design for these vehicles. The Centre for Policy Dialogue organised the discussion at its office in the capital to identify the regulatory, infrastructural and institutional measures to incorporate battery-run three-wheelers safely and sustainably into the country’s urban transport network. CPD research director Khondaker Golam Moazzem, who was also in the study team, said that while at the moment battery-run three-wheelers were rapidly spreading everywhere, the country’s roads were very ill prepared for battery-run vehicles regarding technical and regulatory aspects. ‘It’s already late, let’s not delay anymore,’ he said, adding that the think tank in its proposal elaborated which government agencies should work on them. While presenting a study report titled ‘Integrating electric three-wheelers into urban transport network: challenges and way forward’, CPD programme associate Md Khalid Mahmud said that nearly 90 per cent of these vehicles were locally manufactured. The battery-run rickshaws and ‘easy bikes’ together consumed 78 per cent of the total lead-acid battery market at present, he said. Regarding road accident fatalities caused by battery-run three-wheelers, the study report mentions that these vehicles caused 20.52 per cent deaths in 2023, 21.01 per cent in 2024, and 19.75 per cent in the current year till August. Special guest chief of Physical Infrastructure Division at Bangladesh Planning Commission Kabir Ahamed said that currently about 40 lakh battery-run three-wheelers were running across the country.
