Having mentioned that government bodies held the licensing authority, Kabir Ahamed said that when three-wheelers were being transformed to battery-run ones, the local government bodied did not have the technical workforce and capacities to oversee and regulate the process. ‘As a result these vehicles got down on roads without any permission or licences,’ he said, stressing bringing them under regulation and correcting and mainstreaming their design. Bangladesh Road Transport Authority director Shahidullah said a 15-kilometre per hour speed limit should be imposed on them. Special guest Dhaka Transport Coordination Authority executive director Neelima Akhter stressed execution of existing laws to control these vehicles. ‘Now we have reached a point where it is not possible to ban these vehicles,’ said Professor Asif-Uz-Zaman Khan of urban and regional planning department at Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology. Battery-run three-wheelers should be classified as motor vehicles and be registered under the BRTA, he added. Rickshaw, Battery-Powered Rickshaw-Van, and Easy Bike Sangram Parishad convener Khalequzzaman Liton, however, mentioned the number of battery-run three-wheelers as around 50 lakh with which 60 lakh drivers were dependent for livelihood. Around three crore people were dependent on these drivers’ earning, he added. He alleged that government officials seldom took their opinions in formulating regulations. The discussion was attended, among others, by Local Government Division joint secretary Khondoker Md Nazmul Huda Shamim and Bangladesh Industrial Technical Assistance Centre executive engineer Md Sayed Abdul Baqi.

title: Bangladesh
body: 27 held for illegally entering Bangladesh from India through C’nawabganj border Members of Border Guard Bangladesh detained 27 people allegedly for illegally entering Bangladesh from India through the Chapainawabganj border early Monday. Members of Border Guard Bangladesh detained 27 people allegedly for illegally entering Bangladesh from India through the Chapainawabganj border early Monday. Branches of more than a hundred Krishnachura trees are being cut along a major city road in Rajshahi as part of the Rajshahi Water Supply and Sewerage Authority’s ongoing pipeline installation work, triggering concern for loss of urban greenery. Rajshahi University authorities on Monday relieved six deans of their responsibilities amid protests from a section of students and leaders of its central students’ union, demanding their resignation. Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Monday reiterated his commitment to holding general elections on February 12. Bangladesh missions in New Delhi and Agartala on Monday suspended issuing visas and all consular services for an indefinite period, days after a Hindu extremist group held a demonstration breaching the security fence of the... Armed security personnel have been deployed for 20 individuals, including politicians, who are facing security threats, said home adviser retired Lieutenant General Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury on Monday. Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus has directed law enforcement agencies to swiftly arrest those involved in the killing of Osman Hadi and others engaged in illegal activities and keep the law and order situation normal at any costs before the national elections. Bangladesh interim government has transferred all assets of four flats seized from former Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed to the Chief Adviser’s Relief and Welfare Fund. A Mymensingh court on Monday placed 12 accused on a three-day remand in connection with the killing of Dipu Chandra Das in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh district on December 18... Bangladesh Nationalist Party standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday said that BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman would enrol his name as a voter on December 27, two days after his return to Bangladesh. The Inquilab Mancha on Monday announced indefinite street demonstrations for the arrest of the killers of its convener Sharif Osman Hadi, who has recently died from bullet injuries. Politicians, civil society members, and representatives from business communities and professional bodies of the country on Monday called for unity to resist ‘evil forces’ behind the mob violence that has again created an atmosphere of fear. The authorities of the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star on Monday filed separate cases with the Tejgaon police station over the December 18 vandalism and arson on their offices following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener... A senior leader of Jatiya Sramik Shakti, the labour wing of the National Citizen Party, was shot in the ear at an apartment in the Sonadanga area of Khulna city on Monday, allegedly following a clash over the sharing of money from peddling drugs.

title: 27 held for illegally entering Bangladesh from India through C’nawabganj border
body: Members of Border Guard Bangladesh detained 27 people allegedly for illegally entering Bangladesh from India through the Chapainawabganj border early Monday. Lieutenant Colonel Golam Kibria, commander of BGB-59 battalion, told New Age that they detained the group – twelve women, five children, eight men and two Hijras – from the Chamucha border area under Bholahat upazila of the district. He said that the detainees had informed them that they had gone to India illegally at different times and were returning to Bangladesh at dawn on Monday. The BGB official said that they had handed over the detainees to Bholahat police station for the next procedures. However, Bholahat police station officer-in-charge Ekramul Hossain told New Age that they had handed the detainees over to the upazila administration, following the required procedures. ‘The upazila administration has now kept them at a dak bungalow. Our next step is to contact their relatives, and if their relatives come forward, we will hand them over to the relatives through a general diary,’ he said, adding that the detainees were basically released after serving jail terms in India.

title: RWASA trimes 100 Krishnachura trees
body: Branches of more than a hundred Krishnachura trees are being cut along a major city road in Rajshahi as part of the Rajshahi Water Supply and Sewerage Authority’s ongoing pipeline installation work, triggering concern for loss of urban greenery. The branch trimming is taking place along both sides of the road from Dairapak Mor to Nader Haji Mor, a stretch known for its rows of Krishnachura trees forming a shaded and scenic corridor. Local residents said that the unplanned cutting of tree branches in the name of development could seriously harm the environment and erode the city’s aesthetic character. Rajshahi WASA is implementing a major project to supply potable water from the Padma River at Godagari, about 26 kilometres from the city. Under the Tk 4,062-crore water treatment plant project, pipelines are being installed by excavating around 41 kilometres of city roads. Officials said that heavy cranes were being used to place large-diameter pipes and that branches obstructing the operation were being cut. According to city officials, the Krishnachura trees along the Dairapak–Nader Haji Mor stretch were planted by the Rajshahi City Corporation in 2019. Over the years, the trees grew into a long canopy, providing shade and visual appeal, and the road became widely regarded as one of the city’s most attractive streets. On Monday afternoon, many trees on one side of the road were found with their branches already cut, while more than a hundred others were marked with paint for cutting. Following reports of the branch cutting, officials from the Rajshahi City Corporation’s environment department visited the site. Rajshahi WASA project engineer Borhan Uddin said that cranes were required to lift heavy pipes and that tree branches were obstructing the work. ‘That is why the branches are being cut. WASA has taken permission for this,’ he said. Atiqur Rahman, a member of the environmental platform Sabuj Sanghati, said that WASA could have adjusted project design or work methods instead of cutting tree branches. ‘The way the branches are being cut may kill the trees. Development work should be carried out in a manner that preserves existing trees,’ he said. Rajshahi City Corporation environment development officer Syed Mahmud Ul Islam said that he was not aware of any formal approval being issued for cutting the branches. ‘The branches were not pruned following proper procedure. I have already instructed the town planner overseeing WASA-related matters to take this issue seriously and ensure that trees are not pruned in this manner,’ he said. Rajshahi WASA managing director (additional charge) Rezaul Alam Sarkar said that the branches were cut because they obstructed the installation of heavy pipelines. He claimed that the city corporation had been informed both in writing and verbally prior to the cutting.

title: RU removes six deans after students lock key offices
body: Rajshahi University authorities on Monday relieved six deans of their responsibilities amid protests from a section of students and leaders of its central students’ union, demanding their resignation. Acting registrar Professor Iftikharul Alam Masud told New Age that the six deans submitted resignation letters, which were accepted by vice-chancellor Professor Saleh Hasan Naqib on Monday. He said that the tenures of all the 12 deans of the university had expired on December 18, and the vice-chancellor had allowed all of them to continue until the election of their successors by teachers’ votes, based on precedents during exceptional periods, including the Covid-19 pandemic. ‘Following Sunday protests, the six deans met the vice-chancellor and said that under the circumstances, continuing duty was likely to invite further problems and it became a matter of honour and dignity,’ he said, adding that there were no substantiated criminal allegations against them. As per the university ordinance, administrative responsibility of the deans automatically reverts to the vice-chancellor until their successors are elected. The registrar said that following their resignation, the vice-chancellor retained responsibility for two faculties and assigned the remaining four to the two pro-vice-chancellors. The decision to extend their tenure was met with protests by a section of students, who accused the administration of shielding ‘fascist’ teachers with allegiance to Awami League, which is now banned from running activities after its ouster from power last year through the July uprising. The protests were sparked by a recent Facebook call from RUCSU general secretary Salahuddin Ammar to mobilise against what he described as the continued dominance of pro-AL figures in key academic positions. Meanwhile, three Bangladesh Nationalist Party-aligned RU teachers’ organisations urged the university authorities to ensure security for teachers, alleging mobbing, humiliation and harassment of faculty members. They also called for the trial of teachers allegedly involved in July uprising attacks and demanded suspension of all teacher recruitment processes until after the national election to be held in next February. Leaders of Jatiyatabadi Sikkhak Forum (national teachers forum), University Teachers’ Association of Bangladesh, and Zia Parishad raised the demands during a meeting with the vice-chancellor on Monday. Sikkhak Forum president Professor Abdul Alim alleged that since August 5 a particular group, along with some students, had been humiliating and harassing teachers, officers and employees on the campus. ‘They are locking offices, interrogating and intimidating officials. These cannot be the responsibilities of students,’ he said. Urging the authorities to halt recruitment until after the national election, Professor Abdul Alim said, ‘Only routine activities are permissible during the election period and that no appointments should be made until after the polls.’ Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal, student wing of Bangladesh Nationalist Party, in a media statement on Sunday night accused RUCSU general secretary Salahuddin Ammar of engaging in ‘terroristic behaviour’, warning that such actions were threatening the academic environment on the campus.

title: Bangladesh national election will be held on time, Yunus tells US envoy to India
body: Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Monday reiterated his commitment to holding general elections on February 12. ‘The nation is eagerly waiting to exercise their voting rights which were stolen by the autocratic regime’, he said, says a press release shared by CA press wing. Professor Yunus made the remarks during a telephone conversation with Sergio Gor, the US Ambassador to India and special envoy for South and Central Asia, at around 7:30pm (Dhaka time). The discussion, which lasted about half an hour, focused on trade and tariff negotiations between Bangladesh and the United States, the upcoming general election, the country’s democratic transition, and the murder of young Bangladeshi political activist Sharif Osman Hadi. Sergio Gor congratulated Professor Yunus for his leadership during recent tariff negotiations. Bangladesh succeeded in reducing US reciprocal tariffs on Bangladeshi goods to 20 per cent. The US special envoy also discussed the massive funeral of Osman Hadi. Chief adviser noted that supporters of the ousted autocratic regime were allegedly spending millions of dollars to disrupt the electoral process and that their fugitive leader was inciting violence. However, he said the interim government was ‘fully prepared’ to deal with any challenges. ‘We have roughly 50 days to go before the election. We want to hold a free, fair and peaceful election. We want to make it remarkable,’ Professor Yunus said. Commerce adviser Sheikh Bashiruddin, national security adviser Khalilur Rahman, and SDG coordinator and senior secretary Lamiya Morshed were present during the call.

title: Bangladesh missions in Delhi, Agartala suspend issuing visas
body: Bangladesh missions in New Delhi and Agartala on Monday suspended issuing visas and all consular services for an indefinite period, days after a Hindu extremist group held a demonstration breaching the security fence of the Bangladesh High Commission in the Indian capital. A senior foreign ministry official in Dhaka confirmed the suspension of visa issuance at the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi and the Bangladesh Assistant High Commission in Agartala, capital of the Tripura state. A series of incidents in the recent time dampened the bilateral relations between the two nations already strained since the interim government of Professor Muhammad Yunus took over following the July uprising that forced the fall of Sheikh Hasina on August 5, 2024. Hasina fled to India on the day and has been staying there since. The Indian Visa Application Centre in Bangladesh capital Dhaka was closed from 2:00pm on December 17 amid a march towards the Indian High Commission, which the police intercepted on its way to the High Commission. The Indian Assistant High Commission in Chattogram has also suspended its visa services for an indefinite period from Sunday, citing security concerns. Around 20–25 activists held demonstrations at the Bangladesh mission in Delhi on Saturday, chanting anti-Bangladesh slogans. Bangladesh foreign minister Md Touhid Hossain on Sunday said that ‘normal security’ was not maintained at the Bangladesh mission in India and the high commissioner, who was staying there with his family, felt threatened. Rejecting India’s press statement on Saturday’s demonstration in front of the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, he said that Bangladesh would rely on the host country for the security and expected that the incident in Delhi would not be repeated in the future. ‘We completely reject the press note. How come a group of Hindu militants were allowed to move to that area—much inside the diplomatic enclave? They were not supposed to be allowed there. They have said many things,’ said Touhid responding to reporters’ questions at his ministry. ‘We have come to know that the demonstrators threatened to kill the high commissioner although we don’t have any evidence,’ said Touhid. He said that Dhaka hoped that the Indian government would take necessary steps to enhance the security of the diplomatic mission. Responding to media queries on the reported demonstration in front of the Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi on December 20, 2025, India’s external affairs ministry Randhir Jaiswal on Sunday in a statement said that there was no attempt to breach the fence or create a security situation at any time. He further said that India was committed to ensure safety of foreign missions in its territory. Meanwhile, Bangladesh’s visa centre in Siliguri, West Bengal, was reportedly vandalised by a group of protesters over the lynching of a Hindu youth in Mymensingh, forcing the authorities to suspend its activities there.

title: Bangladesh provides gunmen for 20 individuals facing security risks : adviser
body: Armed security personnel have been deployed for 20 individuals, including politicians, who are facing security threats, said home adviser retired Lieutenant General Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury on Monday. The editors of two leading newspapers, Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, Matiur Rahman and Mahfuz Anam, will also get gunmen following the recent incidents of arson and vandalism at their offices, he said. Jahangir revealed the information at a press briefing after a meeting of the Advisory Council Committee on Law and Order at the secretariat. Besides, Nahid Islam, former adviser to the interim government and convener of the National Citizen Party , the party’s member secretary Akhtar Hossen, NCP leaders Hasnat Abdullah, Sarjis Alam, Nasiruddin Patwari, and Tasnim Jara and Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque Nur and its general secretary Md Rashed Khan are also set to receive gunmen, according to a police official. Noting that police arrested 17 people in connection with the attack on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, the home adviser said, ‘For the security of the editors of the two newspapers, gunmen have been provided and security at their residences has been strengthened.‘ Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, who was shot by assailants, died last Thursday while undergoing treatment in Singapore. After the news of his death spread, attacks and arson took place at various establishments, including Prothom Alo, The Daily Star and Chhayanaut in the capital. Jahangir said, ‘The government is giving the highest priority to bringing to book those involved in the murder of Hadi, a frontline fighter of the July mass uprising, and is committed to ensuring justice.’ Asked whether Faisal Karim, key suspected in Hadi’s killing, is inside or outside of the country, he said, ‘Very soon, the main mastermind of the incident, Faisal Karim Masud, will be identified and brought under the law.’ However, in the interest of uncovering the motive of the murder and maintaining confidentiality, it’s not possible to disclose details at this moment, he added. ‘However, we assure you — there has been significant progress in this regard, and law enforcement agencies are making all-out efforts to locate him (the mastermind).’ ‘If we knew exactly where Hadi’s killer was, we would have arrested him already; he could be inside the country or outside,’ he said. He said, ‘But I can’t say whether Hadi’s killer left the country illegally but he did not leave the country in legal way.’ Referring to rumours of a ‘hit list’ of 50 people, including politicians, that spread after Hadi’s killing, a journalist drew his attention to the matter. In response, Jahangir said, ‘Those who are at risk have already been provided with one gunman each. Our agencies — DGFI, NSI and SB — sat together and prepared a list of those who are at risk.’ ‘Many of them have been given gunmen, while some did not want gunmen,’ he added. When asked whether all those given gunmen are politicians, he avoided a direct answer and said, ‘When they move around with (gunmen), you can find out through investigative journalism.’ Following the failure to arrest Hadi’s assailants, Inquilab Mancha and various other organisations have demanded the resignation of home adviser Jahangir Alam Chowdhury. A journalist asked, ‘There were rumours throughout Sunday that you had resigned.’ At that time, the home adviser said, ‘If I had resigned, I wouldn’t be sitting here.’ Jahangir also said that the highest level of security would be ensured on the occasion of the homecoming of Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chair Tarique Rahman on December 25. ‘Maximum security measures have already been taken to ensure the safe arrival of Tarique Rahman in the country,’ he said. Stating that Christmas is the biggest religious festival for the Christians, Jahangir Alam Chowdhury said that adequate security preparations had been taken to ensure that the festival was observed in a safe, peaceful and festive atmosphere while maintaining religious solemnity. He said that no fireworks will be allowed on Christmas and the 31st Night. No events will be allowed by blocking or barricading roads. Mentioning that law-enforcement agencies are continuing their operations to recover looted and illegal weapons, the home affairs adviser said that to further intensify and accelerate the operations and to suppress fascist terrorists, a decision was taken to launch the Operation Devil Hunt Phase-2 on 13 December. A total of 6,598 people were arrested up to December 20 in the operation. During the operation, 56 firearms, 437 rounds of ammunition, 137 cartridges and 62 locally made weapons were recovered. Grenades, mortar shells, gunpowder, fireworks and bomb-making materials were also seized. During this period, a total of 13,505 people, including 6,907 accused in cases and warrant-holders, were arrested.

title: Maintain law, order for polls: Yunus
body: Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus has directed law enforcement agencies to swiftly arrest those involved in the killing of Osman Hadi and others engaged in illegal activities and keep the law and order situation normal at any costs before the national elections. ‘Ahead of the upcoming national election, the law and order situation must be kept normal at any cost,’ he made the instructions while addressing a meeting to review the country’s overall law and order situation at the state guest house Jamuna in Dhaka on Sunday, said chief adviser’s press wing on Monday. Home affairs adviser Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, national security adviser Khalilur Rahman and senior officials of different security and law enforcement agencies were present at the meeting. During the meeting, detailed discussions were held on several key issues, including security measures centring the return of acting chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party Tarique Rahman to the country, preparations for the upcoming Christmas and New Year celebrations, and related security arrangements. The meeting reviewed the progress of investigations and arrests in connection with the killing of Inqilab Mancha spokesperson and July fighter Shaheed Sharif Osman Hadi. Police officials informed the chief adviser that, by reviewing video footage, 31 individuals had already been identified as suspects in recent attacks on the offices of two national daily newspapers and two cultural organisations. According to law enforcement agencies, as of Monday morning, at least nine people have been arrested in raids conducted in the city and other parts of the country in connection with attacks on the offices of two national daily newspapers and two cultural organisations. Among the arrested, identities of seven people have been confirmed immediately. They are Md Kashem Faruqi, Md Saidur Rahman, Rakib Hossain, Md Naim, Faisal Ahmed Pranta, Md Sohel Rana and Md Shafikul Islam. Operations are ongoing to arrest the remaining identified suspects. Identities of two people arrested by the police’s counter terrorism unit and the intelligence police are being verified. Besides, three individuals involved in attempts to create disorder near the residence of the Indian assistant high commissioner in Chattogram have been identified by analysing video footage. The chief adviser also urged the voters to cast their ballots for candidates of their choice to elect honest and capable candidates in the upcoming parliamentary elections slated for February 12, 2026. He made the urge in a video message at the inaugural ceremony of the 10 voting vehicles — known as the Super Caravan — to conduct a nationwide campaign on the upcoming 13th parliamentary elections and the referendum on the July National Charter. He said, ‘You are the owner of the country. You will decide who will run this country on behalf you for the next five years. Vote for the candidate of your choice. Choose an honest and capable candidate. Vote thoughtfully.’ Information and broadcasting adviser Syeda Rizwana Hasan, cultural afairs adviser Mostofa Sarwar Farooki, senior secretary of the Election Commission secretariat Akhtar Ahmed and chief adviser’s press secretary Shafiqul Alam inaugurated the voting vehicles by cutting the ribbon at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in the capital on Monday. Stressing that the government wants to hold an election free from fear and obstruction, where there will only be the free and fearless expression of the people’s will, Yunus said, ‘The government is determined to ensure such an environment.’ Noting that the country is passing through a crucial moment with the national parliamentary election and the referendum ahead, he said that keeping this goal in view, a ‘super caravan’ of 10 voting vehicles had begun its journey. These vehicles will travel across all 64 districts and 300 upazilas of the country, he said, adding, ‘The caravans will go door to door to deliver information about the election and the referendum, create awareness about voting rights and spread the message of democracy.’ Yunus said, ‘Voting rights are not anyone’s kindness, it is our constitutional rights. Through exercising this right, we decide which path our future will take.’ He stressed that ensuring a free, fair, and participatory election was not only the responsibility of the government, but the responsibility of every citizen of the state. Yunus described the ‘Super Caravan’ as not merely a convoy of vehicles, but a bearer of the joy of democracy. This convoy will convey how important a single vote is and remind citizens that democracy is strengthened not by inactivity, but by participation, he said. He made a special appeal to the youth, women voters and first-time voters, urging them to come forward, ask questions, learn, understand, and cast their votes. ‘Your decisions will shape the future Bangladesh, the new Bangladesh.’ Yunus also noted that voters would cast another vote in this election—on the July Charter. ‘This charter was prepared meetings days after days with all political parties over nine months. If the people of the country accept this charter, I firmly believe the country will move forward safely for many years. If you support this charter, you must cast ‘Yes’ vote in the referendum,’ he said. Calling for collective participation, Yunus said, ‘Let’s all together make this democratic journey successful. Let’s vote—for ourselves, for the country, for future generations and for a new world.’

title: Govt transfers assets of Benazir’s 4 flats to CA’s relief fund
body: Bangladesh interim government has transferred all assets of four flats seized from former Inspector General of Police Benazir Ahmed to the Chief Adviser’s Relief and Welfare Fund. Anti-Corruption Commission deputy director Akther Hossain disclosed the information to the media on Monday. The ACC earlier seized the flats as part of an ongoing investigation into allegations that Benazir Ahmed amassed illegal wealth during his tenure. After completing all required legal and administrative procedures the seized properties were formally handed over to the CA’s relief fund.

title: DU confirms all buildings safe, classes to resume Dec 28
body: Dhaka University has confirmed that its buildings are structurally safe and pose no risk. The university also announced that regular academic activities will resume from December 28. ‘Considering students’ safety and mental well-being after the recent earthquakes, we quickly formed an expert committee. The committee’s report did not identify any major structural risks anywhere,’ said Prof M Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, treasurer of the university and chairman of the post-earthquake monitoring committee, on Monday. He provided an update on renovation and repair works at a press briefing in the university’s Professor Abdul Matin Virtual Classroom. He said that after completing all necessary technical inspections, the buildings have been deemed safe for students, and renovation work is ongoing in a few buildings. Earlier, all academic activities were suspended on November 22 to inspect and repair vulnerable buildings, and students were asked to vacate their halls. The winter vacation was subsequently scheduled from December 6 to December 28.

title: 12 people put on three-day remand over lynching youth in Mymensingh
body: A Mymensingh court on Monday placed 12 accused on a three-day remand in connection with the killing of Dipu Chandra Das in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh district on December 18. Senior chief judicial magistrate Shahdat Hossain passed the order, said court inspector Sheikh Mostasinur Rahman. Those who remanded were identified as Ashiqur Rahman, 25, Quaiyum, 25, Limon Sarkar, 19, Tarek Hossain, 19, Manik Mia, 20, ershad Ali, 39, Nijum Uddin, 20, Alamgir Hossain, 38, Miraz Hossain Akon, 46, Azmal Hasan Sagir, 26, Shaheen Mia, 19, and Nazmul, 21. On December 19, Apu Chandra Das, younger brother of Dipu filed a case with Bhaluka Police Station. Police arrested 12 people raiding different parts of the district. Dipu Chandra Das, 28, a local garment worker, was beaten to death by a mob over ‘allegedly hurting religious sentiment of Muslims’ in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh district on Thursday (December 18). His body was later set on fire.

title: Tarique to register as voter on Dec 27
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed on Monday said that BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman would enrol his name as a voter on December 27, two days after his return to Bangladesh. Salahuddin disclosed the information while speaking to reporters after a meeting with chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin at the commission headquarters in the capital. Tarique Rahman is scheduled to return to the country from London on December 25, he said and added that the voter registration process would be completed on December 27, as December 26 would be a Friday. Election Commission offices remain open on Saturdays during the election period, allowing all formalities related to voter enrolment, including issuance of a national identity card, to be completed on December 27, he explained. According to Salahuddin, the meeting with the CEC also discussed the procedural steps required for the acting chairman to become a registered voter, and the commission confirmed that the process would be carried out on the designated date. Tarique is set to return to Bangladesh after more than 17 years in exile in the United Kingdom. The elder son of BNP chairperson and former prime minister Khaleda Zia, he had been sentenced in several cases, including a life term, and faced multiple charges, most of which were filed during the 2007–08 military-backed caretaker government. He was arrested during an anti-corruption drive in March 2007 and released on bail in September 2008 before travelling to London for medical treatment, where he remained for years. Following the fall of the Awami League’s 16-year rule in a mass uprising on August 5, 2024, the High Court acquitted him of all cases filed during both the caretaker government and Awami League administration periods, removing legal barriers to his return.

title: Inquilab Mancha calls indefinite demo for arrest of Hadi killers
body: The Inquilab Mancha on Monday announced indefinite street demonstrations for the arrest of the killers of its convener Sharif Osman Hadi, who has recently died from bullet injuries. Issuing a 24-hour ultimatum to ensure the Hadi murder trial at the Speedy Trial Tribunal and to seek support from international intelligence agencies if required, the Inquilab Mancha said that justice must be ensured before the forthcoming national elections, scheduled to be held on February 12, 2026. The Inquilab Mancha will organise a programme titled ‘Shahidi Shapath (oath for martyrdom)’ today to continue protests until ensuring justice for Hadi. Addressing a press conference at Shahbagh in the capital, Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Jaber said, ‘Justice must be ensured before the elections.’ Reffering to the address of chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus during Hadi’s namaj-e-janaza, Jaber stated that he did not talk about the government’s actions regarding the investigation, arrest, and trial of the attackers. ‘We can see your (Yunus’) helplessness. We want to know why you are actually helpless. You have to tell us who made you helpless,’ said Jaber. ‘Without informing us about this, you will just go ahead and hold the elections and then leave. This shall not happen,’ he asserted. Announcing the street demonstrations for an indefinite period, Jaber said, ‘We will not leave the streets until the killers of Osman Hadi are arrested and the people who were behind the killers are arrested.’ The Inquilab Mancha raised a two-point demand and issued a 24-hour ultimatum to the government for the fulfilment of the demand within the time limit. The demands are trial for Hadi’s case at the Speedy Trial Tribunal and seeking support from international intelligence agencies, such as the Federal Bureau of Investigation, if necessary. The Inquilab Mancha alleged that home adviser Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury and special assistant to chief adviser on the ministry of home affairs Md Khuda Baksh Chowdhury belittled the killing of Hadi by not attending the ministry’s Sunday press conference on the development of the case over Hadi murder. Later, the Inquilab Mancha on Monday afternoon issued a statement where it pressed a three-point demand in place of the two-point demand they had made the at the Shahbagh press conference earlier. The three-point demand includes completing the trial of the Hadis case within 30 working days at the Speedy Trial Tribunal, the arrest of and trial for the ousted Awami League activists hiding in civil and military intelligences, and the resignation of the home adviser, the special assistant, and law adviser revealing the reasons for their incompetence to the public and taking full responsibility for Hadi’s murder. The organisation in the afternoon brought out a procession from Shahbagh, which ended with a brief rally at the Central Shaheed Minar demanding an immediate arrest and trial of the killers of Hadi and those involved in the killing as planners. In the rally, Jaber announced that the ‘oath for martyrdom’ programme would be held at 3:00pm at Shahbagh today. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in the capital while conducting his electioneering as an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency, a day after the Election Commission had announced the schedule for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. Law enforcers have arrested at least 10 people so far for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi but the main suspected assailants had fled to India. Hadi, also one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last at a Singapore hospital on December 18.

title: Politicians, professionals urge broader unity to resist
body: Politicians, civil society members, and representatives from business communities and professional bodies of the country on Monday called for unity to resist ‘evil forces’ behind the mob violence that has again created an atmosphere of fear. They made the call at a joint protest meeting organised by the Editors’ Council and the Newspapers Owners’ Association Bangladesh at a city hotel against mob violence across the country. Addressing the meeting, the speakers from across society uniquivocally blamed the interim government’s failure to protect the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star offices and the Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir from mob violence in the capital. Leaders from political parties, including the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, National Citizen Party and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islam, rights activists, business community leaders and journalists expressed solidarity with the Editors’ Council and NOAB at the event. They condemned the attacks on the media outlets and cultural institutions, and the harassment of Nurul Kabir by a mob as he attempted to rescue journalists trapped in the Daily Star premises set ablaze on December 18 night. ‘We haven’t dreamt of this Bangladesh. The attack on media houses amounts to attack on democracy. This is an attack on the July uprising. Now is time for all to unite,’ said BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir. He called upon all concerned, who wanted to see a democratic Bangladesh, to resist all the ill forces. Expressing concerns over the threat to the life of the journalists of the two dailies, The Daily Star editor Mahfuz Anam said that the attackers wanted to kill his newspaper’s staff as 26/27 of them were trapped when their office building was set on fire in the early hours of December 19. ‘We have to respond to such attacks together,’ he added. United Nations special rapporteur for freedom of opinion and expression Irene Khan said that the attack on Hadi was carried out in the broad daylight to create a sense a fear among the people while the attacks on the media outlets were a kind of incitement. International Chamber of Commerce Bangladesh president Mahbubur Rahman said that the political party leaderships were important in upholding the democratic practices. On behalf of the business community, Mahbubur vehemently condemned the attacks on Prothom Alo and The Daily Star. He pledged that the business community would stand by the political parties for democracy. Centre for Policy Dialogue distinguished fellow and Citizen’s Platform convener Debapriya Bhattacharya said that he had found the people across the country had a sense of insecurity and lack of trust in the government. He said that the government had lost its moral legitimacy to a large measure. ‘It’s now necessary for the civil society to show courage,’ Debapriya observed. NCP convener and former adviser to the interim government Nahid Islam alleged that the mob attack on the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star had backing from a section within the government. ‘Bangladesh isn’t now moving forward the way we aspired during the July uprising. It’s so unfortunate that the attackers have used OUR slogans…It was completely a planned attack,’ said Nahid. Nahid was one of the student leaders organising and leading the July uprising that ousted the authoritarian regime of Sheikh Hasina on August 5 and led to the formation of the interim government led by Professor Muhammad Yunus three days later. Referring to the recent murder of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, he said that it was a planned killing to derail the national polls slated for February 12, 2026. ‘We should compel the government to ensure a proper investigation into the murder,’ Nahid said. Nurul Kabir underlined the need for a greater unity to continue the people’s struggle for establishing a democratic society. ‘This is not the responsibility of the journalist community alone. We have to show the state that the thinking section of people is united,’ he added. Women rights activist Shireen Haque said that the overnight attack on the media outlets was horrible and the government silence was more horrifying. Transparency International Bangladesh executive director Iftekharuzzaman said that the mobocracy began within the bureaucracy and the state structure during this government following the July uprising in 2024. ‘The government is more responsible for resisting the mob violence and ensure security of the life and property of the people,’ he said, adding that the people’s life was now insecure. Former caretaker government adviser and civil society activist Rasheda K Choudhury vowed to stand by the move to resist all those behind the attacks on educational and cultural institutions. She deplored the inaction of the interim government against mob violence since its beginning. Ganosamhati Andolan chief coordinator Zonayed Saki said that the incidents of setting fire to the media outlets was an attack on democracy to foil the upcoming polls. He demanded an answer to the question as to why the government agencies were silent against the violence. Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami assistant secretary general Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair also condemned the attack on the media outlets. Journalist community leaders also spoke on the occasion protesting at the attack on the media outlets. The speakers at the event also condemned the recent lynching of Hindu youth Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh and the killing of a minor girl by setting their house afire in Lakhsmipur. The attendees observed a one-minute silence to show respect to Osman Hadi. All those present at the meeting later held a human chain on the Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue near the Pan Pacific Sonargaon Hotel protesting at the mob attacks on the media outlets and cultural institutions and also pressing for immediate steps to bring the perpetrators to book. On December 18 night, attackers vandalised and looted the offices of Prothom Alo at Karwan Bazar and The Daily Star on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue near Farmgate, eventually setting both offices ablaze. NOAB president AK Azad alleged that they did not get any help from the government agencies although they were communicated before the media outlets were set ablaze and looted. He expressed gratitude to all those who attended the event and expressed solidarity with them

title: ATTACKS ON MEDIA, CULTURAL INSTTS: 31 identified, 17 arrested: police
body: The authorities of the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star on Monday filed separate cases with the Tejgaon police station over the December 18 vandalism and arson on their offices following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police on the day informed the media that they had identified 31 people and arrested 17 of them for vandalism and arson on the two media houses. Tajgaon police station officer-in-charge Kya Swee Nue said that the Prothom Alo authorities filed the case against 400-500 unnamed people under the Anti-Terrorism Act, the Special Powers Act 1974, and the Cyber Security Ordinance over the attack at their office in the capital’s Karwanbazar area. He said that The Daily Star authorities filed a case against 350-400 unnamed people under the Anti-Terrorism Act and the Cyber Security Ordinance on Monday evening. Addressing a press briefing on Monday afternoon, DMP additional commis sioner for crime and operations, SN Md Nazrul Islam, said, ‘A total of 31 suspects have been identified in connection with the incident. We have arrested 17 suspects so far.’ Of them, 13 were held by local police stations, three by DMP’s Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime unit and the Detective Branch, he said. The arrestees are Md Naim, 26, Md Akash Ahmed Sagor, 28, Md Abdul Ahad, 18, Md Biplab, 22, Md Nazrul Islam Minhaz, 20, Md Jahangir, 28, Md Sohel Rana, 24, Md Hasan, 22, Rasel Shakil, 28, Md Abdul Barik Alamin, 31, Md Rashedul Islam, 25, Md Sohel Rana, 27, Shafiqul Islam, 34, Saidur Rahman, 25, Md Pranto Sikdar alias Faisal Ahmed Pranto, Abul Kashem, and Raju Hossain Chand. He said that they would continue operations to arrest the offenders. Replying to a query, Nazrul said that the intelligence had no information of a further probable attack on more media houses. ‘If we get such information, we will take strict measures,’ he added. On December 18 night, hundreds of attackers vandalised and looted the offices of the Prothom Alo at Karwanbazar and The Daily Star on Kazi Nazrul Islam Avenue, and then set fire to the offices. Veteran journalist and writer Nurul Kabir, the editor of New Age and the president of the Editors’ Council, was harassed when he went in front of The Daily Star office early December 19 to rescue the journalists and staff trapped in the office during the fire. Chhayanaut–Sanskriti Bhaban in the Dhanmondi area was attacked early Friday and the central office of cultural organisation Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigosthi on Topkhana Road in Dhaka was torched Friday evening. Providing further details, the additional commissioner said that one of the arrested suspects, Naim, was found in possession of Tk 50,000 in cash looted from the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star offices. ‘Using the looted money, he bought a television and a refrigerator, both of which we have seized,’ he said. When asked about whether the arrested people had any political affiliation, he said that the police had not yet investigated their political connections. Shahbagh police station officer-in-charge Md Moniruzzaman said that Udichi general secretary Mustafa Jamshed Anwer, popularly known as Jamshed Anwer Tapan, on Sunday afternoon filed a case with his police station against 10-15 unidentified attackers in connection with the arson on their central office. The police collected CCTV footage from the area and they were investigating to identify the miscreants, said the OC, adding that no one was arrested in the case till Monday evening. The case document stated that 10-15 unidentified miscreants on December 19 forcefully entered the Udichi office and carried out vandalism and arson attack on it. Publications and documents from the past 57 years were damaged in the attack, it said. Different national and international organizations on Monday condemned the attack and vandalism on the media outlets , demanding justice and measures to ensure security for all journalists. They also protested at the attack on Chhayanaut, a cultural and educational institutions, and lynching and setting fire to the body of Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh’s Bhaluka. ‘The targeting of politicians, activists, leading media houses, and cultural institutions, particularly at a time of heightened political sensitivity ahead of the 2026 national election, raises serious concerns about erosion of the rule of law and the shrinking space for free expression, civic discourse, and democratic participation,’ read a joint statement issued by the Access Now, the Bangladesh Legal Aid and Services Trust, the Human Rights Watch, the International Truth and Justice Project, the Journalists for Democracy in Sri Lanka and the Tech Global Institute. They also placed a six-point demand that included ensuring immediate and effective protection for journalists, media workers, media houses, cultural and intellectual institutions, and their practitioners across the country, including through the deployment of adequate security measures where credible threats exist. The demands also include conducting swift, independent, and transparent investigations into the attacks on Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, and Chhayanaut, as well as other journalists, media workers, and artists, and ensuring that all perpetrators, planners, and instigators are held accountable through due process of law. Leaders of Ganosamhati Andolan at a protest rally in Dhaka said that certain vested quarters were responsible for attacks on media and cultural organisation houses to foil the upcoming general election scheduled for February 12. July Sanskritik Andalan held a cultural rally in front of Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy Monday evening to protest at the attacks.

title: NCP leader shot at in Khulna city flat
body: A senior leader of Jatiya Sramik Shakti, the labour wing of the National Citizen Party, was shot in the ear at an apartment in the Sonadanga area of Khulna city on Monday, allegedly following a clash over the sharing of money from peddling drugs. The victim, Motaleb Shikder, 45, of the area, is the organising secretary of the labour organisation’s Khulna Divisional unit. Khulna Metropolitan Police’s additional commissioner for crimes, Mohamamd Rashidul Islam Khan, said that Motaleb sustained bullet injuries in his ear as ‘unidentified attackers’ shot at him, targeting his head at about 11:45am. ‘He was rushed to Khulna Medical College Hospital,’ he added. The senior police official denied disclosing more about the incident for the sake of the investigation. KMCH physician Mohamamd Mohiuddin said in the afternoon that the victim was out of danger but assumed that he suffered a mild brain hemorrhage. ‘The patient is now in the cabin. We will also conduct a CT scan,’ he added. Border Guard Bangladesh’s Battalion- 6 has tightened security along the bordering areas in Chuadanga and Meherpur to bar the perpetrators from entering India, said the battalion’s commanding officer, Lieutenant Colonel Md Nazmul Hasan. He also said that they received a photo of a man named Sourav Gazi, the suspect of opening fire at the NCP leader, from their headquarters. Several police officials, seeking anonymity, said that Motaleb was shot inside the apartment and the incident took place following a clash over sharing money from peddling drugs. They said that they had seized several bottles of liquor, instruments for consuming drugs like Yaba, and other substances that are used in doing immoral activities. They said that a woman rented the apartment and the victim used to live there identifying himself as her husband but the woman could not be found after the incident. NCP senior joint convener Samantha Sharmin, responding to a question whether she knew anything about any internal clash for which the incident occurred, said that she knew no details about the incident. ‘It is important to find out whether the bullet is from licensed or unlicensed arms. If anyone uses the name of NCP for their personal reasons, our demands will be the punishment of the perpetrators,’ she added. She urged the members of the law enforcement agencies to arrest whoever is involved in the incident.

title: Case filed over attack on Prothom Alo office
body: A case was filed with the Tejgaon police station on early Monday over the mob attack on Prothom Alo office on Thursday night following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi at a hospital in Singapore. Confirming the news, Tajgaon police station officer-in-charge Kya Swee Nue said that the Prothom Alo authorities filed the case against 400-500 unnamed people. He, however, said that The Daily Star authorities were yet to file any case over the attack on their office. Hundreds of unruly people reached the Prothom Alo office at about 11:00pm on Thursday and vandalised the office and set it on fire. After that the mob moved to the office of The Daily Star near Farmgate at about 12:15am on Friday. They vandalised glass panels, dragged out chairs, tables, and papers, and set them on fire while chanting slogans, including ‘Naray-e-Takbir’, ‘Allahu Akbar’, ‘Bharoter Dalalera-Hushiar, Sabdhan’.

title: Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma visits IVAC in Dhaka
body: Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma on Monday visited the Indian Visa Application Centre at Jamuna Future Park to take stock of the functioning of visa services. He also interacted with visa applicants, many of whom were applying for medical visas to travel to India for treatment. Given the ‘serious threats’ reported last week at the Indian High Commission and its installations in Bangladesh, the Indian High Commission had shut down IVAC operations for a day. The centre was later reopened, and all applicants whose appointment slots fell on that day were provided with early alternative slots. Several visa applicants are travelling to India for treatment of serious medical conditions. Keeping these humanitarian needs in mind, and despite the evolving security situation, the High Commission said it continues to operate visa centres in Dhaka, Khulna, Sylhet and Rajshahi. However, the IVAC in Chittagong remains temporarily shut following a mob attack at the entrance of the Assistant High Commission of India in Chittagong in December 18–19. During the incident, stone-pelting and threats to break the entrance created serious security concerns for AHCI officials and others residing within the same premises. During his visit to the IVAC, officials flagged problems related to the submission of a large number of fake documents, as well as disruptions caused by middlemen and touts who attempt to hack visa servers and create artificial traffic, depriving genuine applicants of appointment slots. The High Commissioner assured that these concerns would be raised with the relevant authorities in Bangladesh.

title: Russia wants Dhaka to reduce tension with Delhi
body: Russian Ambassador to Bangladesh Alexander Grigoryevich Khozin on Monday called for reducing tensions in Bangladesh to create a conducive environment before the next national election scheduled for February 12 next year. During his first interaction with a small group of journalists since his arrival in Dhaka, the Ambassador also highlighted the importance of reducing Bangladesh’s tensions with its neighbour India. ‘The sooner you reduce tensions with India, the better.’ The interactive session was held at the Embassy of the Russian Federation. Alexandra Khlevnoy, the director of the Russian House in Dhaka, among others, spoke at the session. Responding to a question, Ambassador Khozin said this (reducing tensions) is important for both countries and the entire South Asia region. Touching upon geopolitical implications, he said they have read statements of both Bangladesh and India, including comments of foreign affairs adviser Md Touhid Hossain, and said the two sides are trying to find a balanced way to reduce tensions as soon as possible. The Ambassador highlighted the role of India and Russia during 1971 and acknowledged India’s help in gaining Bangladesh’s independence - shoulder to shoulder together. He said they are not interfering with the two countries’ bilateral relations but they think it will be wise to find a way so that the tension does not escalate further from the current level. The Ambassador said the relations should be based on mutual trust and confidence. He welcomed the election date announced by the Election Commission and said they are expecting that the election will be held on time - February 12. ‘This (announcement of polls schedule) is a positive trend.’ Regarding sending election observers, the Ambassador said they are in touch with the Election Commission and they are waiting for the official invitation from the Election Commission. Ambassador Khozin said they are very much interested in creating such a positive, friendly and nonviolent and violation free atmosphere for the upcoming election. ‘This is very important for us.’ He said they are interested in reducing the tension in Bangladesh as it is very important for the election. The Ambassador said Bangladesh remains their second largest trade partner in South Asia. For the past three years, despite the existing global hindrances, he said, the bilateral turnover steadily exceeded 2 billion US dollars. He said Russia mainly exports machinery and agricultural products to Bangladesh and imports ready-made garments and textile goods. He said Russia has been continuously contributing to the food security of Bangladesh being one of its key sources of food and agricultural products, including wheat and fertilizers. In 2025 the export volume of Russian wheat to Bangladesh is 2 million tons. ‘This year we managed to achieve two times the increase in the supply of Russian fertilizers and mustard seeds to your country. We have also supplied almost 400 thousand tons of potash fertilizers to Bangladesh this year. Export of Russian veterinary vaccines has also increased by 25 percent,’ he said. ‘Our flagship development project is the construction of Bangladesh’s first nuclear energy facility – Rooppur nuclear power plant. ‘Rosatom’ State Corporation and its engineering division ASE are building the plant utilizing the most advanced engineering solutions, following the most stringent safety standards and environmental requirements,’ he said. Once commissioned, he said, the Rooppur NPP will contribute to the stability of national energy security, providing an additional 2,400 MW to the grid. Moreover,he said, it will create an entire hi-tech industry for the benefit of Bangladesh’s agriculture, health sector and engineering. ‘Another field of our bilateral cooperation is gas production. Since 2012, Russian company ‘Gazprom International’ has designed and built about 20 wells, including 7 on Bhola island,’ he said. Ambassador Khozin said a significant amount of natural gas has been discovered there. Gazprom is interested in continuing its operations in Bangladesh by participating in drilling, seismic survey and gas transportation projects. The company’s proposals for gas evacuation and exploration of new fields are under consideration. Ambassador Khozin said Russian exporters of LNG and crude oil are in the discussion to arrange the supplies of these products on a long-term basis that will meet the needs of Bangladesh facing shortage of energy resources required for the rapidly developing economy and daily communal activities. Besides, he said, Russian companies engaged in the sphere of renewable energy are ready to share their developments with the Bangladeshi partners, as well as to invest in this sector and open joint ventures. Ambassador Khozin said a skilled work force from Bangladesh is in demand in many countries, and Russia has joined this list.

title: BIUOA elects new committee
body: The 101-member biennial committee of the Bangladesh Inter-University Officers Association was elected for the 2026-2027 and 2027-2028 sessions at a hotel in the capital on Saturday. Khandaker Shafiqul Hasan Ratan, director (finance and accounts) of Bangladesh Medical University, has been elected president of the committee and Md Monowarul Islam Enam, additional registrar of Sher-e-Bangla Agricultural University, has been elected secretary general. Mohammad Mostafa Kamal Pasha, additional registrar of Bangladesh Medical University, has been elected chief patron of the committee and Md Abdullah Mridha, registrar of Gazipur Agricultural University, has been elected senior vice-president. Khandaker Nazmul Hasan, additional registrar of Kabi Nazrul Islam University, has been elected 1st joint secretary-general. Md Rezaur Rahman Mia Raju, deputy registrar of National University, has been elected organising secretary post. Currently, the number of government universities in Bangladesh is 59, and the Bangladesh Inter-University Officers Association has been formed with 101 members from the officers of all the universities, said a press release.

title: 31 identified, nine arrested over attacks on newspapers, cultural organisations
body: Police have identified 31 individuals from video footage in connection with recent attacks on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and two cultural organisations, with at least nine suspects arrested as of Monday morning. Of those detained, the identities of seven suspects have been immediately confirmed, chief adviser’s press wing said in a statement. The arrested are Md Kashem Faruk, Md Saidur Rahman, Rakib Hossain, Md Naim, Faisal Ahmed Pranto, Md Sohel Rana and Md Shafiqul Islam. Referring police, the statement said that the Counter Terrorism Unit and the Detective Branch have separately arrested two additional suspects, whose identities are currently being verified. Police and other law enforcement agencies informed chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Sunday that analysis of video footage from the incidents has so far led to the preliminary identification of 31 suspects linked to the attacks. In a separate development, three individuals have also been identified through video footage for attempting to create disorder near the residence of the Indian assistant high commissioner in Chattogram. According to chief adviser’s press wing, among those arrested, Kashem Faruk is a former student of Al-Jamia Al-Islamia Kasemul Ulum Madrassah in Bogura and a resident of Mohammadpur in Dhaka. Md Saidur Rahman hails from village Noakanda in Bhanga upazila of Faridpur district. Rakib Hossain, a resident of Sherpur district, was identified in video footage as an active participant in vandalism and arson attack on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star. Police said that he posted photographs of the damaged premises from his social media account and shared provocative content online. Md Naim, a resident of Kunipara in Dhaka’s Tejgaon area, was arrested in Chauddagram upazila of Cumilla with Tk 50,000 allegedly looted during the attacks. During preliminary interrogation, Naim admitted to looting a total of Tk 123,000, which he used to purchase a television and a refrigerator from Mohammadpur. Md Sohel Rana, arrested at Karwan Bazar railway line area in Dhaka, faces 13 cases in various police stations in the capital on charges, including drug-related offences. Another arrested from the same area, Md Shafiqul Islam, has two previous cases against him linked to arson and explosions involving crude bombs. On the night of December 18, hundreds of people attacked the media houses at Karwan Bazar and cultural institutions in Dhaka, following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, who was shot in the head in the capital on December 12 and died at a hospital in Singapore.

title: Man killed as boat hits bulkhead in Padma
body: A 57-year-old man was killed when a passenger boat collided with a sand-laden bulkhead in the River Padma in Chapainawabganj Sadar Upazila on Sunday afternoon. The deceased was identified as Md Bhikhu, son of late Abdus Salam of Rashiya Rustum Morler Para in Narayanpur Union under the upazila. According to eyewitnesses and family members, the passenger boat left Alimnagar Ghat for Narayanpur in the afternoon. As the vessel approached the ghat area at Charbaghdanga, it struck a bulkhead standing in the river, leaving Bhikhu critically injured. He was rescued and taken to the 250-bed Chapainawabganj District Hospital, where he died at about 7:45pm while undergoing treatment. On-duty physician Umme Habiba said that Bhikhu suffered injuries in his hands and chest in the accident and also had existing heart complications. Noor Alam, officer-in-charge of Chapainawabganj Sadar Model Police Station, said that an investigation was underway. ‘No complaint has yet been filed by the victim’s family. If a complaint is received, legal action will be taken following investigation,’ he added.

title: Attacks on The Daily Star, Prothom Alo protested in London
body: Journalists, media professionals, cultural activists, and members of the British Bangladeshi community protested at the recent attacks on The Daily Star and Prothom Alo and growing threats against journalists, after gathering at the historic Altab Ali Park in East London on Sunday. The demonstration, organised by Bangla-speaking journalists working in London, strongly condemned the vandalism, arson, looting, and alleged attempts to kill journalists during coordinated attacks on the two media houses in Bangladesh. Calling the attacks ‘unprecedented’ and ‘unacceptable,’ they termed it a ‘black day’ in the country’s media history. Speakers at the rally said that the attacked-media had long stood for independent, objective, and responsible journalism—principles that have increasingly made them targets of intimidation and violence. They demanded an immediate and transparent investigation into the attacks and accountability for those responsible. Addressing the protest, former BBC Bangla journalist Uday Shankar Das said that while media outlets in Bangladesh had faced attacks in the past, the recent violence marked a dangerous escalation. ‘Differences of opinion are natural in a democratic society, but resorting to organised violence is never acceptable,’ he said. Syed Nahas Pasha, vice-president of the Commonwealth Journalists Association, warned that the attacks went beyond institutional damage and directly endangered journalists’ lives. ‘This reflects a serious failure of governance,’ he said, adding that ensuring the safety of citizens and journalists is a fundamental responsibility of the state. Former general secretary of the London Bangla Press Club, Muhammad Abdus Sattar, said journalists are not intimidated by the attacks. ‘Bangladeshis in the diaspora stand united. We do not want forces that oppose the spirit of the Liberation War to gain ground in Bangladesh,’ he said. The protest, moderated by broadcast journalist and writer Bulbul Hasan, was attended by senior journalists, freedom fighters, writers, and community leaders, including Prothom Alo UK correspondent Saidul Islam, Nilufar Hasan, Urmee Mazher, Abu Musa Hasan, freedom fighter Luqueman Hussain, Hamid Mohammad, Ansar Ahmed Ullah, Sarwar E Alam, A S M Masum, Rupi Amin, and SM Tanvir Ahmed. Holding banners and chanting slogans in defence of press freedom, participants said the gathering was an expression of solidarity with journalists in Bangladesh and a call to protect independent media as a cornerstone of democracy. Meanwhile, the London Bangla Press Club issued a statement condemning the attacks on Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, and other media outlets, editors, and journalists in Bangladesh. Expressing deep concern, the Press Club said the arson, vandalism, and assaults constituted a direct attack on press freedom, freedom of expression, and the people’s right to information, posing a serious threat to the country’s democratic progress.

title: Dhaka becomes 3rd most polluted city with AQI score of 250
body: Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked third on the list of cities with the worst air quality with an AQI score of 250 at about 9:50am on Monday morning. On Monday, Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘very unhealthy’ referring to an alarming healthy threat, according to the air quality index. When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 50 and 100, air quality is considered ‘moderate’, usually sensitive individuals should consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion, between 101 and 150, air quality is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, between 150 and 200 is ‘unhealthy’, between 201 and 300 is said to be ‘very unhealthy’, while a reading of 301+ is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks to residents. India’s Delhi, Egypt’s Cairo and again India’s Kolkata cities respectively occupied the first, second and third spots on the list, with AQI scores of 284, 261, and 205 respectively. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon. As per World Health Organisation, air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, mainly due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: Shab-e-Meraj to be held on Jan 16
body: The holy Shab-e-Meraj will be observed in the country on the night of January 16 (Friday). The National Moon Sighting Committee took the decision at a meeting held at the Islamic Foundation office at Baitul Mukarram on Sunday evening. Religious affairs adviser AFM Khalid Hossain chaired the meeting. On the night of 26th Rajab every year, Muslims observe Shab-e-Meraj when Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) embarked on a special journey to meet Allah. In the journey, the Prophet travelled on the ‘Buraq’ to Heaven where Allah gave him some instructions to take back to the faithful regarding the details of prayers.

title: EU supporting 7 citizen election observer groups
body: The European Union has said it is supporting seven Bangladeshi citizen election observer organisations as part of its efforts to promote free, fair and participatory elections and strengthen public trust in the electoral process ahead of the country’s upcoming polls and referendum on February 12. With the support of the EU, the European Partnership for Democracy is helping these organisations develop observation checklists and templates, monitor online gender-based violence, and much more, said the embassy on Sunday. The union said an independent and strong election commission is the key to any successful election in all democratic countries. The Bangladesh Election Commission has built its human capacity and is acting now to ensure transparency and efficiency before, during and after the elections. With support from the European Union, the International Foundation for Electoral Systems is providing technical assistance to the BEC to run smooth, fair, and credible elections.

title: Tarique urges unity of pro-democracy parties
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Sunday called upon all political parties that believe in democracy, including the BNP, to remain united in the interest of safeguarding the country’s democratic future. ‘The coming days will not be easy for us. The country’s economic condition has collapsed, and different forms of anarchy have already begun or are being instigated in various parts of the country,’ he said, urging all to remain vigilant. Tarique was virtually addressing a programme organised in Bogura to inaugurate a digital memorial in remembrance of the martyrs of the July movement at Shaheed Titu Auditorium in the city, with Bogura district BNP president Rezaul Karim Badsha in the chair. Calling upon all to work hard from their respective positions to rebuild the country, he said millions of people are becoming unemployed and sustainable employment opportunities must be created. ‘The farmers are in distress. They are not getting fair prices for their produces. Syndicates in the market system must be eliminated so that people can easily purchase daily necessities at fair prices,’ he said, adding that ensuring these issues would require collective efforts. Tarique said that after 1975, Ziaur Rahman rescued the country from the brink of destruction, while BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia later led the country out of autocratic rule and towards development. ‘Once again, the soldiers of these two leaders have been given the opportunity to rebuild the country from the brink of destruction,’ he said. Referring to Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi, Tarique said the July martyr stood firmly in favour of democracy and believed in electoral politics. ‘If we truly wish to honour Shaheed Osman Hadi, the July martyrs and the freedom fighters of 1971, we must work together to establish peace and take the country forward,’ he added. BNP central information and technology affairs secretary AKM Wahiduzzaman, BNP chairperson’s advisers AKM Mahbubur Rahman and Helaluzzaman Talukder Lalu, and former lawmakers Kazi Rafiqul Islam, Golam Mohammad Siraj, Mosharraf Hossain, Saiful Islam and Ali Azgar Hena also addressed the programme virtually.

title: BSF member detained in Lalmonirhat for intrusion
body: The Border Guard Bangladesh detained a constable of India’s Border Security Force for entering Bangladesh territory illegally through the Dahagram-Angarpota border at Patgram upazila in Lalmonirhat district early Sunday. The BGB 51 Battalion detained Ved Prakash, 35, a member of the 174/Arjun BSF camp, at Dangapara of Dahagram union as he entered Bangladesh violating the border law at about 4:00am on Sunday, according to BGB officials. He crossed the zero line and entered 200 yards inside Bangladesh while chasing an Indian cow and was detained by a BGB Angarpota patrol team and brought to the camp. The BGB recovered one shotgun, two rounds of bullets, one wireless and an android phone from him. Rezanur Rahman Reza, a resident of Dahagram union, said that as Dahagram is surrounded by India, BSF members often carried out provocative activities. ‘Earlier in 2024, the BSF had erected a barbed wire fence in no-man’s land and hung large liquor bottles on the fence with the intension of provocation,’ Rezanur said. BGB Angarpota camp Subedar Ayub Ali said that when a BSF member entered Bangladesh early hours, BGB members detained him and brought him to the camp. ‘The matter has been reported to BGB senior officials,’ he added. BGB 51 Battalion commanding officer Lieutenant Colonel Selim Al Deen said that the detained BSF member in preliminary interrogation claimed that he mistakenly entered Bangladesh territory while chasing cow smugglers in dense fog. Selim said that the BGB handed him over to the BSF along with the seized arms following a BGB-BSF flag meeting.

title: Ex-Jhalakati mayor from AL arrested
body: Former Jhalokathi municipality mayor Afzal Hossain Rana was arrested in the district town while he was going to the deputy commissioner’s office to renew his firearm licence. On Sunday morning, the Detective Branch of the district police arrested him while he was leaving the DC office after completing the licence renewal process. Sadar Police oficer-in-charge Imtiaz Ahmed confirming the matter said that he was sent to jail as an accused in a case under the explosive act after being produced in court around 4:30pm. Afzal Hossain Rana served as the organising secretary and joint general secretary of Jhalokathi district Awami League. He served as the Jhalokathi municipality mayor for one full term. Jhalokathi DB sources said that after his arrest, Afzal Hossain Rana was taken to the DB office and was handed over to the Sadar police later around 3:00pm. District detective police inspector Touhiduzzaman also confirmed the matter.

title: Hop Lun launches Foundation to Future
body: Leading global apparel manufacturer Hop Lun has officially launched ‘Foundation to Future’, an education sponsorship programme aimed at helping workers resume their learning journey and build skills beyond the workplace. The pilot phase of the programme was launched on December 18, 2025, at Hop Lun Fashion, with 35 workers selected for the first cohort. The programme is part of Hop Lun’s broader #SHECAN initiative and aligns with the company’s Wheel of Wellbeing framework, which recognizes education as a key pillar of employee well-being and personal development. ‘Foundation to Future’ is designed for workers who have completed Grade 5 and wish to continue their studies through Grade 8. Eligibility criteria include a minimum of two years of service with Hop Lun, consistent attendance and discipline records, and satisfactory job performance. The selection process also considered participants’ eagerness to learn, positive attitude, and workplace engagement. The program focuses on five core subjects—Bangla, Basic English, Mathematics, General Science, and Social Science—aimed at strengthening literacy, numeracy, comprehension, and confidence. Classes will be held twice a week over the next six to eight months. TalenTracker Limited, an experienced HR consultancy specialising in workforce training and development, will train the workers. The programme includes a pre-assessment in December 2025, classes beginning in January 2026, a mid-term review in March 2026, and final assessments between June and August 2026. A graduation ceremony is planned for the final quarter of 2026. ‘At Hop Lun, we believe our people are our greatest asset,’ said Nishantha Mohottige, Country Head of Hop Lun Bangladesh. ‘Foundation to Future is an investment in the dreams and potential of our workers, enabling them to build brighter futures for themselves and their families.’ Mohammed Fakhruzzaman, general manager at Hop Lun Fashion, said the programme reflects the company’s belief in the transformative power of education. ‘We are not just helping workers pass exams; we are helping them discover their capabilities and build confidence in what they can achieve.’ For participants like Amena Khatun, an operator at Hop Lun, the programme represents a second chance. ‘I completed Class 5 many years ago and always dreamed of studying further, but life took me in a different direction,’ Amena shared. ‘This programme isn’t just about learning English or Math—it’s about believing in myself again. I want to show my children that education matters and that it’s never too late to learn.’ The Foundation to Future programme reflects Hop Lun’s people-centric approach and long-term investment in its workforce, recognising workers not just as employees but as individuals with aspirations and opportunities to grow.

title: 2 more die of dengue, 194 fresh cases
body: Health officials on Sunday said that they recorded 194 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts, killing at least two persons in the past 24 hours. ‘We recorded deaths of two dengue patients in 24 hours ending at 8:00am on Sunday,’ a spokesman of Directorate General of Health Services said, adding that his office simultaneously recorded 194 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts during the same period. Out of the 194 fresh cases, 32 were hospitalised in Barishal division, 45 in Chattogram, 26 in Dhaka division excluding the capital, 22 in Dhaka South City Corporation and 28 in Dhaka North City Corporation areas, 23 in Khulna, five in Mymensingh, 12 in Rajshahi and one in Rangpur division, a DGHS statement said. Since the start of the dengue onslaughts, Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 412 deaths while the disease inflicted 101,791. The dengue last year claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in the country.
