title: River erosion sparks alarm in Kushtia
body: RESIDENTS of Kumarakhali municipality in Kushtia are gripped by fear as rapid riverbank erosion along the River Gorai threatens homes, farmland, and local infrastructure of this densely populated area. As a vital distributary to the Ganges (Padma), The Gorai flows through this municipality and upazila town, providing a lifeline for nearly 60,000 residents. A one-kilometre stretch between Tebaria’s Shahid Golam Kibria Bridge and Agrakunda in Wards 8 and 9 remains unprotected by embankments. In the past week alone, approximately 30 bighas of farmland and riverbanks have been lost, with an additional 50 bighas of cultivable land and the homes of at least 300 families now at imminent risk. Locals blame the accelerated erosion on years of neglected river management in the Tebaria-Agrakunda area. Farmers report that newly formed sandbanks are redirecting water flows toward the banks, intensifying erosion and destroying crops. Residents are urging authorities to construct permanent embankments to protect homes, roads, mosques, temples, and other vital infrastructure. Madina Khatun, 62, a long-time resident of Tebaria, described the alarming speed of the collapse, saying, ‘I have lived here for 30 years, but I have never seen the riverbank erode like this. Every few moments, the bank collapses, and we fear our homes may be swept away’. She added that receding water levels have exposed sandbanks mid-river, while strong currents continue to undermine the banks. Officials from Kushtia municipality have inspected the affected areas. Executive engineer Rashidul Islam said that no government funds are currently available for embankment construction or erosion control, though the issue has been forwarded to higher authorities. Upazila Nirbahi Officer Farzana Akhtar said that discussions with municipal officials are ongoing to promptly implement interventions when necessary. The incident highlights long-standing vulnerabilities in the Gorai River basin, where seasonal flow reductions, upstream diversions including those linked to the Farakka Barrage, and natural channel migration contribute to erosion risks. Experts emphasize the need for integrated river management, including dredging, revetments, and community participation, to protect this critical waterway and the livelihoods it supports in south-western Bangladesh.

title: S Alam Group sued for embezzling Tk 62.43b from Janata Bank
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission on Sunday filed three cases against three companies of S Alam Group for taking undue benefits and embezzling of Tk 62.43 billion from Janata Bank’s Agrabad branch of Chattogram as loans. The accused in the cases include the group’s chairman Saiful Alam Masud, his wife Farzana Parveen, his brother Abdus Samad and officials of Janata Bank and various concerns of the group, totalling 95 people. The three cases were filed at the ACC integrated district office in Chattogram by its deputy director Sirajul Islam, deputy director Subel Ahmed of the ACC Chattogram office confirmed. According to the cases, the accused persons in connivance with each other embezzled Tk 62.43 billion by taking loans against S Alam Vegetable Oil Limited, S Alam Cold Rolled Steel Mill and S Alam Trading Company Private Limited. All the companies are sister concerned of S Alam Group. According to the first case, S Alam Vegetable Oil Limited allegedly embezzled Tk 20.03 billion including interest and principal amount. The alleged irregularities took place between September 13, 2005 and March 6 of this year. There are 32 accused in the case. including managing director of the group Saiful Alam Masud, director Farzana Parveen and 28 officials of Janata Bank, Agrabad branch. According to the 2nd case, S Alam Cold Rolled Steels Limited embezzled Tk 22.97 billion, including interest and principal amount of the loans. The alleged embezzlement was taken place from February 23, 2010 to April 6, 2025. There are another 32 accused, including Saiful Alam Masud, six officials of the company and 25 officials of Janata Bank. The third case was filed over the embezzlement of Tk 19.42 billion including interest and principal amount of the loans taken in the name of S Alam Trading Company Private Limited. The alleged irregularities were taken place from May 10, 2005 to April 6, 2025. There are 31 accused in the case, including Saiful Alam Masud, Farzana Parveen, five family members and 26 officials of Janata Bank PLC. The accused have been charged under sections 409, 420 and 109 of the Penal Code, section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and section 4(2) of the Money Laundering Prevention Act, 2012. On December 17, the commission filed two more cases against two companies under S Alam Group over embezzlement of Tk 30.85 billion through loans.

title: Court imposes travel ban on Hasina, 16 others
body: A Dhaka court on Sunday imposed travel ban on 17 people, including ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former roads and bridges minister Obaidul Quader, in a corruption case filed by the Anti-Corruption Commission. Dhaka metropolitan senior special judge court vacation bench judge Mohammad Abdullah Al Mamun passed the order following a petition submitted by the commission. The petition was filed by ACC assistant director Tanzil Hasan. Those barred from leaving the country include former ministers Amir Hossain Amu, Anisul Haque, Tofail Ahmed and Khandaker Mosharraf Hossain, former state minister MA Mannan, secretary MAN Siddique, additional secretary Md Faruk Jalil, deputy secretary Md Shafiqul Karim, engineer Md Firoz Iqbal, Ibne Alam Hasan, Md Aftab Hossain Khan. Md Abdus Salam and CNS Limited managing director Munir Uz Zaman Chowdhury, along with directors Selina Chowdhury and Ikram Iqbal. According to the case statement, Computer Network Systems Limited was given a contract in 2016 to collect tolls through a single-source tender, cancelling a previously valid tender without negotiations with other organisations. Under the arrangement, CNS Limited was given the work order on a service charge basis of 17.75 per cent of the total toll collected, excluding VAT and IT. As a result, the company received bills amounting to more than Tk 489 crore. In contrast, the cost of assigning toll collection jointly to MBEL-ATT during the 2010-2015 period on the same bridge was slightly over Tk 15 crore. The commission filed the case on October 12 against 17 people, including Sheikh Hasina, over the alleged irregularities.

title: Election campaign materials removed from DSCC area
body: All types of materials related to election campaigning for the 13th national parliament election and referendum have been removed from the Dhaka South City Corporation area. A public notice was issued on December 2 requesting concerned organisations, individuals and institutions to remove all unauthorised banners, festoons, posters, advertisements, signboards and election leaflets from areas under the jurisdiction of the DSCC. In this connection, the removal of all unauthorised advertisements and election campaign materials from all wards began on December 8. On December 11, the election commission announced the schedule for the 13th national parliament election and referendum. In line with the election commission’s directive to remove all election campaign materials within 48 hours of the announcement, the city corporation successfully removed almost all such materials within the stipulated time. The process is still ongoing. The corporation has urged all concerned to comply with the code of conduct for parliamentary elections to protect the environment and preserve the beauty of the city. However, if anyone places any unauthorised election materials again in the DSCC area, the central control room should be informed by dialling 02223386014.

title: Left leader Abdul Haque’s death anniv today
body: The 30th death anniversary of eminent left leader Abdul Haque will be observed today. The National Democratic Front chalked out elaborate programme at several places across the country to mark the day, said a press release of the party. Abdul Haque was born at Jashore town’s Kharki on December 23, 1920. His father Shah Muhammad Abul Khayer was a pir, Islamic preacher, and mother Amena Khatun was a housewife. Without completing his master’s degree at Kolkata University, he joined Communist Party in India. He played a key role in the peasant conference at Bangaon in 1941. He also took part in the Tebhaga Movement and many other movements in the country and wrote several books as well. He died on December 22, 1995.

title: Biman launches body cameras for all airlines
body: Biman Bangladesh Airlines on Sunday started using body-worn cameras to monitor the baggage handling activities of every international flight arriving at the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in the capital. The decision to implement the body-worn camera security system was taken with the aim of protecting passenger baggage, bringing transparency to the luggage handling process, and identifying the relevant station or individuals, also said a press release, issued by the airlines on the day. Earlier, Biman has introduced the system since June 2024 for the staff engaged in baggage delivery activities in its own flights to strengthen the baggage protection and luggage handling procedures. Following the positive results, the press release read, this body-worn camera security system is now being provided to all international airlines that use Biman’s ground handling services. Biman Bangladesh Airlines’ director (customer services) Badrul Hassan Liton officially inaugurated the expansion of the services on Sunday. He said that this body-worn camera security service will ensure transparency and accountability at every step of luggage handling. ‘This will not only increase passenger confidence but also enhance the professionalism of our staff,’ he said, adding, ‘We firmly believe that this initiative will further enhance the quality of our overall passenger service.’ International flight safety and security is the top priority, the release continued, while security authorities follow strict policy at all airports across the world. Due to concerns about carrying prohibited and contraband items, security authorities at various airports remove prohibited items by breaking locks, cutting chains, or cutting off parts of the luggage while searching passengers’ luggage. As per the international security protocols, prior permission from passengers or airlines is not required to take such security measures. The release said that unfortunately many passengers arriving from abroad entirely blamed Biman Bangladesh Airlines or the Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh for such baggage deductions. Besides, there are also allegations against some dishonest quarters for being involved in these incidents.

title: Steady rise in internet use: BBS
body: There has been a steady rise in internet use in recent years as internet usage at individual level rose from 44.5 per cent in 2023 to 48.9 per cent this year. At the household level, however, technology access appears broader, said the recent ICT Access and Use Survey 2025-26 (1st quarter, July-September) report conducted by the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics. The survey shows that 98.9 per cent of households have at least one mobile phone, and 72.4 per cent now own a smartphone. Television is available in 58.9 per cent of households, radio use has fallen to 15.1 per cent, and only 9.1 per cent of homes own a computer. Electricity coverage is almost universal, reaching 98.9 per cent of households. There has been urban-rural divide as smart phone ownership is far higher in towns and cities, where 80.8 per cent of households have at least one device, compared with 68.8 per cent in rural areas. The BBS survey covered around 61,632 households across the country aiming to inform national ICT policy as well as international platforms, including the International Telecommunication Union and the SDG Tracker. According to the findings, online services increasingly shape access to education, healthcare, finance and government support. By the end of September this year, 48.9 per cent of people aged five and above were direct internet users. At the household level, just over half of homes—about 56.2 per cent—had at least one internet user in the July-September period, according to the report. At the individual level, the survey found that 80.6 per cent of people use mobile phones, while 56.5 per cent own their own handsets. Usage among men and women is almost equal, 80.9 per cent for men and 78.8 per cent for women. But, handset ownership and internet access show a gender gap. About 63.2 per cent of men own a mobile phone compared with 52.8 per cent of women. Internet use follows a similar pattern, with 51.2 per cent of men online compared with 46.3 per cent of women.

title: Two more arrested amid protests against lynching Hindu youth
body: Two more arrests have been made for their suspected involvement in the lynching of a Hindu youth in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh, allegedly for hurting religious sentiments by making derogatory remarks about Prophet Muhammad. Different student and labour bodies on Sunday staged demonstrations in Dhaka and elsewhere, demanding justice for victim Dipu Chandra Das. A team of Detective Branch of police on Saturday night arrested Ashiqur Rahman, 25, and Qayyum, 25, from the upazila’s Kashar area in the upazila’s Habirbari union, said a DB press release. With the two new arrests, 12 people have been arrested in connection with the Dipu Chandra Das murder case filed by the victim’s brother. Mymensingh additional superintendent of police Abdullah Al Mamun said that the police and the Rapid Action Battalion were conducting drives to arrest the involved persons. Meanwhile, central leaders of some garment workers organisations on Sunday at a protest rally in front of the Pioneer Knit Composite Factory in Bhaluka said that the interim government and factory owners must take responsibilities of the gruesome murder of Dipu. Garment worker leaders Mushrefa Mishu, Joly Talukder, Shabnam Hafiz, Taslima Akther Buty, Satyajit Das and others spoke at the rally demanding exemplary punishments of the killers. Dhaka University unit of Jatiyatabadi Chatra Dal, the student wing of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, brought out a protest procession from the Teacher-Student Centre on the campus against recent violence. Marching through different roads, Chatra Dal ended the procession with a brief rally at the Anti-Terrorism Raju Memorial Sculpture, demanding justice for all mob violence victims, including Dipu and Ayesha, a daughter of a BNP leader who was burnt to death on the late night of December 19 in Lakshmipur. Jatiya Sramik Shakti, labour wing of National Citizen Party, also held a rally at Shahbagh demanding the immediate arrest of and exemplary punishment for the ‘mob attackers’. Expressing deep concern, Ain o Salish Kendra issued a statement condemning the ‘mob attacks’ and death of Dipu and Ayesha. The Hindu youth, Dipu Chandra Das, 25, a worker at Pioneer Knit Composite Factory, was lynched and his body was burnt after hanging it from a tree branch near his workplace in Dubaliapara area in the upazila on December 18 night. Dipu’s younger brother Apu Das said that Dipu used neither an Android phone nor any social media platforms, while the Rapid Action Battalion said that they found no evidence that Dipu Chandra Das made any derogatory remarks about Prophet Muhammad.

title: Nine airguns seized in Moulvibazar
body: Rapid Action Battalion recovered nine airguns from an abandoned homestead at Kamalganj upazila in Moulvibazar early Sunday. RAB-9 media officer KM Shahidul Islam confirmed the news of recovering nine airguns to New Age. He said that a patrol team of the battalion came to know that something suspicious was there in a box inside the bushes next to an abandoned home of Purba Jalalpur village of Adampur union under Kamalganj upazila. ‘Based on the secret information, the battalion team recovered nine airguns wrapped with a jute sack from the spot at 12:30am,’ the RAB officer said. He said that they suspected that the airguns might have been collected for conducting sabotage. ‘The seized airguns were handed over to the Kamalganj police station after filing a general diary in this regard,’ the RAB officer said in the afternoon, adding that investigation was underway to identify the owner of the airguns.

title: Deadline to appeal against death verdict expires for Hasina, Kamal
body: The 30-day deadline for deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal to appeal against the death sentences awarded by the International Crimes Tribunal-1 has expired. The deadline ended on December 17, 30 days after the tribunal delivered the verdict on November 17 over crimes against humanity committed during the July uprising. The International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973 requires an appeal to be filed within 30 days of conviction and bars appeals after the expiry of that period. Both Hasina and Kamal are absconding and are believed to be staying in India. ICT prosecutor Mizanul Islam said that Hasina and Kamal lost their rights to appeal as they neither surrendered nor were arrested to file appeals within the stipulated time. Meanwhile, former inspector general of police Chowdhury Abdullah Al Mamun, who received a reduced five-year jail sentence after testifying as a state witness, filed an appeal on December 17, the last date for filing the appeal. He sought his acquittal, arguing that he had made a truthful disclosure and assisted the tribunal in reaching its decision, and this is why he should be acquitted of the charges according to the ICT and other laws of the land. On December 15, the chief prosecutor filed an appeal seeking the death penalty for Hasina and Kamal on the charge of provocation, challenging the tribunal’s sentence of imprisonment until death on that count. The tribunal found that Hasina provoked violence by referring to student protesters as ‘Razakars’ during a press conference at Ganabhaban on July 14, 2024. Hasina and Kamal were convicted on three counts of crimes against humanity for their role in the July 2024 uprising. They were sentenced to death on two counts and to life imprisonment on one count related to provocation. Prosecutor Gazi Monwar Hossain Tamim said that the prosecution had asked the Appellate Division to enhance the sentence on the provocation charge to death. The tribunal observed that Hasina’s remarks and her instruction to Dhaka University vice-chancellor Maksud Kamal triggered violence on university campuses across the country. It held that the provocation led to the killing of student coordinator Abu Sayeed in Rangpur on July 16, 2024. The tribunal also sentenced Hasina and Kamal to death for ordering the use of lethal force against protesters, including aerial surveillance, during conversations with Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh and Hasanul Haq Inu. According to the verdict, several students were killed during incidents in Chankharpool and Ashulia. ‘Since convict Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman Khan Kamal are on the run, the sentence of death as awarded above shall be executed after their arrest or surrender, as the case may be,’ the tribunal said in the verdict. ‘The convict accused be at liberty to prefer appeal to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court against the order of conviction and sentence within 30 days from today in connection with the provisions under Section 21 of the Act,’ the verdict said.

title: Next govt must ensure press freedom: senior journalists
body: Editors and senior journalists on Sunday demanded that the next government must ensure that the media feels safe and free to carry out critical journalism for good governance. Independent media is the only institution that tells the truth, which is crucial for a government to ensure good governance in the country, they said. They made the remarks while speaking at a views exchange programme organised by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party before the homecoming of BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman after more than 17 years of his exile in the United Kingdom. Tarique is expected to arrive in Dhaka from London on December 25. Welcoming the journalists at the event at a hotel in the capital Dhaka, BNP standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed said that although politicians held the driving seats in society, they must be guided by journalists to ensure social stability. Criticising the arson attacks on the Dhaka offices of the Bangla daily Prothom Alo and the English daily The Daily Star on December 18 night, Salahuddin slammed the weakness of the interim government in controlling mob attacks at several places in the country. He said that his party also slammed the attack on the English daily New Age editor, Nurul Kabir, also the president of the Editors’ Council, in front of The Daily Star office near Farmgate in the capital early December 19 during Nurul Kabir’s attempt to enter the Daily Star premises to rescue its journalists trapped there during the violence. Salahuddin said that the media would enjoy full freedom of constructive journalism if voters elect the BNP to power. Manabzamin editor-in-chief Matiur Rahman Chowdhury said that Tarique was returning to Bangladesh at a time when security breaches were a big concern. He said, ‘No government in the past five decades supported full freedom of the media. It would be great if the BNP implements 25 per cent of its promises about media freedom.’ Echoing Matiur, The Daily Star editor Mahfuz Anam said that the country was currently in a ‘very devastating situation’ with many collapsed institutions. He demanded that the media must feel the fresh air in the quest for a reformed Bangladesh. He requested the other journalists to question why the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star were attacked and raise their voice for the freedom to express critical thinking. ‘Critical journalism is not only for freedom of journalism, but it is a chance for good governance,’ Mahfuz said, adding that if the ruling party did not accept criticism, it would make mistakes and would repeat those mistakes. Prothom Alo editor Matiur Rahman said that there was a vacuum in political leadership. ‘The next general elections must be held credibly, and the media must keep surveillance on what the next government will do,’ he said. BBC Bangla senior journalist Kadir Kollol said, ‘A sense of terror is engulfing the media, and we must be freed from this situation.’ Former Jai Jai Din editor Shafik Rehmen, BNP senior joint secretary general Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, BNP media cell convener Moudud Hossain Alamgir Pavel, Newspaper Owners’ Association of Bangladesh president and Bangla daily Samakal publisher AK Azad, Editors’ Council general secretary and Banik Barta editor Dewan Hanif Mahmud, The Daily Star consultant editor and former Media Reform Commission chief Kamal Ahmed, Press Club president and Bangla daily Kaler Kantho editor Hasan Hafiz, broadcaster Channel 24 executive director Zahirul Alam and freelance journalist Kazi Jesin, among others, also spoke, at the event.

title: ICT defers decision on charges against Hasina, 11 army officers to Dec 23
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Sunday deferred until December 23 its order on whether crimes against humanity charges will be framed against deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan, her former defence adviser retired major general Tarique Siddique, 11 army officers and three senior police officers. The 17 accused in the case are accused of superior command responsibility for enforced disappearances carried out through abduction, detention and torture at the Task Force for Interrogation of the Rapid Action Battalion headquarters in Dhaka. Sunday was scheduled for giving the tribunal’s decision, but the newly appointed defence lawyer for the army officers, Munsurul Haque Chowdhury, sought time to place his legal submissions in support of a petition seeking their discharge. The tribunal, chaired by Justice Md Golam Mortuza Mozumder, allowed him two days to submit his arguments before delivering its order on December 23. Besides Hasina, Asaduzzaman and Tarique, the 11 army officers were serving as assistant directors general for operations at Rapid Action Battalion and the three police officers were serving as director generals of RAB at the time of the alleged offences during the Hasina-led Awami League regime. The 10 detained army officers in the case are Colonel KM Azad, Colonel Abdullah Al Momen, Lieutenant Colonel Mashiur Rahman Jewel, Brigadier General Kamrul Hasan, Brigadier General Md Mahbub Alam, Brigadier General Tofayel Mostafa Sarwar, Lieutenant Colonel Anwar Latif Khan, Brigadier General Md Jahangir Alam, Lieutenant Colonel Sarwar Bin Kashem and Lieutenant Colonel Saiful Islam Suman. The absconding accused army officer is retired Lieutenant Colonel Muhammad Khairul Islam, a former RAB intelligence chief who is now living in the United Kingdom. The three former police officers accused in the case are also former RAB director generals during the AL regime. They are Benazir Ahmed, who is also a former inspector general of police, Khurshid Hossain and barrister Harun-or-Rashid. On October 9, chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam submitted formal charges against the 17 accused. During the hearing, Munsurul Haque Chowdhury argued that the duty roster of the ADG (Operations) did not assign responsibility for abduction, detention, or torture, while chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam countered that enforced disappearances were carried out under their command authority and such crimes are not kept in documents. During the earlier hearing, the tribunal observed that it had found prima facie grounds to frame charges in the case against the 17 accused linked to the Task Force Interrogation, noting that the accused could not evade command responsibility for the enforced disappearances committed under their authority, with their knowledge and continuity of the crimes. On December 3, the tribunal began hearing the case against the 17 accused for the enforced disappearance of 11 victims between May 23, 2016 and April 14, 2020 at RAB-1’ secret detention cell popularly known as TFI cell. The accused in the case are linked to the enforced disappearance of 11 victims, including Supreme Court lawyer and executed war crimes convict Mir Quasem Ali’s son Mir Ahmad Bin Quasem Arman, Tajul Islam Suman, physician Ashik Ul Akbar, Mahmudul Hasan, Nur-e-Alam, Md Shariatullah, Md Rajibul Islam, Saiful Islam, Rizwanul Mahmud Anik, Md Foyez and Masrur Anwar Chowdhury, according to the charges. On December 18, the same tribunal framed charges against Hasina, Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and 11 other serving and retired army officials for their alleged involvement in committing crimes against humanity, including abduction, detention and torture of 26 people with dissenting views against the Awami League.

title: Suspects identified in arson attacks on Prothom Alo, The Daily Star
body: Law enforcement agencies have identified several individuals involved in the vandalism and arson attacks on the offices of two newspapers, the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star. Religious affairs adviser AFM Khalid Hossain, while talking to reporters at the Secretariat on Sunday, described taking the law into one’s own hands as a serious impediment to good governance. ‘We have already identified the individuals responsible for setting fire to the offices of the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and have taken steps to arrest them and bring them to justice,’ he said. The adviser said that the act was utterly condemnable and heinous, and that mob justice would not be tolerated. Meanwhile, a meeting of the Election Commission with law enforcement agencies on Sunday addressed the attacks on the two newspapers. Following the discussion, election commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah said that at least 20 individuals involved in the attacks had been identified and legal action had been taken against them. He said that those responsible would face appropriate consequences. Sanaullah explained that the attacks occurred during a period of national mourning following the death of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi, which opportunistic groups exploited to commit acts of vandalism, at times overwhelming law enforcement personnel. ‘The message is clear. Such incidents will not be allowed to recur,’ he said. The religious affairs adviser also confirmed that he had requested the home affairs adviser to take action against those involved in the killing of a man in Mymensingh, whose body was subsequently set on fire. Dipu Chandra Das, a local garment worker, was beaten to death by a mob over alleged hurting religious sentiments in Bhaluka Upazila on Thursday night. On the state of law and order, Khalid Hossain said that the situation was now under control. ‘Although violent incidents continue to occur, we remain hopeful that the upcoming elections will take place on schedule in a free, fair, inclusive, and festive environment,’ he added. Regarding the attacks on the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star, the adviser said that efforts were underway to prevent such incidents in the future. The attacks followed Osman Hadi’s death in Singapore, with an organised group targeting media offices in Dhaka on Thursday night. On the same night, Chhayanaut was also attacked and set on fire. The religious affairs adviser emphasised that while comments made from abroad were beyond the government’s control, arson attacks and the killing of individuals by burning were unacceptable and would be treated as heinous crimes, with perpetrators held accountable. Asked whether the simultaneous attacks indicated an intelligence lapse, the adviser declined to label it as such directly, highlighting the difficulty of predicting the precise direction of such violent acts.

title: ATTACK ON MEDIA, CULTURAL INSTTS: None held, protests continue
body: None was arrested following the vandalism and arson attacks on two media houses, The Daily Star and the Prothom Alo, and the offices of cultural organisations, Chhayataut and Bangladesh Udichi Shilpigoshthi, in Dhaka until Sunday, three days after the incidents. Different political parties and socio-cultural organisations on Sunday also continued to protest against the attacks. The religious affairs adviser, AFM Khalid Hossain, while talking to reporters at the Secretariat on the day, however, said that the government had identified several individuals involved in the attacks. ‘We have already taken measures to arrest them and bring them to book,’ he said. On the night of December 18, hundreds of people attacked the media houses at Karwan Bazar and cultural institutions in Dhaka, following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, who was shot in the head in the capital on December 12 and died at a hospital in Singapore. The police said that no case was filed over the attacks on the media houses but a case was filed in connection with the vandalism and arson attack on Chhayataut in the capital’s Dhanmondi area. Tajgaon police station officer-in-charge Kya Swee Nue at about 10:00pm on Sunday said that the Prothom Alo authorities were filing a case with his police station. He, however, said that the Daily Star authorities were yet to file any case. Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Tejgaon Division additional deputy commissioner Fazlul Karim on Sunday evening said that they would arrest the accused persons after filing the cases. He said that none was arrested so far. Chhayanaut chief manager Dulal Ghosh filed a case against a group of unidentified attackers with Dhanmondi police station, said the police station officer-in-charge Muhammad Saiful Islam on Sunday. The case was filed for damaging the infrastructure through vandalism and arson attack and for attempting to murder the security guards, according to the police official. The case alleged that a total of 5,069 rare books by different writers were damaged in the attack. The building and different kinds of furniture, musical instruments and electronic devices, among others, worth about Tk 2.40 crore were damaged in the attack, according to the case statement. OC Saiful said that the police could not arrest anyone in the case. The European Union ambassador in Dhaka, Michael Miller, visited the damaged office of the Prothom Alo on Sunday and said that the attacks were attacks on the freedom of expression and independent media. He condemned the attacks and said that he wouldn’t want to see any repetition of any such incidents. The Press Club of India and the Karachi Press Club, in separate statements, expressed grave concern over the incidents of recent attacks, vandalism, and arson at the offices of media outlets, as well as the harassment of veteran journalist Nurul Kabir, the editor of New Age and the president of the Editors’ Council. Bangladesh Nationalist Party standing committee member Salahuddin Ahmed at a city hotel said that the attacks on the media damaged the country’s image. He said that the BNP condemned the incident and demanded justice. He also criticised the role of the law enforcement agencies for their failure to control the mob. The leaders of the Ganosamhati Andolan on Sunday called on the people to resist the anarchy created in Dhaka after the death of Sharif Osman Hadi. A central team of the party, led by its chief coordinator Zonayed Saki, visited Prothom Alo and The Daily Star offices on Sunday. Zonayed Saki said that such anarchy was a bad sign to divert the issue of holding the next general election in February. Chhayataut and Udichi were also attacked and set on fire following the attacks on the two media houses and the harassment of veteran journalist and writer Nurul Kabir. Bangladesh Hindu Buddhist Christian Unity Council, in a press statement, condemned attacks on media houses and other cultural organisations and demanded exemplary punishments for the attackers. They also condemned the incident of harassing New Age editor Nurul Kabir and the killing of garment worker Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh, said that statement signed by its acting general secretary Mannindra Kumar Nath. Local journalists in Gazipur and Sylhet also held protests demanding the immediate arrest of the attackers. They, in separate human chains in their respective cities, demanded justice for the affected media houses and journalist Nurul Kabir.

title: No case filed over death of sleeping child in Lakshmipur house fire
body: No case was filed so far till Sunday night over the incident of killing a seven-year-old girl in an alleged arson attack on the house of a local Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader in Lakshmipur Sadar upazila on Friday late night. BNP Lakshmipur district unit joint convener advocate Hasibur Rahman said that no case has been filed so far in this connection, as the incident triggered fear among the people in the entire district. After visiting the spot, Lakshmipur district superintendent of police Md Abu Tarek said that it was a sad incident and they would take legal actions after investigation. ‘Police are working to dig out the truth of the incident,’ the SP added. The deceased, Ayesha Begum, was the youngest daughter of Md Belal, assistant organising secretary of the BNP Bhabaniganj union unit at the upazila. Belal and his two other daughters, Bithi Akhter, 17, and Smrity Akhter, 14, were also injured in the incident. Lakshmipur Sadar police officer-in-charge Wahid Parvez said that the police, on information, visited the scene. ‘One child died, and three others were injured in the fire. The incident is being investigated, he added. Fire Service Sadar station official Ranjit Kumar Saha said that firefighters rushed to the spot after receiving the information and brought the fire under control after about an hour of effort. The police and family members said that Belal was sleeping in the house with his wife and children when unidentified attackers locked the two doors from outside, sprinkled petrol around the house and set it on fire. At one point, sensing the fire, his wife darted out of the house screaming for help, but flames readily spread through the house. Neighbours could rescue Belal and his two daughters but failed to recover Ayesha. Ayesha died on the spot, as neighbours took the injured to Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital. Smriti and Bithi were shifted to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka as their condition deteriorated.

title: Amjanatar Dal receives registration, election symbol from EC
body: Amjanatar Dal on Sunday received the registration certificate with election symbol of ‘butterfly’ from the Election Commission. The registration certificate, signed by EC senior secretary Akhtar Ahmed, was handed over to the party’s general secretary Tarique Rahman. Earlier, the Election Commission held a hearing on December 15 to review two objections submitted against the registration of Amjanatar Dal. Following the hearing, the EC said the party had fulfilled all the required conditions for registration under Chapter VI (A) of the Representation of the People Order, 1972, and expressed its satisfaction in registering the party as a political organisation. With the inclusion of Amjanatar Dal, the total number of registered political parties in the country has now risen to 57, while the registration of the Awami League remains suspended, according to the EC website.

title: Diplomatic journalism boosts foreign policy, says foreign secy
body: Bangladesh interim government foreign secretary Asad Alam Siam on Sunday said diplomatic journalism is playing an important role in strengthening Bangladesh’s foreign policy as three journalists received the DCAB Media Award for outstanding reporting on diplomacy. The Diplomatic Correspondents Association, Bangladesh organised the DCAB Media Award and Members’ Writers’ Honour Ceremony at the Foreign Service Academy in Dhaka, with Asad Alam Siam attending as the chief guest. The Foreign Secretary, along with jury board head editor of Dhaka Tribute Riaz Ahmed, handed over the awards to the winners. Arifuzzaman Mamun, diplomatic correspondent of Daily Amader Shomoy, won the award in the print category, while Mahfuzur Rahman Mishu, foreign affairs editor of Jamuna Television, received the television category award. Apurbo Kumar Piku, diplomatic correspondent of Sarabangla.net, was named the best reporter in the online category. Speaking at the event, Asad Alam Siam said that amid complex geopolitical realities, diplomatic journalists are playing a constructive role in addressing multifaceted challenges related to foreign policy and international relations. He expressed hope that journalists covering the diplomatic beat would continue to serve national interests through responsible and professional journalism, and commended DCAB for the initiative. DCAB president A K M Moinuddin and general secretary Arifuzzaman Mamun also spoke at the programme.

title: Indian online visa application services resume in Khulna
body: Online Indian visa application services resumed in Khulna on Sunday morning after remaining suspended since Wednesday afternoon. However, due to security concerns, physical entry to the Indian deputy high commission office in Khulna has been closed and all visa-related activities are being conducted online. A strict security cordon has been put in place around the mission. While visiting the Indian deputy high commission office on Samsur Rahman Road on Sunday morning, this correspondent found that barricade was put on nearly half a kilometre of road--from Ahsan Ahmed Road intersection to Baiti Para crossing. Members of the Army, joint forces and police have been deployed to ensure security. The administration has closed four roads surrounding the deputy high commission office, resulting in a complete suspension of vehicular movement on Samsur Rahman Road. Vehicles are being diverted through alternative routes, causing inconvenience to local residents. Pedestrians are also being allowed to enter the area only after security checks. Overall, the area has been placed under a tight security blanket. Owners of several visa brokerage firms on Sir Iqbal Road said that following the death of Osman Hadi and subsequent unwanted incidents in Dhaka on Wednesday, online visa applications were suspended from Wednesday afternoon. Although the online system initially remained active in Khulna, applications were fully halted from 12 noon on Thursday after a ‘March to Indian Consulate Office’ programme was announced. Sadhan Sarkar, proprietor of a visa brokerage firm, said that appointments for applications submitted between Thursday morning and noon were being issued from Sunday morning. Fresh online applications are also being accepted again from today, he added. On Sunday morning, four roads adjacent to the deputy high commission remained closed. Vehicles were seen using alternative routes near the Press Club, leading to heavy traffic congestion in that area. Law enforcement personnel were also seen standing guard on both sides of the main road in front of the Indian mission. Contacted, Deputy Commissioner of Khulna Metropolitan Police (KMP) Md Tajul Islam said extensive security measures have been taken around the Indian deputy high commission. He added that patrols across the city have been intensified to maintain law and order and that police are fully prepared to prevent any untoward incident.

title: Police in dark over location of Hadi shooter
body: The police are still in the dark about the current location of Faisal Karim Masud, the alleged shooter in the attack on Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. Even nine days after the incident, the law enforcement agencies have failed to confirm the whereabouts of Faisal Karim while there has been an allegation that the prime suspect has fled to India. Besides, the Criminal Investigation Department on Sunday started an investigation into money laundering by Faisal Karim as the agency found information of unusual transactions of Tk 127 crore after analysing the bank account dealings of Faisal and people related to him. In response to a reporter’s question on whether Faisal Karim was inside the country or abroad, additional inspector general of police Khandaker Rafiqul Islam at a press briefing said, ‘Whether Faisal is in the country or has crossed the border has not been confirmed yet.’ ‘We are continuing our investigation and all sorts of efforts are going on to arrest the prime suspect,’ he added. Asked about the attacks and vandalism at different places after Hadi’s shooting, he said, ‘We are investing the incidents with utmost importance.’ The joint press briefing by the police, Rapid Action Battalion and Border Guard Bangladesh was organised at the home ministry at the secretariat on Sunday evening on the latest updates of Phase-2 of the ‘Devil Hunt’ operation. Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Branch chief Shafiqul Islam at the press briefing also said that they have no specific information about the current location of Faisal Karim.’ ‘Various types of information are coming in from different places, but there is no information on whether the accused is still in the country or has gone abroad,’ he said. He said that so far a total of 10 people, including Faisal’s parents and wife, had been arrested in connection with the Hadi killing. He also said that the motorcycle used in the shooting on Hadi has been recovered, along with weapons. Of the weapons, one is suspected to have been used in the killing of Hadi. But it will be confirmed after examination,’ he added. Asked whether the murder was due to political or personal reasons, and whether any findings had emerged from the investigation so far, Shafiqul said, ‘Primarily, it is being suspected that the killing was politically motivated. The investigation is going on.’ RAB’s Law and Media Wing director Intekhhab Chowdhury said that information obtained from the detainees indicated that after the incident of shooting Hadi, Faisal and Alamgir (the motorcycle rider) went to Agargaon and planned to hide the pistol and ammunition used in the attack. ‘He (Hadi) instructed his father to hand over the bag containing the weapons to his brother-in-law Shipu, and he set off for Savar by a CNG scooter,’ he said. Later, Faisal Karim’s father handed over the bag to Shipu. Shipu then went to Narsingdi and gave the bag to Faisal’s wife Samia. Samia later asked Shipu to hide the bag, and Shipu handed it over to his friend Faisal to keep it at his residence. The RAB official said that after news of the shooting spread and panic set in, the bag containing the weapons and ammunition was thrown into nearby Turua beel (wetland) from where the RAB later recovered the bag. BGB sector commander Colonel Mostafizur Rahman said that security was tightened in the border areas after the shooting of Hadi while several people were arrested on the charge of assisting human trafficking. ‘Efforts are under way to arrest Philip, one of the key human traffickers in the border area to know about the alleged fleeing of Faisal Karim,’ he said. Such press briefing is usually held by home adviser retired Lieutenant General Jahangir Alam Chowdhury. However, neither the adviser nor home secretary Nasimul Ghani was present at the Sunday press conference. Earlier, to inform about the progress in connection with arresting the killers of Osman Hadi, the Inquilab Mancha on Saturday gave a 24-hour deadline to the home adviser and the chief adviser’s special assistant Khoda Baksh Chowdhury. The organisation demanded their resignation if they failed to respond within the stipulated time. About the demands, the Inquilab mancha in a statement on Sunday said that not even one of the two mancha demands has been met till now. Home adviser did not appear at the press conference on the day to provide any explanation in this regard, it said. The platform also said that the killing of Osman Hadi had been downplayed and treated as a trivial matter by holding the press conference by an additional IGP. It also said that they would announce further programmes at a press briefing at 12pm on Monday. The 10 arrested in the case are Faisal’s father Md Humayun Kabir and mother Hasi Begum, wife Saheda Parvin Samia, girlfriend Maria Akhtar Lima, brother-in-law Wahid Ahmed Shipu, rent-a-car businessman Md Mufti Nuruzzaman Nomani alias Ujjwal; Faisal’s associate Md Kabir; and Sibun Dew and Sanjay Chisim. Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Sefatullah on Sunday put two youths -- Sibun Dew and Sanjay Chisim, 22, who allegedly aided Hadi’s murderers to flee were put on fresh five-day remand for more quizzing in connection with the Sharif Osman Hadi shooting case. Besides, another Dhaka court imposed travel ban on Faisal Karim Masud, following a petition of the investigation officer in the case.

title: RU students lock key offices demanding resignation of pro-AL deans
body: A group of Rajshahi University students on Sunday padlocked the offices of the vice-chancellor, pro-vice-chancellors, proctor, registrar and several deans, demanding the resignation of pro-Awami League deans. The move came a day after RU Central Students’ Union general secretary Salahuddin Ammar, in a Facebook post on Saturday night, called on students to gather at the RUCSU building on Sunday, stating that they would compel the deans having alleged leaning towards Awami League, the party led by fallen prime minister Sheikh Hasina, to resign. The agitation followed the university administration’s decision to extend the tenure of six deans whose official terms expired on December 17, ignoring students’ objections. Witnesses said that Ammar, accompanied by other students, went to the deans’ offices on Sunday morning carrying prepared resignation letters but did not find any of them present on the campus. He also contacted the deans by phone, informing them that he was visiting their offices with resignation letters. Ammar, in another Facebook post on Sunday, claimed that none of six deans with alleged leaning towards Awami League, which is now banned from holding activities, came to the campus and informed him that they had informed the vice-chancellor that they would not continue with their duty. ‘Now we will see what decision the vice-chancellor takes,’ he wrote. Ammar also stated in the Facebook post that after hearing that the then vice-chancellor and pro-vice-chancellor were taking classes, he went there but they too were nowhere to be found and appeared to have fled. ‘Today, most AL-leaning offices across departments were found locked. This is exactly what I want—that they remain locked until justice is served,’ he wrote, adding that he had prepared a list of teachers who, at different times last July, took position against students. He also sought additional names from student organisations, including Chhatra Dal and Islami Chhatra Shibir. Meanwhile, a group of students led by senate student representative and former Students Against Discrimination leader Akil Bin Taleb padlocked the offices of the arts, social sciences and law faculties. Later about noon, the group of students also hung locks at the offices of the vice-chancellor, pro-vice-chancellors, proctor, registrar and other administrative offices at the university’s main administrative building, demanding the resignation of pro-AL deans. The group also locked in an altercation with the pro-VC (education) Professor Farid Uddin Khan while attempting to lock his office. Later on the day, a delegation, including RUCSU general secretary Salahuddin Ammar, cultural affairs secretary Zaid Hasan Zoha, media and publication secretary Islam, assistant cultural secretary Rakibul Hasan, senate member Akil Bin Taleb, the university’s Islami Chhatra Shibir general secretary Mujahid Faisal and RU Chhatrapokkho convener Golam Mostafa held a meeting with the pro-vice-chancellors and other senior officials. At the meeting, Ammar questioned the legality of allowing deans to continue beyond their tenure and alleged that the administration had failed to show visible progress in investigating incidents of violence involving teachers, officials and staff allegedly aligned with Awami League. He further alleged that some teachers accused in murder cases or of promoting political narratives in classrooms were still taking classes, contributing to ideological indoctrination of students. Mujahid Faisal expressed disappointment that the current administration had failed to take decisive action against teachers accused of opposing or undermining the July movement. He said that while punitive measures were taken swiftly against students, including cancellation of certificates, similar ‘tough decisions’ were taken against teachers facing serious allegations. The protesters warned that unresolved issues related to governance, accountability and campus safety could undermine the spirit of the July movement and destabilise the academic environment ahead of upcoming elections. Vice-chancellor Professor Saleh Hasan Naqib could not be reached for comments despite repeated attempts. Pro-vice-chancellor (education) Professor Farid Uddin Khan said that the administration had extended the deans’ tenure due to ongoing academic and administrative activities, including admission tests, cautioning that removing them at this stage could create serious complications.

title: Man beaten to death over theft allegation
body: A man was beaten to death over theft allegations at Konaura village of Kaitola union at Nabinagar upazila in the district in the early hours of Sunday. Sahed Ali, 55, son of Milad Ali of village Semontaghar, was beaten to death between 3:00am and 3:30am on Sunday, according to the police. Nabinagar police station officer-in-charge Mohammad Rafiqul Islam said that the police recovered the body of the victim at about 8:00am on Sunday after receiving information. The police official said that local people alleged that Sahed went to Konaura village to steal at a house on Saturday night and when he tried to enter another house, he was detained by local people. ‘Agitated people beat him, leaving him dead on the spot,’ said Rafiqul. The police official said that they detained four people in this connection. ‘We will take necessary legal actions after receiving complaint from the victim’s family,’ he added.

title: Two minor children die of ‘food poisoning’ at Dhaka
body: Two siblings died of suspected food poisoning at Wireless Mor in the capital’s Hatirjheel area on Sunday. The deceased were identified as Afrida Chowdhury, 10, a Class III student of Viqarunnisa Noon School and College and her one-year-old brother Ilham Chowdhury, children of Mosleh Uddin Chowdhury. Golam Mortuza, officer-in-charge of Hatirjheel police station, said the bodies were handed over to the family on Sunday following post-mortem examinations. Police said that the children’s father Mosleh Uddin Chowdhury, mother Saida Jakawat Ara, and their two children had dinner together on Friday night before going to sleep. On Saturday morning, Afrida fell sick and was taken to a local hospital where doctors declared her dead at about 7:00am. Her body was later brought home. Shortly afterwards, Ilham began vomiting and became critically ill. He was rushed to another hospital where he died in the afternoon while undergoing treatment. Both parents also became sick but recovered after receiving medical treatment. ‘Initially, it appears the children may have died from food poisoning, but the exact cause of death will be confirmed after receiving the post-mortem reports,’ the OC said.

title: AK Khandker buried
body: The deputy chief of staff of the Bangladesh Armed Forces during the War of Independence, Air Vice Marshal AK Khandker Bir Uttam, was buried at the Shaheen graveyard at the Bangladesh Air Force Base Bashar in the capital Dhaka on Sunday. His namaz-e-janaza was held and guard of honour was also given in the presence of interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, said an Inter Services Public Relation Directorate press release. On behalf of the president, his military secretary paid homage to AK Khandaker by placing a wreath on his coffin following the namaz-e-janaza. The chief adviser also paid tribute to AK Khandaker by placing a wreath on his coffin. Following which, Liberation war affairs adviser Faruk E Azam, Chief of Army Staff General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Chief of Naval Staff Admiral M Nazmul Hassan, Chief of Air Staff Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan also paid homage to the first chief of the Bangladesh Air Force after the War of Independence in 1971. AK Khandker died on Saturday morning at the Combined Military Hospital in the capital Dhaka. He took charge of the Bangladesh Air Force chief on April 7, 1972, and successfully reorganised the war-ravaged Bangladesh Air Force, and retired from the Force on October 15, 1975 after completing more than 23 years’ service in the commission rank. The ISPR said that he was not only a valiant freedom fighter but also a visionary leader who played a vital role in the formation of the Bangladesh Air Force. AK Khandker’s firm commitment, strategic intelligence and devotion had been a source of inspiration during the Liberation War in 1971, said the ISPR, adding that he played an important role through his directed efforts and coordination in the liberation struggle that led the country towards victory. AK Khandker, 95, left a daughter and two sons to mourn his death. He was born in Pabna on October 31, 1930. He completed his matriculation in 1947 and ISC in 1949. He completed his graduation from PAF College in September 1952 and PSA in 1965 from Pakistan Air Force Staff College. He started his career as a general duty pilot in January 1951. He was commissioned in the Pakistan Air Force in September 1952. When the War of Independence began in 1971, he was posted at the Pakistan Air Force Base in Dhaka. He defected from the Pakistan Air Force with Wing Commander MK Bashar and several other pilots in May 1971 and reached India. The then Bangladesh government of Mujibnagar appointed him as the deputy chief of staff of the Bangladesh Armed Forces, and he was given the responsibility of the operation and training of the freedom fighters. He is credited as the main architect of establishing the Sector Commanders Forum in 2005. AK Khandker was awarded the Independence Award in 2011 for his contribution to the War of Independence and for reorganising the Bangladesh Air Force. He worked as the Bangladesh high commissioner to Australia between 1976 and 1982 and the Bangladesh high commissioner to India between 1982 and 1986. In 1986, he was appointed as an adviser to military dictator HM Ershad and then as a planning minister of the autocratic government. AK Khandker was later elected lawmaker for the Pabna-2 constituency twice. In 2009, he became the planning minister of the Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League government.

title: Three people killed, one missing as five vehicles plunge into Dhaleshwari from ferry
body: Three people were killed and one remained missing after a truck and four other vehicles fell into the River Dhaleshwari from a ferry in Baktaboli area in Narayanganj on early Sunday. The deceased were identified as Masud Rana, 30, a Bangladeshi expatriate in Singapore, van puller Shadhin, 25, and Rafique, 35. Md Rakibuzzaman, in-charge of Baktaboli River Police, said the ferry left Narsinghpur in Fatullah for Baktaboli at about 9:00pm on Saturday. When the ferry reached the middle of the river, a truck suddenly started rolling and plunged into the water dragging along a motorcycle, two auto-rickshaws and a van. Eight to ten people managed to swim to safety while four others went missing, police said. On information, a firefighting unit rushed to the spot and recovered the bodies of three victims at about 3:00am. Md Hasanuzzaman, additional superintendent of police in Narayanganj, said police are investigating the incident.

title: Normal security not ensured at Delhi mission, says Touhid
body: Bangladesh foreign minister Md Touhid Hossain on Sunday said that ‘normal security’ was not maintained at the Bangladesh mission in India and the high commissioner, who was staying there with his family, felt threatened. Rejecting India’s press statement on Saturday’s demonstration in front of the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi, he said that Bangladesh would rely on the host country for the security and expected that the incident in Delhi would not be repeated in the future. ‘We completely reject the press note. How come a group of Hindu militants were allowed to move to that area -- much inside the diplomatic enclave? They were not supposed to be allowed there. They have said many things,’ said Touhid responding to reporters’ questions at his ministry. ‘We have come to know that the demonstrators threatened to kill the high commissioner although we don’t have any evidence,’ said Touhid. He said that Dhaka hoped that the Indian government would take necessary steps to enhance the security of the diplomatic mission. The foreign affairs ministry later in a press release said that the ‘unjustifiable incident’ at the Bangladesh high commission residence in New Delhi was highly regrettable and could not be accepted as ‘misleading propaganda’. Bangladesh has, however, noted the commitment of the government of India to ensure the safety and security of all Bangladesh diplomatic posts in India. Responding to media queries on the reported demonstration in front of the Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi on December 20, 2025, India’s external affairs ministry Randhir Jaiswal on Sunday in a statement said that there was no attempt to breach the fence or create a security situation at any time. He further said that India was committed to ensure safety of foreign missions in its territory. ‘We have noted misleading propaganda in sections of the Bangladesh media on the incident. The fact is that about 20-25 youth gathered in front of the Bangladesh high commission in New Delhi on 20 December and raised slogans in protest against the horrendous killing of Dipu Chandra Das in Mymensingh, while also calling for the protection of all minorities in Bangladesh,’ he said. Jaiswal said that the police stationed on the spot dispersed the group after a few minutes. ‘Visual evidence of these events is available publicly for all to see. India is committed to ensure the safety of foreign missions/posts in its territory in accordance with the Vienna Convention,’ he added. India continues to keep a close watch on the evolving situation in Bangladesh, according to the statement. ‘Our officials remain in touch with Bangladesh authorities and have conveyed to them our strong concerns at the attacks on minorities. We have also urged that the perpetrators of the barbaric killing of Das be brought to justice,’ Jaiswal said. About the lynching of the youth in Mymensingh, the Bangladesh foreign adviser said that the murder of an individual was not an issue of minority and it might happen anywhere. The victim was a Bangladeshi citizen and the important thing was that prompt actions were under way in the case, he mentioned. The government of Bangladesh has promptly apprehended the suspects in this incident, the foreign ministry release said. ‘The inter-communal situation in Bangladesh is better than in many other parts in South Asia. Bangladesh believes that it is the duty of all governments in the region to ensure protection of minorities in their respective countries,’ it mentioned.

title: CEC holds meeting with representatives of law enforcement, intelligence agencies
body: Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin has convened a high-level meeting with senior officials from law enforcement and intelligence agencies to assess the country’s overall security situation ahead of the national election and referendum scheduled for February 12, 2026. The discussion began at about 2:50pm on Sunday at the Election Commission headquarters, Nirbachan Bhaban, in Dhaka. Those attending included the home secretary, the principal staff officer of the Armed Forces Division and the inspector general of police. Senior representatives from Border Guard Bangladesh, the Coast Guard, Ansar and VDP, the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence, National Security Intelligence, National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre and the Rapid Action Battalion were also present at the meeting. In addition, the additional inspectors general of police from the Special Branch and the Criminal Investigation Department, along with the Inspector General of Prisons, took part in the meeting. Election commissioners Abdur Rahmanel Masud, Tahmida Ahmed, Md Anwarul Islam Sarkar, Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah and Election Commission Secretary Akhtar Ahmed also joined the session.

title: Case filed over attack on Chhayanaut
body: A case has been filed over recent vandalism and arson attack on the building of cultural organisation Chhayanaut in Dhanmondi area of the capital. Chhayanaut chief manager Dulal Ghosh on early Saturday filed the case against a group of unidentified assailants with Dhanmondi police station, said officer-in-charge of the police station Muhammad Saiful Islam on Sunday. The case was filed under the Special Powers Act, 1974 alleging sabotage of the infrastructure and the Penal Code, 1860 mainly alleging attempt to murder of the security guards, according to the police official. The case document stated that the group of unidentified assailants on December 19 forcefully entered inside Chhayanaut building carried out vandalism and arson attack on it. A total of collected 5069 rare books written by different writers were damaged in the attack, it said. The building and different kinds of furniture, musical instruments and electronic devices, among others, worth about Tk 2.40 crore were damaged in the attack, according to the case document. It also alleged that the miscreants also beaten four security guards with an intention to murder. Attackers carried out the vandalism, arson attack and plunder in a planned manner in the building of cultural organisation with the aim of damaging the image of the country in abroad and creating an embarrassing situation for the government, it alleged. OC Saiful said that police were investigating the case to bring the perpetrators to book. On December 19, a group of unidentified people set fire to the building of Chhayanaut as violence spread in the country over the death of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi. Various socio-political organisations and cultural activists have condemned the attack on the old cultural institution.

title: Indian visa services from Ctg centre suspended for an indefinite period
body: Indian Assistant High Commission in Chattogram has suspended its visa services for an indefinite period, citing security concerns. A notice was posted on the Indian Visa Application Centre website on Saturday in this regard. The Indian visa services at Chattogram centre will remain suspended from Sunday until further notice, the notice reads. It also said that the decision to reopen the visa centre would be taken considering the situation. The move followed chaos on December 18 when a group of people staged a demonstration near the Assistant High Commission at Khulshi in the city after news of the death of Inquilab Manhca leader Sharif Osman Bin Hadi. During the protests, the protesters pelted bricks at the office, prompting police intervention. A chase and counter-chase took place between the protestors and police while 12 people were detained from the spot. Since then, additional police and Army members have been deployed to secure the office. Earlier, on December 17, the Indian visa centre at Jamuna Future Park of Dhaka was briefly closed for security reasons but resumed normal operations the following day.

title: EC asks forces to ensure secure polls
body: The Election Commission has issued stringent directives to law enforcement and security agencies to ensure a safe and orderly electoral environment, warning that any attempt to disrupt the process would be dealt with firmly. Election commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah made the remarks at a briefing on Sunday following a meeting with the heads of law enforcement agencies at the commission’s headquarters in the capital. The EC on Sunday held separate meetings with senior security officials, including, for the first time, with the chiefs of the Army, Navy and Air Force, as part of preparations to ensure a secure and credible election. Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin presided over the meetings. The commission has adopted a zero-tolerance stance towards the activities that damage the electoral atmosphere, including vandalism, violence, and attempts to intimidate voters, said Sanaullah after the meetings. The election commissioner said that the forces and relevant agencies, though the state would act humanely, had been given a firm and unambiguous message that no leniency would be shown to those involved in crimes, vandalism, efforts to undermine the electoral environment or acts of violence resulting in loss of life. He said that joint forces operations would be relaunched at the field level with the objectives of recovering illegal weapons and ammunition, arresting terrorists, and bringing offenders to justice, while a concomitant objective would be to restore confidence among the public, voters, candidates and political parties. According to the election commissioner, the meeting also discussed recent attacks on the offices of The Daily Star and Prothom Alo. According to the commission, such incidents are directly linked to the electoral environment. Sanaullah said that the attack on media houses took place during a period of national mourning and public anger following the death of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi, which opportunist groups exploited to carry out acts of vandalism, at times overwhelming law enforcement personnel. The commissioner said that the message was very clear that such opportunities would not be allowed again. He said that authorities have identified at least 20 individuals involved in the attacks on newspaper offices and have taken legal action against them. The commission said that those responsible would face appropriate consequences. Sanaullah said that the EC also directed agencies to strengthen surveillance by setting up area-based checkpoints and conducting regular checkpoint operations, with particular emphasis on remote areas known for the movement of weapons. Intelligence agencies were questioned over possible lapses in assessing the risks that led to the killing of Hadi and were instructed to take all lawful measures to prevent similar incidents in future. The commission first met with Army chief General Waker-Uz-Zaman, Navy chief Admiral Mohammad Nazmul Hasan, and Air Force chief Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmud Khan, and then held a broader meeting with the heads of other law enforcement and security agencies, including the home secretary, the Principal Staff Officer of the Armed Forces Division, and the inspector general of police. Senior representatives from the Border Guard Bangladesh, Coast Guard, Ansar and VDP, the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence, National Security Intelligence, the National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre, and the Rapid Action Battalion were also present at the meeting. According to Sanaullah, the three service heads assured the commission of their full preparedness and coordinated readiness to ensure a smooth and credible election. The chiefs confirmed that all necessary arrangements had been completed and briefed the commission on deployment plans, with the Army set to deploy a total of 1,00,000 troops, one-third already in the field while the rest would be gradually deployed ahead of the final five days before polling. In response, the EC issued directives focusing on security and control, calling for the relaunch of joint forces operations, the recovery of illegal weapons, and the arrest and prosecution of terrorists and serious criminals. Special emphasis was placed on close coordination between forces and executive magistrates during the operations. Discussions also addressed command, control and coordination at the local level, agreeing that while each force would operate according to its own chain of command, coordination would be managed through existing cells, and a lead controller would be appointed for operations involving multiple forces.

title: Namaz-e-janaza of six Bangladeshi peacekeepers killed in Sudan held
body: Namaz-e-Janaza of six peacekeepers who were martyred in a barbaric terrorist drone attack on a United Nations peacekeeping mission base in the Abyei area of Sudan on December 13 last was held on Sunday at the Central Mosque of Dhaka Cantonment. Home adviser Lieutenant General (retired) Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury, chief of army staff General Waker-Uz-Zaman, chief of naval staff Admiral M Nazmul Hassan and chief of air staff Air Chief Marshal Hasan Mahmood Khan, senior military and civil officials, members of different ranks and media personnel attended the janaza, according to the chief adviser’s press wing. Prior to the janaza, brief life sketches of the martyred peacekeepers were read out and their next of kin spoke. Afterwards, chief community liaison officer of UNISFA Boris-Ephrem Tchoumavi, on behalf of the United Nations secretary-general, addressed the gathering. Following the Namaz-e-Janaza, state honours were accorded to the martyrs. On the occasion, the chief adviser’s military secretary, on behalf of the chief adviser, placed wreaths to pay tribute to the martyred peacekeepers. Later, the chief community liaison officer of UNISFA handed over the United Nations flag to the next of kin of the martyrs on behalf of the UN secretary-general. After the Janaza, separate condolence messages, signed by the chief adviser, were handed over to the families of the martyrs. The government of Bangladesh and senior officials of the United Nations earlier strongly condemned the heinous drone attack. Expressing deep concern, the Bangladesh Army sent a formal letter of protest to the UN headquarters and urged the adoption of prompt drone countermeasures in all mission areas, including UNISFA. In the terrorist drone attack, six peacekeepers were martyred and nine others were injured. Of the injured, eight are currently undergoing treatment at Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi, the capital of Kenya. All of them are now out of danger.
