title: NDF president Anisul’s Ctg house set on fire
body: Unidentified arsonists set the house of Anisul Islam Mahmud, president of National Democratic Front, on fire at Hathazari in Chattogram on Friday night. Witnesses said that some unidentified people swooped on the house of Anisul around 11:40pm and carried out vandalism. Later, they exploded crude bombs and set the house on fire. Meanwhile, the arsonists also set a private vehicle, owned by Akbar Haidar Chowdhury, paternal uncle of the NDF leader, on fire. On information, a firefighting unit went to the spot and extinguished the blaze. Kazi Md Tarek Aziz, additional superintendent, Hathazari circle, said that the police were trying to arrest the arsonists. The fire gutted valuables, including furniture, said Zahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Hathazari police.

title: 24-hr ultimatum issued for arrest of Hadi killers
body: The Inquilab Mancha on Saturday issued a 24-hour ultimatum to the government for the arrest of those responsible for the killing of the platform’s convener Sharif Osman Hadi. Protests were held at places demanding justice for Hadi while gayebana namaz-e-janazas of Osman Hadi were also held in districts. Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Jaber issued the 24-hour ultimatum at a rally at the Shahbagh Crossing in the capital at around 5:00 pm. ‘If the government does not respond by Sunday 5:30 pm regarding the arrest of the killers of Osman Hadi, we will again stage a sit-in at Shahbagh,’ he said. Earlier in the day, Osman Hadi was laid to rest beside the grave of National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam adjacent to the Dhaka University Central Mosque at around 3:30pm, following his funeral prayers at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. After Hadi’s burial, most of the people left the area, but a few thousand people, including activists of the Inquilab Mancha, gathered at the Shahbagh Crossing demanding justice for Hadi. Expressing condolences, they held a rally demanding the arrest of the killers and promised to finish Hadii’s unfinished work, including stopping Indian hegemony and establishing a truly independent and democratic Bangladesh. Addressing the rally, Abdullah Al Jaber said, ‘We have two demands. First, all those involved in the killing of Osman Hadi — the killers, planners and collaborators — must be arrested and brought to justice. The second demand is that the Awami League collaborators existing within the civil-military intelligence apparatuses must be arrested immediately. Besides the home adviser retired Lieutenant General Jahangir Alam and special assiisetnt to chief adviser Khoda Baksh Chowdhury have to come before the people within the 24 hours and explain what progress has been made in arresting the killers of Hadi over the past week, Jaber said. If he cannot provide an answer, then he must resign, Jaber announced at the Shahbagh rally. Jaber said, ‘Osman Hadi was not killed by a single person. There was an entire network behind this. We don’t look at any political party in Bangladesh only with suspicion, nor do we keep anyone completely beyond suspicion.’ He said, ‘Those who killed Osman Hadi, planned the killing, assisted it and created the overall situation — all of them must be brought to justice as quickly as possible. We urge the government to do this.’ ‘It’s been 172 hours since Osman Hadi was killed, but the state has still not been able to say where his killers are,’ he added. Noting about conspiracies to obstruct the election, he said, ‘Various conspiracies are under way to obstruct the upcoming election — so that the election does not take place and the Awami League can return using this chance. The plot has been designed with that goal.’ After that, Inquilab Mancha leaders and activists left the Shahbagh Crossing at about 5:30pm, allowing traffic to resume after nearly three hours of disruption due to the protest. New Age Staff Correspondent from Sylhet reported that a ‘gayebana namaz-e-janaza’ of Osman Hadi was held in Sylhet on Saturday morning. Leaders of political parties, including the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, Bangladesh Jamaat-e Islami and National Citizen Party, administration officials and local residents took part in the gayebana janaza prayers held in front of the Collectorate Mosque at the Court Point in the city after the Zuhr prayer. New Age correspondents reported that gayebana janaza prayers of Hadi were also held in Rajshahi, Chattogram, and Jamalpur. New Age correspondent in Jashore reported that protest rallies were held at several places in Jashore protesting the killing of Osman Hadi. Protests were held at Daratana in Jashore town and Nawapara industrial town while a grand supplication prayer was held at Jashore Central Eidgah on Saturday in which leaders of politicl parties and people of different walks of life took parts. Osman Hadi, also one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last at a Singapore hospital at around 9:45pm Bangladesh time on Thursday. The 32 year-old leader, Osman Hadi, who was very vocal against Indian hegemony and an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad polls, was shot in the head on December 12 in the city. The incident took place a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. He initially underwent surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and was later admitted to Evercare Hospital. For advanced treatment, he was airlifted to Singapore, where he succumbed to his injuries on the night of December 18. Hadi’s death, mourned by people from all walks of life, sparked street protests across the country with the demand for justice for Hadi.

title: Sleeping child dies as BNP leader’s house set on fire
body: A seven-year-old girl was burned to death in an alleged arson attack on the house of a local Bangladesh Nationalist Party leader in Lakshmipur Sadar upazila Friday late night. The deceased, Ayesha Begum, was the youngest daughter of Md Belal, assistant organising secretary of the BNP Bhabaniganj union unit at the upazila. Belal and his two other daughters Bithi Akhter, 17, and Smrity Akhter, 14, were also injured in the incident. Lakshmipur Sadar police officer-in-charge Wahid Parvez said that the police on information visited the scene. ‘One child died and three others were injured in the fire. The incident is being investigated, he added. Fire Service Sadar station official Ranjit Kumar Saha said that firefighters rushed to the spot after receiving the information and brought the fire under control after about an hour of effort. The police and family members said that Belal was sleeping in the house with his wife and children when unidentified attackers locked the two doors from outside, sprinkled petrol around the house and set it on fire. At one point, sending the fire his wife darted out of the house screaming for help, but flames readily spread through the house by the time neighbours could rescue Belal and his two daughters, but failed to recover Ayesha. Ayesha died on the spot, as neighbours took the injured to Lakshmipur Sadar Hospital. Smriti and Bithi were shifted to the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka as their condition deteriorated. The police could not yet identify the assailants till this report was filed at 8:00pm Saturday.

title: Protests over attacks on media, cultural organisations continue
body: Different political parties, students’ organisations and civil society platforms on Saturday continued to protest against the vandalism and arson attacks on the offices of two newspapers, The Daily Star and the Prothom Alo, and other cultural organisations’ establishments in Dhaka and elsewhere in the country. They also urged the government to bring the perpetrator to book immediately in the incident of harassing New Age editor and Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir. The protesters also alleged that the government could not avoid responsibility for the attacks as it failed to respond in time to save the institutions. They also questioned the government’s silence during the incidents. The Ganatantra Mancha, Gono Odhikar Parishad, Jatiya Mukti Council, Bangladesh Students’ Union, Students Against Discrimination, Bangladesh Lekhak Shibir, and civil society organisations in separate programmes and statements also urged the government to ensure justice over the incidents. On December 18 night, a violent mob attacked the media houses at Karwan Bazar and cultural institutions in Dhaka, following the death of Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, who was shot in the head in the capital on December 12 and died at a hospital in Singapore while he was undergoing treatment there. Cultural organisation Bangladesh Udichi Shilpi Goshthi’s central office in Dhaka was also vandalised and set on fire on the following day. The attackers also attacked several district offices of the Prothom Alo. The attacked newspapers, after a one-day suspension, resumed their operation under different capacities from Saturday. No case was filed and none was arrested until Saturday in connection with the attacks. Tejgaon police station officer-in-charge Kya Swee Nue said that the authorities of The Daily Star and the Prothom Alo told them that they were taking time to file cases as they were calculating the damage in the arson attacks. ‘We will take necessary legal actions after receiving the cases,’ the OC said, adding that none was arrested or detained in this connection. He said that they collected some evidence and were analysing video footage to identify the attackers. Journalists at The Daily Star said on Saturday that they were working from their homes as their office building was badly damaged. Reporters at the Prothom Alo said that they were working in the office on a limited scale. A group of civil society leaders, at a press conference at the National Press Club in Dhaka, urged the government to find out the offenders immediately. Addressing the press conference, Jahangirnagar University professor and rights activist Anu Muhammad said that the interim government could not avoid their responsibility for the attacks as they failed to stop the attacks and vandalism. He also condemned the attack on New Age editor Nurul Kabir when the journalist and writer went to The Daily Star office to save the journalists working there. The platform placed six demands, including a proper investigation into the killing of Sharif Osman Hadi and ensuring punishment for the killers, an investigation into the attacks on Thursday night, ensuring safety and security for the citizens, and the home adviser’s resignation for his failures to control the law and order situation. Acclaimed photographer Shahiful Alam, rights activist Shamsul Huda, Barrister Sara Hossain, garment labour leader Taslima Akhter, women’s leader Shima Datta, and former student leader Baki Billah, among others, also spoke at the press conference. The central steering committee members of the Ganatantra Mancha, a combine of five political parties, called on the government to take adequate measures to stop attacks on media houses. A delegation of the combine, led by its coordinator and Revolutionary Workers Party general secretary Saiful Huq, visited the affected media houses Saturday afternoon. Nagarik Oikya president Mahmudur Rahman Manna expressed concern over the attacks and urged the government to identify the attackers and punish them exemplarily. Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal-JSD general secretary Shahid Uddin Mahmod Shapon, Bhashani Janashakti Party chairman Sheikh Rafiqul Islam Bablu, among others, were present. Gono Odhikar Parishad president Nurul Haque Nur, in a statement, expressed concern and condemned the incidents and demanded a fair and fast investigation into the attacks. ‘Attacks on free media are nothing but attacks on democracy,’ the statement said. Bangladesh Students’ Union president Tamzid Haider Chanchol and general secretary Shimul Kumbhkar, in a joint statement, accused extremist groups of attacking the media houses and cultural institutions in a bid to create an anarchic situation in the country to cancel the upcoming national election. They alleged that the communal forces launched the planned attacks to destroy the achievements of the July uprising. Students Against Discrimination, in a statement, termed the attacks premeditated and disgraceful acts and said that such acts were unacceptable in the ‘new Bangladesh’ that emerged following the student-led July uprising. It said that violence, intimidation and destruction undermine the spirit of the July uprising and pose a serious threat to democratic values, freedom of expression and cultural life in Bangladesh. The Human Rights Development Centre, a human rights organisation, expresses concern over the killing of Hadi and attacks on media and cultural institutions. The HRDC urged the interim government to ensure public safety, protect freedom of expression and peaceful assembly, strengthen intelligence and law enforcement responses, and support the Election Commission in conducting a free, fair, and credible election. Bangladesh Lekhak Shibir president Kazi Iqbal and general secretary Shafi Rahman condemned the attacks and said that the government failed to ensure safety. ‘We urge all democratic forces of the country to be united to fight against the vested force,’ the statement said.

title: Army, navy, air chiefs to meet CEC Nasir today
body: The chiefs of the Bangladesh Army, Bangladesh Navy and Air Force will meet chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin today. ‘The meeting will be held at 12:00pm at Nirbachan Bhaban,’ said EC director, PR, Ruhul Amin Mollik on Saturday. Due to the meeting, the Election Commission shifted its pre-scheduled meeting over law and order from 10:00am to 2:30pm. In the afternoon, the EC will sit with top representatives of law enforcing agencies and intelligences to review the overall law and order situation ahead of the upcoming national election and referendum scheduled to be held on February 12, 2026. CEC Nasir will chair the meeting on law and order at the Conference Room of the Election Commission in the city. Top representatives of the armed forces, the principal secretary, the home affairs secretary, the principal staff officer of the Armed Forces Division, the inspector general of police, directors general of Border Guard Bangladesh, the Bangladesh Coast Guard, Ansar and VDP, Directorate General of Forces Intelligence, National Security Intelligence, National Telecommunication Monitoring Centre and Rapid Action Battalion, along with additional IGPs of Special Branch and Criminal Investigation Department, and the inspector general of prisons are supposed to attend the meeting. The major agendas of the meeting are to review pre-election law and order situation, the activities of joint forces to recover illegal arms and prevent terror acts and the compliance with electoral code by candidates and political parties as well as the issues related to maintaining an election-friendly environment. Four election commissioners will be present in the law and order meeting. Meanwhile, the Election Commission on Saturday amended the election schedule gazette, bringing change in the timeframe to file appeals challenging the decisions of the returning officers against the acceptance and rejection of nomination papers during the scrutiny. According to the amended gazette, the appeals against the decisions of the returning officers can be filed from January 5 to 9, while the appeals will be disposed of on January 10-18. In the original schedule, the time for submission of appeals was January 5-11 and the time for disposal of the appeals was January 12-18. On December 11, the CEC announced the schedule to arrange the 13th parliamentary elections and the referendum on the July National Charter (constitutional reform) Implementation Order simultaneously on February 12 next. According to the election schedule, the deadline for the submission of nomination papers is December 29, while the last date for the withdrawal of candidature is January 20. The election campaign will start on January 22 and continue till 48 hours before the balloting period (7:30am on February 10).

title: Hadi’s brother questions failure to arrest killers
body: Abu Bakar Siddique, the elder brother of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, on Saturday questioned the failure to arrest the killers even after seven to eight days of the shooting. ‘If criminals can open fire after Jum’a prayers in the heart of Dhaka and escape, there can be no greater disgrace for us as a nation,’ he said while addressing thousands of mourners before the namaz-e-janaza of Hadi at Manik Mia Avenue in the capital. He also demanded a quick and public trial of those responsible for the killing. Siddique said his younger brother had devoted his life to protecting Bangladesh’s independence and sovereignty and left behind a message for the country’s people on how to safeguard the freedom. ‘Hadi is survived by an eight-month-old child who will never know his father,’ he said, adding, ‘When the child was born, my brother asked me to choose a name reflecting revolutionary spirit and courage. I named him Firnas.’ He said the family has been shattered by the loss, with their mother repeatedly losing consciousness and other siblings suffering severe trauma. He urged people to pray for Hadi’s wife and child, for his injured brother Omar Faruk who was with him during the attack and for his sister Masuma, who is undergoing treatment for severe trauma. Siddique led the janaza prayers at about 2:30pm. Religious affairs adviser AFM Khalid Hossain described Hadi as a poet and cultural activist who co-founded the Inquilab Cultural Center to help shape a new cultural narrative for the country. Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al-Jaber alleged that the killing was the result of a planned conspiracy involving multiple actors. He demanded that the killers, planners and facilitators be brought to justice and urged the home affairs adviser and other officials to publicly explain within 24 hours what steps have been taken so far. He also called on supporters to refrain from violence and warned against acting on any propaganda outside Inquilab Mancha’s directives, saying future programmes would be announced by the platform.

title: Bangladesh govt urges Meta to act against violences inciting content
body: The interim government has sent an urgent letter to Meta, calling for immediate action to prevent the use of its platforms—particularly Facebook—to incite violence and undermine social stability in Bangladesh. In the letter, the government expressed serious concern that social media had increasingly been used to fuel large-scale violence, intimidation and calls to disrupt the country’s upcoming national elections, scheduled for February 2026. The letter sent by the National Cyber Security Agency on Friday said that Meta’s platforms, particularly Facebook, were being exploited at a critical moment when Bangladesh was on a path towards democratic transition. The government urged Meta to take stronger and more proactive measures to prevent its services from being used for societal destabilisation. It specifically requested heightened monitoring of Bangladesh-related content at least until the completion of the national election, warning that unchecked online activity could further escalate tensions and threaten public order. Referring to recent incidents of vandalism and arson at the offices of two media houses—The Daily Star and Prothom Alo—the letter said that the attacks triggered widespread fear, disrupted public life and posed grave threats to press freedom. Despite repeated requests from government agencies and civil society sources, the letter noted, Meta had failed to cooperate in deactivating accounts identified as being responsible for inciting and mobilising violence. It also linked the escalation of violence to real-world consequences, including the recent death of the Inquilab Mancha convenor Sharif Osman Hadi from bullet injuries, who is described as a key figure in the July uprising. The letter said that individuals linked to the former regime had publicly expressed approval of Hadi’s death, while others had openly called for violence against media institutions and journalists on social media platforms. It said that posts explicitly or implicitly calling for violence and mob action had been reported through appropriate channels, but community standards had not been applied in a timely or effective manner. The continued circulation and amplification of such content, the letter said, had contributed directly to incidents of arson and demolition of media houses. Stating its concerns ‘with humility but clarity’, the government warned that the unchecked spread of violence-inciting content posed a direct threat to national stability, social harmony, media freedom and the lives and safety of minority groups. In this context, it said, Meta’s role was not merely technical but one of public responsibility. The government urged Meta to acknowledge its responsibility in preventing the use of its platforms for violence and to enforce community standards in a stricter, faster and more contextual manner for Bangladesh-related content. It also called on the company to strengthen Bengali-language moderation and contextual review, and to take immediate action against content inciting violence, intimidation or coordinated harm. Describing the issue as one of national importance, the letter said that Bangladesh had not experienced a genuinely participatory election for more than 17 years, and that the forthcoming polls were closely tied to democratic rights, minority safety and long-term stability.

title: Bodies of six Bangladeshi peacekeepers arrive in Dhaka from Sudan
body: Bodies of the six United Nations peacekeepers from the Bangladesh Army, killed in a terrorist drone attack in Sudan on December 13, were flown back to Bangladesh on Saturday. An Emirates Airlines aircraft carrying the peacekeepers’ bodies reached Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka city on the day, said an Inter Services Public Relation Directorate press release. Bangladesh Army chief of general staff Lieutenant General Mizanur Rahman Shameem received the bodies at the airport. Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh chairman, United Nations acting resident coordinator in Bangladesh, and high ranking army officers, among others, were also present at the time. One minute of silence was observed and a salute was given in paying tribute to the fallen soldiers while discharging their peacekeeping duties at the time of receiving their bodies, said the ISPR. The namaz-e-janaza for the peacekeepers will be held today at the Dhaka Cantonment Central Mosque, after which helicopters will fly the bodies to their own addresses for burial with due military honour. Nine Bangladeshi peacekeepers were also injured in the drone attack. Of the injured, eight were undergoing treatment at Aga Khan University Hospital in Nairobi in Kenya, the ISPR release added. Abyei is a disputed, oil-rich region on the Sudan-South Sudan border, designated as a ‘special administrative area’ with a complex history of conflict, displacement, and stalled referendum promises, currently managed by UN peacekeepers amidst ongoing ethnic tensions, particularly between the Dinka Ngok and Misseriya tribes, and regional instability from Sudan’s civil war, making it a fragile buffer zone. Bangladesh is the third-largest contributor of UN peacekeepers, with more than 5,600 military and police personnel currently deployed in some of the world’s most fragile regions, according to a recent report. Bangladeshi peacekeepers are serving in Abyei, the Central African Republic, South Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Western Sahara, Lebanon and Cyprus.

title: Hadi will never be forgotten: Professor Yunus
body: Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus on Saturday said martyr Sharif Osman Hadi would never be forgotten, stressing that he would remain alive through the lessons he left for the nation. ‘Dear Hadi, you wanted to take part in the election. In expressing your desire to contest, you also taught us how elections should be conducted. Let us all accept that process,’ Professor Yunus said while speaking before the namaz-e-janaza of Hadi, convener of Inquilab Mancha. He said Hadi demonstrated how to run an election campaign and how to connect closely with people. ‘By embracing the lessons you gave us, we ensure that you remain alive in our memories. Hadi, you will never be lost. No one will ever be able to forget you. You will remain with us for decades,’ Professor Yunus added. The chief adviser also said they would continue walking on the path of national progress while remembering Hadi. Thousands of people from different walks of life joined the Janaza at Manik Mia Avenue near the Jatiya Sangsad. Many arrived in processions, chanting slogans demanding justice for Hadi and vowing that his death would not go in vain. The chief adviser, in his recent televised speech said, Hadi was an enemy of the defeated forces and fascist terrorists. ‘The evil attempt to intimidate revolutionaries by silencing his voice will be completely thwarted. No one can stop the journey to democracy of this country through fear, terror or bloodshed. Shaheed Hadi was an integral part of this process. His sole desire was to contest the upcoming elections and play an active role in the next phase of building a new Bangladesh,’ he said. The chief adviser said the government would take responsibility for Hadi’s wife and his only child. The nation observed a one-day state mourning on Saturday following Hadi’s death. On this occasion, the national flag was flown at half-mast at all government, semi-government and autonomous institutions, educational institutions, as well as government and private buildings across the country and at Bangladesh missions abroad. At the same time, special prayers and munajat were held at every mosque across the country after Jum’a prayers on Friday for the eternal peace of martyr Hadi. Expressing deep sorrow and grief at Hadi’s untimely death, Prof Yunus said the loss is irreparable for the country’s political and democratic landscape. ‘I pray for the eternal peace of his soul and express my deepest condolences to his bereaved wife, family members, relatives and colleagues,’ he added.

title: Hadi buried beside national poet’s grave on Dhaka University campus
body: Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, who died during treatment in Singapore for gunshot injury in the head, was laid to rest on Saturday afternoon by the grave of National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam, adjacent to the Dhaka University Central Mosque. Addressing Hadi’s namaj-e-janaza at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban, chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus paid an emotional tribute to Hadi, saying that his ideals would live on in the hearts of Bangladeshis for generations and would guide the nation’s political path. Yunus said that the gathering was not to bid farewell but to make a solemn pledge. ‘Osman Hadi, you are within our hearts, and for as long as Bangladesh exists, you will remain in the hearts of all Bangladeshis forever,’ he said. Security in the Manik Mia Avenue and Shahbagh areas were beefed up over the funeral as thousands of people took part in the namaj-e-janaza at about 2:30pm. Hadi was laid to rest beside the grave of the National Poet after 3:00pm, as sought by his family. At the massive gathering, Yunus said that thousands of people had not gone there to bid farewell, but to make a promise to fulfil what Hadi had left behind, stressing that the pledge would not be fulfilled by them alone and that generation after generation of people across Bangladesh would carry it forward. The chief adviser said that Hadi’s love for humanity, his conduct, his interactions with people and his political outlook were widely admired, adding that these values must remain alive in people’s minds and be pursued in practice. Recalling Hadi’s wish to take part in the upcoming Jatiya Sangsad elections, Yunus said that he had also demonstrated how electioneering should be conducted. He cited Hadi’s emphasis on ethical campaigning, reaching out to people respectfully, expressing views without causing hardship to others, and approaching citizens with humility. ‘We have accepted this teaching and we want to put it to practice,’ Yunus said. The chief adviser said that a pledge was being made to remember Hadi’s words, on behalf of all, and to continue on the path of national progress. Besides, Hadi’s brother Abu Bakar Siddique, who led the janaza prayers, and Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Jaber also spoke there. Leaders from different political parties, including the Bangladesh Nationalist Party, the Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, and the National Citizen Party attended the janaza rituals. A large number of personnel of the police, Bangladesh Army, Border Guard Bangladesh, Armed Police Battalion, Special Weapons and Tactics group, Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Party, and Detective Branch, among other law enforcement, security and intelligence forces, were seen deployed to maintain the law and order in the areas. Funeral-goers started gathering at the Manik Mia Avenue area hours before the namaj-e-janaza. The massive gathering filled the JS South Plaza field, Manik Mia Avenue, stretching to the Farmgate metro rail station. Police checkposts were also set up at the entry points to check the participants in the funeral prayers. The Dhaka Metropolitan Police deployed a big number of police personnel, including 1,000 body-worn cameras, to maintain the law and order in the area, said a text message sent by DMP deputy commissioner (Media) Talebur Rahman. Twenty BGB platoons, equipped with body-worn cameras and riot control gear, were also deployed at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban and important areas of the capital, said another text message sent by BGB headquarters public relations officer Shariful Islam. At one stage, a few hundred emotionally charged funeral attendees rushed towards the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban breaking the barricades after the namaj-e-janaza despite tight security. The law enforcers and army personnel, however, managed to stop the crowd and return them from the place without using force. Earlier on the day, the body of Hadi was taken from the cold storage of the National Institute of CardioVascular Diseases to the Suhrawardy Medical College morgue for an autopsy in the morning. A national mourning day was observed on Saturday across the country as interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus on Thursday in a televised address to the nation announced the one-day state mourning. The DMP also restricted vehicular movement on Manik Mia Avenue, diverting vehicles from several surrounding points. Following the namaj-e-janaza, Hadi’s body was taken to the burial ground at about 3:00pm and laid to rest beside the grave of the National Poet. A huge number of law enforcement, security, and intelligence personnel were also deployed around the grave site on the Dhaka university campus. They, along with volunteers, set up several layers of security barricade on the Shahbagh-DU Teacher-Student Centre road to restrict people’s access to the area and control the crowd in Shahbagh where they eventually gathered. Born in June 1993 in Nalchhiti upazila of Jhalokathi district, former Dhaka University student Hadi completed his higher secondary education at a local madrassah. Hadi, also one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last in a Singapore hospital at around 9:45pm Bangladesh time on Thursday at the age of 32 while his body was brought to the country on Friday evening. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in the capital while conducting his electioneering as an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th parliamentary elections and the national referendum slated for February 12, 2026. The law enforcers arrested at least 10 people for their suspected involvement in the attack on Hadi but the main suspected assailants were found to have fled to India.

title: Zubaida Rahman returns London
body: Zubaida Rahman, wife of BNP acting chairman Tarique Rahman, left for London on Saturday morning, aiming to return to Bangladesh on Thursday with her husband and daughter. Bangladesh Nationalist Party Media Cell member Atiqur Rahman Rumon said Zubaida departed Dhaka at about 8:30am on Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight BG-201 from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport. ‘She has gone back to London. InshaAllah, she will return to the country on Thursday with Tarique Rahman and their daughter Zaima Rahman,’ Rumon said. Zubaida came to Dhaka on December 5 from London to stay beside BNP chairperson Khaleda Zia who has been undergoing treatment at Evercare Hospital. As a member of Khaleda’s medical board, Zubaida remained at the hospital round the clock and supervised treatment activities. The BNP chief was admitted to Evercare Hospital on November 23 due to her deteriorating health. As her condition worsened, she was shifted to the Critical Care Unit under a medical board made up of local and foreign specialists, led by Professor Shahabuddin Talukder. Medical board member AZM Zahid Hossain on Friday said Khaleda Zia’s physical condition became much more stable and expressed hope that she would gradually recover. Following the encouraging improvement in Khaleda’s condition, Zubaida has decided to return to London to prepare to come back to Bangladesh permanently with her family. On September 11, 2008, Zubaida travelled to London with her daughter Zaima to support Tarique Rahman’s advanced medical treatment abroad.

title: Independence War deputy chief of staff AK Khandker dies
body: The deputy chief of staff of the War of Independence, Air Vice Marshal AK Khandker Bir Uttam, died on Saturday morning at the Combined Military Hospital in Dhaka. He was 95. He left a daughter and two sons to mourn his death. Chief adviser Muhammad Yunus expressed deep shock at the death of the liberation war veteran. Different political and socio-cultural organisations, in separate statements, also mourned his death. A press release issued by the Inter Services Public Relation Directorate said that the War of Independence veteran, also the first chief of the Bangladesh Air Force, breathed his last at about 10:35am on Saturday. His namaz-e-janaza and guard of honour will be held at Bangladesh Air Force Base Bashar at 1:45pm on Sunday. The ISPR said that he was not only a valiant freedom fighter but also a visionary leader who played a vital role in the formation of the Bangladesh Air Force. AK Khandker’s firm commitment, strategic intelligence and devotion had been a source of inspiration during the Liberation War in 1971, said the ISPR, adding that he played an important role through his directed efforts and coordination in the liberation struggle that led the country towards victory. He was appointed as the first Chief of Air Staff after the War of Independence and successfully reorganised the war-ravaged Bangladesh Air Force. The BNP leader also prayed for the eternal peace of his departed soul. AK Khandker was born in Pabna on October 31, 1930. He completed his matriculation in 1947 and ISC in 1949. He completed his graduation from PAF College in September 1952 and PSA in 1965 from Pakistan Air Force Staff College. He started his service career as a general duty pilot in January 1951. He was commissioned in the Pakistan Air Force in September 1952. When the War of Independence began in 1971, he was posted in the Pakistan Air Force Base in Dhaka. He defected with Wing Commander MK Bashar and several other pilots in May 1971 and reached India. The then Bangladesh government of Mujibnagar appointed him as the deputy chief of staff of the Bangladesh Armed Forces, and he was given the responsibility of the operation and training of the freedom fighters. He is credited as the main architect of establishing the ‘Sector Commanders Forum’ in 2005. AK Khandker was awarded the Independence Award in 2011 for his contributions to the War of Independence and for reorganising the Bangladesh Air Force. He worked as the Bangladesh High Commissioner to Australia between 1976 and 1982 and the Bangladesh High Commissioner to India between 1982 and 1986. In 1986, he was appointed as an adviser to military dictator HM Ershad and then as a planning minister of the autocratic government. AK Khandker was later elected lawmaker for the Pabna-2 constituency twice. In 2009, he became the planning minister of the Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League government. In his condolence message, the chief adviser said that AK Khandker’s works, thoughts and ideology would inspire new generations. Bangladesh Nationalist Party secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, in a condolence message, expressed deep shock at his death and condoled the War of Independence hero’s grieving family members. The National Citizen Party, Liberation war affairs adviser Faruk E Azam Bir Pratik and the Rural Journalists’ Foundation, in separate condolence messages on Saturday, expressed deep shock at the death of AK Khandker.

A 10-year-old boy was killed after being hit by a truck in the capital’s Uttara area on Saturday morning. body: UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres urges calm, restraint ahead of Bangladesh polls United Nations secretary-general Antonio Guterres has called for calm and urged all concerned in Bangladesh to refrain from violence, reduce tensions and exercise maximum restraint in order to preserve a peaceful electoral environment as the country heads to elections in February...

title: UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres urges calm, restraint ahead of Bangladesh polls
body: United Nations secretary-general Antonio Guterres has called for calm and urged all concerned in Bangladesh to refrain from violence, reduce tensions and exercise maximum restraint in order to preserve a peaceful electoral environment as the country heads to elections in February. The UN secretary-general condemned the killing of Sharif Osman Bin Hadi and extended his condolences to his family. The UN chief called on the authorities to conduct a prompt, impartial investigation, in line with international human rights standards. ‘I have been asked about the current situation in Bangladesh, and I can tell you that the secretary-general condemns the killing of a youth protest leader, Sharif Osman Bin Hadi, and extends his condolences to his family,’ said Stephane Dujarric, spokesman for the secretary-general, during a regular briefing at the UN Headquarters on December 19.

title: HRW urges Bangladesh authorities to prevent mob attacks; ensure ‘free, fair, participatory’ polls
body: The Human Rights Watch on Saturday said Bangladesh authorities should now take urgent steps to prevent the ‘mob attacks’ that have taken hold in the country since the Hasina government was ousted last August, and should ensure conditions for ‘free, fair, and participatory’ elections in February. ‘The attacks on the offices of Prothom Alo and The Daily Star are an alarming assault on freedom of expression,’ said Meenakshi Ganguly, deputy Asia director at Human Rights Watch. Ganguly said that incitement to violence by some political actors, including on social media, is contributing to an environment in which journalists, political and social activists, and even artists and singers, are deliberately placed in danger. The attacks followed the killing of an election candidate, Sharif Osman Hadi, who came to prominence during the 2024 student movement that overthrew the previous authoritarian government in 2024, said the New York-based rights body. Bangladesh is engaged in a fraught struggle to re-establish democracy and respect for human rights after the autocratic rule of Sheikh Hasina, it said. The interim government has announced elections for February 12, 2026, but political violence and failures to uphold the rule of law severely threaten civic space and risk further rights abuses, said the HRW. ‘The assassination of the youth leader Osman Hadi was a terrible act,’ said Ganguly.

title: Thousands of people attend Hadi’s janaza at Manik Mia Avenue
body: The namaz-e-janaza of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi was held at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban on Saturday afternoon. Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, advisers and leaders and activists of BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami, Inquilab Manchao, National Citizens Party and the chiefs of the three services, among others, attended the namaz-e-janaza. Chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus, religious affairs adviser AFM Khalid Hossain and an Inquilab Mancha leader spoke before the namaz-e-janaza. Hadi’s brother Abu Bakar Siddique administered the janaza at about 2:30pm. Earlier, thousands of people gathered at Manik Mia Avenue in small processions to attend the janaza. Mourners chanted various slogans, including ‘We will all be Hadi for ages, we will fight’ and ‘We will not let Hadi Bhai’s blood go in vain.’ Osman Hadi, also a prospective candidate for Dhaka-8, was shot in the head on December 12 while travelling by a rickshaw at Culvert Road in Puratan Paltan. For advanced treatment, he was airlifted to Singapore, where he succumbed to his injuries on the night of December 18. People from different parts of the capital were seen using the Metro Rail from early morning to reach the janaza venue, resulting in heavy passenger pressure at key stations. Additional police personnel and members of Border Guard Bangladesh have been deployed at key points in the capital to maintain law and order during the namaz-e-janaza. Police personnel equipped with around 1,000 body-worn cameras have been deployed to ensure overall security and prevent any untoward incident. Besides, 20 platoons of BGB have been deployed in and around important areas of the capital including the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban to strengthen security, said Shariful Islam, public relations officer of BGB. Hadi will be buried beside the grave of national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam on the Dhaka University campus in line with the wishes of his family, according to a Facebook post from Inquilab Mancha’s official page.

title: Bangladesh observing national mourning day over death of Osman Hadi
body: Bangladesh is observing the National Mourning Day on Saturday over the death of Inquilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi. The national flag has been kept at half-mast at all government, semi-government and autonomous institutions, educational institutions, as well as government and private buildings across the country and at Bangladesh missions abroad. The namaz-e-janaza of Hadi will be held at 2:30pm on Saturday at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban. The government requested those wishing to attend the janaza not to carry any bags or heavy objects. It also said that flying drones in and around the parliament complex will remain completely restricted during the funeral prayers. Meanwhile, a decision has been taken to bury Hadi beside national poet Kazi Nazrul Islam on the Dhaka University campus, in line with the wishes of his family, said a separate Facebook post from Inquilab Mancha’s official page. Hadi was shot in the head on December 12 while travelling by a rickshaw at Culvert Road in Puratan Paltan. He initially underwent surgery at Dhaka Medical College Hospital and was later admitted to Evercare Hospital. For advanced treatment, he was airlifted to Singapore, where he died from his injuries on the night of December 18. The body of Hadi arrived in Dhaka on Friday evening.

title: 10 arrested over lynching youth in Mymensingh
body: The members of law enforcement agencies have arrested 10 people for their suspected involvement in the lynching of a Hindu youth in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh, allegedly for hurting religious sentiments by making derogatory remarks about the Prophet. Seven of the suspects were arrested by the Rapid Action Battalion and three others were arrested by a joint team of the Detective Branch of police and Bhaluka police station at Square Masterbari under Bhaluka upazila at the night following Friday, the police said. The Hindu youth, Dipu Chandra Das, 25, a worker at Pioneer Knit Composite Factory, was lynched and his body was burnt after hanging it from a tree branch near his workplace in the Dubaliapara area under Bhaluka upazila Thursday night. RAB-14 commanding officer Naimul Hasan, at a press briefing on Saturday, said that they arrested the seven people after reviewing CCTV footage. The arrestees are Md Limon Sarkar, 19, Md Tareq Hossain, 19, Md Manik Miah, 20, Ershad Ali, 39, Nijum Uddin, 20, Alamgir Hossain, 38, and Md Miraj Hossain Akon, 46, he said. Nazmul said that they found no evidence of hurting religious sentiments by making derogatory remarks about the Prophet against the victim. Dipu was forced to resign from his job when agitated people gathered in front of his workplace, Pioneer Knit Composites Factory, the RAB officer said. ‘Later, when he was thrown out of the factory, the angry people beat him to death and burnt his body after hanging it from a tree branch,’ he said. The factory’s floor manager, Alamgir Hossain, and in-charge Md Miraj Hossain Akand have been arrested for handing him over to the public instead of the police, added the RAB official. ‘No one could say whether Dipu made the derogatory remarks on social media. We are investigating the whole incident,’ he said. Bhaluka police station officer-in-charge Jahidul Islam said that the police went to the scene after receiving the information, but, meanwhile, agitated people beat him to death. Mymensingh additional superintendent of police Abdullah Al Mamun said that three people were arrested in a joint operation by the Detective Branch of police and Bhaluka police station. ‘No one has the right to take the law into their own hands. An investigation is underway to determine why Dipu was handed over to the angry people instead of the police,’ he added. Dipu’s younger brother Apu Das claimed that Dipu used neither an Android phone nor any social media platforms. His father Rabi Chandra Das claimed that Dipu was educated and aware and that he could not have done such an act like insulting a religion. Alleging that Dipu was intentionally killed on a false allegation, he demanded a proper investigation into the incident. The Communist Party of Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Garment Sramik Samhati, in separate statements on Saturday, condemned the lynching and demanded the arrest of all individuals involved in the killing.

title: Election office set on fire in Kushtia
body: Miscreants set fire to the office of the senior district election officer in Kushtia town early Saturday. The incident took place at around 8:30am when attackers broke the glass of a rear window of the office building and set fire inside. Following the incident, Kushtia deputy commissioner Iqbal Hossain visited the scene at around 9:30am. Later, at 10:00am, he held an emergency closed-door meeting with the officials and staff of the office. Election office security guard Razzak said that the fire broke out at around 8:30am while he was on the second floor of the building. ‘Smelling smoke, I came downstairs and saw the fire. I immediately extinguished it using nearby water,’ he said. Kushtia district election office accountant M Asaduzzaman said the burnt room was the storeroom of the Sadar Upazila Election Office, where voter-related information is stored. It was not immediately clear whether any documents or materials were damaged, he added. Kushtia superintendent of police Mohammad Jasim Uddin said that police inspected the site. An investigation into the incident was underway, he said, adding that legal action would be taken against those found involved in the incident.

title: Security beefed up at Manik Mia Avenue over Hadi’s janaza
body: Security at Manik Mia Avenue has been beefed up as the namaj-e-janaza of Inquilab Mancha convener Sharif Osman Hadi, who died on Thursday while undergoing treatment in Singapore, is scheduled to be held in Sangsad Bhaban area on Saturday afternoon. Hadi’s namaj-e-janaza will be held at 2:00pm on Saturday at the South Plaza of the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban in Dhaka. Additional number of the police, Border Guard Bangladesh and Armed Police Battalion, among other law enforcement, security and intelligence forces personnel were seen deployed in the area to maintain law and order situation. Police check posts were also set up at the entry points to check the participants in the namaj-e-janaza. Hadi will be laid to rest beside National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam today, as demanded by his family, according to a post on Inquilab Mancha’s official Facebook page. Dhaka Metropolitan Police has deployed an adequate number of police personnel, including 1,000 body-worn cameras, for maintaining law and order in the area, said a text message sent by DMP deputy commissioner (Media) Talebur Rahman. Twenty platoons of BGB, equipped with body-worn cameras and riot control gear, also have been deployed at the Jatiya Sangsad Bhaban and important areas of the capital to maintain overall law-and-order over Hadi’s funeral, said a text message sent by BGB headquarters public relations officer Shariful Islam. Meanwhile, Hadi’s body was taken from the cold storage of the National Institute of Cardio Vascular Diseases to the Suhrawardy Medical College morgue for post-mortem examinations in the morning. A national mourning day is being observed today across the country as interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus on Thursday in a televised address to the nation announced the one-day state mourning. Sharif Osman Hadi, also one of the organisers of the July uprising, breathed his last in a Singapore hospital at about 9:45pm Bangladesh time on Thursday. The Biman Bangladesh Airlines Flight BG 585, carrying the body of Osman Hadi landed at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 5:48pm on Friday. On December 12, Hadi was shot in the head in Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering as an aspiring independent candidate for the Dhaka-8 constituency, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. The DMP has also restricted vehicular movement in surrounding areas of Manik Mia Avenue diverting vehicles at several surrounding points.

title: Enam Medical College suspends professor over ‘offensive’ comment on Hadi
body: Privately-owned Enam Medical College and Hospital in Savar has suspended a professor after she posted what authorities described as an ‘offensive’ comment on social media regarding the death of Sharif Osman Hadi. An official order issued on Friday and signed by the college principal professor Md Motahar Hossain Bhuiyan, said that professor Tazin Afrose Shah of the medicine department had been relieved of her duties with effect from December 19. The notice directed Professor Tazin to submit a written explanation within seven working days as to why she should not be permanently dismissed from her post. The action followed a Facebook post in which she commented on Hadi’s death, writing, ‘No need to be unnecessarily diplomatic. He was nothing but a worthless thug and terrorist … zero sympathy for him’. According to a copy of the post that has circulated widely on social media, professor Tazin also quoted Hadi as an architect of demolishing the house at Dhanmondi 32 of the country’s founding president Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. ‘It is unfortunate that he did not die in prolonged suffering — he went too easily’, she wrote. Hadi, a spokesman of the socio-cultural platform Inqilab Mancha, died on Thursday while undergoing treatment at a Singapore hospital after being shot in the head on December 12. Hadi’s death triggered tensions and demonstrations across the country. Professor Tazin could not be reached for comment.

title: Govt urges people to report social media posts containing calls for violence
body: The National Cyber Security Agency on Saturday urged users to directly report social media posts containing calls for terrorism and violence. A press release, issued by the posts, telecommunications and information technology ministry on Saturday morning, also read that people could directly report these posts through WhatsApp and email. It also read that after initial reviews of the complaints, the agency would report these posts to the social media platforms concerned through the Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission. People are requested to report such incidents at 01308332592 (WhatsApp number) or send mail to [email protected]. The government made the call amid widespread condemnations on arson attacks on media outlets the Prothom Alo and The Daily Star and a mob attack on Editors’ Council president and New Age editor Nurul Kabir who attempted to enter the Daily Star premises to rescue its journalists trapped there during the violence on December 18 night and early hours of the next day. The attacks were carried out after the news of the death of Inquilab Mancha convener and one of the July uprising organisers, Sharif Osman Hadi, spread on December 18 night. The Saturday release also read that it should be noted that the government could not take down any social media post, rather could only report posts related to violence to the relevant platform by citing legitimate reasons. ‘It is important to remember that hate speech that directly inspires violence or calls for violence is a punishable offence under the National Cyber Security Ordinance 2025,’ the release continued. The agency also urged people to refrain from using social media as a tool for violence or incite violence, as well as to be aware of the security of the country and the lives and property of its citizens. An interim government statement issued on Friday also called on all citizens to resist ‘all forms of mob violence committed by a few fringe elements’. ‘We strongly and unequivocally condemn all acts of violence, intimidation, arson and destruction of properties,’ said a statement issued by the chief adviser’s press wing.

title: Bangladesh interim govt must take steps over Hadi murder, mob violence: Amnesty International
body: Amnesty International has said the interim government of Bangladesh must take immediate steps to hold perpetrators of acts of violence and killings accountable in a fair trial without recourse to the death penalty. It called on the interim government of Bangladesh to ensure prompt, thorough, independent and impartial investigations into the killing of youth leader Sharif Osman Hadi, and the subsequent mob violence which led to the burning of the offices Prothom Alo and Daily Star and Chhayanaut, and the harassment of New Age editor Nurul Kabir. ‘Furthermore, we are alarmed by the lynching of Hindu garment worker Dipu Chandra Das following allegations of blasphemy,’ said the rights body in a statement. The Amnesty International condemned the mob violence which has resulted in injuries, destruction of property, and even death.

title: DMP issues seven traffic directives to avoid untoward situation during Hadi’s Janaza
body: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police on Friday issued seven traffic directives ahead of the Janaza of Inqilab Mancha spokesperson Sharif Osman Hadi, scheduled to be held on today after Zohr prayers at the South Plaza of the National Parliament. In a press release issued Friday night, DMP deputy commissioner (Media) Muhammad Talebur Rahman said that a large gathering is expected, which will restrict vehicular movement at Manik Mia Avenue. For the convenience of the Janaza, traffic from Khejur Bagan Crossing to Manik Mia Avenue will remain closed during the event. To ensure smooth traffic management, city residents and drivers have been requested to follow the following alternative routes: Mirpur Road to Farmgate via Manik Mia Avenue: Vehicles coming from the north toward Farmgate or Sonargaon should proceed via Ganabhaban Crossing–Lake Road–Urojahaj Crossing–Bijoy Sarani Crossing, then turn right toward Farmgate. Farmgate to Manik Mia Avenue via Indira Road: Vehicles should move from Farmgate to Khejur Bagan Crossing, turn right toward Urojahaj Crossing, then turn left onto Lake Road and proceed toward Ganabhaban Crossing. Dhanmondi to Farmgate: Vehicles from Dhanmondi-27 should go via Asad Gate–Ganabhaban Crossing, make a U-turn to Lake Road–Urojahaj Crossing–Bijoy Sarani Crossing, then turn right toward Farmgate. Asad Gate to Farmgate Crossing: Vehicles should turn left at Asad Gate, then right at Ganabhaban Crossing, proceed via Lake Road–Urojahaj Crossing–Bijoy Sarani Crossing, and turn right toward Farmgate Crossing. Elevated Expressway or Indira Road to Dhanmondi: Vehicles should turn right at Khejur Bagan Crossing, proceed to Urojahaj Crossing, turn left to Lake Road, then left again at Asad Gate and continue toward Dhanmondi. Mirpur Road to Dhanmondi-27: As the blockade on Manik Mia Avenue will be lifted for this route, southbound vehicles from Mirpur Road should use Shyamoli–Shishu Mela–Ganabhaban–Asad Gate and proceed straight toward Dhanmondi-27. Vehicles using the Elevated Expressway: During the Janaza, vehicles are requested to use the FDC (Hatirjheel) exit ramp instead of the Farmgate exit ramp. The DMP has urged all drivers to avoid the Manik Mia Avenue area from Saturday morning until the completion of the Janaza and burial, and to strictly follow the prescribed traffic instructions. For security reasons and to avoid inconvenience, attendees have also been requested not to carry any bags or heavy items. The DMP sought the full cooperation of city residents to ensure orderly traffic management and overall security.

title: Govt sets up 8 enforced disappearance tribunals
body: In a move aimed at addressing long-standing allegations of enforced disappearances and strengthening accountability mechanisms, the government has established Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Tribunals in all eight administrative divisions of Bangladesh. The specialised tribunals have been formed to hear and try cases of enforced disappearances within their respective divisions, including metropolitan areas, marking Bangladesh introduce for the first time a dedicated judicial framework to deal exclusively with such allegations. According to a gazette notification issued on December 17, the tribunals were established in exercise of the powers vested under Section 13 of the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Ordinance, 2025. The ordinance criminalises enforced disappearance and outlines procedures for investigation, prosecution, and redress for victims and their families. The eight tribunals will operate as: Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Tribunal, Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet, Mymensingh, Rajshahi, Rangpur, Khulna and Barishal, ensuring countrywide jurisdictional coverage. Under the ordinance, the tribunals will have the authority to officially declare a person as ‘disappeared’ if the individual remains missing for at least five years and does not return alive. Such declarations are expected to play a crucial role in enabling families to pursue legal remedies, compensation, and other civil entitlements. The government on December 18 approved the draft of the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress (Amendment) Ordinance, 2025, further strengthening the legal framework. The amendment allows the government to appoint the required number of public prosecutors for the tribunals based on recommendations from the National Human Rights Commission, a move aimed at ensuring independence and expertise in prosecution. The ordinance also expands access to justice for victims and their families. Victims or complainants will be allowed to appoint lawyers to the tribunals on their own initiative, while the spouse or any dependent family member of a disappeared person will be able to use the property of the missing individual without prior approval from the commission. Legal experts say that the establishment of the tribunals represents a major institutional step towards addressing enforced disappearances, an issue that has drawn sustained domestic and international attention over the years. Observers, however, note that the effectiveness of the new system will ultimately depend on transparent investigations, impartial prosecutions, and timely disposal of cases. With the formation of the tribunals and the amendment to the ordinance, the government has signalled its intention to institutionalise accountability and provide long-awaited legal redress to victims of enforced disappearance and their families.

title: Shipping ministry hands over water ambulance for coastal people
body: The Ministry of Shipping handed over a modern water ambulance to ensure emergency healthcare services for people living in coastal and remote char areas. The initiative was taken under the guidance of shipping adviser M Sakhawat Hossain. The water ambulance has been named Shaheed Osman Hadi Water Ambulance in memory of Sharif Osman Hadi, a fighter of the July uprising and spokesperson of Inqilab Mancha. The adviser handed over the ambulance to the Monpura upazila administration at a ceremony held at Ramnewaz Launch Ghat at Monpura on Friday. The water ambulance will facilitate patient transportation, emergency medical assistance and rapid healthcare services in river- and sea-surrounded remote areas. Speaking at the handover ceremony, Sakhawat Hossain said that the government was giving the highest priority to ensuring the fundamental rights of people in coastal and remote regions, particularly access to healthcare services. He also prayed for the departed soul of Sharif Osman Hadi and expressed heartfelt sympathy to his bereaved family members. Officials of the Ministry of Shipping and the Monpura upazila administration were present at the ceremony.

title: Thakurgaon Sugar Mill’s 68th sugarcane threshing season inaugurated
body: The 68th sugarcane threshing season of Thakurgaon Sugar Mills Limited was inaugurated on Friday by dumping sugarcane in a donga on the Cane Carrier premises of the sugar mill. Bangladesh Sugar and Food Industries Corporation chairman, additional responsibilities, and additional secretary of the Ministry of Industries Rashidul Hassan inaugurated the season at a programme as chief guest. The inaugural ceremony, organised by Thakurgaon Sugar Mills Ltd, was presided over by the managing director of the mill Md Shahjahan Kabir. Deputy commissioner Ishrat Farzana, superintendent of police Md Belal Hossain, secretary of BSFIC Mohammad Mujibur Rahman and chief of BSFIC Manjurul Haque were present as special guests, among others. During the time, various senior officials and employees of Thakurgaon Sugar Mill, Panchagarh Sugar Mill, Setabganj Sugar Mill were present. This year, the target of sugarcane planting at Thakurgaon Sugar Mill in the sugarcane threshing season is 90,000 tonnes while the production target is 5,670 tonnes and the target of sugar extraction is 6.30 per cent. In the 2024-2025 planting season, there are 6,060 acres of standing sugarcane, and the target of sugarcane planting is 6,500 acres in the season of 2025-2026. In the current season, 3,000 acres of land have been planted (in progress) so far. The threshing workday is estimated to be about 70 or 80 days. Thakurgaon Sugar Mill has been occupying the first or second place in sugar production among all the sugar mills across the country by maintaining a relatively high level of sugar quality and extraction. Those concerned are hopeful that it will continue to maintain that consistency throughout the season.

title: House of ex-Dhaka-18 MP Habib’s brother set ablaze at Uttara
body: A house belonging to the brother of former Dhaka 18 lawmaker Habib Hasan was set on fire at Uttara in Dhaka early Friday, according to the Fire Service and Civil Defence. Duty officer Shahjahan at the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters control room said that they received information about the fire at 12:15am at the house of the former Awami League MP’s brother at Uttara. Following the report, a firefighting unit was dispatched to the scene. However, the fire service vehicle was obstructed by a crowd on the way, he said. As of the last update, the fire service unit had not been able to reach the spot.
