She argued that democracy must be cultivated, not merely ‘established’ through voting, noting that an excessive focus on electoral outcomes reduced democracy to numbers. Reflecting on the 1971 Liberation War, Shireen Huq said that economic justice was central to the independence struggle, particularly in response to the disparity between the eastern and western wings of Pakistan, where equality was understood to imply a socialist economic order. However, the post-independence adoption of a free-market economy left little room for that vision. As a result, she said, Bangladesh has failed to make meaningful progress on equality, democracy or social justice. Ganosamhati Andolan chief coordinator Zonayed Saki said that the Liberation War carried clear and explicit commitments to equality, human dignity and social justice for all citizens, but these promises have remained unfulfilled even after 54 years. In many cases, he said, the country had moved in the opposite direction. Saki said that through the mass uprising of 2024, the aspiration for a discrimination-free Bangladesh had re-emerged, once again bringing to the fore the goals of establishing equality, human dignity, and social justice. To achieve these objectives, he said, a democratic transformation of the state system and the establishment of a new political settlement are essential. Saki said that a struggle must continue to ensure the rightful share of working people, protect the rights of all citizens, establish genuine dignity and justice, and create equal opportunities for everyone.

title: Victory Day today
body: The nation celebrates the 55th Victory Day, remembering the heroic and supreme sacrifices of freedom fighters to free the country from the marauding Pakistani military in the War of Independence on December 16, 1971. This year, the nation celebrates the day in a different Bangladesh after the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina regime on August 5, 2024 with renewed calls to build a society free of discrimination, restore democracy, giving people back their right to vote through holding a fair election. On this day, the nation would also take a fresh pledge to build a new Bangladesh in the spirit of the Liberation War and the 2024 July mass uprising with the aim of establishing equality, human dignity, and social justice, as pledged in the Declaration of Independence. People from all walks of life start visiting the National Memorial at Savar from the dawn and other memorials across the country to pay profound tributes to the martyrs of 1971, who sacrificed their lives for the independence of the nation culminating in the Great Victory. Law enforcement agencies have taken measures to ensure foolproof security and proper traffic management for the peaceful celebrations of the day in Dhaka and elsewhere in the country. Back on the night of March 25, 1971, the Pakistani occupation forces launched an onslaught on the Bangalee community and committed genocide on the unsuspecting and unarmed people to tame the struggle for self-determination. The War of Independence was preceded by 23 long years of intense political struggle for democracy and national identity. The commander of 92,000 marauding troops of the Pakistan military, Lieutenant General AAK Niazi, surrendered at Ramna Race Course, now Suhrawardy Udyan, in Dhaka on December 16, 1971 following nine months of independence war what was a people’s war. On the eve of the 55th Victory Day, president Mohammed Shahabuddin and interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus in separate messages greeted the nation. In their messages, they paid their deepest respects to the valiant martyrs who sacrificed their lives in the war, the wounded freedom fighters, the mothers and sisters who were raped by the Pakistani forces and their local collaborators during the war. President Shahabuddin said ‘The aim of the Liberation War was not confined merely to political independence; one of its fundamental objectives was to establish economic emancipation and social justice.’ ‘Yet even after five decades, our people have not achieved complete political and socio-economic freedom. In this context, the student-led mass uprising of 2024 has rekindled a hope for building a just Bangladesh, free from discrimination and corruption.’ Chief adviser Yunus said, ‘Through the July Uprising, we have once again gained the opportunity to establish a democratic system free from discrimination, corruption, and tyranny.’ ‘The extensive reform initiatives undertaken by the present interim government to build a well-governed and progressive Bangladesh are now advancing towards a successful completion, with the collective participation of our citizens,’ he added. He hoped that these efforts would eliminate authoritarianism and ensure transparency and accountability, while promoting people-centric and sustainable development across all spheres of the state. The Victory Day would be welcomed with 31 gun salutes at sunrise in the capital, districts, and upazilas. President Shahabuddin and chief adviser Yunus are scheduled to pay homage to the war martyrs by placing wreaths at the National Memorial at Savar on the outskirts of the capital at dawn today. Then, the Bir Shrestha families, valiant war-injured freedom fighters and freedom fighters, under the leadership of the Liberation War Affairs Adviser, will lay wreaths there. Foreign diplomats in Bangladesh and various political and social organisations, educational institutions will also pay tributes to the martyrs who made supreme sacrifices for the victory. The president will felicitate the members of the Bir Shrestha families at the Bangabhaban in the afternoon while receptions will be held for the family members of freedom fighters and martyrs in the metropolis, districts and upazilas. As part of the nationwide grand celebrations, Bangladesh has been planned to make a world record by parachuting with the highest number of national flags. The Bangladesh Army, Navy, and Air Force are scheduled to conduct separate fly-past demonstrations at the Tejgaon old airport in the city from 11:00am while a special Victory Day band show will also take place there. Besides, 54 paratroopers of ‘Team Bangladesh’ will perform a flag-bearing skydive at 11:40am to mark the 54 years of the country’s independence, which would be the largest-ever flag-parachuting display in the world, setting a new Guinness World Record. Similar fly-past demonstrations will also be conducted by the armed forces in other cities across the country while the police, BGB, and Ansar will organise band shows nationwide. On the occasion, like the previous years, the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs will organise three-day Victory Fairs across the country. The district and upazila administrations will arrange recitation sessions, essay writing and painting competitions on the Liberation War for children and organise cultural events to celebrate the day. Victory Day songs will be performed at the Suhrawardy Udyan in the city from 3:00pm today while new-generation artists will perform songs of Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra simultaneously in the 64 districts across the country. The national flag will be hoisted atop government, semi-government and private offices and autonomous bodies across the country. The day is a public holiday. Improved diet will be served in prisons, hospitals, old homes and orphanages across the country marking the day which is a public holiday. The day’s programmes also include decorating city streets with miniature national flags and illuminating important public establishments, roads and street islands. Newspapers will publish special supplements while television channels and radio stations will air special programmes. Political parties, socio-cultural and professional organisations as well as educational institutions have taken elaborate programmes to celebrate the day. The Bangladesh Nationalist Party will hoist national and party flags atop the party offices across the country to mark the day. Party leaders and activists, led by senior leaders, will place wreaths at the National Memorial at Savar in the morning. The party will also lay wreaths at the grave of BNP founder and former president Ziaur Rahman at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar in the capital at 9:30 am to mark the day. Besides, the National Citizen Party, Communist Party of Bangladesh, Workers Party of Bangladesh, Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal factions, Revolutionary Workers Party of Bangladesh, Gono Forum, Ganosamhati Andolan, Bhashani Oikyajote, Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy, Bangla Academy, Liberation War Museum, National Press Club, Dhaka Reporters Unity, Dhaka Club, among other organisations, have also taken elaborate programmes to mark the day.

title: Arms licence policy issued for politicians, JS polls candidates
body: Amid mounting concerns over security lapses ahead of the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections, the interim government on Monday approved a policy on the issuance of firearm licences to politically important persons and JS election contestants. The Election Commission has set February 12, 2026, for holding the 13th JS polls and a referendum on the July national charter concerning reforms. The Firearm Licence and Retainer Appointment Policy, 2025 was issued through a gazette on Monday. According to the gazette, the policy aims to ensure public safety, maintain law and order and prevent election-related violence by permitting eligible political figures and national election candidates to obtain firearm licences and appoint retainers under strict conditions. Home adviser retired Lieutenant General Md Jahangir Alam Chowdhury on December 13 first disclosed the information on the policy while briefing journalists at the secretariat in the capital Dhaka following a meeting on the law and order situation. The previous day, Sharif Osman Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate in the 13th parliamentary elections for the Dhaka-8 constituency, was shot in the head by assailants in the capital’s Bijoynagar area in the afternoon. Under the firearms policy, applicants must apply to the respective deputy commissioners. Licences would be issued within five days following scrutiny by the district administration, police and intelligence agencies. The licence would remain valid until 15 days after the publication of the election results. The policy allows only one non-automatic firearm for personal defence purposes, excluding weapons used for military operations. It also permits politically important persons and parliamentary election candidates to appoint one retainer, who must be at least 25 years old and trained in handling firearms. The policy explicitly prohibits the use of retainers to influence political activities or intimidate others. Firearms Act 1878, Firearms Rules 1924, Penal Code 1860, Code of Criminal Procedures 1898, the Election Commission-directed code of conduct and related policies of the home ministry were considered as the legal basis of the new licensing policy.

title: Journalist Anis Alamgir on 5-day remand
body: A Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court on Monday remanded journalist Anis Alamgir in police custody for five days for interrogation in a case filed under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Dhaka Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Jashita Islam passed the order as the investigation officer of the case, inspector Muniruzzaman, produced him before the court seeking a seven-day remand. During the hearing on the remand petition, Anis Alamgir said that he did his work as a journalist—to question the power. Anis Alamgir on Monday afternoon was shown arrested in an anti-terrorism case filed with the Uttara (west) police station over hatching conspiracy to destabilise the country committing anti-state crimes. July Revolutionary Alliance central organiser Aryan Ahmed filed the case against Anis Alamgir, actress Meher Afroz Shaon and two others under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Two other accused in the case are model Maria Kispotta and Imtu Ratish Imtiaz. Earlier, on Sunday evening, Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch took Anis Alamgir to its office in the capital’s Minto Road for questioning. The Editors’ Council in a statement on Monday condemned the arrest of journalist Anis Alamgir and filing ‘baseless’ case against him. Uttara (west) police station officer-in-charge Kazi Rafiq Ahmed on Monday afternoon said that the case was filed on Monday afternoon taking consideration of Aryan’s complaint submitted early Monday. The Detective Branch handed over Anis Alamgir to the police station, said Rafiq. According to the case statement, the accused were involved in conspiring to destabilise the country and destroy its infrastructure. It alleged that followers of fascist Sheikh Hasina were hiding in the country and hatching such conspiracy although she fled the country amid the July mass uprising in August 2024. The accused are spreading propaganda through various television talk shows and social media posts for the rehabilitation of ousted Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, it said. Anis Alamgir in recent times have expressed critical views on the activities of the Professor Muhammad Yunus-led interim government formed following the ouster of the authoritarian Awami League regime amid the July mass uprising in August 2024. He gained fame by reporting from the field during the Iraq War. He served as the editor of the daily Manabkantha. Earlier, he served as the head of news of Asian TV and Boishakhi TV. He also worked for RTV and Ajker Kagoj. Anis Alamgir studied mass communication and journalism at Dhaka University and taught at different private universities.

title: Editors’ Council condemns arrest of Anis Alamgir, demands withdrawal of false murder cases against journalists
body: The Editors’ Council in a statement on Monday strongly condemned the ‘arbitrary’ arrest of journalist Anis Alamgir and filing ‘false murder cases’ against many journalists. The council reiterated its demand for the immediate withdrawal of all baseless cases filed against journalists. On Sunday, journalist Anis Alamgir was summoned to the Detective Branch office in the capital Dhaka without any specific allegation and after keeping him detained there, he was later shown arrested in a case filed subsequently against him under the Anti-Terrorism Act, according to the statement issued by Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir and general secretary Dewan Hanif Mahmud on behalf of the council. The Editors’ Council thinks that similar practices were seen during the Awami League government tenure, when false cases, harassment and arbitrary arrests of journalists had become a routine. ‘The current incident is a repetition of that same painful reality,’ said the statement. The Editors’ Council stated that if there were any specific allegations against any journalist, those must be resolved strictly through existing laws and due legal process. ‘Summoning a journalist to an office without charges, detaining them there, or later arresting them by filing a case under the Anti-Terrorism Act is in no way acceptable,’ the statement mentioned. The council said that it was worth noting that since the fall of the Hasina government following the mass uprising on August 5, 2024, numerous journalists had been implicated in false murder cases, and many of them were still in prisons. The Editors’ Council had earlier made its position clear, demanding the withdrawal of these false cases filed against journalists. Although the government side, including the interim government law adviser, had promised action against such fabricated cases and harassment, the cases have yet to be withdrawn. The council said that such an attitude reminded them of the memoires of torture of journalists during the authoritarian regimes in the past.

title: Forces against independence still active: BNP
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Monday said that domestic and foreign forces still remained active in making the country’s independence and the legacy of the Liberation War controversial, just as they had been since 1971. Speaking virtually as the chief guest at a discussion held by the BNP at the Engineers’ Institution Auditorium in the capital Dhaka on the occasion of Victory Day, he said that while the faces and methods of these conspirators might have changed over time, their character and objectives remain unchanged. Indicating the ousted Awami League-led government, Tarique said that a fugitive clique had distorted the history of Bangladesh’s independence and the Liberation War to serve its own petty partisan interests. ‘As a result of the reckless attempt to turn the history of independence and the Liberation War into a party narrative, a defeated clique of the Liberation War is now exploiting the situation to try to write a new history of victory,’ he said. He said that the people of the country were witnesses to how, by imposing one unjustified condition after another or citing various pretexts, several anti-Bangladesh quarters had repeatedly attempted to create obstacles to holding national elections. He said that defying all such impediments, the Election Commission had finally announced the date for the long-awaited national election. Tarique said that the conspirators had not stopped yet, adding that the December 12 shooting of pro-democracy activist and Inquilab Mancha leader Sharif Osman Hadi was part of that very conspiracy. He said that those who would benefit from postponing elections and prolonging the interim government were behind acts of violence and obstruction. Tarique urged the people of Bangladesh to remain vigilant, stating that those who attempt to intimidate the nation’s freedom-loving, democratic population would ultimately fail. He stressed that instead of seeking revenge, the focus should remain on building a self-reliant, prosperous, democratic Bangladesh, ensuring that the achievements of Victory Day reach every household. Highlighting the sacrifices made to achieve the country’s independence, Tarique said that Bangladesh was won through the blood of millions of martyrs and the struggles of countless mothers and sisters. The significance of Victory Day will never diminish as long as Bangladesh exists, he mentioned. The BNP believes that freedom and democracy cannot be firmly established unless the people of the country are politically and economically empowered, Tarique said. He reiterated that the BNP had consistently supported free, fair and impartial elections to ensure that the government remained accountable to the people. Tarique said that the forthcoming national election was not merely an experiment or a routine exercise, but more complex and significant than any previous election, as it involved the aspirations, rights and future prospects of the people, as well as sovereignty and interests of Bangladesh. He said that the next decade must be one of transformation, driven by a plan to harness the potential of the country’s youth, women, farmers and workers. Tarique said that the BNP’s ultimate goal was to consolidate Bangladesh’s independence by building a self-reliant and prosperous nation, ensuring that every future Victory Day would be more meaningful. At the discussion chaired by BNP secretary general Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, the party’s standing committee members, Mirza Abbas, Abdul Moyeen Khan, Nazrul Islam Khan, Salahuddin Ahmed and Hafiz Udin Ahmed, among others, spoke.

title: CEC remarks on Hadi spark outrage
body: Chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin has dismissed the concerns that deterioration in the law and order could hinder a free and fair election, describing the recent violent incidents as isolated and not indicative of a broader disorder. Responding to a question whether the law and order poses an obstacle to credible elections, the CEC said, ‘Where is the deterioration in the law and order?’ ‘Occasionally there are one or two murders or violent incidents. The recent incident involving Sharif Osman Hadi is something we consider an isolated case,’ he further said He made the remarks on Monday while speaking at the ‘Gen Vote Festival’ held at Gulshan, Dhaka. The CEC’s comments on the shooting of Hadi have sparked strong criticism from political parties, with calls for an explanation. Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami amir Shafiqur Rahman said that the nation had not taken the CEC’s remarks well and urged him to clarify his statement. He said that it was the CEC’s responsibility to address the distress caused to the public. Meanwhile, National Citizen Party convener Nahid Islam said that by describing the incident as an isolated event, the CEC had morally lost the right to remain in office. He hoped that the CEC would withdraw his remarks on Hadi. Referring to past political violence, Nasir Uddin cited the killings of Awami League leader Ahsanullah Master and former finance minister Shah AMS Kibria, saying that such incidents occurred before and were not new in the context of elections in Bangladesh. ‘I want to unequivocally say that we have no apprehensions about the election. We are fully prepared. The election will be held with the participation and cooperation of all,’ he said. The CEC said that the commission had recently held a meeting with senior law enforcement officials and issued necessary instructions. He said that the security forces assured the commission that they were fully prepared to maintain peace and order until the polling day and to support the conduct of the election in a proper manner. The CEC urged people to remain confident that the election would be held on time in a free, fair, competitive and orderly environment. Nasir Uddin reiterated that the Election Commission remained committed to fulfilling the promises made to the nation. He also stressed the importance of youth participation, saying that Bangladesh must move forward by placing trust in its younger generation. Describing the upcoming polls as historic, the CEC said that they would, for the first time in 54 years, introduce several new measures, including the use of postal ballots to enable expatriate Bangladeshis to vote. He said that around 10 lakh officials and employees, including members of the law enforcement agencies involved in election duties, who were previously unable to vote, would be able to cast their ballots through the postal system. The CEC said that voting arrangements were also being made for prisoners, expatriates and government employees posted outside their constituencies. He said that a referendum would be held alongside the election, which would make the overall process unprecedented in scope. The CEC said that if people, particularly the younger generation, stood alongside the Election Commission in this bold initiative, the process would be successful and the election would be free, fair and credible.

title: No progress in war crime trials in 16 months
body: No progress has been made in trials of 24 cases linked to 1971 crimes against humanity in International Crimes Tribunal 1 for 16 months since Muhammad Yunus became chief adviser to the interim government. The government took office three days after the ouster of the Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League regime on August 5, 2024 amid a mass uprising. The International Crimes Tribunal was initiated by the Awami League government in March 2010 to try 1971 war crimes suspects, mostly Jamaat-e-Islami leaders, and the interim government, after taking office, reconstituted the tribunal and appointed Muhammad Tajul Islam, a lawyer who represented many Jamaat leaders in 1971 war crimes cases, as the tribunal’s chief prosecutor. The cases linked to uprising-related cases in which Awami League leaders and police and security personnel during the AL regime are accused are now getting importance in the tribunals. A total of 24 crimes against humanity cases involving 100 accused remain pending for trials before the ICT-1. Of the accused, 96 are now free on bail and four others are still in hiding, according to the records of the tribunal. ICT prosecutor, Abdus Sattar Palwan, however, referring to the office of the tribunal’s chief prosecutor’s record, said that there are 30 pending cases linked to 1971 war crimes, 29 of which are under trial, and one under investigation. He said that the cases involved a total of 210 accused. Of them, 108 are free on bails, 36 are still in hiding and 66 others died during the trials. As of December 15, 2025, jail records showed 54 detainees, 14 of whom were serving life sentences or imprisonment until death, and 40 were death sentence recipients. The Appellate Division has not heard the convicts’ appeal in at least 30 cases. The Appellate Division, however, heard the review petition of death row convict and Jamaat-e-Islami leader ATM Azharul Islam and acquitted him of the war crimes charges on May 25. It also heard the appeal filed by death-row convict Mobarak Hossain and acquitted him of the charges on July 30. Senior jail superintendent Abdullah Al Mamun, who is in charge of Kashimpur Central Jail (Part-1) and Kashimpur High Security Central Jail, said that the authorities, following the political changeover, released war crimes convict ATM Azhar three days after his acquittal. He said that another war crimes convict, Shamsul Haque alias Badar Bhai of Jamalpur, was released on November 21, 2024, after completing one year and six months of the remaining term of his total 10-year sentence. His sentence had been reduced by the Appellate Division in 2023 after he had appealed against a life term imprisonment. The copy of the verdict was released during the interim government. Shamsul Haque, a senior lawyer of Jamalpur district bar association, is the father of Barisal Range DIG Md Manzoor Morshed Alam and an uncle-in-law of ICT chief prosecutor Tajul Islam. ICT senior prosecutor Mizanul Islam said that two tribunals are currently prioritising crimes against humanity cases related to the July atrocities. ‘For the time being, we are giving more importance on the crimes against humanity cases linked to the July uprising,’ Mizanul, who earlier acted as a defence counsel for top 1971 war crimes accused, said. He said that the prosecution would take up the pending 1971 war crimes cases after two months, apparently leaving the matter to be decided by the next elected government. A total of 13 crimes against humanity cases related to the July–August atrocities are currently pending before the two International Crimes Tribunals. Several hundred complaints over the July violence are also under investigation by the tribunal’s Investigation Agency. Jail department statistics show that as of November 30, 2025, a total of 185 influential individuals were detained in connection with the July uprising cases. The detainees include about 40 former ministers or state ministers, 40 former lawmakers, and nearly 100 government officials. Prosecutor Abdus Sattar Palwan, who was also a defence counsel of many 1971 cases, said that the accused in the 1971 cases were politically targeted during the Sheikh Hasina-led Awami League regime. ‘They were implicated in the cases to serve a political agenda,’ Palwan said. Defence lawyers and court officials said that the reconstituted tribunals regularly rescheduled hearings, citing the non-appearance of witnesses. The tribunals have remained busy with newly filed crimes against humanity cases over the July–August 2024 atrocities. At least 30 appeals filed by war crimes convicts against death sentences or life imprisonment have remained pending with the Appellate Division since 2013, according to the criminal case register. The appellate process has also faced prolonged delays. In November 2025, ICT-1, chaired by Justice Golam Mortuza Mozumder, granted bail to accused Shahadat Hossain after he surrendered, lawyer Abdus Sukkur Khan told New Age. Several elderly accused travel from districts such as Jashore, Lalmonirhat and Mymensingh to appear before the tribunal. However, hearings are often adjourned to distant dates. Lawyers said that repeated rescheduling had frustrated the accused who appear in person, while others on bail often do not attend hearings as there is no visible progress in the cases. The activities of the war crimes tribunals slowed down after the execution of top Jamaat-e-Islami leaders Motiur Rahman Nizami, Abdul Quader Mollah, Muhammad Kamaruzzaman, Ali Ahsan Mohammad Mujahid and Mir Quasem Ali, and BNP leader Salauddin Quader Chowdhury.

title: Caretaker govt adviser Fazlur Rahman dies
body: Kazi Fazlur Rahman, an adviser to the country’s first caretaker government, passed away at his resident in Dhaka on Saturday. He was 93. The eminent educationist, administrator, social worker, and litterateur Fazlur Rahman died from his age-related complications, said a press release. In the post-independence Bangladesh, he held the positions of secretary to the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources and the Ministry of Education. Before retirement, he was a member of the Planning Commission with the status of Cabinet Secretary. Beyond his national responsibilities, Fazlur Rahman served various international development organisations, including the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank. He served as chairperson of the Radda MCH–FP Centre, a non-profit child and mother healthcare institute, from its inception. Fazlur Rahman authored three novels, six Bengali short story books, one English short story collection, and a five-volume diary series published in national newspapers.

title: Bangladesh SC restricts access to courtrooms over security reasons
body: Bangladesh’s Supreme Court has restricted access to its courtrooms for trial candidates and anyone other than lawyers in both its divisions from Monday, citing security concerns. The Supreme Court, being the highest judicial institution of the country, requires strict security to ensure the safety of the chief justice, judges of both divisions, lawyers conducting cases, and all concerned, said a notification issued on the order of the chief justice and signed by Supreme Court Registrar General Muhammad Habibur Rahman Siddiqui. It noted that recently trial candidates, litigants and other unauthorised persons have been entering the courtrooms, creating obstacles to security, a peaceful environment and the smooth conduct of judicial proceedings. Such activities, the notification said, have disrupted the security of judges, lawyers, officials and employees. ‘For the sake of security, access of trial candidates or any persons other than lawyers to the courtrooms of both divisions of the Supreme Court has been limited and restricted,’ it said. The notification also said that any kind of gathering, procession, and carrying of legal or illegal weapons, including deadly weapons, explosives and narcotics, has been completely banned on the Supreme Court premises. The order will remain effective from December 15 to December 31. Legal action will be taken against anyone violating the order, it warned. Lawyers, their assistants, court officials and employees, and trial seekers have been asked to remain vigilant and comply with the directive.

title: US embassy in Dhaka issues security alert for American citizens in Bangladesh
body: The US embassy in Dhaka on Monday issued a security alert for American citizens in Bangladesh, saying they should practice vigilance and remember that demonstrations intended to be peaceful in this period leading up to elections can turn confrontational and escalate into violence. ‘You should avoid demonstrations and exercise caution in the vicinity of any large gatherings,’ said the embassy in the security alert shared from its verified Facebook page. Bangladesh’s Election Commission announced that the next parliamentary election and a national referendum will occur simultaneously on February 12, 2026. Political rallies and demonstrations may become more frequent and intense as the election date approaches, said the embassy. Talking about actions to take, the embassy said, ‘Be aware of your surroundings. Monitor local media for updates. Avoid crowds. Avoid demonstrations.’

title: Authorities announce traffic diversions in Dhaka for Victory Day celebrations
body: Traffic diversions will be enforced at Gabtoli and Bypile points on the Dhaka-Ashulia and Dhaka-Aricha Highways on the occasion of the Victory Day. According to the Superintendent of Police, Dhaka, the diversions will remain in effect from 3:00am to 9:00am on December 16. During this period, vehicle drivers have been advised to use alternative routes to avoid congestion and ensure smooth traffic flow. Meanwhile, the National Memorial will be open to the public from 9:00am on December 16 for paying tribute on Victory Day.

title: Training session on quality control, quality assurance of fortified wheat flour production held in Dhaka
body: Millers for Nutrition Coalition (powered by TechnoServe) funded by Gates Foundation organised a daylong intensive training on Quality Control and Quality Assurance of Fortified Wheat Flour Production on December 14, 2025, at Hotel Lakeshore Heights in Dhaka. The training placed strong emphasis on practical application, equipping participants with the skills to identify food safety hazards, implement effective control measures, and align their production systems with international certification requirements. Representatives from nine wheat flour milling factories participated in the programme, significantly enhancing their capacity to produce high-quality fortified wheat flour that complies with both national regulations and global fortification standards. TechnoServe country programme manager Md Guljer Ahmmed delivered the welcome speech at the event. He emphasised the importance of robust food safety management systems for sustainable industry growth. Ashek Mahfuz, portfolio lead, LSFF of GAIN Bangladesh and Mahfujur Rahaman, team manager (project extension) of Buhler Bangladesh also delivered speeches during the opening session and highlighted the government’s commitment to advancing large-scale food fortification in Bangladesh. He praised TechnoServe’s continued efforts in strengthening the fortification ecosystem and encouraged producers to maintain high standards in delivering quality fortified products, including fortified wheat flour, to the market. The technical sessions, led by Md Nayem Zobayer, senior food fortification specialist, TechnoServe, covered critical components of food safety and quality management highlighting the essential steps millers must follow to ensure product safety, consistency, and compliance with national fortification standards. The presentation covered critical areas such as premix handling, dosing accuracy, process monitoring, record-keeping, and end-product testing. He emphasised that a strong QC/QA system not only safeguards public health but also strengthens consumer trust and enhances the competitiveness of Bangladesh’s flour industry in both domestic and international markets. Adwait Rode of Hexagon Nutrition highlighted that, high-quality premix is the foundation of effective wheat flour fortification — every step of the process depends on its accuracy and stability. When mills use reliable, scientifically validated premixes, they ensure that consumers receive the intended nutritional benefits consistently and safely. Md Jamal Hossain, additional director general of DG Food, attended the closing session as the chief guest. He emphasised that, although the Bangladesh government had not yet introduced fortified wheat flour within its social safety net programs, it was committed to exploring this opportunity to better nourish vulnerable populations in the future. He noted that the government was closely monitoring the rapid growth and strong potential of the consumer market for fortified wheat flour and praised the large conglomerates that have taken proactive steps to market and promote fortified products nationwide. He commended TechnoServe’s continued efforts in strengthening Bangladesh’s food fortification ecosystem. The event concluded with strong commitments from TechnoServe and Millers for Nutrition to continue supporting fortified wheat flour producers in strengthening food safety practices and advancing national nutrition outcomes. Participants gained practical knowledge on production excellence, quality control, documentation systems, and process controls — capacities that will directly help mills producing and supplying high-quality fortified wheat flour that meets both national and international standards.

title: Doctor Serajul Islam dies
body: Renowned physician and public health expert Mohd Serajul Islam passed away at a hospital in the capital on Sunday. He was 93. He was laid to rest at Uttara Sector 4 graveyard, said a press release. The former director at the National Tuberculosis and Leprosy Program and former Vice-president at the National Heart Foundation, he was undergoing treatment at the hospital for his old age complications. He is survived by his children, Dr. Rezwan Islam, Tanvir Islam, and Nabila Islam, their spouses and six grandchildren, and many family members and well-wishers. Serajul Islam is remembered for his integrity, leadership, humility, and lifelong dedication to medicine and public health. He was born in Jhenidah to the late Kismat Ali, a prominent attorney, his brothers Amirul Islam and Nazrul Islam were founding members of ABC Ltd.

title: Journalist Anis Alamgir shown arrest in anti-terrorism case
body: Journalist Anis Alamgir on Monday afternoon was shown arrested in an anti-terrorism case filed with Uttara (west) police station over hatching conspiracy to destabilise the country committing anti-state crimes. July Revolutionary Alliance central organiser Aryan Ahmed filed the case with Uttara (west) police station filed the case against Anis Alamgir, actress Meher Afroz Shaon and two others under the Anti-Terrorism Act. Two other accused in the case are model Maria Kispotta and Imtu Ratish Imtiaz. Uttara (west) police station officer-in-charge Kazi Rafiq Ahmed on Monday afternoon said that the case was filed on Monday afternoon taking consideration of Aryan’s complaint was filed on early Monday. The Detective Branch of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police handed over Anis Alamgir to the police station, said Rafiq, adding that he would be produced before the court on the same day. According to the case statement, the accused are involved in hatching conspiracies to destabilise the country and destroy its infrastructure. It alleged that followers of fascist Sheikh Hasina were hiding in the country and hatching such conspiracies although she fled the country amid the July Mass Uprising in August 2024. The accused are spreading propaganda through various television talk shows and social media posts for the rehabilitation of Awami League, though the party’s activities are currently banned. DMP DB on Sunday evening took senior journalist Anis Alamgir to its office in the capital’s Minto Road area for questioning. DMP DB additional deputy commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam, on that night said, ‘He (Anis Alamgir) has been brought here for questioning.’ Asked why he would be questioned, the DMP DB chief said that it would be disclosed later. Anis Alamgir in recent times expressed critical views on the activities of the Professor Muhammad Yunus-led interim government which was formed following the ouster of the authoritarian Awami League regime amid the July Mass Uprising in August 2024.

title: Bangladesh interim govt asks ministries, agencies to fully cooperate with EC
body: The government has issued a directive urging all ministries, divisions, directorates and agencies to ensure full cooperation with the Election Commission ahead of the 13th National Parliamentary Election and a concurrent referendum, scheduled for February 12, 2026. The Cabinet Division issued the circular on Monday, emphasising that officers and employees must perform their assigned electoral duties impartially and in accordance with the law. The circular referred to Article 126 of the Constitution of Bangladesh and Section 5 of the Representation of the People Order, 1972, emphasising that providing assistance to the Election Commission was a mandatory duty for all. It also said that in accordance with Section 446 of the RPO, no officer or employee involved in the elections might be transferred elsewhere without the commission’s permission from the announcement of the election schedule until 15 days after the results were declared. The circular also instructed the education ministry and the primary and mass education ministry to issue similar directives to teachers in government, government-aided and private educational institutions. It further directed that officers and employees, assigned with election responsibilities, should not be granted leave, transferred, or assigned any other duties that could disrupt the election process until all electoral work is complete. The circular, signed by the cabinet secretary Sheikh Abdur Rashid, urged all authorities concerned to implement the directives and take all necessary measures to provide full support to the Election Commission, ensuring a free, fair and impartial election and referendum. According to the circular, the EC has already taken all necessary steps to conduct the elections efficiently. In response to a request from the EC secretariat, the government has planned essential measures to maintain law and order throughout the electoral process. The directive highlights the need for participation from officers and employees across all public, semi-public, autonomous and semi-autonomous offices and institutions. In certain cases, personnel from private offices and institutions might also be appointed as presiding officers, assistant presiding officers or polling officers, the circular said. Teachers from government, government-aided and private educational institutions are expected to serve as election officials and assist in other electoral responsibilities. School and college buildings may also be used as polling stations and their furniture may be used for election-related purposes. The circular stressed that cooperation from all government and private employees was vital for successful execution of the elections. It cited the Electoral Officials (Special Provisions) Act, 1991 and said that any officer or employee who was assigned with election duties would remain under the supervision of the Election Commission from the date of their appointment until the completion of their responsibilities. The circular said that during this period, their election duties would take precedence and they would be required to comply with all lawful orders issued by the EC or, where applicable, the returning officer.

title: Protests at Hadi shooting on
body: Political parties and platforms on Monday continued holding rallies to voice protest at the assassination attempt on Sharif Osman Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election, demanding the arrest of the perpetrators. They blocked roads, held rallies and brought out a procession in the capital, pressing for the demand. Inqilab Mancha held an ‘All-party protest rally’ at Central Shaheed Minar in the capital protesting at the attack, demanding justice for him. Leaders and activists of several political parties, including Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami, National Citizen Party, Amar Bangladesh Party, Bangladesh Labour Party, and Gono Odhikar Parishad, joined the rally. NCP convener Nahid Islam said that the July uprising and Bangladesh itself were attacked through the attack. Criticising chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin for calling the attack on Hadi as an ‘isolated incident,’ Nahid urged him to withdraw the comment. Dhaka University Central Students’ Union vice-president Abu Shadik Kayem in a separate demonstration warned that the home adviser, the law adviser and the foreign affairs adviser would have to resign if their three-point demand, including the arrest of those involved in the Hadi killing attempt, were not met, reported New Age DU correspondent. Shadik made the demands while talking to journalists with home adviser Jahangir Alam Chowdhury standing beside him at the home affairs ministry office on Monday afternoon. At the time, he was briefing the journalists after a meeting with the adviser. Earlier on that day, DUCSU leaders began a march from DUCSU building towards the Bangladesh Secretariat around 1:00pm to lay siege to the office of the home adviser. Jatiya Chhatra Shakti, the student wing of the National Citizen Party, on Monday blocked the Shahbagh crossing for about three hours from about 12:30pm and staged a sit-in, demanding resignation of the home adviser. The blockade triggered severe traffic congestion in the city’s one of the busiest thoroughfares, causing patients and commuters serious suffering, particularly as two large hospitals are situated overlooking the crossing. Addressing the sit-in, Jatiya Chhatra Shakti Dhaka University unit president Tahmid Al Muddassir said, ‘We have blocked the road as the interim government has failed to arrest Hadi’s shooters.’ ‘The overall law and order situation has also deteriorated and therefore we are demanding resignation of the home adviser,’ he added. Critically injured Inqilab Mancha convener Hadi on Monday afternoon was flown to Singapore from Dhaka in an air-ambulance for advanced medical treatment. Meanwhile, an attempted murder case was filed on Sunday night, two days after the attack, against suspected shooter Faisal Karim Masud and several other unidentified assailants. So far, six were arrested in this connection. On Friday afternoon, Hadi was shot in the head in Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum slated for February 12, 2026. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar on a battery-run rickshaw when a helmeted pillion rider on a riding motorcycle opened fire on him on the Box Culvert road. The motorcycle rider, who was also in helmet, sped to flee the scene, with the gunman at his back. The police and Inquilab Mancha activists suspect that the two unknown individuals who, wearing facemasks, took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for the past few days and also on the day of the assassination attempt were involved in the shooting. Physicians said that Hadi was seriously injured as a bullet pierced his head above the right ear, causing significant brain damage.

title: 507 people killed in 526 accidents across Bangladesh in Nov: report
body: At least 507 people were killed and 899 others were injured in 526 road accidents across Bangladesh in November this year, according to a report of the Passenger Welfare Association of Bangladesh. Motorcycle accidents caused significant numbers of deaths, said the report released on Monday. It said that 201 people (41.1 per cent of the deaths) were killed and 171 people (20.82 per cent of the injured) were injured in 195 road accidents (38.69 per cent of the accidents) involving motorcycles. In 44 railway accidents, 40 people were killed and one was injured. In seven waterways accidents, six people were killed and four remained missing. The association issued a press release with a summary of its monthly report, which was based on tallying the incidents reported by the media. Regarding the occupations of those who died, 127 were transport workers, including drivers, 93 were pedestrians, 43 students,12 teachers, six political leaders and activists, six were members of differently law enforcement agencies and five were physicians. Of the dead, 50 were children.

title: Hadi airlifted to Singapore for advanced treatment
body: Critically injured Sharif Osman Hadi, the convener of Inquilab Mancha, was on Monday flown to Singapore from Dhaka in an air ambulance for advanced medical treatment. A leader of the Mancha, on the other hand, filed an attempted murder case against suspected shooter Faisal Karim Masud and several other unidentified attackers Sunday night, two days after the attack. The law enforcers arrested three more individuals in connection with the attempted murder. As a result, six people have been arrested for their suspected involvement in the incident. The air ambulance carrying Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad election for the Dhaka-8 constituency, departed from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at about 2:00pm on Monday. After the departure, Professor Md Sayedur Rahman, a special assistant to the chief advisor, told reporters at HSIA that the government arranged the air ambulance to shift Hadi to Singapore General Hospital from the Evercare Hospital in Dhaka where the victim had been under treatment since December 12, following operations in his head at Dhaka Medical College Hospital. He was airlifted following the approval of Singapore General Hospital and Evercare Hospital authorities for a four-hour flight, said Sayedur. He said that Hadi can complete the flight as his different organs, including the kidney, heart and respiration, except the bullet-wounded brain, could be controlled by medicine or oxygen support. Hadi’s brother Omar Bin Hadi and one of Omar’s friends are accompanying Hadi. Paltan police station officer-in-charge Mohammad Mostafa Kamal Khan said that Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Jabir, with the consent of Hadi’s family, filed an attempted murder case against Faisal Karim Masud and several unidentified people. He said that the Detective Branch of Dhaka Metropolitan Police would investigate the case. OC Mostafa Kamal said that the Rapid Action Battalion arrested three more people in connection with the incident and handed them over to the police Sunday night. The arrestees are prime suspect Faisal’s wife Samia, his brother-in-law Shipu and Faisal’s girlfriend Maria. The metropolitan police’s Detective Branch produced the trio before a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court that allowed the police to take them in custody for five days for interrogation in the case, he said. Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s deputy commissioner for media and public relations Muhammad Talebur Rahman on Monday evening said that different specialised units of the police were conducting operations to arrest the assailants. Different political parties and platforms on Monday continued to rally protesting at the attack on Hadi, demanding the arrest of the perpetrators. They blocked roads, held rallies and brought out processions separately in the capital and elsewhere in the country to press home the demand. Border Guard Bangladesh’s sector-39 commander Colonel Sarkar Mohammad Mostafizur Rahman, at a press briefing at its sector headquarters in Mymensingh on Monday, said that the issue of the two identified attackers’ escaping to India illegally would be determined only after arresting Philip Snal, who helps people to cross the border illegally. The BGB official held the press conference as it was believed that the main identified assailants, Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, and the pillion of the motorcycle, Faisal Karim Masud, the suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days, fled to India illegally through the Haluaghat border in Mymensingh, New Age correspondent in Mymensingh reported. On December 12 afternoon, Hadi was shot in the head in the Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th Jatiya Sangsad elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. Physicians said that Hadi was seriously injured as a bullet pierced his head above the right ear, causing significant brain damage. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar on an auto-rickshaw when the two men wearing helmets on a motorcycle opened fire on him on the Box Culvert road before fleeing the scene.

title: ICT prosecution appeals seeking death sentence for Hasina, Asaduzzaman
body: The chief prosecutor on Monday filed an appeal against the November 17 verdict of the International Crimes Tribunal-1, jailing deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina and former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan until death for provocation on the crackdown against July-August 2024 protesters. The appeal seeks the death penalty instead of life-term imprisonment on the provocation charge. The tribunal found that Hasina, also the Awami League president, provoked nationwide unrest by calling student protesters ‘Razakars’ at a press conference at Ganabhaban on July 14, 2024. Hasina and Asaduzzaman were convicted on three counts of crimes against humanity for their role in atrocities committed during the July 2024 uprising. They were sentenced to death on two counts and life term imprisonment on one count linked to the provocation. Both the accused are absconding and are believed to be staying in India. Prosecutor Gazi Monwar Hossain Tamim told reporters that the prosecution had prayed to the Appellate Division to enhance the ICT awarded jail until death sentence to death sentence for Hasina and Asaduzzaman on the provocation charge. Another accused, former inspector general of police Chowdhury Abdullah Al Mamun, received a reduced sentence of five years after testifying as a state witness. He is currently in custody. The tribunal said that Hasina’s provocative remarks, along with her instruction to Dhaka University vice-chancellor Maksud Kamal to ‘hang them like Razakars’, sparked violent protests on the university campuses across the country. It found that the provocation directly led to the killing of student coordinator Abu Sayeed in front of Begum Rokeya University in Rangpur on July 16, 2024. Hasina and Asaduzzaman were also sentenced to death on charges of ordering the use of drones, helicopters and lethal weapons against protesters. The tribunal said that the orders were given during conversations with Sheikh Fazle Noor Taposh and Hasanul Haq Inu. Six students were killed at Chankharpool, while six others were burned to death in Ashulia, according to the verdict.

title: Metro rail services to remain briefly halted today
body: Metro rail services in Dhaka city will remain suspended for 40 minutes today, Tuesday, to ensure safety during a parachute jump as part of Victory Day celebration. Metro rail system’s implementing agency Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited in a press release on Monday also stated that the services would remain closed from 11:50am till 12:30pm on the entire route to ensure safety of the paratroopers. The services of the country’s first 20.1-kilometre metro rail system were inaugurated on December 28, 2022, on the Uttara-Agargaon section. Later, the services were extended up to Motijheel. Currently, work is going on to extend the route up to Kamalapur.

title: Attempt to murder case filed over shooting Hadi, three more suspects held
body: An attempt to murder case was filed on late Sunday against suspected shooter Faisal Karim Masud and unidentified assailants over shooting Sharif Osman Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate in the upcoming national polls for the Dhaka-8 constituency. Meanwhile, the Rapid Action Battalion detained three more people and handed them over to police over the incident. Hadi is now undergoing treatment with ‘very critical’ health condition at Evercare Hospital’s critical care unit and scheduled to be shifted to Singapore by an air-ambulance on Monday afternoon for better treatment. Paltan police station officer-in-charge Mohammad Mustafa Kamal on Monday morning said that Inquilab Mancha member secretary Abdullah Al Jaber filed the case with the police station after 11:00pm on Sunday with the consent of Hadi’s family. The case was filed against one named and several unnamed accused, he said, adding that the Detective Branch of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police would investigate the case. The three more detainees are Faisal’s wife Samia, his brother-in-law Shipu and Faisal’s girlfriend Maria. According to RAB, Samia and Shipu were detained from Narayanganj and Maria from Dhaka. They were handed over to Paltan police station on Sunday night. OC Mustafa said that detainees were being interrogated to find out the motive behind the incident and the role of those involved. Earlier, a team of the RAB-2 identified the motorcycle used in the attack on Hadi and detained the owner Hannan from Mohammadpur area in the capital on Saturday night while the police nabbed Sivion and Sanjay, who help people to cross the border illegally, from Sherpur’s Nalitabari on Sunday. On Friday afternoon, Hadi was shot in the head in Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar on an auto-rickshaw when the two men wearing helmets on a motorcycle opened fire on him on the Box Culvert road before fleeing the scene. Police and Inquilab Mancha activists suspected that the two unknown individuals, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for the past few days wearing face masks and also on the day of the incident, were involved in the shooting. The police identified the two assailant as Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, and the pillion of the motorcycle Faisal Karim Masud, suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days. Physicians said that Hadi was seriously injured as a bullet pierced his head above the right ear, causing significant brain damage.

title: Complaint filed against Anis Alamgir, Shaon, two others
body: A complaint was filed on early Monday against journalist Anis Alamgir, actress Meher Afroz Shaon and two others over committing anti-state crimes and hatching conspiracies to destabilise the country. July Revolutionary Alliance central organiser Aryan Ahmed filed the complaint with Uttara (west) police station. The two other accused are model Maria Kispotta and Imtu Ratish Imtiaz. According to the complaint, the accused are involved in hatching conspiracies to destabilise the country and destroy its infrastructure. It alleged that followers of fascist Sheikh Hasina were hiding in the country and hatching such conspiracy although she fled the country amid the July Mass Uprising in August 2024. The accused are spreading propaganda through various television talk shows and social media posts for the rehabilitation of Awami League, though the party’s activities are currently banned. Uttara (west) police station officer-in-charge Kazi Rafiq Ahmed on Monday morning said that the complaint was filed at about 2:30am. ‘Further legal action regarding the complaint will be taken after having discussions with higher authorities,’ said Rafiq. Detective Branch of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police on Sunday evening took senior journalist Anis Alamgir to its office in capital’s Minto Road area for questioning. DMP DB additional deputy commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam, on that night told New Age, ‘He (Anis Alamgir) has been brought here for questioning.’ Asked why he would be questioned, the DMP DB chief said that it would be disclosed later. Anis Alamgir in recent times expressed critical views on the activities of the Professor Muhammad Yunus-led interim government which was formed following the ouster of the Awami League regime amid the July Mass Uprising in August 2024.

title: Youth shot to death by unidentified killers in Khulna
body: A youth was shot dead by unidentified killers near the east side of the Rupsa Bridge in Chourasta area of Japusa in Rupsa upazila of Khulna district on Sunday night. The deceased was identified as Sagar Sheikh, 30, son of Foyek Sheikh and a resident of Green Bangla Residential Area. He used to run a clothing shop. According to Rupsa police, local resident Abdur Rahman, hearing gunshots at about 11:00pm, called the national emergency service 999 to report the incident. The police were subsequently informed and rushed to the scene. Sub-inspector Saurav Das of Rupsa Police Station said he was on duty in Japusa area and reached the spot after receiving the information. Preliminary investigation suggest that Sagar had recently purchased land and built a new house in the area, which might have led to the killing, he suspected, saying that the motive and identities of the attackers are yet to be determined. Officer-in-charge of the police station Abdur Razzak Mir said efforts were underway to detain those involved in the murder.

title: Dhaka becomes 9th most polluted city with AQI score of 155
body: Dhaka, the overcrowded capital city of Bangladesh, has ranked ninth on the list of cities with the worst air quality with an AQI score of 155 at about 9:50am on Monday. On Monday, Dhaka’s air was classified as ‘unhealthy’ referring to a healthy threat, according to the AQI score. Such unhealthy air quality continued for the past few days. When the AQI value for particle pollution is between 50 and 100, air quality is considered ‘moderate’, usually sensitive individuals should consider limiting prolonged outdoor exertion, between 101 and 150, air quality is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, between 150 and 200 is ‘unhealthy’, between 201 and 300 is said to be ‘very unhealthy’, while a reading of 301 and above is considered ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks to residents. India’s Delhi, Pakistan’s Karachi and again Lahore cities respectively occupied the first, second and third spots on the list, with AQI scores of 316, 213, and 196 respectively. The AQI, an index for reporting daily air quality, informs people how clean or polluted the air of a certain city is and what associated health effects might be a concern for them. The AQI in Bangladesh is based on five pollutants — particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), NO2, CO, SO2, and ozone. Dhaka has long been grappling with air pollution issues. Its air quality usually turns unhealthy in winter and improves during the monsoon. As per World Health Organisation, air pollution kills an estimated seven million people worldwide every year, mainly due to increased mortality from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer, and acute respiratory infections.

title: Smugglers attack BGB in Sylhet border
body: The Border Guard Bangladesh on Sunday filed a case with the Companiganj police in Sylhet against about 30 suspected smugglers on charge of attacking BGB personnel along the Companiganj border early Saturday. Companiganj police officer-in-charge Shafiqul Islam Khan said that the case was filed against 30 attackers, including seven people named. The police officer said that none of the suspects had yet been arrested. According to the case statement, a motorcyclist, who was driving recklessly, fled the scene at Uttar Ranikhai of Companiganj on Saturday morning after a BGB team had chased him. The BGB personnel found 167 bottles of Indian liquor from the spot. But soon, a group of about 30 people started pelting the BGB personnel with stones, forcing them to fire blank shots to disperse the attackers. The BGB 48 Battalion commander Lieutenant Colonel Nazmul Haque said that the soldiers had fired four blank shots in self-defence.

title: Management of liabilities from third quarter
body: The Finance Division under the finance ministry will introduce Liability Management Operation from the third quarter of the current financial year of 2025-26 to minimise the government exposure to debt distress. The division will also issue a budget implementation plan soon, said Finance Division officials. The government faces increasing debt distress due to rapidly rising external and domestic borrowing for mega projects, leading to higher repayment burdens and dwindling foreign exchange reserves. The liability management operations will be among the exercises the Finance Division has to do as part of the progress and evaluation framework for a smooth transition strategy of the country that is scheduled to exit the least developed countries bloc on November 24, 2026, add the officials. By introducing the Liability Management Operation, the Finance Division will strengthen the monitoring system for the State Owned Enterprises and Autonomous Bodies to mitigate the financial hazards that may incur from them. The total debt of the 101 SOEs and Abs was Tk 6,39,782.58 crore as of 30 June 2023 which was 26.04 per cent higher compared to the previous year, according to the Debt and Contingent Liability of 101 SOEs and ABs released by Finance Division in December 2024. Of the 101 SOEs and ABs, 24 SOEs possess contingent liability. The total contingent liability in FY23 was Tk 18,590.74 crore on June 30, 2023. As many as 14 SOEs face very high risk They include Bangladesh Power Development Board, Maddhapara Granite Mining Company Limited, Dhaka Leather Company Limited, Shaympur Sugar Mill Ltd, Joypurhat Sugar Mill Ltd, Rajshahi Sugar Mill Ltd, Natore Sugar Mill Ltd, Kushtia Sugar Mill Ltd, Mobarakgonj Sugar Mill Ltd, Pabna Sugar Mill Ltd, Faridpur Sugar Mill Ltd, Renwik Jajneswar and Company Limited, Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation, and National Tea Company Limited. These SOEs have been identified to have very high risk. In June 2025, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank said that Bangladesh faced a moderate risk of external and overall debt distress, from the previous low, due to revised lower export data for 2023-24. A WB report on December 5 said that Bangladesh’s external repayments grew the fastest in South Asia as it paid $7.3 billion in total in 2024, a 617 per cent jump from 2010. Finance Division officials said that under the budget implementation plan all ministries, divisions and agencies had been asked to devise separate budget implementation plans aiming to ensure proper implementation of the country’s fiscal budget. They were also asked to prepare the implementation progress reports of their respective budgets quarterly. The Finance Division has long been trying to increase the budget implementation rate without much success. The country’s budget implementation rate generally has been hovering around 80-90 per cent for non-development budget, while development budget execution has been staying at about 72 per cent,

title: ACC finds Tk 711cr ‘illegal’ assets of Aziz Khan, family
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission on Sunday issued a notice to Summit Group chairman Mohammad Aziz Khan, his wife and daughter to submit wealth statements to the commission as inconsistencies of Tk 711 crore were found with their incomes. The commission also found evidence of money laundering abroad against Aziz Khan and his family members, said its director general (prevention) Md Akhter Hossain at a press briefing at its headquarters in Dhaka city. Earlier, the inquiry team led by commission deputy director Md Alamgir Hossain submitted a report to it regarding the assets of Aziz Khan and his family members. The inquiry report stated that information on movable assets worth Tk 330.93 crore was found in the name of Summit Group chairman Aziz Khan. However, a review of the income tax documents showed that he did not mention any information about immovable assets. The amount of assets shown by him in the submitted wealth statement was inconsistent with his known income, said the report. Aziz Khan also acquired assets through laundering money in various countries, including Singapore, it said. The commission also found information on immovable assets worth Tk 1.57 crore and movable assets worth Tk 91.5 crore in the name of Aziz’s wife Anjuman Aziz Khan. But the value of the immovable assets shown in the income tax documents was lower than their actual value, the inquiry revealed that also found these assets inconsistent with her income. The ACC also found information on assets worth Tk 287.43 crore in the name of their daughter Ayesha Aziz Khandkar that were inconsistent with her income. Summit Corporation Limited in a statement on ‘Personal Tax Return of Khan Family’ has said that Muhammead Aziz Khan, Anjuman Aziz Khan, and Ayesha Aziz Khan had noted several news releases concerning an inquiry report by the Anti-Corruption Commission. ‘We learned of these actions entirely through the media reports. We are committed to cooperating fully with any official legal process,’ said the statement issued on December 15. ‘The monetary figures cited in the newspaper reports, i.e. Tk 330.94 crore for Muhammead Aziz Khan, Tk 92.62 crore for Anjuman Aziz Khan, and Tk 287.43 crore for Ayesha Aziz Khan (overstated by exactly Tk 3 crores), correspond precisely to the assets that have been regularly, consistently, and transparently declared in their respective individual income tax returns filed with the National Board of Revenue (NBR) in Bangladesh,’ the company claimed. It said that these income tax returns were comprehensive documents that not only list assets but also explicitly provided the detailed source of every earning. ‘Therefore, the allegations of "misdeclaration," "inconsistency," or a "mismatch" between declared income and assets are fundamentally misplaced. The reported figures are the declared figures in the tax returns,’ the statement claimed.

title: S Alam, Nabil Group MD among 38 sued
body: The Anti-Corruption Commission on Sunday filed a case against 38 people, including S Alam Group chairman Mohammad Saiful Alam, Nabil Group managing director Md Aminul Islam and former and current senior officials of Islami Bank Bangladesh, on charges of embezzling Tk 1,045 crore through a fictitious entity ‘Zaman Syndicate’ at the bank’s Pabna branch. The commission also filed a case against private satellite television channel Bangla TV managing director Syed Samadul Haque on charges of amassing illegal wealth worth Tk 4.05 crore. ACC director general (prevention) Md Akhtar Hossain disclosed the information to media at a briefing at the commission’s headquarters in the capital Dhaka. According to the ACC, the accused with the connivance of each other committed the crime by creating forged and fabricated documents and embezzled nearly Tk 7,000 crore from various banks across the country in the name of loans taken by Nabil Group and other related entities, both directly and through proxies. As part of the scam, a paper-based institution named ‘Zaman Syndicate’ was opened in the name of an employee of Nabil Group at Islami Bank’s Pabna branch, through which Tk 1,045 crore was approved and disbursed as Bai-Murabaha TR (trust receipt) investment. The inquiry revealed that out of the approved amount, over Tk 1,008 crore was disbursed and embezzled by showing fake trading activities. At the same time, crimes of money laundering were also committed through transfer and conversion of funds to conceal the source and nature of the money. Along with S Alam Group chairman Mohammad Saiful Alam, his family members, Nabil Group managing director Md Aminul Islam and Zaman Syndicate chairman Rokunuzzaman Mithu, former and current managing directors, deputy managing directors, members of the executive committee and other senior officials of Islami Bank’s Pabna branch, zonal office and head office are among the 38 accused in the case. The ACC filed a case against Bangla TV MD Samadul Haque over allegation of amassing illegal wealth worth Tk 4.05 crore beyond his known sources of income. The ACC, during its inquiry, found a total wealth worth about Tk 11,41,66,771 belonging to Syed Samadul Haque, but he provided valid documents against wealth worth about Tk 7,34,10,908.

title: Bangladesh
body: Opinions of judges play opinions play key role in shaping state direction: CJ Chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed on Sunday said that many opinions of the judges played an exceptional role in shaping the direction of the state and the history. Chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed on Sunday said that many opinions of the judges played an exceptional role in shaping the direction of the state and the history. At least 258 factories shut down over the past year, leaving more than 100,000 workers unemployed and heightening social and economic risks, according to a report by the Asia Floor Wage Alliance. The farewell of retirees, reception of past executive committee and the awarding of Election Commission of the Staff Association of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology were held on the campus on Sunday. Gazipur Agricultural University concluded its two-day international conference titled Regenerative Agriculture for Food Security at the GAU on Saturday. The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Sunday alleged that the killings of the nation’s intellectuals at the fag end of the 1971 War of Independence were carried out by Indians as part of a planned conspiracy devised in Delhi to create an intellectual vacuum in the country. The Business Club of BGMEA University of Fashion and Technology inaugurated a two-day National Entrepreneurship Expo 2025under the theme ‘leadership and how to create success at the BUFT in Dhaka on Sunday. The road transport and bridges ministry plans to develop 42 natural multi-modal transport hubs across the country to increase the shares of passenger and cargo on railways and waterways. Jagannath Hall authorities at Dhaka University on Sunday removed the portraits of convicted war criminals and former Jamaat-e-Islami leaders Ghulam Azam, Matiur Rahman Nizami and Quader Mollah drawn on the streets inside the hall. Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Sunday said that the next elected government must prioritise establishing the rule of law and addressing systemic corruption. The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Sunday set December 21 to decide whether charges of crimes against humanity would be framed against 17 accused allegedly involved in the abduction, detention and torture of people with dissenting views... The Rajshahi divisional administration on Sunday directed the eight deputy commissioners of the division to submit detailed information on the installed and unsealed deep tube wells amid growing concerns over public safety. Two people, including a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver and a vegetable vendor, were found dead in Sylhet and Habiganj on Sunday morning. The heads and members of the reform commissions and others at a discussion said on Sunday that the expected reform did not happen despite people’s eager aspirations mainly due to bureaucracy along with other anti-reform actors, including some political parties. Election commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah on Sunday said that any attempt to obstruct, sabotage or undermine the upcoming election would fail, warning that law enforcement agencies would act firmly wherever necessary to ensure security. Highlighting the importance of Dhaka-Delhi friendship, Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma on Sunday said they are willing to work together to fulfil the aspirations of their people and forge closer people-to-people ties, inspired by their shared sacrifices of the past and guided by the new aspirations for the future.

title: Opinions of judges play opinions play key role in shaping state direction: CJ
body: Chief justice Syed Refaat Ahmed on Sunday said that many opinions of the judges played an exceptional role in shaping the direction of the state and the history. ‘It cannot be denied that, in different political junctures, the judiciary has been considered as an unacknowledged accomplice in unconstitutional power, misrule, and state deception. Many judges have shrouded the circle of misrule and have been directly or indirectly involved in injustice and oppression. I believe that this moral deviation of the judiciary, alongside other state institutions, was one of the key factors that ultimately compelled the public to take the decision, even in July uprising 2024’ he said. Refaat Ahmed came up with the observations while speaking at his farewell address at Supreme Court auditorium at noon, before going into retirement as the 25th chief justice on December 27. In his address to the judges present on the occasion, the chief justice urged them to regard the pursuit of knowledge and reading habits as the highest duty of their lives. He encouraged them to constantly engage in study, research, and the development of judicial experience. ‘Let the primary foundation of all our efforts be not merely the execution of work, but the pursuit of excellence in that work,’ he said. He further urged the judges to go beyond traditional learning and expand their knowledge in the realms of society, culture, anthropology, history, economics, and political thought. At the same time, he encouraged them to explore diverse branches of modern science and technology, such as artificial intelligence, environmental science, and cyber security. ‘Because as judges, we can never be certain which daily occurrences in people’s lives may give rise to disputes and when these will come before the court. From which level of life, under what circumstances, unprecedented questions will be brought to the court, testing our judgment and discernment,’ he added. He concluded that all forms of knowledge and every pulse of society, influence decision-making and the writing of judgments, and that many judges’ opinions also play an exceptional role in shaping the direction of the state and history. Referring to the historic establishment of the Supreme Court secretariat, the chief justice said that the separate secretariat and the independence of the judiciary must be established as the primary guardian of all constitutional rights of the people of the country. He emphasised that strict action must be taken against corrupt and dishonest judges. He further stated that judges should no longer point fingers at others for injustices committed by the judiciary itself. ‘We must fulfil our hundred per cent responsibilities to ensure quick justice for the people. Political influence must be avoided in the pursuit of preferred outcomes.’ Refaat Ahmed reminded that while the law is part of broader politics, judges must strive to rise above politics. ‘If the judiciary’s role is limited to maintaining the balance necessary for the ruling class, there is no need for a separate judicial institution—the executive and police would suffice. Regardless of the ideals on which the constitutional foundation of the state is built, judges must perform their duties with integrity and sound judgment.’ Judges from Appellate Division of the Supreme Court, attorney general Md Asaduzzaman, senior advocate Zainul Abedin, Supreme Court Bar Association president AM Mahbub Uddin Khokon, all district and session judges, metropolitan sessions judges, chief judicial magistrates and chief metropolitan magistrates, were among others, present.

title: 258 factories shut in a year, 1,00,000 lose jobs: AFWA
body: At least 258 factories shut down over the past year, leaving more than 100,000 workers unemployed and heightening social and economic risks, according to a report by the Asia Floor Wage Alliance. Amrin Hossain Annie, gender officer of Bangladesh Nari Progati Sangha, presented the findings at a dialogue titled ‘Actions needed amid technological transition, climate change and existing labour conditions’ held at the National Press Club on Sunday.
