Presided over by labour leader Abul Hossain, the function was addressed, among others, by economist Professor MM Akash, joint convenor of Sramik Karamchari Oikya Parishad Abdul Quader Howlader, president of Bangladesh Mahila Parishad Fouzia Moslem and Bangladesh representative of AFWA Arifur Rahman. Speakers said the combined impact of technological transformation, climate change and fragile labour conditions had pushed the garment sector into a more complex and uncertain reality. They stressed the need for a coordinated roadmap integrating technology, climate resilience and labour rights to overcome the ongoing crisis. Amrin said there was a clear disparity between the total profits generated by the garment industry and the wages received by workers. Despite Bangladesh’s critical position in the global supply chain, workers’ wages have yet to reach a living standard, she noted. Production costs and international competition are often shifted onto workers, limiting improvements in their quality of life. Currently, nearly four million workers are employed in the garment sector, more than 60 per cent of them women. While women’s participation in the workforce is a major achievement for economic development, their access to safe employment, gender-sensitive workplaces and decision-making processes remain limited. Political instability, declining buyer confidence, export market competition, power and energy shortages, and the global economic slowdown have further deepened uncertainty in the sector, she added. Professor Akash said resolving the crisis required coordinated action, including the declaration and enforcement of a humane, living national minimum wage. No worker’s wage should fall below the poverty line, he said, calling for rationing systems, training centres and the right to form trade unions across all sectors. He urged labour organisations to unite on a common platform to strengthen workers’ solidarity. Labour leader Abul Hossain said resolving the industry’s problems required the participation of all stakeholders, including workers, owners and the government. He emphasised the need to address low wages and wage discrimination and to ensure healthy and safe working conditions in factories.

title: CUET Staff Association holds farewell, reception
body: The farewell of retirees, reception of past executive committee and the awarding of Election Commission of the Staff Association of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology were held on the campus on Sunday. CUET vice-chancellor Professor Mahmud Abdul Matin Bhuiyan was chief guest at the event organised at CUET central auditorium. The special guests were the chief election commissioner of the Staff Association Election 2025 and Department of Petroleum and Mining Engineering head Professor Abu Sadat Muhammad Sayem, vice-president of the teachers association and professor of mathematics Ujjwal Kumar Deb and officers association president Syed Mohammad Ikram. In addition, chief engineer Md Sirajul Islam and retired employee Raji Ahmed also spoke. The event was presided over by CUET Staff Association president Mohammad Jamal Uddin and the address of welcome was delivered by its general secretary Priyatosh Chakraborty. The event was moderated by Abdul Al Hannan and Bishwajit Bhattacharya, said a press release.

title: GAU concludes conference on regenerative agriculture
body: Gazipur Agricultural University concluded its two-day international conference titled Regenerative Agriculture for Food Security at the GAU on Saturday. The second day began with a session on science, innovation and practice for regenerative agriculture, where national researchers, policymakers and international participants shared scientific insights, innovative ideas and real-world field experiences, said a press release. The closing ceremony was held in the presence of Professor GKM Mustafizur Rahman, vice-chancellor of GAU, as chief patron, while Major General Hussain Muhammad Masihur Rahman attended as chief guest. Head of Agrospace of Switzerland Stefan Mann attended as guest of honour while GAU pro-VC Professor M Moynul Haque and Islamia University of Bahawalpur, Pakistan’s Professor Wajid Nasim Jatoi attended as special guests at the conference. The conference featured 10 high-quality research presentations across 10 thematic areas, highlighting advancements in regenerative farming technologies, soil health, climate-resilient agriculture and food security. A poster presentation session further encouraged knowledge exchange among participants. Professor Md Mizanur Rahman, convener of the scientific committee, presented a brief overview of the conference outcomes. Outstanding researchers were recognised with Outstanding Presentation Awards in oral, poster and oral flash categories. Masihur Rahman emphasised regenerative agriculture as a key driver of future food security in the face of climate change, urging researchers and agricultural professionals to continue their efforts with renewed commitment. Professor Mustafizur Rahman said that international conference served as a strong platform for knowledge exchange, policy dialogue, and future collaboration among researchers, policymakers and global experts. He expressed hope that the research insights and recommendations would have a lasting positive impact on Bangladesh’s food security and open new horizons for advancing regenerative agriculture, concluding with sincere thanks to all. Professor Md Safiul Islam Afrad, treasurer of GAU and convener of the organising committee, expressed sincere thanks to all guests, researchers, sponsors and volunteers.

title: Indians killed intellectuals as per Delhi’s conspiracy: Jamaat
body: The Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami on Sunday alleged that the killings of the nation’s intellectuals at the fag end of the 1971 War of Independence were carried out by Indians as part of a planned conspiracy devised in Delhi to create an intellectual vacuum in the country. Jamaat secretary general Mia Golam Parwor made the remarks while speaking as the chief guest at a discussion marking Martyred Intellectuals Day, organised by the party’s north city unit at the Krishibid Institute auditorium in the capital’s Farmgate area. He alleged that evidence of India and its local agents’ involvement in the massacre could be found in the writings of noted Indian individuals and authors. He claimed that although Pakistani forces were supposed to surrender on December 14, 1971, the surrender was delayed by two days under Indian planning, during which time teachers, poets, writers, engineers, lawyers and other leading intellectuals were killed in the country. Those who were murdered supported independence but were ideologically opposed to India and its local allies, and were therefore eliminated to clear the way for the Indian agenda, he claimed. Mia Golam Parwor said that even 54 years after independence, the mystery surrounding the killings of intellectuals remained unresolved. He said that no government since independence had taken effective steps to ensure justice for the killings and that the issue had instead been used to politically target opponents by placing the blame on Jamaat. No investigation report into the killings of the intellectuals had been made public since the independence, he said and claimed that the Awami League had suppressed such reports. He called for the formation of an independent investigation commission to uncover the truth behind the killings of the intellectuals. Referring to recent political developments, Mia Golam Parwor said that a brutal attack on Sharif Osman Hadi was carried out to undermine the July uprising. He alleged that despite repeated death threats against Osman Hadi, the government had failed to ensure his security. On Bangladesh–India relations, he said that ties with the neighbouring country should be based on equality and justice. He said that Bangladesh did not want a master–servant relationship and that India’s unwarranted interference in the country’s internal politics was not desirable. He demanded advanced medical treatment for Osman Hadi and called on the government to strengthen security for July fighters and national leaders, warning that failure to do so could put the upcoming election at risk. The Pakistani occupation forces and their local collaborators, towards the end of the War of Independence, sensing their imminent defeat, systematically killed prominent Bangladeshi intellectuals and professionals, mostly on December 14, 1971, just two days ahead of the victory of Bangladesh on December 16.

title: BUFT’s 2-day entrepreneurship expo begins
body: The Business Club of BGMEA University of Fashion and Technology inaugurated a two-day National Entrepreneurship Expo 2025under the theme ‘leadership and how to create success at the BUFT in Dhaka on Sunday. The event, powered by Taza Hair Oil and Prime Bank, and co-powered by Step Footwear, KOI The Bangladesh, and MSI International, is featuring a variety of activities, including a business case competition, panel discussions, seminars, cultural shows, and training sessions, said a press release. More than 50 stalls showcasing handmade crafts, fashion, food and various other categories from different parts of the country are participating in the fair. The fair was attended by guests, including Faruque Hassan, chairman of the BUFT board of trustees; acting vice-chancellor Professor Ayub Nabi Khan; film artistes Ananta Jalil and Afia Nusrat Barsha; Imtiaz Ahmed Imon, CEO of Taza Hair Oil; Shaila Abedin, senior executive vice-president of Prime Bank; MM Mahbub Hasan, senior vice-president of Prime Bank; Aminul Islam Shamim, CEO of Step Footwear; and Sheikh Mohammad Imran, adviser of the BUFT Business Club, along with several entrepreneurs, corporate leaders, faculty members, officials and students.

title: Govt plans to build 42 natural multi-modal transport hubs
body: The road transport and bridges ministry plans to develop 42 natural multi-modal transport hubs across the country to increase the shares of passenger and cargo on railways and waterways. At a seminar, a baseline assessment and strategic road map on Sunday revealed that currently the passenger share by roads is 88 per cent followed by 8 per cent by railways and 4 per cent by waterways in the country. Regarding cargo, the share is 76 per cent by roads, 14 per cent by waterways, and 10 per cent by railways. The Roads and Highways Department under the ministry has been tasked with the formulation of the National Integrated Multi-modal Transport Master Plan. The roads and highways department organised the stakeholder seminar on the proposed master plan at its headquarters Sarak Bhaban in the capital. The National Integrated Multimodal Transport Policy, 2013 laid the foundation for coordinated development, but a comprehensive master plan is required to operationalize integration, optimize modal use, and align transport investments with national development priorities, said the discussants. Planning adviser and chief guest professor Wahiduddin Mahmud said that earlier railways and waterways had been neglected due to political and commercial reasons. He suggested revamp of railways and waterways to ensure greater use as an alternative to roads for transporting goods and decentralisation of the transport ssytem. Adviser to the ministries of road transport and bridges and railways and special guest Muhammad Fouzul Kabir Khan said that lack of coordination in the transport sector affecting other sectors including agriculture and environment. For reducing the affects the government is emphasising on this master plan, he added. While presenting the keynote paper, Islamic University of Bangladesh’s civil and environmental engineering professor Moinul Hossain said that despite having extensive road, rail, and waterway networks, the country remains heavily dependent on roads, leading to congestion, accidents, and high logistics costs. Currently due to dependency on roads - delays by traffic congestion cost 3 to 5 per cent of GDP, 3,500-20,000 road crash fatalities annually, port dwell time 5 to 7 days while transport costs 35 per cent higher due to congestion, he said. For implementing the plan, enhancement or extension of 676.5 kilometres rail network, modernisation of 53 river ports modernization and 4,800 km waterways draft management and enhancement of 855.7 km roads required. As for potential natural multimodal hubs the department divided these into five classes - 11 hubs under Class I including in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Khulna, Chandpur, Rajshahi, Chittagong, and Cox’s Bazar; nine hubs including Ashugonj-Bhairab, Daulatdia, Rooppur, and Kumira and 22 hubs under Class III-V including Jamalpur, Mymensingh, Barisal, Bhola, Tejgaon, and Jessore. The seminar was chaired by the Road Transport and Highways Division secretary (routine duty) Mohammed Ziaul Haque while special assistant to the chief adviser Sheik Moinuddin attended as special guest and other senior officials of different ministries including railways were present. The government is planning to implement the proposed plan in three phases, phase I (2025-2030), phase II (2030-2040) and phase III (2040+).

title: Jagannath Hall admin removes portraits of war crimes convicts
body: Jagannath Hall authorities at Dhaka University on Sunday removed the portraits of convicted war criminals and former Jamaat-e-Islami leaders Ghulam Azam, Matiur Rahman Nizami and Quader Mollah drawn on the streets inside the hall. Resident students of the hall painted their portraits on Saturday night, as part of a programme titled ‘Art exhibition and defiance through brushstrokes’ organised by Jagannath Hall Sangsad (hall student union), marking Martyred Intellectuals Day observed on December 14. The hall administration said that the university administration asked them to remove the portraits. Former chief of Jamaat-e-Islami Ghulam Azam, and leaders of the party Matiur Rahman Nizami and Quader Mollah were convicted by the International Crimes Tribunal for their role in the atrocities during the 1971 War of Independence. Ghulam Azam died in jail while serving 90-year term and Matiur Rahman Nizami and Quader Mollah were executed. The portraits were drawn on the roads adjacent to Rabindra Bhaban and October Memorial Bhaban at the hall. The images were erased on Sunday morning. Jagannath Hall Students’ Union vice-president Pallab Barman said on Sunday, ‘From Hall Sangsad, we encouraged students to express their defiance in honour of the day through colours and brushes. The programme was scheduled to begin at 11:00am today.’ ‘But without informing us, the university administration removed the images. We are deeply angered and ashamed and condemn their act of erasing the portraits of these hated Razakars,’ he added. When contacted, Jagannath Hall provost professor Debashish Pal told New Age that the matter of drawing such images was not mentioned while Hall Sangsad sought permission. He also said that the portraits were removed following instructions from the university administration. Proctor Saifuddin Ahmed did not respond to phone calls. A group of students at Dhaka University expressed their hatred for the killers of the nation’s brightest sons and daughters by hurling shoes at a post marked as ‘Razakar hatred pillar’ on Martyred Intellectuals Day. The pillar was set up in front of the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union cafeteria building on the campus where students gathered from about Sunday noon to hurl shoes at. Photographs of war crimes convicts Ghulam Azam, Matiur Rahman Nizami and Ali Ahsan Mohammad Mujahid, along with Pakistan president in 1971 Yahya Khan, and some of the chief Pakistani generals leading the genocide of Bangladeshi people Tikka Khan, Ameer Abdullah Khan Niazi and Khadim Hussain Raja, among others, were hung on the wall behind the pillar. Alongside hurling shoes at the pillar, participants also wrote comments expressing hatred towards Razakars (collaborators of Pakistan military in committing genocide) on a mass-signature board titled ‘Silent hatred’.

title: Next elected govt must prioritise rule of law: Tarique
body: Bangladesh Nationalist Party acting chairman Tarique Rahman on Sunday said that the next elected government must prioritise establishing the rule of law and addressing systemic corruption. Speaking at a discussion titled ‘Upcoming National Parliamentary Election and Public Expectations’ organised by the BNP at Lakeshore Hotel in Dhaka, he said that the first task of any incoming government must be to ensure public safety and improve the law and order situation. ‘If these can be secured, many other problems can start to be addressed,’ Tarique said. He also emphasised the importance of ending the long-standing practice of granting undeserved privileges across social, administrative, and business sectors, describing controlling the ‘reins of corruption’ as a top priority. He also drew attention to urban and environmental challenges, particularly Dhaka’s severe traffic congestion and water crisis, saying that immediate action would be taken to address the city’s growing population pressures and industrial pollution if his party was voted to power. Tarique reaffirmed his commitment to providing the family card for women to promote financial independence and the farmer card to support marginal, small, and medium farmers with long-term assistance in fertilisers, seeds, and other inputs. He also proposed leveraging public-private partnerships to expand healthcare access, with 100,000 Healthcare Aides appointed nationwide to focus on prevention, minor treatments, and family health management. Education reforms were highlighted, including digitally training over 350,000 primary teachers and instilling social values among the younger generation. Tarique said that employment and skill development would also be prioritised, with vocational institutions planned to teach key foreign languages to enhance job opportunities abroad, particularly in healthcare and technical sectors. He added that a strong mandate in the upcoming election is crucial for the next government to implement these reforms effectively, ensuring sustainable development, social justice, and inclusive governance.

title: ICT decision on charges on Dec 18, 21
body: The International Crimes Tribunal-1 on Sunday set December 21 to decide whether charges of crimes against humanity would be framed against 17 accused allegedly involved in the abduction, detention and torture of people with dissenting views against the Awami League at the Task Force for Interrogation Cell run by the Rapid Action Battalion. The accused are the deposed prime minister and Awami League president Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman, Hasina’s former defence adviser retired major general Tarique Ahmed Siddique, and 14 former Rapid Action Battalion officers including 11 army officers deputed to the RAB-1 and the three police officers deputed to RAB as directors general. The tribunal also set December 18 to give its decision whether crimes against humanity charges would be framed against 13 accused allegedly involved in abduction, detention and torture of the people with dissenting views against the Awami League in Joint Interrogation Cell of the Directorate General of Forces Intelligence inside Dhaka Cantonment. The 13 accused are Sheikh Hasina, Tarique Siddique, and 11 former DGFI officers who were deputed there from the army. On Sunday, the tribunal rescheduled its order on charges in the enforced disappearance in DGFI’s JIC on the prayer of the chief prosecutor Muhammad Tajul Islam. On December 7, the tribunal set December 14 for passing its order. The tribunal also deferred until December 21 the date for passing its order on charges against Lieutenant Colonel Ridwanul Islam and Major Rifat Bin Alam Moon, who were serving in the Border Guard Bangladesh during the July 2024 mass uprising, in a separate case over the murders of 28 people during the movement at Rampura in the capital on July 18, 2024 and July 19, 2024. The three-judge tribunal, headed by Justice Md Golam Motuza Mozumder, set the dates after hearing charge-framing arguments in three cases involving 32 accused. Fifteen of the accused are serving army officers who were produced before the tribunal from the sub-jail inside Dhaka Cantonment in a Bangladesh Jail’s air-conditioned prison bus. The tribunal observed that it had found prima facie grounds to frame charges in the case against the 17 accused linked to the Task Force Interrogation, noting that the accused could not evade command responsibility for the enforced disappearances committed under their authority, with their knowledge and continuity of the crimes. Defence lawyer Tabarak Hossain, representing 10 detained army officers in TFI enforced disappearance cases, sought their discharge, arguing that responsibility for the alleged crimes lay with the directors general of the RAB. He claimed that the army officers were innocent. He engaged in a heated exchange of debate with the tribunal while pressing for their discharge before trial. He argued that, without wasting the tribunal’s time, his clients should be cleared without framing charges. Tabarak contended that there were no specific allegations against the army officers in the cases. In response, the tribunal said that he had failed to show any legal ground to support his plea for discharge. The tribunal further observed that it must first determine whether prima facie grounds exist and that such issues could not be examined without holding a trial. ‘You may have a point, but there is no scope to examine it without trial,’ the tribunal said. Tabarak also argued that the charge sheets appeared to have been prepared to malign the army, as no deputy inspectors general of police or other police officers deputed to RAB were named as accused in the enforced disappearance cases. Three lawyers appointed by the tribunal—Amir Hossain, Hasan Imam and Sujat Miah—represented 13 absconding accused, including Sheikh Hasina, former home minister Asaduzzaman Khan and Tarique Siddique in the RAB’ TFI case. The absconding accused in the case also includes three former Rapid Action Battalion directors general—Benazir Ahmed, a former inspector general of police, Barrister Harun-ur-Rashid and Khurshid Alam—along with seven retired army officers.

title: Rajshahi admin seeks data on open pipes after child’s death
body: The Rajshahi divisional administration on Sunday directed the eight deputy commissioners of the division to submit detailed information on the installed and unsealed deep tube wells amid growing concerns over public safety. In a letter issued by additional divisional commissioner (development and ICT) Rezaul Alam Sarker, the deputy commissioners were asked to provide the information by December 18. The directive came two days after a two-year-old boy died falling into an abandoned test bore near his home in Tanore upazila of Rajshahi on December 10. Local residents said that the bore was one of several test wells drilled last year by private operators in search of irrigation water. Most of the failed bores were left uncovered or loosely filled with soil and straw, they alleged. According to the letter, deep tube wells have been installed across the eight districts of the Rajshahi division by the Barind Multipurpose Development Authority, the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation, and through local initiatives. It noted that in many cases the mouths of deep tube-well pipes were left open and unsecured, creating serious safety hazards and increasing the risk of fatal accidents. ‘In this context, to prevent accidents caused by exposed and hazardous deep tube well pipes, the district administrations of the eight districts under this division are specially requested to submit district-wise information in the prescribed format to this office by December 18,’ the letter said.

title: Auto-rickshaw driver, vegetable vendor found dead in Sylhet, Habiganj
body: Two people, including a CNG-run auto-rickshaw driver and a vegetable vendor, were found dead in Sylhet and Habiganj on Sunday morning. The deceased are Shipan Ahmad, 25, an auto-rickshaw driver, son of Ashraf Ali of Raikdara village at Dayamir union under Osmani Nagar upazila in Sylhet, and Jitu Miah, 48, son of late Maurash Miah of Sataihal village at Gaznaipur union under Nabiganj upazila in Habiganj, police said. Family members of Shipan told reporters that he did not return home after going out with the auto-rickshaw at about 8:00pm Saturday and his mobile phone was found switched off at 10:00pm. Osmani Nagar police station officer-in-charge Morshedul Hasan Bhuiyan told New Age that they recovered the throat-slit body of the victim from Sadaipur area at about 9:00am Sunday after being informed by the locals. ‘He might have been killed so that his auto-rickshaw could be snatched,’ he said, adding that the body was sent to Sylhet Osmani Medical College Hospital for post-mortem examination. Meanwhile, In Nabiganj upazila of Habiganj, police recovered the body of Jitu Miah from a cropland near Janatar Bazar of Gaznaipur union on Sunday morning. Locals said that Jitu Miah used to sell vegetables at Janatar Bazar, he went out of his shop Saturday evening, leaving his son in the shop, and since then he had been missing. Nabiganj police station officer-in-charge Md Monayem Miah told New Age that they recovered his body at about 9:00am Sunday after being informed by the locals and sent it to Habiganj Sadar Adhunik Hospital for post-mortem examination. ‘Efforts are under way to identify the reason and men behind the death,’ he added.

title: Bureaucrats, politicians blamed for ruining reform
body: The heads and members of the reform commissions and others at a discussion said on Sunday that the expected reform did not happen despite people’s eager aspirations mainly due to bureaucracy along with other anti-reform actors, including some political parties. The Citizens’ Platform for SDGs, Bangladesh organised the discussion to launch the Bangladesh Reform Tracker at a convention centre in the capital. Speakers said that though the interim government formed a dozen reform commissions to fulfil the people’s aspiration for reform and the commissions submitted their recommendations, but hardly any of them has been implemented so far. ‘Only three recommendations of the Anti-Corruption Reform Commission are expected to be implemented and the remaining proposals will remain on paper as the anti-reform forces, including political and bureaucratic powers, did not take any lesson from the July uprising,’ said Iftekharuzzaman, head of the anti-corruption reform commission and the executive director of Transparency International Bangladesh. He commented that the reform proposals could help transform the Anti-Corruption Commission into an independent and accountable agency. He also blamed bureaucrats for introducing the mob culture in the country that they started at the secretariat immediately after the formation of the new government. Media Reform Commission head Kamal Ahmed echoed Iftekharuzzaman that bureaucratic resistance and a lack of political will remain the main obstacle to reforming the media while some resistance also came from business oligarchs. ‘We presented more than 100 reform recommendations, but I am sorry to say that not even a single proposal has been accepted or implemented by the government,’ he said. He said that the publication of parts of the commission’s report was withheld on the ground of confidentiality, including the sections related to the process of issuing television channel licences, due to bureaucratic obstacle. He observed that some of the steps taken even after the submission of the commission’s report are against reform proposals, which resulted in the deterioration of the media situation. Shipping adviser retired Brigadier General Sakhawat Hossain also admitted to the bureaucratic resistance from the administration. ‘I will not rule out that, definitely it was there,’ he said while answering a question if the bureaucracy acted as an obstructing power against reform. He further said that they could not carry out many things due to administrative obstacles as the bureaucracy was ruined over the past years. He said that the reform proposals were expected and the government implemented some. ‘Reforms will depend on political will and make political parties accountable for them,’ he said. Election Reform Commission head Badiul Alam Majumdar also said that many of their proposals were not included in the Representation of the People Order. He said that the nation had obtained a huge opportunity for a better Bangladesh, which was left unused for the lack of political will. ACC chair Mohammad Abdul Momen said that whatever reforms would take place now might be the only ones, as the next government was unlikely to prioritise the issue. However, election commissioner retired Brigadier Genener Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah said that he was not a pessimist like many as he thought that this was the time to restore people’s trust and confidence that they had lost over the past years. He said that the reform agenda was mostly evolutionary, not revolutionary. He said that many advisers of the interim government were also accused of corruption. Economist Professor Rehman Sobhan said that tracking reform agenda was a great initiative by the civil society to keep the government under monitoring about the proposals. Not only tracking, he made advice for facilitatating them in implementing reforms. ‘Keep pressurising the government if you are serious about it,’ he said. New Age editor and Editors’ Council president Nurul Kabir questioned the transparency of the interim government as advisers did not disclose their wealth statements. CPD Distinguished Fellow Debapriya Bhattacharya said that they would keep the update open for people on the website so that people can know about it. Among others, political leaders, civil society actors and officials spoke at the event.

title: Law enforcers firm to ensure security: EC
body: Election commissioner Abul Fazal Md Sanaullah on Sunday said that any attempt to obstruct, sabotage or undermine the upcoming election would fail, warning that law enforcement agencies would act firmly wherever necessary to ensure security. ‘The Election Commission’s message is very clear. There is no reason for concern about the election. It will be held on time,’ he said, adding that both the commission and the government remained aware of efforts to create obstacles in the electoral process. Sanaullah made the remarks while speaking to reporters after a meeting with senior officials of the home ministry and representatives of law enforcement agencies at the EC headquarters at Agargaon, Dhaka. The Election Commission held a special meeting with the heads of law enforcement agencies, presided over by chief election commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, following Friday’s shooting incident targeting Sharif Osman Hadi, a prospective candidate for Dhaka-8, just 24 hours after the election schedule was announced on Thursday. Sanaullah said that the special meeting reviewed the law and order since the election schedule was announced, assessed emerging challenges, and discussed future strategies. The meeting discussed several recent incidents, including attack on Inquilab Mancha leader Hadi, which the election commissioner said had caused serious concerns. Without going into details because of the ongoing investigation, he said that authorities had been briefed on certain internal aspects linked to electoral security. Sanaullah said that the main suspect had built close access to Hadi over time adding that he had a past involving political violence and criminal records. Asked whether the attack on Hadi could affect the election, Sanaullah said that the perpetrators were aiming to create an atmosphere of fear and the meeting had been held to counter that. The commissioner also said that concerns were raised about the release on bail of a significant number of criminals previously arrested during the ‘Devil Hunt’ operation, and discussions were held on how to address the risks posed by their presence in society. Another key issue was whether recent covert attacks were isolated incidents or part of a larger plan, and whether any security lapses had occurred. During the attempts to set fire to election offices at two upazilas were also reviewed. Sanaullah said that authorities were satisfied with the steps taken so far but identified areas requiring stronger action, including increasing checkpoints, restricting criminal movement, arresting known offenders, and recovering illegal arms and ammunition. He confirmed that the second phase of the ‘Devil Hunt’ operation had resumed and would continue in a coordinated manner, with a strong emphasis on intelligence-sharing among agencies. Special attention is being given to border regions, particularly the south-eastern and Rohingya-populated areas, to assess whether recent trends are linked to broader security threats, the commissioner said. He said that law enforcement agencies were actively working in the field, investigations into recent attacks were going on, and effective measures would be taken to prevent recurrence. Sanaullah also urged political actors and citizens to remain vigilant, warning that saboteurs might infiltrate in the guise of allies. On cyber security, Sanaullah said that existing cyber security structures were being used to monitor election-related threats, including misinformation, stressing that while disinformation cannot be eliminated entirely, its spread is being actively restrained. The meeting was attended by home ministry senior secretary Nasimul Gani, Principal Staff Officer of the Armed Forces Division Lieutenant General SM Kamrul Hassan, Inspector General of Police Baharul Alam, director general of Border Guard Bangladesh Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui, Director General of Ansar and VDP Major General Abdul Motaleb Sazzad Mahmud, and Dhaka Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sheikh Md Sajjat Ali.

title: India willing to work together with Bangladesh : Pranay Verma
body: Highlighting the importance of Dhaka-Delhi friendship, Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma on Sunday said they are willing to work together to fulfil the aspirations of their people and forge closer people-to-people ties, inspired by their shared sacrifices of the past and guided by the new aspirations for the future. ‘The bonds we share with Bangladesh are not transient; they are everlasting. A relationship forged in blood and sacrifice cannot be weakened. Together, we will carry this shared legacy forward into the future,’ he said while speaking at a programme in the evening. The high commissioner said Bangladesh and India have come a long way since 1971. ‘We are today two fast-growing economies. Our societies and economies are closely linked, so closely that we are interdependent on each other. Our geographical proximity with each other offers us new opportunities driven by our growing capabilities and new ambitions,’ he said. Pranay Verma said India stood with the people of Bangladesh in 1971 and will continue to support them, in realising the vision for a democratic, stable, peaceful, progressive and inclusive nation. Itihash O Oitijjo Parishad hosted the programme where the High Commissioner and his wife joined marking the anniversary of Bangladesh’s Mahaan Muktijuddha - the Great Liberation War of Bangladesh. ‘December is the Victory Month. It is a time of remembrance and gratitude for the sacrifices millions of people made during Bangladesh’s freedom struggle,’ Pranay Verma said. He paid tributes to the people of Bangladesh who overcame the long ordeals of oppression, killings and subjugation, with valour, grit and determination. ‘It is a time to cherish the values that underpinned that freedom struggle,’ said the High Commissioner. ‘Today is the Martyred Intellectuals Day. This day takes us back to one of the darkest chapters of 1971, when Bangladesh stood on the threshold of freedom,’ Verma said. The systematic elimination of scholars, doctors, journalists, artists and educators by the occupation forces was an act of desperation aimed at destroying the very soul of a future nation, he said. ‘We remember and honour all those martyred intellectuals whose sacrifices serve as a guiding light - inspiring us to uphold the values of knowledge, wisdom, intellectual pursuit, and the courage of conviction,’ he mentioned. During the Liberation War, the envoy said, India stood with their brothers and sisters in Bangladesh, with immense pride, supporting them at every step in their cause for truth, justice, dignity and freedom of Bangladesh. ‘And in doing so, we also lost our own soldiers - in thousands. Countless more were left wounded,’ he said. There are many historical moments in India’s support to Bangladesh during the Liberation War that are milestones in the history of our two countries that cannot be erased, said the High Commissioner. Just eight days ago, on 6th of December, he said, they commemorated the historic anniversary of the Maitri Dibos, the day when India recognized Bangladesh as an independent and sovereign nation 54 years ago, ten days ahead of Bangladesh’s liberation. He said the Liberation War of 1971 was the beginning of a relationship built upon humanism, empathy and trust that has sustained, despite changes, challenges and ups and downs in our relationship. ‘As we approach the Victory Day on the 16th of December, we reflect on the historic triumphs and the indomitable spirit of the people of Bangladesh that led to the birth of Bangladesh as an independent nation,’ Pranay Verma said. He said it has been fifty-four years since the Bangladesh achieved its liberation, and it is as important as ever that today’s youth and children-the future custodians of this nation-learn and carry forward this indelible history. ‘The programme organised today by the Itihash O Oitijjo Parishad reflects this responsibility, which we greatly commend,’ the envoy said. He made a special mention of the remarkable paintings depicting the glorious Liberation War, created by school students from Daka, that we just saw. ‘Their creativity, empathy and sense of history are truly inspiring.’ In the presence of the heroic war-wounded freedom fighters of 1971, he said the place their hopes in today’s children-that they will uphold the ideals, spirit, and values of the great Liberation War. ‘Only then will the sacrifices of all our martyrs find their true meaning.’ ‘Occasions like today’s are meant to reflect on what we have achieved together. But these are also the moments when we look forward, rising above distractions, to see new horizons of our partnership,’ the High Commissioner said.

title: Hadi to be flown to Singapore for treatment on Monday
body: Bangladesh interim government in consultation with doctors and family has decided to shift Sharif Osman Hadi to Singapore by an air-ambulance on Monday afternoon for better treatment, said a press release shared by chief adviser’s press wing. On Friday afternoon, Hadi was shot in the head in Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar on an auto-rickshaw when the two men wearing helmets on a motorcycle opened fire on him on the Box Culvert road before fleeing the scene. A 13-member interdisciplinary medical board said that Hadi’s overall health condition remained very critical. Law enforcement members detained three suspects over shooting Sharif Osman Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate in the upcoming national polls for the Dhaka-8 constituency as his health condition remained ‘very critical’ till Sunday night. While the police identified one more assailant as Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, the law enforcers was yet to arrest Alamgir and the pillion of the motorcycle Faisal Karim Masud, suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days.

title: Journalist Anis Alamgir taken to DB office
body: The Detective Branch of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police on Sunday took senior journalist Anis Alamgir to its office in the capital’s Minto Road for questioning. DMP DB additional deputy commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam, at about 9:30pm on told New Age, ‘He (Anis Alamgir) has been brought here for questioning.’ Asked why he would be questioned, the DMP DB chief said that it could not be disclosed at that moment. He also said that Anis Alamgir was brought to the DB office after 9:00pm. Anis Alamgir in recent times expressed critical views on the activities of the Professor Muhammad Yunus-led interim government formed following the ouster of the authoritarian Awami League regime amid the July Mass Uprising in August 2024.

title: Guterres expresses condolences to Yunus over deaths of Bangladeshi peacekeepers
body: United Nations secretary-general António Guterres on Sunday called Bangladesh interim government chief adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus to express his profound condolences over the tragic death of six Bangladeshi peacekeepers in a drone attack in Sudan. ‘I am calling to express my deep condolences. I am devastated,’ Guterres told Professor Yunus, adding that he was horrified by the attack. The UN chief expressed his solidarity with Bangladesh and requested the Chief Adviser to convey his condolences to the bereaved families, said the Chief Adviser’s Press Wing this evening. Professor Yunus said he was deeply saddened by the loss of the Bangladeshi peacekeepers and urged the UN to facilitate the evacuation of the injured soldiers to top medical facilities, as well as to ensure the swift repatriation of the bodies. Guterres informed the Chief Adviser that the injured peacekeepers were initially treated at a local hospital in Sudan and that arrangements were underway to transfer the seriously wounded to better-equipped hospitals. Professor Yunus thanked the UN chief for paying attention to the treatment and evacuation of Bangladeshi soldiers. During the phone call, which was made around 7:00 pm (BST), Professor Yunus also recalled UN Secretary-General's visit to Bangladesh during last Ramadan. The two leaders discussed the upcoming general elections, with Professor Yunus assuring Guterres that the interim government would hold a free, fair, peaceful, and festive election on February 12. Guterres expressed confidence that Bangladesh would successfully conduct the elections.

title: Three suspects held over shooting Hadi
body: Law enforcement members detained three suspects over shooting Sharif Osman Hadi, an aspiring independent candidate in the upcoming national polls for the Dhaka-8 constituency as his health condition remained ‘very critical’ till Sunday night. While the police identified one more assailant as Alamgir Sheikh, the motorcycle rider, the law enforcers was yet to arrest Alamgir and the pillion of the motorcycle Faisal Karim Masud, suspected shooter, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for a few days. Meanwhile, the interim government in consultation with doctors and family has decided to shift Hadi to Singapore by an air-ambulance today afternoon for better treatment, said a press release shared by chief adviser’s press wing. In the hospital, a 13-member interdisciplinary medical board said that Hadi’s overall health condition remained very critical. Dhaka Metropolitan Police additional commissioner for crime, SN Nazrul Islam, at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre said that passports of the main suspected assailants were blocked to bar their border escape and the police did not have confirmation about their border escape. ‘Drives are under way in various locations to arrest the offenders,’ said Nazrul. The individuals detained so far were identified as Abdul Hannan, Sivion Dio and Sanjay Chisim. A team of the Rapid Action Battalion-2 identified the motorcycle used in the attack on Hadi and detained the owner Hannan from Mohammadpur area in the capital on Saturday night while the police nabbed Sivion and Sanjay, who help people to cross the border illegally, from Sherpur’s Nalitabari on Sunday. A Dhaka court on Sunday placed Hannan on a three-day remand after the police produced him before the court under Section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Investigators initially sought a seven-day remand for him but Metropolitan Magistrate Didarul Alam passed a three-day remand. Police also seized the motorcycle used in the attempted murder while the Central Intelligence Cell of the National Board of Revenue froze all the bank accounts of Faisal. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs summoned the Indian high commissioner and urged him to ensure India’s cooperation with Bangladesh to prevent the perpetrators from fleeing to India, and, if still they managed to escape to India, the Indian authorities should immediately take steps to arrest them and extradite them to Bangladesh, said the chief adviser’s press wing on Sunday. The press wing also said that although the suspects’ locations were traced several times within the country, it was not possible yet to arrest them for their frequent changes of locations. Hadi was now undergoing treatment at Evercare Hospital’s critical care unit. Referring to the medical board’s observations, Evercare Hospital senior consultant Zafar Iqbal in a statement said that Hadi’s Sunday CT scan report showed that cerebral edema increased further, indicating a very concerning clinical situation. Law enforcement and intelligence agencies, including the Detective Branch, thana police, the Criminal Investigation Department and the Rapid Action Battalion, are working to identify and arrest the assailants while the Border Guard Bangladesh has imposed maximum alert in border areas. Responding to journalists’ questions, DMP additional commissioner Nazrul at a briefing said that the motive behind the attack could be a ‘target killing’ of Hadi by his opponents. About the detention of Sivion and Sanjay, Nazrul said that police would interrogate them whether they knew anything about the assailants. When asked about filing of case over the shooting, Nazrul said that although no case was filed yet over the incident, a general dairy was filed. The police contacted Hadi’s family members to file a case as plaintiff but they were busy with the patient. The police will arrange to send the case papers to the family for signature. If failed, the police will file a case as the plaintiff, said Nazrul. About the identification of the motorcycle and the detention of its owner Hannan, RAB-2 senior assistant director (Media) Md Shamsul Islam said, ‘The identified motorcycle number is Dhaka Metro-La-54-6375. It is registered in his name.’ DMP deputy commissioner for Motijheel division Mohammad Harun-or-Rashid said that police were investigating whether Hannan had any involvement in the attack. Seeking anonymity, an NBR official on Sunday confirmed that all the bank accounts of Faisal and Faisal’s IT company Apple Soft IT Limited had been frozen. The NBR official said that all the transactions in Faisal’s bank accounts would be reviewed. Whether there had been any unusual transactions, the source of the transactions, whether there had been any tax evasion, or whether there had been any customs evasion in the import-export sector — all would be reviewed, the official added. Moreover, Faisal’s another company, YCU Technology, with the support of the Bangladesh Association of Software and Information Services and the sponsorship of government’s Information and Communication Technology Division, created a computer game titled Battle of 71 on the Liberation War of Bangladesh and the country’s founding president Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. On Friday afternoon, Hadi was shot in the head in Box Culvert area of Bijoynagar while he was conducting his electioneering, a day after the Election Commission announced the schedule for the 13th JS elections and the national referendum on February 12, 2026. CCTV footage showed that Hadi was heading towards Bijoynagar on an auto-rickshaw when the two men wearing helmets on a motorcycle opened fire on him on the Box Culvert road before fleeing the scene. Police and Inquilab Mancha activists suspected that the two unknown individuals, who took part in Hadi’s electoral campaign for the past few days wearing face masks and also on the day of the incident, were involved in the shooting. Physicians said that Hadi was seriously injured as a bullet pierced his head above the right ear, causing significant brain damage.

title: ERP condemns attack on Hadi, urges action on violence
body: The Education Rights Parliament has condemned the daylight shooting of Sharif Osman Hadi, aspiring independent candidate for Dhaka-8 constituency and convener of Inquilab Mancha, calling the attack a stark reminder of the persistence of political violence in Bangladesh. In a statement issued on Sunday, the organisation said that the attack reflected the continuing fragility of political and civic safety, despite months of reforms following the July uprising. The organisation warned that such violence undermines the promise of a reformed ‘Bangladesh 2.0’ and raises serious concerns about the safety of young leaders, first-time voters and citizens engaged in democratic participation, particularly ahead of the 13th national elections scheduled for February 2026. The organisation urged the interim government to ensure safe and inclusive civic spaces at all times, not only during election periods. Highlighting Hadi’s role in the organisation, ERP said he has been a prominent voice since its launch in September 2024, advocating civility, principled engagement and education-led social reform. The statement also linked the attack to the unresolved legacy of authoritarian rule, saying the pledge of ‘Never Again’ remains unfulfilled while political violence persists. The statement was sent by ERP convenor Professor M Niaz Asadullah.

title: ATTACK ON HADI: Two suspects identified, passports blocked to prevent escape
body: The Dhaka Metropolitan Police have identified two suspects involved in the attack on Inqilab Mancha spokesperson Osman Hadi, who was seriously injured in a shooting incident in the capital on Friday. The police have also blocked the suspects’ passports to prevent them from fleeing the country. ‘After collecting and analysing CCTV footage from the scene, police have initially identified two suspects. They are Faisal Karim Masud and Md Alamgir Sheikh,’ said Additional Police Commissioner (Crime and Operations) SN Md Nazrul Islam speaking at a news briefing at DMP media centre. To prevent the suspects from fleeing the country, their passports have been blocked and border alerts have been issued, he said. Immediately after the incident, he said that the DMP launched an intensive investigation and beefed up efforts to arrest the attackers. ‘Law enforcement agencies have conducted operations at various locations to uncover the full details of the incident and to arrest the identified suspects. These operations are ongoing,’ he said. In addition, the interim government has announced a reward of Tk 50 lakh for information leading to the arrest of the suspects. Meanwhile, the DMP has arrested two individuals suspected of assisting in border crossing during a raid in Nalitabari area of Sherpur. The arrested individuals are Sibion Deo and Sanjay Chisim. In a separate operation, the Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) arrested another suspect, Md. Abdul Hannan, owner of the motorcycle reportedly used in the attempted murder, along with his bike, he said. The DMP has urged the public to come forward with any information related to those involved in this heinous incident. Citizens are requested to inform the nearest police station or contact the national emergency service number 999. The authorities have stated that police are working earnestly to arrest all those involved in this sensational incident. On Friday, December 12, at 2:25pm, several miscreants riding motorcycles wearing helmets carried out the heinous attack on Osman Hadi in the Paltan Box Culvert area of Dhaka. He was shot from close range and sustained critical injuries. He is currently undergoing treatment at the Evercare Hospital in the capital.

title: PUST observes Martyred Intellectuals Day
body: The Pabna University of Science and Technology on Sunday observed Martyred Intellectuals Day by paying rich tribute to the best sons of the soil with due respect. On the occasion of the day, teachers, students, officials and employees wore black badges in the morning. The national flag was hoisted at half-mast at about 8:00am to mark the day. A procession, led by vice-chancellor Professor Dr SM Abdul-Awal, was brought out from the administrative building at about 8:30am. The procession ended at Swadhinata Chattar on the campus after parading different roads. The university administration paid tribute to the martyred intellectuals at Swadhinata Chattar. After paying tribute, vice-chancellor Professor Dr SM Abdul-Awal gave a brief speech there. He remembered the contributions of the martyred intellectuals and the freedom fighters, as well as all the people who sacrificed their lives in different democratic movements of the country. A prayer session was held for the eternal peace of the departed souls of the martyrs.

title: BSF pushes 15 more people into Bangladesh through C’nawabganj border
body: India’s Border Security Force pushed 15 more people, including two children and nine women, into Bangladesh through the Bibishan border point at Gomastapur upazila in Chapainawabganj district early Sunday. With the latest push-ins, the number of people, including Rohingyas and Indian nationals, pushed into Bangladesh by India since May 7 has increased to 2,417. The Indian border force has so far pushed at least 223 Rohingyas, including 50 registered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees in India, into Bangladesh. Nayek Subedar Abdul Mannan, commander of the Bibishan border outpost under the Border Guard Bangladesh-16 battalion, said that BGB personnel spotted the group during routine border patrols early in the morning and took them to the camp for preliminary interrogation. He said that initial questioning revealed that the detainees — two children, nine women and four men — were Bangladeshi nationals from Jashore, Narail, Khulna and Manikganj districts. ‘After confirming their identities, we handed them over to the Gomastapur police station,’ he added. Abdul Barik, officer-in-charge of the Gomastapur police station, said that the individuals were currently in police custody. ‘Further legal steps will be taken after consultation with higher authorities,’ he said.

title: Five more dengue patients die in Bangladesh
body: Health officials on Sunday said they recorded 387 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts, killing at least five persons in the past 24 hours across Bangladesh. ‘We recorded deaths of five dengue patients in 24 hours ending at 8:00am today,’ a spokesman of Directorate General of Health Services said adding his office simultaneously recorded 387 fresh cases of dengue onslaughts during the same period. ‘Out of the 387 fresh cases, 40 were hospitalised in Barishal division, 71 in Chattogram division, 83 in Dhaka division excluding capital, 55 in Dhaka South City Corporation and 53 in Dhaka North City Corporation areas, 33 in Khulna division, 26 in Mymensingh division, 22 in Rajshahi division and four in Sylhet division, a Directorate General of Health Services statement said. Since the start of the dengue onslaughts, Bangladesh this year witnessed so far 409 deaths while the disease inflicted 100,447. The dengue in the past year claimed 575 lives and inflicted 1,01,214 people in Bangladesh.

title: Families wail
body: The Inter-Services Public Relations on Sunday disclosed the identities of the Bangladeshi peacekeepers who were killed and injured in a drone attack on a United Nations peacekeeping base in Sudan on Saturday. Six Bangladeshi peacekeepers were killed and eight others were injured in the attack on the Kadugli logistics base in Sudan’s Abyei area. Mourning family members of the deceased demanded that the government bring back their bodies as soon as possible. The Bangladesh government and the United Nations secretary-general, Antonio Guterres, condemned the deadly attack on Bangladeshi peacekeepers in Sudan. The ISPR, on its official Facebook page, wrote that the attack was carried out by a separatist armed group between 3:40pm and 3:50pm local time on Saturday when the peacekeepers were on duty at the UN base. The deceased Bangladeshi peacekeepers are Corporal Md Masud Rana of Natore, Sainik Md Mominul Islam of Kurigram, Sainik Shamim Reza of Rajbari, Sainik Shanta Mondal of Kurigram, Mess Waiter Mohammad Jahangir Alam of Kishoreganj, and laundry employee Md Sabuj Mia of Gaibandha. The injured peacekeepers are Lieutenant Colonel Khondaker Khalekuzzaman of Kushtia, Sergeant Md Mostakim Hossain of Dinajpur, Corporal Afroza Parvin Eti of Dhaka, Lance Corporal Mohibul Islam of Barguna, Sainik Md Mezbaul Kabir of Kurigram, Sainik Umme Hani Akter of Rangpur, Sainik Chumki Akter of Manikganj, and Sainik Md Manazir Ahsan of Noakhali. The ISPR said that all the eight injured peacekeepers were receiving necessary medical treatment. Among them, Sainik Md Mezbaul Kabir underwent successful surgery after his condition was reported as critical. He is currently under close observation. The other seven injured peacekeepers have been evacuated by helicopter for advanced treatment and are now out of danger, the ISPR said. The Bangladesh Army described the attack as a ‘brutal terrorist attack’ and strongly condemned it. It said that the sacrifice of the fallen peacekeepers would remain a proud testament to Bangladesh’s commitment to global peace. Bangladesh’s interim government chief adviser Muhammad Yunus in a statement said that he was ‘deeply saddened’ by the attack, and put the toll at six dead and eight wounded. He urged the UN to ensure that his country’s personnel are offered ‘any necessary emergency support’. ‘The government of Bangladesh will stand by the families in this difficult moment,’ Yunus added. Bangladesh foreign ministry in a statement strongly condemned the attack. UN chief Antonio Guterres condemned the ‘horrific’ attack, saying it ‘may constitute war crimes under international law’. ‘Attacks as the one today in South Kordofan against peacekeepers are unjustifiable. There will need to be accountability,’ he said in a statement. International news agency Agence France-Presse reported that the Sudanese army published a video on its Facebook page showing fires blazing and two columns of smoke rising from the UNISFA base. The army-aligned government based in Port Sudan issued a statement condemning the attack and accusing the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces of being behind it. In a statement, the Sovereignty Council headed by army chief General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan called the attack a ‘dangerous escalation’. The RSF in a statement on Telegram said that it rejected ‘the claims and allegations... regarding an air attack that targeted the United Nations headquarters in Kadugli, and the accompanying false accusations against our forces of being behind it through the use of a drone’. Meanwhile, Sudanese prime minister Kamil Idris said that ‘the terrorist rebel militia has met all the conditions to be classified as a terrorist group’, and urged the UN to ‘bring the perpetrators to justice’. The RSF has been at war with the military since April 2023 and has deployed fighters, drones and allied militias to the fertile region. Analysts say the RSF seeks to punch through the army’s defences around central Sudan, paving the way for recapturing Khartoum, the capital city of Sudan. Quoting family members of deceased Corporal Md Masud Rana, New Age’s staff correspondent in Rajshahi reported that Masud was the eldest son of Sahar Uddin of Boaliyapara village under Arbab union at Lalpur upazila in Natore. He joined the Bangladesh Army in 2006. Before being deployed to the peacekeeping mission on November 7, Masud was posted at Jashore Cantonment. Masud’s mother, Marjina Khatun, repeatedly fell unconscious after hearing of her son’s death. ‘I spoke to him just yesterday. When I asked about his duty, he told me not to worry, that the workload was less. He told me to stay well — and then he was gone,’ she said amid tears. His two younger brothers, Monirul Islam and Roni Alam, also serve in the army, having joined in 2012 and 2018 respectively. Roni said, ‘We are proud of his sacrifice, though our grief is beyond words.’ Our Kurigram correspondent reported that deep sorrow descended on the families of Sainik Shanta Mondol and Sainik Md Mominul Islam at their villages in Kurigram district. Shanta hailed from Mondolpara of Chhat Madhai village under Rajarhat upazila in the district. He was the youngest son of the late former army member Nur Islam Mondol and Sahera Begum. His elder brother, Sohag Mondol, is also currently serving in the Bangladesh Army. Shanta joined the Bangladesh Army as a soldier in 2018 and was deployed to Sudan under a UN peacekeeping mission in November 2025. Mominul was a resident of Uttar Pandul village under Ulipur upazila in the district.

title: Indian high commissioner summoned over Hasina’s statements
body: The foreign affairs ministry on Sunday summoned Indian high commissioner to Bangladesh Pranay Verma to convey the Bangladesh government’s serious concern to the Indian government about allowing fugitive deposed prime minister Sheikh Hasina to continue to make ‘incendiary statements’. Sheikh Hasina, also the president of Awami League, activities of which are now banned over its atrocities during the July mass uprising, fled to India on August 5, 2024, for shelter amid the student-led mass uprising that ousted her authoritarian regime. Foreign secretary Asad Alam Siam on Sunday conveyed the concern to the Indian envoy at the state guest house Padma in the capital Dhaka about the Indian authorities allowing Hasina to make statements calling upon her supporters to engage in ‘terrorist activities’ in Bangladesh in a bid to thwart the general elections scheduled for February 12, 2026, officials said. Bangladesh also sought India’s cooperation in preventing the escape to India of the suspects involved in the December 12 assassination attempt on Bangladeshi political leader Sharif Osman Hadi and, in case they manage to enter into Indian territory, to ensure their immediate apprehension and extradition to Bangladesh, according to a press release issued by the foreign ministry in Dhaka. In a press note issued later on the day in New Delhi, India, however, rejected the ‘assertions’ made by the interim government of Bangladesh regarding Hasina. ‘We have consistently reiterated our position in favour of free, fair, inclusive and credible elections being held in Bangladesh in a peaceful atmosphere,’ said the Indian external affairs ministry in the note. Bangladesh reiterated her call for the expeditious extradition of Sheikh Hasina and former home affairs minister Asaduzzaman Khan, who is also staying in India, to face the sentences handed down by the judicial authorities in Bangladesh. On November 17, the International Crimes Tribunal-1 sentenced Sheikh Hasina and Asaduzzaman to death for committing crimes against humanity during the July–August 2024 mass uprising. Pranay emphasised that India looked forward to peaceful elections in Bangladesh and expressed his country’s readiness to extend all cooperation in this regard, according to the foreign ministry release. The foreign ministry also drew the attention of the Indian envoy to anti-Bangladesh activities, including planning, organising and helping to carry out ‘terrorist activities’ inside Bangladesh, by fugitive Awami League members staying in India in order to hinder the forthcoming elections. The Indian government was called upon to expeditiously act to end the criminal actions by these ‘fascist terrorists’ and extradite them to Bangladesh as soon as possible, said the release. Bangladesh emphasised that as a neighbour, India is expected to stand with the people of Bangladesh in upholding justice and safeguarding democratic processes. The Indian government in the note said that India had never allowed its territory to be used for activities inimical to the interests of the friendly people of Bangladesh. ‘We expect that the interim government of Bangladesh will take all necessary measures for ensuring internal law and order, including for the purpose of holding peaceful elections,’ it said. New Delhi has not yet responded to Dhaka’s request for the extradition of Hasina despite repeated requests since December past year.

title: United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemns attack on peacekeepers in Sudan
body: United Nations chief Antonio Guterres condemned Saturday’s ‘horrific’ drone attack on Bangladeshi peacekeepers in Sudan, a strike that killed six people and wounded six others. ‘I strongly condemn the horrific drone attacks that targeted the United Nations peacekeeping logistics base in Kadugli, Sudan,’ Guterres said in a statement. ‘Attacks targeting United Nations peacekeepers may constitute war crimes under international law,’ he added. ‘Attacks as the one today in South Kordofan against peacekeepers are unjustifiable. There will need to be accountability.’

title: Maize seed production hampered by syndicate traders
body: Nilphamari Correspondent : Bangladesh is losing a huge amount of foreign currency every year due to excessive dependence on imported maize seeds. Experts believe that self-sufficiency in maize seed production is being hindered by syndicate traders, vested interests of some officials involved in seed import, insufficient research, and weak policy frameworks. Despite long-term investment in agriculture, the country has yet to produce maize seeds of international standard. This has raised serious questions where exactly does the problem lie? Why has Bangladesh failed to achieve self-reliance in maize seeds despite ongoing research activities? Md. Abu Taleb Mia, Deputy Director of the BADC Farm in Domar upazila of Nilphamari, said that during the last season, hybrid maize seed varieties B-3355 and B-3255 (Advanta) were cultivated experimentally on three to four bighas of land at the farm. He stated, “If maize seed production is carried out by following specific methods and maintaining genetic purity, Bangladesh can certainly succeed. We have achieved significant success on an experimental level. With more government-led research and support, producing quality maize seeds is definitely possible.” According to experts, major obstacles to domestic maize seed production include lack of advanced research, absence of modern laboratories and technologies, excessive dependence on private companies, and the absence of long-term policies. Although the Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute (BARI) and BADC produce seeds on a limited scale, their output is far from meeting market demand. As a result, dependence on imported seeds continues to rise. Md. Mahafuza Rahman, a maize seed trader at Pulhat Bazar in Kundapukur Union of Nilphamari Sadar upazila, said that farmers from three unions of Nilphamari Sadar and several areas of Khansama upazila in Dinajpur regularly collect maize seeds from him. “I sell maize seeds worth around 5 to 6 million taka every season,” he added. Nilphamari District Agricultural Extension Officer Md. Manjur Rahman said that Bangladesh still lacks the advanced technology, long-term research investment, and skilled scientists required to produce international-standard hybrid maize seeds. In contrast, countries like India have made significant progress in hybrid seed production due to years of planned research and investment. He also pointed out that weaknesses in seed production and certification systems, problems in preserving breeder seeds, and reliance on individual-centric projects are major barriers to achieving self-sufficiency in maize seeds.

title: Nur Alam files JaPa nomination
body: Rangpur Correspondent : Nur Alam Jadu has filed his nomination papers from the Jatiya Party (JaPa) for the upcoming 24 Pirganj-6 constituency in the national parliamentary elections. His nomination was submitted on his behalf by his son, Alhaj Mehedi Hasan (Shovon). Present at the event were Golam Mostofa Monglu, President of Pirganj Municipal Jatiya Party; Saiful Islam, Upazila Jatiya Party Propaganda and Publication Secretary; Aminul Islam Moinul, President of Ramnathpur Union; Masud Sarkar, leader of Pirganj Union Jatiya Party; along with presidents and leaders from 15 unions of the upazila. The leaders stated that the Jatiya Party has been working for the overall development of Pirganj and the protection of citizens’ rights. They expressed hope that the plow symbol would secure victory in the upcoming elections and that welfare-oriented initiatives for the people would continue. Political analysts believe that Nur Alam Jadu’s nomination will set a new precedent in Pirganj’s political landscape and strengthen the position of the Jatiya Party.

title: Rickety bridge turned into major safety hazard
body: Khulna Correspondent : A rickety wooden bridge over the Chitra River in Terokhada upazila of Khulna has turned into a major safety hazard, exposing hundreds of commuters to daily life-threatening risks, while authorities remain largely indifferent. During a recent visit, this correspondent found that most of the wooden planks of the bridge have rotted away, leaving wide gaps through which the river below is clearly visible. Several handrails are broken, and the entire structure shakes dangerously even under the weight of light vehicles. Local residents described the bridge as a “death trap”, saying it has long exceeded its usable lifespan. Tarofdar Miraj Hossain, Headmaster if Terokhada Government Primary School told This Correspondent that The School is an ancient institution and famous in this locality whuch is also a Poll Center. The bridge is used daily by school and college students, teachers, farmers, patients and pedestrians from several surrounding villages. The risk escalates during the monsoon, when rain-soaked wooden planks become extremely slippery. “There have already been multiple incidents of people falling and getting injured, but many of these go unreported,” alleged locals. Residents further claimed that repeated complaints both written and verbal have been lodged with the Union Parishad, upazila administration and concerned departments over the years. However, neither permanent reconstruction nor temporary repairs have been carried out so far. The continued neglect has sparked anger and frustration among locals, who questioned the accountability of public representatives and officials.

title: 103 expatriates honoured in Sylhet
body: Sylhet Bureau : Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications Secretary Abdul Naser Khan said, Bangladesh is economically very strong because of expatriates. Expatriates have contributed to every aspect of this country. The government will provide various benefits including tax-free investment to expatriates. He said this as the chief guest in the expatriate honor program organized by the Sylhet District Administration at the Kabi Nazrul Auditorium in Rikabi Bazar on Saturday. He said that there can be an NRB investment zone in Sylhet for safe investment. He also called for the establishment of an NRB smart city in Sylhet. For this, he emphasized the need to remove all the sufferings including land, documents, security. Earlier, 582 applications were submitted in the last 20 days. Out of these, the district administration reviewed various aspects and honored 103 people.

title: 3 held with fake notes
body: Bandarban Correspondent : In Naikhongchhari Upazila, a border area of Bandarban, police have uncovered a organised gang involved in counterfeit currency. Based on secret intelligence, a special operation was conducted in which three individuals were arrested with a large amount of fake notes. Late Thursday night, police raided the border-adjacent Wachakhali area of Dochhari Union in Naikhongchhari Upazila and caught them in the act of exchanging counterfeit money. During the operation, fake notes worth Tk 1,138,000 were recovered. On Saturday morning, Bandarban Superintendent of Police Abdur Rahman told a press conference that two of the arrestees are Rohingya brothers, and the third is a CNG driver. They had been using the border area as a safe route for collecting and distributing counterfeit currency in the market for a long time. The Superintendent added that investigations are ongoing to determine whether the fake notes were printed inside the country or abroad. A case has been filed at Naikhongchhari Police Station in connection with the incident.

title: Season starts with Tk 58cr loss
body: Joypurhat Correspondent : The 63rd sugarcane threshing season has begun with the dumping of sugarcane into the Joypurhat sugar mill’s boats. The country’s largest sugar producing company has started the 2025-26 sugarcane threshing season with the burden of last year’s loss of Tk 58 crore. Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Industries Maksura Noor inaugurated the sugarcane threshing and sugar production activities on Friday afternoon. Additional Secretary of the Ministry of Industries MA Kamal Billah, Managing Director of Joypurhat Sugar Mills, Agronomist Mohammad Khabir Uddin Molya, Deputy Director of Joypurhat Local Government Uttam Kumar Roy, District Jamaat Ameer Fazlur Rahman, Officer-in-Charge of Joypurhat Sadar Police Station Anisur Rahman, and Executive President of Bangladesh Sugar Industry Corporation Workers’ and Employees’ Federation Ali Akhtar spoke at the rally organized on this occasion at the Joypurhat Sugar Mill premises. This time, sugarcane has been cultivated on 3,020 acres of land in the current 2025-26 season. The sugar mill authorities have set a target of producing 2,970 metric tons of sugar from 55,000 metric tons of sugarcane on these lands.

title: Shishu Sworgo holds winter festival
body: Panchagarh Correspondent : Panchagarh, a district bordering the Himalayas, often faces severe winter conditions with heavy fog and cold. In this unique initiative, a Winter Fun Festival was organized for students from various educational institutions across the district. Warm hoodies, school bags, and other educational materials were distributed among the students. On Saturday afternoon, the festival was held at the Sugar Mill Field in Panchagarh town, organized by the volunteer organization Shishu Sworgo Foundation, with support from Everest Pharmaceuticals Limited. This was the third event of the Winter Fun Festival series. The event was attended by Panchagarh Additional Superintendent of Police Shoimi Imtiaz, Managing Director of Panchagarh Sugar Mill Atikuzzaman, OC of Sadar Police Station Ashraful Islam.

title: CCC Mayor meets Tarique Rahman
body: Chattogram Bureau : After returning to the country after a long exile, Acting Chairman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) Tarique Rahman was paid a courtesy call by Mayor of Chattogram City Corporation (CCC) Dr. Shahadat Hossain. During the meeting at the VIP lounge of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport on Thursday, Mayor Dr. Shahadat Hossain greeted the Acting Chairman with flowers and wished him good health and long life. In this very cordial meeting, they briefly discussed the current political situation in the country and the developmental activities of Chattogram. Mayor Shahadat Hossain said, the heroic return of patriot Tarique Rahman was a long-awaited desire of the people of Bangladesh. Under his strong leadership, the movement to rebuild the country and restore democracy has gained a new dimension. On behalf of the people of Chattogram, I extend my heartfelt congratulations to him. During the meeting, Tarique Rahman inquired about the current activities of the Chattogram City Corporation and gave the mayor necessary directions to develop Chattogram as a modern, clean and livable city. He urged the CCC Mayor to continue working with honesty and dedication in serving the people. The party’s central and local level leaders were present at the time.
