title: Sundarbans grappling with bandits
body: Bagerhat Correspondent : Sundarbans forest was declared free from the jungle pirates on November 01 in the year 2018. But the jungle pirates raised their heads once again. At present some 20 gangs of jungle pirates are active. They are now realizing lakhs of Taka after kidnapping the fishermen as ransom from their family members. As a result, a great panic was created among the fishermen fishing in Sundarbans and other forest-earners. After the declaration that Sundarbans, the biggest mangrove forest of the world and a world heritage fishermen, Bawalis and other forest-earners were undisturbed and free from anxieties for long six years. But after August 05, 2024 the situation began to be deteriorated gradually from bad to worse. It is learnt from the forest department, law enforcing agencies, fishermen and fish traders that the jungle bandits/pirates are now well organized under the new leaderships and they are committing different crimes in Sundarbans, mainly in the Eastern Division (under Bagerhat district). Out of them Jahangir Bahini, Manjur Bahini and Dada Bhai Bahini are equipped with modern arms and weapons and huge man power. These 3 jungle pirates are very powerful. Besides these 3 gangs of jungle pirates, there are some other gangs of jungle pirates like Karim Sharif Bahini, Asabur Bahini, Dayal Bahini, Rabi Bahini, Ranga Bahini, Suman Bahini, Dula Bhai Bahini, Anarul Bahini, Hannan Bahini, Ranga Bahini and Alif Bahini. Each gang of jungle pirates consists of 20 to 40 members. They put up temporary camps in the deep forest, kidnapping the fishermen and realizing ransom from their family members. It was revealed that more than 300 fishermen were kidnapped and tortured in those temporary shelters in order to realize ransom during the last one year alone. It is learnt that the jungle pirates are very active at Mara Bhola, Alibanda, Dhanchebaria, Dudmukhi, Shyela, Narkelbaria, Teearchar, Pashur, Andharmanik, Shibsha and other places within Sharankhola and Chandpai Forest Ranges under the Eastern Sundarbans in Bagerhat district. Dr. Shaikh Faridul Islam, Chairman of the Environmentalist’s Association and Nur-e-Alam Shaikh, Chief Co-coordinator of the organization “Sundarban Rakkhay Amra” told, Godfathers of those gangs of jungle pirates control them through their trusted sources after living in the human habitations. They added, until and unless the jungle pirates and their godfathers cannot be subdued the biodiversity of Sundrbans will be destroyed forever and consequently, the life and livelihood will be thrown into utter distress. In this connection they urged upon the law enforcing agencies to adopt zero tolerance. Lt. Commander Abrar Hossain, Staff Officer of the Coast Guards, Western Zone deployed Mongla (Port) told, members of the coast guards are conducting normal patrol duties in and around Sundarbas in order to subdue the jungle pirates. Besides this, very often special raids are being conducted with a view to free the Sundarbans from jungle bandits/pirates.

title: CAB alleges traders creating artificial crisis
body: Sr. Staff Reporter, Kishoreganj : The price of onion has been increasing for a month . The price of the spice has now crossed 150 taka as the demand increases. In the last one week, the price per kg has increased by 25 to 35 taka. Not only this time, the price of onion increases every year in November- December in the country. The Trade and Tariff Commission has conducted a review to find out why onion prices increase in the last two months of the year. Tariff Commission has revealed that onion prices increase for four reasons during this time. These reasons are the violence of middlemen at every stage from production to consumer; lack of onion storage; and damage to onions during the last stages of the season and due to rain. Onion traders said that the new advance onions have not yet started arriving in the market in full. That is why the supply of onions in the market is not as before. Due to these reasons, the price of the product is increasing. However, the news of relief amidst this increase is that the government has allowed the import of onions in a limited scale. In addition, there is hope in the market for advance variety of cut onions in Kishoreganj kitchen market. Due to this, the price of other onions has also decreased by at least 10 taka than before. Today (Thursday) , cut onions wholesale sold at a price of tk.110, retail leaves tk. 120-130. Md.Sairz Wasi, a wholesaler in Kishoreganj ‘s Bara Bazar told the New Nation that, “Onion prices increased excessively last week due to low supply. However, the arrival of cut onions in the market at the beginning of this week has started to have an impact. Prices have decreased compared to before. Onion prices will normalize in a few days after imports start.” Prices are increasing for 4 reasons: A Tariff Commission investigation has revealed that onion prices have increased at this time of year due to lack of storage, violence by middlemen, damage to onions due to rain, and the end of the season.Onion storage season is usually from January to April. Farmers store onions on their own initiative. The Tariff Commission has identified that the price of onions increases due to the lack of government storage. Onions change hands multiple times from the farmer to the market. Middlemen make a profit at every stage. The price of onions also increases due to the excessive profits of middlemen. Consumers Association of Bangladesh (CAB), Kishoreganj ‘s President Alam Sarowar Tito has alleged that traders have increased prices by creating an artificial crisis. Traders have created an artificial crisis to make an excuse to import onions from India. Because if they can now import onions from India, they will be able to make several times more profit.”

title: Islamic knowledge contest held
body: Mymensingh Correspondent : The largest upazila-based competition ‘Pibaria Group – Light of Islam’ Islamic Knowledge Competition-2025 was held in Gafargaon, Mymensingh. On Thursday, the day-long competition was held at the ground of the madrasa at the initiative of Ghagra Porabaria Abdur Rahman Khan Islamia Madrasa, a pioneering institution in the practice of religious knowledge and spreading moral education, and under the overall supervision of prominent industrialist and education enthusiast Md. Nuruzzaman Khan Rana. About 300 students from various madrasas, schools and colleges of the upazila participated in the day-long competition in 6 categories. The main attraction of this competition of Pibaria Group was ‘Hifzul Quran’. In addition, hundreds of spectators were fascinated by the participation of students in various stages of the fascinating recitation, Azan-Ekkamat and Hamd-Naat competition. Cash prizes were awarded to the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th place winners in 6 categories, attractive prizes were awarded to the 6th to 10th place winners and consolation prizes to 100 people. In addition, the teachers of the 1st, 2nd and 3rd place winners were awarded with honorary crests. The competition was attended by 15 experienced judges led by International Qari and Gold Medalist Hafiz Maulana Abu Saleh Mohammad Musa and International Hafiz and Islamic Scholar Mufti Maulana Zakaria Mahmud, along with the Muhtamim Mostafizur Rahman (Charbuhi) of the said madrasa, teachers, guardians and well-wishers. After the day-long competition, the 6th Annual Islamic Conference began in the evening. Eminent scholars and invited guests presented the prizes to the winners on the conference stage.

title: Kulaura gets new OC
body: Moulvibazar correspondent : Muhammad Moniruzzaman Mullah has joined Kulaura Police Station as the new OC. He took over from outgoing OC Md Omar Farooq on Monday. The new OC Muhammad Moniruzzaman Mullah is the son of Md. Bachchu Mullah of Panchbaria village of Araihazar upazila of Narayanganj district. He joined Bangladesh Police as an SI in 1999 and was appointed as OC in 2024. He was promoted. He first worked as an OC at Golapganj Police Station and then joined Kulaura Police Station. He also worked in the United Nations peacekeeping mission. In his personal life, he is the father of 1 son and 1 daughter. It is noteworthy that the recently retired OC Md. Omar Faruk joined the Beanibazar Police Station in Sylhet as the OC.

title: BRUR demands justice for Osman Hadi
body: Rangpur Correspondent : Students of Begum Rokeya University (BRUR) held a protest march following the shooting of Osman Hadi, the potential parliamentary candidate for Dhaka-8 and convener of the Inqilab Forum. The protest march began on Friday, at 4:30 pm from the main gate of the campus. The march proceeded along Bijoy Road in the university and gathered at Shaheed Abu Saeed Gate, where a brief rally was held. Students demanded the immediate arrest and trial of those responsible for the attack on Osman Hadi. During the protest, students raised slogans such as: “Light the fire, light the fire,” “Why attack Hadi? We demand answers,” “Break the den of terrorists,” “Terrorism and politics cannot go together,” and “If anything happens to Hadi Bhai, fire will spread. to every home.” Zahid Hasan Joy, convener of BRUR Inqilab Forum and a student of the Department of Sociology, said, “Our Hadi Bhai, who has been a leading fighter against Indian aggression, has been subjected to this despicable attack. The interim administration must take responsibility. We know who attacked him-it is the terrorists who oppose his politics. The administration must answer why they failed to provide security to Hadi, just as they failed to protect the revolutionaries of ’24.” Mehedi Hasan, member secretary of the Inquilab Forum and a student of the Department of Economics, said, “For a long time, the people of Bangladesh have been unable to exercise their voting rights properly. The interim government announced the election schedule just yesterday. Soon after, we see that Osman Hadi, who played a major role in the July uprising and has been a strong voice against Indian imperialism, has fallen victim to a targeted killing. Those responsible for the attack must be arrested and unmasked.”

title: Nat’l tea company rebounds auction sales
body: Moulvibazar Correspondent : Despite the most difficult obstacles of the times, crises, adversities, natural disasters, and worker discontent the workers and owners fought hand in hand to improve the quality of tea, and a record amount of tea was sold at this year’s auction market, despite earlier losses. Tea is now being produced in 13 tea gardens run by the state-owned National Tea Company (NTC), including Madhabpur, Madanmohanpur, Patrakhola, Kurma, and Champara in Kamalganj upazila of Moulvibazar. The quality has increased significantly. This positive change has been directly reflected in the Chattogram tea auction market. NTC has created a new record for the highest sales in two consecutive auctions in the company’s hundred-year history. This year’s auction market is being considered a major success in the overall development and management reforms of NTC. In the 30th auction of the Chattogram auction market, tea produced by NTC’s gardens was sold for about Tk 4 crore. In the next auction, number 31, this amount increased to about Tk 6 crore. With tea worth around Tk 10 crore sold in just two auctions, the government-owned National Tea Company has regained vitality as its tea gardens have returned to a profitable position after years of losses. This has sparked new hope for the state-owned tea sector, which has long been lagging behind. Those concerned say this success has come from a combination of increased productivity, quality control, and modern management. A special action plan was adopted for the 2024-25 financial year to ensure quality in NTC’s government-run gardens. The use of organic fertiliser has been increased across all 13 gardens, including Madhabpur, Madanmohanpur, Patrakhola, Kurma, Champara, Bijoya, Premnagar, Lakkartura, Teliapara, Jagadishpur, Ch-i, and Parkul in Kamalganj upazila. In addition, due to the modernisation of irrigation management, production has not been disrupted even during droughts or adverse weather. Major changes have also been made in the training of tea workers. According to garden sources, workers strictly followed the ‘two buds and one leaf’ principle when plucking leaves. This greatly improved the quality of raw leaf collection and resulted in visible improvement in the colour, flavour, and density of processed tea. As a result, buyers’ interest in NTC tea has increased significantly in the auction market. Dipan Sinha, General Manager of Madhabpur Tea Garden in Kamalganj upazila, said that they were able to maintain quality production this time due to guidance from senior NTC officials, regular monitoring, and coordinated efforts at the field level. “The sincerity and hard work of the workers, employees, and officers are the main driving forces behind this success. If the market remains favourable, the gardens of the National Tea Company will be able to play an important role in earning foreign exchange by exporting quality tea abroad. We are moving towards that goal,” he said. He added that Managing Director HSM Ziaul Ahsan has been working tirelessly to increase productivity, ensure quality control, and modernise the National Tea Company since taking office on 2 February. Visible improvements have been made in the colour, taste, and density of the tea as a result of these reforms. NTC Deputy General Manager (DGM) Rafiqul Islam said that the National Tea Company has made significant progress in recent years. The company had faced a financial crisis, and in 2023, it was downgraded to the ‘Z’ category on the Dhaka and Chattogram Stock Exchanges. Therefore, under the directives of Managing Director HSM Ziaul Ahsan, the management staff and tea workers in each tea garden have been paying close attention to production. The company is focusing on reducing production costs, exploring new markets, and improving product quality. Steps are being taken to modernise all 13 gardens and develop the skills of workers.

title: Chapainawabganj farmer amazes with Chinese orange harves
body: National Desk : A quiet village in Chapainawabganj has become the centre of local curiosity and inspiration after an agricultural entrepreneur successfully cultivated Chinese oranges, an achievement many had believed impossible in Bangladesh. Forty-one-year-old farmer Sayem Ali has drawn visitors from across the area, all eager to witness the clusters of bright, ripe oranges hanging heavily from the trees in his orchard. The scene has created both excitement and a stir among villagers, who until now had only seen Chinese oranges in markets as imported fruit. Sayem, who previously relied on mango farming, said he struggled to maintain a steady income from the crop. His interest in Chinese oranges began when he noticed the fruit increasingly available in local markets. Intrigued, he approached the local agriculture office for advice. With guidance and technical support from agricultural officials, he brought three bighas of land under cultivation in Baharam of Sadar Upazila in 2022. The initial investment stood at Tk 1.5 lakh. Now, just a few years later, the orchard is teeming with fruit, reports UNB. “I managed to recover my costs and even made a small profit from my first harvest in 2024,” Sayem said, adding, “But this year the trees are full. I’m selling the oranges at Tk 100 per kilogram, and after expenses, I expect to earn Tk 6 to 7 lakh.” Farm worker Anarul Islam, who has cared for the orchard since its early days, echoed the optimism. “The harvest has been excellent. These oranges taste very good, and the demand is high. We don’t even need to take them to the market, as buyers come directly to the orchard,” he said. Sayem’s success has quickly inspired others. Curious farmers and residents have been flocking to Baharam, many considering whether they too should switch to or start cultivating Chinese oranges. Local resident Abdul Malek admitted he had never imagined the fruit could grow locally. “We always thought Chinese oranges came from abroad. After visiting the orchard and speaking with the owner, I’m convinced it’s profitable. I plan to start cultivating them too, with support from the agriculture office,” he said. Another visitor, Abdul Gaffar from Ramchandrapur, was impressed by the quality. “I’ve eaten imported oranges for years. Now we have them grown just near my home-and they’re delicious,” he said. Similar enthusiasm was echoed by villagers Taifur and Karim, both of whom said the success story had motivated them to consider starting orchards of their own. According to Dr Yasin Ali, Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) in Chapainawabganj, local conditions are well suited for the fruit. “The soil and climate here are favourable for cultivating Chinese oranges. Sayem Ali is one of our successful farmers, and we are providing him with all necessary support. New entrepreneurs will also receive full technical assistance,” he said. What began as an experiment has now become a model of rural innovation, locals said. They said Sayem’s flourishing orchard has not only transformed his own livelihood but has also opened up new possibilities for agricultural diversification in Chapainawabganj, proving that with the right guidance, even unexpected crops can thrive.

title: Int’l Human Rights Day observed
body: Feni Correspondent : Odhikar has called on human rights activists to stand united against human rights violations in the country. This was the call made by guests and human rights activists at the exchange of views organized by Odhikar at Feni Press Club last Wednesday morning. Former president of Feni Press Club and veteran journalist AKM Abdur Rahim presided over the meeting, and Rawshan Ara Begum, mother of missing person Mahbubur Rahman Ripone, was the chief guest. Odhikar Feni’s focal person, journalist Nazmul Haque Shamim, moderated the keynote speech, while Shahjalal Bhuiyan, executive editor of human rights organizer Daily Ajeyo Bangla, read the main article. The special guests were former president of Feni Press Club Rabiul Haque Robi, Muhammad Abu Taher Bhuiyan, General Secretary of Feni for Sujan-Sushasan, Mohammad Shahadat Hossain, Central Secretary General of Bangladesh Primary. Teachers Association Mohi Uddin Khondoker, President of JASAS Feni branch, cultural organizer Kazi Iqbal Ahmed Paran, and advisor of Feni Bandhushaba Sheikh Nur Uddin Chowdhury Mamun. The speakers included Weekly Swadespatra editor NN Jiban, Chief Editor of Daily Suprabhat Feni Firoz Alam, General Secretary of Feni Journalist Union Syed Monir, Chairman of Ekta Mahila Unnayan Sangstha Rokeya Islam, July fighter Md. Abul Hasan Shahin in the 24th movement, Mahfuzur Rahman Shipu, brother of missing person Ripon, and others. The meeting was attended by journalists, human rights organizers, and people from different classes and professions. After the exchange of views, they formed a human chain in front of the Feni Press Club.

title: Outsourcing staff rally over unpaid wages
body: Khulna Bureau : Outsourcing employees of Khulna 250-bed general hospital have formed a human chain expressing their anger and protest over not receiving their salaries for 18 consecutive months. The human chain was held at 12 noon on Thursday in front of the main gate of the hospital. A total of 46 outsourcing employees, including 14 people working under the supervisory office and 32 more under the civil surgeon’s office, participated in it. The banners displayed in the human chain read – “No salary for 17 months! Want salary, not begging”, “Why ignore the High Court’s order?”, “Khulna 250-bed hospital – want answers.” The speakers in the human chain said that they have not been receiving salaries for about one and a half years, including this December. One office is blaming the other office for the salary issue. The employees alleged that the hospital’s superintendent Dr. Gazi Rafiqul Islam and the chief assistant cum accountant Tariqul Islam have deliberately not sent the necessary documents to the higher office for the last 6 months. As a result, the process of paying their outstanding salaries has stalled. The employees further alleged that the hospital authorities are conspiring to call tenders to recruit 107 new people, ignoring the 2025 outsourcing policy and the High Court’s instructions. They even claimed that 7 people have been secretly hired without any tender. However, according to the instructions of the Ministry of Finance, it is clearly stated that old employees should not be dismissed. They said that many employees have been serving in this hospital for the last 7-8 years, but there is a sudden attempt to dismiss them in a conspiratorial manner. They are facing a humanitarian crisis along with the families of the employees who have not received their salaries. Md. Mamun Hossain, Md. Abdur Rahim, Shahnaz, Murshida, Chattar, Masum, Quader, Shahin, Setu, Erashad, Rajesh, Debashish, Alam, Sadhan, Dipankar, Parimal, Nipa, Abdul Halim Khan, Ashiq, Farooq, Jasim and outsourcing employees employed at the hospital were present in the human chain.

title: Colorful rally held for Harmony Festival
body: Srimangal Correspondent : A colorful rally was held in Srimangal, Moulvibazar, keeping in mind the ‘Harmony Festival’, a symbol of multicultural harmony. On Thursday morning, under the initiative of the Bangladesh Tourism Board and the Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism and in cooperation with the Srimangal Upazila administration, people of various ethnic groups including Khasi, Garo, Tripura, and Manipuri participated in the rally wearing their own clothes. Srimangal Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md. Islam Uddin, Assistant Commissioner (Land) Mohibullah Akon and others were present at the rally. Srimangal Upazila Nirbahi Officer Md. Islam Uddin said, 26 gazetted small ethnic groups live in our Srimangal. To showcase their culture in Bangladesh and the world, last year, Bangladesh Tourism Board and Ministry of Civil Aviation and Tourism organised Ne Harmony Festival Season 1 in collaboration with Srimangal Upazila Administration. Continuing its success. a three-day festival has been organized on December 18, 19 and 20 at the Phulchhara Tea Garden Ground in Srimangal. There will be 63 cultural performances here in three days. There will be various stalls of small ethnic groups.

title: Aid for road accident victims’ families
body: Natore Correspondent : BRTA Chairman and Additional Secretary Abu Momtaz Saad Uddin Ahmed has said that the loss of a life in a road accident does not only devastate a single family, but also affects the entire society. “We cannot bring back the lives that have been lost, but the financial assistance provided by the state will offer the families some support to stand on their feet again,” he said. He added that the government has been working continuously to ensure safety on the roads. “With the combined efforts of the public, transport owners and workers, and the administration, it is possible to reduce road accidents. We want to ensure that no family has to endure the pain of losing a loved one again.” He made these remarks on Thursday at 10 am while addressing the cheque distribution ceremony organised by the Natore District Administration and BRTA Natore Circle at the conference room of the Deputy Commissioner. At the event, cheques from the BRTA Trustee Board were distributed among families of those killed or injured in road accidents in Natore and Pabna districts. The ceremony was presided over by Deputy Commissioner Asma Shaheen. Among others present were Additional Superintendent of Police Ifte Khair Alam, Additional District Magistrate Md Arif Hossain, Assistant Director of BRTA Natore Circle Altaf Hossain, Motor Vehicle Inspector Uttam Kumar Debsharma, President of Natore Press Club Shahidul Haque Sarkar, and President of the Safe Road Movement Natore District Committee Golam Mostafa. Later, the chief guest distributed cheques worth a total of Tk 83 lakh to the families of 16 deceased victims and one injured individual from the two districts. Under two categories, families of nine deceased from Natore and seven from Pabna received Tk 5 lakh each, while the family of the injured person received a cheque of Tk 3 lakh.

title: Prayer ceremony held in Singra
body: Natore Correspondent : A prayer ceremony was held for the recovery and long life of BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia. The event took place on Tuesday afternoon at the Gol-e-Afroze College ground in Singra. The ceremony was presided over by Sakhawat Hossain Sakha, coordinator of the BNP Ward and Member Registration Committee. The chief guest, Principal Anwarul Islam Anu, the BNP nominee for Natore-3 (Singra) constituency and a district BNP member, delivered a speech. The programme was conducted by Advocate Shamim Hossain, former Organisational Secretary and former Vice-Chairman of the Upazila BNP. Other speakers included Professor Sharful Islam Bulbul, Secretary of the Upazila BNP Member Registration and Union Election Committee, Md Afsaruzzaman, former Chairman of Ramanand Khajura Union Parishad, Ibrahim Khalil Fotik, former Chairman of Kolom Union Parishad, Shahadat Hossain, former Chairman of Tajpur Union Parishad, Bojlar Rahman Bacchu, former Chairman of Italy Union Parishad, BNP members Atikur Rahman Liton, Mahidul Islam, Alhaj Rezaul Karim Bablu, Abdullah Al Kafi, coordinator of the Upazila Volunteer Party, and Shahadat Hossain Mintu, coordinator of the Upazila Student Party, among others. The prayers and Milad ceremony were led by Maulana Asaduzzaman Asad, coordinator of the Upazila Ulama Party.

title: Fakhrul urges BNP to prepare for Tarique’s ‘imminent return’
body: NN ONLINE: Just hours before the announcement of the election schedule, BNP Secretary General Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Thursday called on party leaders and activists to get ready to welcome their Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman, saying he will return to the country ‘very soon’. “Since all our leaders are here today, I want to tell you that our leader (Tarique) will come back to us very soon,” he said while speaking at the opening session of the fifth day of BNP’s ‘Plan to Build the Country’ workshop. The BNP leader called on his colleagues to be ready to give Tarique a grand reception on the day he returns home, ending his 17 years of exile in London. “The day our leader arrives and sets foot in Bangladesh, the whole country should shake. You must remember this… You will be able to do it, InshaAllah. On that day, we want to change the face of the entire country,” he said. Fakhrul said the party wants to move forward with a progressive vision to take Bangladesh ahead. “We want to move ahead. We want progress. To place Bangladesh in a position of dignity, we want to carry forward our leader’s thoughts and plans.” Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin is scheduled to address the nation in the evening to announce the schedule for the 13th parliamentary election. Fakhrul said the election schedule will be announced today, opening the way for the people to establish new leadership for Bangladesh through a fresh election. “We now have the chance to work with the people to form a truly representative parliament — a parliament that will lead Bangladesh towards a new horizon, under the leadership of our leader Tarique Rahman,” he said. He said the BNP must win the upcoming election and secure a full victory so it can take Bangladesh forward. “Many barriers will come. Many difficulties will appear. There are many campaigns against us, and there will be more. But we want to stand tall by overcoming all of these. BNP has never been defeated, and it will not be defeated,” he added. Describing BNP as the party of the people, the Liberation War and the struggle for democracy, Fakhrul urged leaders to stay united. “Nothing else will bring you success. What will bring success is unity — a strong, steel-like unity — and the spirit to move forward with our nationalist and democratic ideals,” he said. The party earlier announced the six-day workshop on 27 November involving Chhatra Dal, Krishak Dal, Ulema Dal, Swechchhasebak Dal and other front organisations to prepare them for campaigning before the polls. Fakhrul inaugurated the fifth day’s programme at the Krishibid Institution Bangladesh (KIB) auditorium in Dhaka’s Farmgate, with BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi in the chair. BNP Acting Chairman Tarique Rahman is expected to address the concluding session virtually in the afternoon. Leaders and activists of BNP joined the programme to receive training on different issues so they can reach out to people and explain BNP’s plans, election manifesto and promises before the polls.

title: Bangladesh, Australia identity new avenues of bilateral cooperation
body: NN ONLINE: Bangladesh and Australia have identified new avenues for cooperation in areas such as renewable energy, skills partnership and technology sharing, blue economy, artificial intelligence, cyber security and anti–money laundering initiatives. The issues were discussed at the 6th round of Senior Officials’ Talks (SOT) between Bangladesh and Australia held in Dhaka on Wednesday. Dr Md Nazrul Islam, Secretary (Bilateral–East and West), Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Sarah Storey, First Assistant Secretary, South and Central Asia Division, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), Government of Australia led the respective delegations. With the commitment to strengthen the ever growing bilateral relations between the two friendly countries, the 6th SOT was held in a ‘warm and cordial’ atmosphere, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Thursday. The discussion featured constructive, forward-looking exchanges covering a wide spectrum of bilateral relations including sectoral cooperation, trade and investment, development partnership, migration and mobility, maritime cooperation, multilateral engagement, climate change and people-to-people linkages. Both sides also exchanged views on regional and global matters of mutual interest, including the Indo-Pacific, IORA engagements, and the Rohingya situation. First Assistant Secretary Storey reiterated Australia’s continued support to the Interim Government and its reform initiatives. About the upcoming General Election, she conveyed that Australia looks forward to a free and fair election and democratic transition in Bangladesh, including extending full support to the Bangladeshi expatriates for the postal voting. Storey highlighted Australian Government’s priority areas in its relations with Bangladesh namely expansion of people to people linkages, growth of trade and investment, implementation of development partnership, support Bangladesh in managing Rohingyas, defence and security cooperation, Indo Pacific cooperation. The Australian side conveyed their intention to prioritize Bangladesh as a secondary manufacturing location for its cotton and wool industries. Secretary Nazrul Islam proposed resumption of Work and Holiday visas for Bangladeshis in Australia, employment of Bangladeshi specified skilled workers in the Australian mining sector, establishment of University of Canberra’s campus in Dhaka and collaboration between Australian TAFE and Bangladeshi TVET. He underscored the importance of increased high-level visits to advance the growing partnership between Bangladesh and Australia. The talks concluded with the signing of ‘MoU on Employment of the Dependents of Diplomatic and Consular Personnel between Bangladesh and Australia’. The visiting Australian delegation arrived in Dhaka on December 9 and attended the Joint Working Group on Trade and Investment Meeting under the Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (TIFA) at the Ministry of Commerce. The 7th SOT is expected to be held in Canberra next year.

title: Over 3 lakh expatriates enrolled for postal voting system
body: NN ONLINE: More than three lakh expatriate Bangladeshis have already registered to take part in the country’s first-ever postal voting initiative, marking a milestone in efforts to enfranchise citizens living abroad. The Election Commission (EC) today reported that a total of 307,577 overseas Bangladeshis had successfully completed registration through the “Postal Vote BD” app as of 10:00am today. This digital gateway enables them to cast ballots in the upcoming 13th Jatiya Sangsad election as well as the referendum. Of the registered voters, 284,349 are men while 23,228 are women, according to the EC’s updated figures. Officials described the turnout as a significant step in broadening democratic participation, noting that the postal ballot system is designed to ensure inclusivity for millions of Bangladeshis residing overseas. Among the country-based registrations, Saudi Arabia has the highest number of 84,600, Qatar 25,257, the United States 20,755, the United Arab Emirates 19,852, Malaysia 18,156, Singapore 15,294, the United Kingdom 13,663, Oman 12,625, Italy 9,965, Canada 9,852, South Korea 9,602, Australia 8,221, Kuwait 8,204 and Japan 7,068. Besides, government servants who are engaged in electoral duties to vote in the 13th National Parliament Election and Referendum and are residing outside their voting area can register to exercise their voting rights through the “Postal Vote BD” app from the date of announcement of the schedule until December 25. In this regard, the EC message said, “Voters engaged in electoral duties in the 13th National Parliament Election, government servants residing outside their voting area and voters in legal custody can register through the app from the date of announcement of the election schedule until December 25.” EC Secretariat Senior Secretary Akhtar Ahmed said, “The registration deadline for out-of-country voting has been extended until midnight on December 25. Now, any adult Bangladeshi can register to vote by downloading our app from anywhere in the world.” Besides, the EC has extended the time for expatriate Bangladeshis to correct their addresses on the “Postal Vote BD” app for seven countries including Saudi Arabia until 9:00 am on December 14. The other six countries are Qatar, United Arab Emirates, Malaysia, Oman, Kuwait and Bahrain. However, there is no further opportunity for registered voters from other countries to correct their addresses, according to a message sent by the EC to media. The EC has requested expatriate Bangladeshis to provide correct address while registering through the Postal Vote BD app. In this regard, a message from the EC said that to get a postal ballot, provide the correct address as per the prevailing rules of the country where you are staying while registering on the “Postal Vote BD” app. If necessary, provide the address of your workplace or a known person. Postal ballot papers will not be sent to voters without providing the correct and complete address. On November 18, the Chief Election Commissioner launched the “Postal Vote BD” app and announced the schedule for voter registration in 148 specific countries for the 13th National Parliament Election. To vote through postal ballot, expatriate voters must use the mobile number of the country from which they will vote. To register, first download and install the “Postal Vote BD” app from the Google Play Store or App Store. Providing the correct address is essential to ensure receipt of the ballot abroad.

title: Sylhet jolted as 2 mild quakes strike
body: Within a span of five minutes, Sylhet experienced two mild earthquakes early Thursday, triggering panic among people. The first quake struck at 2:20:31 am followed by a second at 2:25:14 am, Shah Md Sajib Hossain, assistant meteorologist of the Sylhet Seismic Observatory Centre, said on Thursday morning. No damage or casualties were reported so far, he said. According to the Seismic Observatory of the Bangladesh Meteorological Department, the first quake measured 3.5 on the Richter scale, with its epicentre reported to be in Beanibazar upazila of Sylhet district. The second tremor, measuring 3.3 on the Richter scale, originated from Borolekha upazila in neighbouring Moulvibazar district, according to the BMD. Bangladesh had recently experienced several earthquakes, with the epicentre in Narsingdi, raising concerns among people across the country.

title: A Rajshahi village holds its breath as little Sajid remains trapped underground
body: NN ONLINE: For nearly 20 long hours, the people of Koelhat village in Tanore upazila have been living in fear, worry and helplessness. Two-year-old Sajid, who slipped into an abandoned deep tube well pipe on Wednesday afternoon, is still missing underground, and rescue teams have yet to reach him. By 9:30am on Thursday, firefighters said there was still no sign of movement inside the pipe. The long night that passed brought no relief. Sajid’s family and villagers stayed awake, their faces stiff with hope and anxiety. The Fire Service said the little boy fell into an 8-inch-wide pipe, too narrow for anyone to enter. Rescuers dug a larger hole beside it, using three excavators to create a tunnel that could lead to the child. But even after hours of work, they have not been able to find him, said Didarul Alam, Assistant Director of the Rajshahi Fire Service. “We are trying every possible method,” he told UNB on Thursday morning from the site, his voice carrying the weight of the tense rescue effort. A special camera was lowered into the pipe to look for Sajid, but it got stuck around 40 feet deep. It showed no trace of the child. Fire Service officials believe he may be somewhere around that depth, and they are continuously supplying oxygen into the pipe in an effort to keep him alive. Witnesses had earlier reported hearing faint sounds from inside the pipe soon after the accident. But by nightfall, the cries fell silent, leaving rescuers and villagers deeply worried about whether the child is still alive. The tragedy began around 1pm on Wednesday, when Sajid was walking behind his mother on their way home. The entrance of the abandoned well was covered with straw. In a moment that now haunts his mother, the child suddenly called out, “Ma, Ma.” When she turned, she watched him fall through the hidden hole. “He slipped further down before anyone could reach him,” said his mother, Runa Khatun, her voice breaking as she recalled the moment. Locals immediately called the Fire Service, and rescue operations began at 1:45pm. But by the time firefighters arrived at 2:30pm, the soil around the well had already been disturbed by villagers desperately trying to save the boy. Some faint responses from Sajid were heard until 4pm, Didarul Alam said. But after that, the child’s voice was drowned out by noise and movement at the rescue site. Still, oxygen continues to be pushed into the pipe, as teams refuse to give up hope.

title: Khaleda Zia receiving intensive care, says Dr. Zahid
body: NN ONLINE: BNP Chairperson and former Prime Minister Begum Khaleda Zia is currently receiving advanced medical care in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) of Evercare Hospital in the city, according to her personal physician and BNP standing committee member Dr. AZM Zahid Hossain. “Begum Zia is undergoing treatment in the ICU, where the highest level of care has been ensured. She is receiving all necessary medical support for a critically ill patient,” Dr. Zahid told reporters during a press briefing in front of the hospital on Wednesday evening. He urged the public not to be misled by rumors regarding her condition. “Khaleda Zia is under treatment. I sincerely request everyone not to pay attention to any rumors about her,” he said. When asked for further details about her latest condition, Dr. Zahid declined to provide specifics, citing medical ethics. “She is a patient. She has certain rights and privileges. As a doctor, I am not permitted by medical science to disclose everything publicly, even if I want to.” “She is regularly receiving treatment and is genuinely responding to it,” he said.

title: DoE, UNIDO jointly arrange seminar in Barguna
body: Barguna Correspondent : As plastic pollution continues to pose a growing environmental and public health challenge across Bangladesh, the Department of Environment (DoE) and the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO), with financial support from the Government of Norway, jointly organised a seminar and community clean-up campaign titled “Integrated Actions for Sustainable Plastic Use and Marine Litter Prevention.” The event took place on 10 December 2025 at the Barguna Municipality Auditorium, bringing together more than 300 participants, including government officials, civil society representatives, environmental groups, business leaders, and volunteers. The programme was attended by Mr. Md. Ibrahim, Additional Superintendent of Police (Crime), Barguna, as Chief Guest. Special Guests included Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam, Executive Officer (Secretary), Barguna Municipality; Mr. S. M. Arafat, National Expert, UNIDO Bangladesh; Hayat Mahmud Rokib, Assistant Director, DoE Barguna; Dr. Arunava Chowdhury, Upazila Health & Family Planning Officer; Mr. Mushfiq Arif, Member Secretary of Dhoritri Rokkhay Amra (Dhara); Naim, Coordinator, BD Clean Barguna; Mr. Shafiqul Islam Tipu, President, Mizan Tower and Mosque Market Business Association; and Mr. Moniruzzaman Taslim, President, Municipal Super Market Business Association. The event was moderated by Mr. Mushfiq Arif, Member Secretary of Dhara.In his welcome remarks, Mr. S. M. Arafat, National Expert, UNIDO Bangladesh, emphasised that plastic pollution has evolved from a national challenge into a global crisis. He highlighted that countries worldwide are moving toward a legally binding international treaty on plastic management. He noted that improper disposal of daily-use plastics is contributing to environmental degradation, blocking drainage systems, polluting rivers, and entering the ocean-ultimately harming marine ecosystems and public health. Speaking at the event, Mr. Hayat Mahmud Rokib, Assistant Director, DoE Barguna, stressed the importance of individual and community responsibility. He noted that Bangladesh uses approximately 410,000 metric tons of plastic annually, much of which remains unmanaged. He urged increased public awareness and the adoption of eco-friendly alternatives. Dr. Arunava Chowdhury highlighted the need to shift personal habits and prioritise environmentally responsible choices, noting that sustainable plastic use is achievable through collaboration. Mr. Md. Rafiqul Islam, Executive Officer of Barguna Municipality, underscored the importance of civic responsibility, acknowledging the work of the municipality’s 180 sanitation workers who clean the city every day. He called for additional waste bins and strengthened waste management systems with support from the district administration and development partners. As Chief Guest, Mr. Md. Ibrahim emphasised that meaningful progress in reducing plastic pollution requires a change in mindset. He noted that people often follow strict cleanliness rules abroad and encouraged similar behaviour at home. He also urged youth to develop affordable, environmentally friendly alternatives to plastic. At the conclusion of the seminar, all participants took a pledge to promote sustainable plastic use, proper waste management, and environmental protection. A large-scale community clean-up campaign was then conducted in 7 No Ward, Borgun Lanchghat, Kheyaghat, Tempu Stand area of Barguna town, where participants collected approximately 312.15 kilograms of plastic waste. The collected materials were handed over to authorized recycling agencies for reprocessing. Following the cleanup, local youth groups, civil society organisations, and community volunteers will continue a three-month door-to-door advocacy campaign across Barguna. This extended mobilisation aims to reinforce responsible plastic use, encourage proper waste disposal, and strengthen long-term community-led stewardship of the environment.

title: Int’l Human Rights Day observed
body: Thakurgaon Correspondent : International Human Rights Day was celebrated at Pirganj Upazila under Thakurgaon district with the theme ‘We are with those who have nothing and those who have no one, human rights are essential in our daily lives. A rally and discussion meeting was held on Wednesday in collaboration with the upazila administration, organized by the non-governmental organization Community Development Association (CDA). The rally started from the upazila parishad and went through various roads before terminaling at the upazila parishad auditorium under the chairmanship of Abinash Chandra Roy, the head of the Upazila Landless Coordination Committee. The speakers included Assistant Commissioner (Land) NM Ishfaqul Kabir, Press Club President Joynal Abedin Babul, Upazila Corruption Prevention Committee President Mokaddes Hayat Milon and CDA Unit Manager Mamata Ghosh.

title: World Human Rights Day celebrated
body: Narayanganj Correspondent : With this year’s theme, “Human Rights are an essential part of our daily lives,” the Narayanganj District Branch of the Journalists Society for Human Rights celebrated World Human Rights Day 2025 in a befitting manner. A human chain programme and rally were held in front of Siddhirganj Pool S.M Tower on Wednesday morning, to uphold dignity, freedom, and justice for all. The chief guest of the programme was prominent journalist Advocate Manir Hossain, Central Chairman of the Journalists Society for Human Rights. The event was organised under the chairmanship of Nurul Aziz Chowdhury, President of the Narayanganj District Branch of the Journalists Society for Human Rights and Editor and Publisher of the Daily Amader Jagran. Attendees included District Branch General Secretary Md. Amir Hossain, journalist of the Daily Amar Sangbad; veteran journalist S. M. Mizan; Abul Khair; Md. Liton Mia; Abu Bakr Siddique Siam; Md. Sayhan; Mukta Akhter; among others. Prominent journalist Advocate Manir Hossain, Central Chairman of the Journalists Society for Human Rights, remarked that the Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations on December 10, 1948, and since then, the day has been observed worldwide. He said, “The main goal of this organization is to uphold human rights, establish justice, ensure freedom of speech, and promote democratic practices.

title: 4 ladies conferred Begum Rokey Padak
body: Chandpur Correspondent : Four indomitable ladies in three Upazilas of the district were awarded Begum Rokeya Padak at a function held at the Sadar UZ Auditorium on Tuesday. District Administration and District office of Women Affairs Directorate jointly organised this function. The awardees of Rokeya Padak are: Tanjina Huque ( a resident of Mokimabad, Hajiganj) ,awarded for achieving laudable success in Economical activities , Rabeya Akter (a resident of Mokimabad, Hajiganj UZ ) for being a successful mother, Romana Papri ( a resident of Adurviti, Matlab Uttar) for Education and Services and Bilkis Akter ( a resident of Naula village in Kachua UZ) awarded for being a struggling and enterprising woman overcoming many repressions, social drawbacks and taboos. As chief guest, DC spoke highly of these awardees for their excellent achievements and then formally handed over the Padaks to them amid applauses. ADC (General) Ershaduddin presided while Additional SP Nadia Noor, UNO Sadar SMN Jamiul Hikma and District Women Affairs Officer Nasima Akter Program Officer SM Tanvir Rashid among others spoke on the occasion.

title: CCC, MSF join hands to combat dengue
body: Chattogram Bureau : Chattogram City Corporation Mayor Dr. Shahadat Hossain said, “Prevention of dengue and chikungunya is now the top priority of urban health management. CCC and Doctors Without Borders (MSF) will work together in the future to take effective and scientific initiatives in this regard. International experience and a coordinated action plan in public health protection will further strengthen our fight.” In a meeting with the mayor at the CCC office on Tuesday afternoon, a senior MSF delegation presented an outline of possible dengue prevention activities, preparedness initiatives and joint cooperation in Chattogram. At the meeting, MSF highlighted their global emergency health response experience, especially effective measures to combat AIDS-related diseases, technical support, training, surveillance and emergency response capacity building.Mayor Dr. Shahadat Hossain said, “Dengue has become a major health threat to Chattogram for the past few years. We are conducting mosquito control activities throughout the year to protect the lives and health of the city residents. Expert cooperation from the international organization MSF will make our work plan more scientific, technology-based and effective.” He added that the CCC is considering new methods and technologies in field-level mosquito density surveys, hotspot identification, larva control, public awareness raising and emergency response systems. At the meeting, the MSF delegation presented a possible plan for implementing dengue prevention activities in Chattogram, including data analysis, first aid preparation, vector control strategy, health worker training and emergency response systems. The delegation expressed interest in developing a sustainable and research-based dengue prevention framework in coordination with the Chattogram City Corporation. The Mayor said, “Dengue control in Chattogram is not the sole responsibility of CCC; it is a collective social and institutional effort. Having an international humanitarian health organization like MSF standing by our side is a major success and a realistic direction for the future.” The meeting was attended by MSF Regional Operational Director Paul Brockman, Regional Health Director Dr. Mark Sherlock, Country Director, Mike Harsvoort, Chief of Health Dr. Carmenza Galvez, Deputy Chief of Health, Dr. Rezwan Masum, Head of Dengue Response Dinali De Jaysa. The meeting was attended by CCC representatives on the dengue situation, ongoing programs and the possibility of new partnerships. Both sides agreed to formulate a coordinated action plan, technical cooperation, joint programs and build a rapid response healthcare system for citizens in the future. The mayor expressed hope that this joint initiative of CCC and MSF will create a new milestone in the prevention of dengue and chikungunya in Chattogram.

title: Unauthorized structures removed in Nilphamari
body: Nilphamari Correspondent : The busy Badiyar Mor area, an important junction connecting Nilphamari’s Jaldhaka, Domar, and Panchagarh-bound roads, had long been plagued by illegal shops, hawkers, occupied footpaths, waste accumulation, and a disorderly rickshaw stand. These issues caused persistent traffic congestion and created an unhealthy environment for residents and commuters. To address the situation, a major eviction drive was carried out under the directive of Nilphamari Superintendent of Police Sheikh Zahidul Islam, PPM. The operation was initiated by Additional Superintendent of Police (Circle) Faruk Ahmed, PPM-Service, in coordination with the Roads and Highways Department (RHD), an executive magistrate team, the traffic division, and the local market committee. During the drive, illegal shops and hawker stalls built on roads and footpaths were dismantled, and the chaotic rickshaw stand was removed. As a result, movement through this key intersection has already started returning to normal. According to the district police, the primary goals of the operation were to ease traffic congestion, ensure safe movement for pedestrians, maintain a healthy environment, and improve urban management. Authorities also stated that similar operations will continue regularly to keep the city and its roads well-organized.

title: Begum Rokeya Day held
body: Feni Correspondent : On the occasion of Begum Rokeya Day 2025, as every year, Deputy Commissioner Monira Haque presented the Indomitable Women Medal to five distinguished women in Feni in recognition of their special contribution to women’s awakening in various fields. The medals were presented to five people at a ceremony organized by the District Administration and Women’s Affairs Department, Feni, at the conference room of the Deputy Commissioner on Tuesday. Presided over by Nasrin Akhter, Deputy Director of the Women’s Affairs Department, Feni, Feni ADC (General) Md. Ismail Hossain, Feni Additional Superintendent of Police Sadar Nishat Tabassum and Feni Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Sultana Nasrin Kanta were special guests. Representatives of various women’s organizations and senior officials of the administration were present at the time. At the end, the guests presented crests, certificates and gifts to the five women who received the Indomitable Women Medal. ?The recipients of the medal this time are: economically successful woman Chumki Karmakar from Parashuram, successful woman in education and employment Mosammat Shirin Akhter from Chagalnayar, successful mother Begum Tajkera Chowdhury from Sonagazi, victorious woman in life Shirina Akhter from Sonagazi, and Shahnaz Akhter from Chagalnayar for her contribution to social development.
